docs.title: 8. REST API Reference
docs.text: mcctl-api is the Fastify REST API behind the Web Console: port 5001 (PORT), listening on HOST (mcctl console init writes 127.0.0.1 for the internal access mode, 0.0.0.0 for the others; unset → 0.0.0.0), run on the host by PM2 as mcctl-api (not in Docker). Full reference: docs/api/index.md (authentication, errors, SSE, Swagger) and docs/api/endpoints.md (every route with bodies, responses and status codes). Paths below are complete; only the legacy /servers/:id/console/exec lacks /api. :name and body fields serverName take the server name without mc- (survival, not mc-survival).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
AUTH_MODE and its settings are environment variables of the mcctl-api app in <root>/ecosystem.config.cjs, written by mcctl console init:

AUTH_MODE Requirement Request header mcctl console init mode disabled none - open api-key AUTH_API_KEY X-API-Key: <key> api-key (key printed once) ip-whitelist client address in AUTH_IP_WHITELIST (IPs or CIDR, comma-separated) - internal (default; 127.0.0.1,::1,::ffff:127.0.0.1) or ip-whitelist basic user in AUTH_USERS (JSON [{"username","passwordHash"}], bcrypt) Authorization: Basic <base64> not offered combined API key and IP whitelist X-API-Key: <key> api-key-ip 
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers   # api-key / combined
curl -u admin:password http://localhost:5001/api/servers            # basic
  • Unset or unknown AUTH_MODE: api-key when NODE_ENV=production, else disabled. mcctl-api does not start when the mode's required variable is missing. AUTH_EXCLUDE_PATHS (default /health,/health/) skip authentication.
  • The key is read only from X-API-Key; Authorization: Bearer gets 401. Failures: 401 {"error":"AuthenticationError","message":"Missing X-API-Key header"} (also Invalid API key, Invalid credentials), 403 AuthenticationError IP address not allowed.
  • X-Role: admin is required by DELETE /api/audit-logs, GET /api/platform-settings and PUT /api/platform-settings (403 Forbidden otherwise). X-User becomes the audit actor api:<user> for the file routes and PUT /api/platform-settings (other routes record api:console) and is required by GET /api/auth/me. The console adds both headers when it forwards requests that need them.
  • Change the mode or key with mcctl console init --force; mcctl console api ... only edits api-config.json, which mcctl-api does not read (#633).
  • Swagger UI /docs and the spec /docs/json are served only when NODE_ENV is not production or SWAGGER_ENABLED=true; they need the same authentication as other routes.

docs.title: All Endpoints
docs.text:
105 routes, one line each (details in docs/api/endpoints.md).

Health

Method Path Notes GET /health {status: "ok", timestamp}; always 200; no auth by default

Servers

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers servers/ dirs with config.env + mc-* containers: {servers: [{name, container, status, health, hostname}], total}. ?include=summary adds type, version, memory, players (null on RCON failure), stats {memoryUsage, memoryLimit} and totals {playersOnline, playersMax, running} (RCON ~2 s, stats ~3 s, cached ~10 s); other include values → 400 GET /api/servers/:name {server}: list fields + type, version, memory, uptime, uptimeSeconds, players {online, max, players[]}, stats {memoryUsage, memoryLimit, memoryPercent, cpuPercent}, worldName, worldSize, playitDomain; no container → status: "not_created" from config.env GET /api/servers-status [{serverName, status, health, timestamp}] (status: running/exited/created/stopped/unknown); ?follow=true&interval= → SSE server-status per server GET /api/servers/:name/status Same object for one server; SSE with follow POST /api/servers Create; 201 {success, server {name, container, status: "starting" or "created"}, warning?}; ?follow=true → SSE server-create / server-create-log messages; 400 validation, 409 exists or world in use DELETE /api/servers/:name Delete; world inside the server moved to worlds/ (?deleteWorld=true deletes it); optional body {sudoPassword}; reply may add warning; 409 refusals, 500 Docker failures POST /api/servers/:name/start docker compose up -d mc-<name> → {success, server, action, timestamp, message} (message = compose stdout, may be empty); failure 500 {success: false, error, message} POST /api/servers/:name/stop docker compose stop mc-<name>; with BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true also a background world backup POST /api/servers/:name/restart docker compose restart mc-<name> POST /api/servers/:name/exec {command} (1-1024 chars) → docker exec mc-<name> rcon-cli -- <command> → {success, output} (stdout only; success is true whenever the container exists) GET /api/servers/:name/logs ?lines= (1-10000, default 100) → {logs, lines}; ?follow=true → SSE data: {"type":"server-log","data":{"log":"..."}}, then connection-closed; 404 without a container

Server configuration

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/config {config}: camelCase fields for config.env variables present (61 fields, e.g. maxPlayers = MAX_PLAYERS, gameMode = MODE (a server with only the older GAMEMODE shows that value; saving gameMode writes MODE and removes GAMEMODE), motd, memory, level) PATCH /api/servers/:name/config Any subset → {success, config, restartRequired, changedFields}; a changed level is a world assignment (stopped server, R1); 409 on refused server.yaml writes POST /api/servers/:name/world/reset Empties worlds/<LEVEL> (keeps .meta); 409 unless the container is stopped, and for internal or shared worlds

Hostnames

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/hostnames {serverName, hostnames[], systemHostnames [{hostname, type, description}], customHostnames[]}; system = <server>.local, <server>.<ip>.nip.io PUT /api/servers/:name/hostnames {customHostnames: []} replaces all custom hostnames; reply adds success, recreateRequired: true, playitDomain; applies after stop + start

Mods (source modrinth, stored in MODRINTH_PROJECTS)

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/mods {mods: {modrinth: [slugs]}} POST /api/servers/:name/mods {slugs: [], source?} → {success, added, mods} DELETE /api/servers/:name/mods/:slug {success, removed}; 404 if not listed GET /api/servers/:name/mods/installed {mods: [{filename, excluded}]} from data/mods/*.jar PATCH /api/servers/:name/mods/installed/:filename/exclude {excluded} toggles the name in MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES (CF_EXCLUDE_MODS for AUTO_CURSEFORGE) → {success, filename, excluded, excludeList, restartRequired} GET /api/mods/search ?q=&limit=10&offset=0&type=modpack → {hits, totalHits, offset, limit} GET /api/mods/projects ?slugs=a,b&source= → {projects: {<slug>: {...} or null}} GET /api/mods/:slug/versions {slug, loaders, byLoader: {<loader>: {gameVersions, recommended}}}; 404 when none GET /api/mods/:slug/client-only ?version= → {slug, clientOnly: []} (partial file names for excludeFiles); 502 on failure

Files (inside servers/<name>/data; path relative to it; leaving it, also via symlinks, → 403; audited as api:<X-User>)

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/files ?path=/ → {path, files: [{name, type, size, modifiedAt}]} (dot entries hidden) GET /api/servers/:name/files/read ?path= → {path, content, size, modifiedAt}; 413 over 5 MB PUT /api/servers/:name/files/write ?path= + {content} (5 MB max) → {success, path, size, modifiedAt} DELETE /api/servers/:name/files ?path= (not /): file or directory POST /api/servers/:name/files/mkdir ?path=; 409 if it exists POST /api/servers/:name/files/rename {oldPath, newPath}; 409 if the target exists POST /api/servers/:name/files/upload ?path= (existing dir) + multipart; 100 MB per file (413) → {success, path, files[]} GET /api/servers/:name/files/download ?path= → application/octet-stream attachment

Players and access lists (changes, ban/op lists and kick need a container, else 404)

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/players {serverName, running, online, max, players[], roster [{uuid, name, lastSeen, isOp, isBanned, isWhitelisted, online}]}; works while stopped; ?follow=true → SSE players GET /api/servers/:name/players/:uuid One known player; ?include=stats,nbt,sessions adds stats, data + livePosition, sessions (unknown value 400, unknown player 404) GET /api/servers/:name/players/live {players: [{uuid, name?, x, y, z, dimension, online, health?, food?, xpLevel?}]} over RCON; empty when stopped; SSE players-live GET /api/players/:username Mojang lookup → {username, uuid, skinUrl} GET /api/servers/:name/whitelist {players: [{name, uuid}], total, source: rcon/file/config, enabled} POST /api/servers/:name/whitelist {player} → {success, message, source}: RCON when running, else whitelist.json DELETE /api/servers/:name/whitelist/:player Same handling as add GET /api/servers/:name/whitelist/status {enabled, source: "config"} (ENABLE_WHITELIST) PUT /api/servers/:name/whitelist/status {enabled} writes ENABLE_WHITELIST (+ RCON whitelist on/off while running) GET /api/servers/:name/bans {players: [{name, uuid, reason, created, source, expires}], total, source: "file"} POST /api/servers/:name/bans {player, reason?}: RCON ban when running, else banned-players.json DELETE /api/servers/:name/bans/:player RCON pardon or the file GET /api/servers/:name/ops {operators: [{name, uuid, level, role, bypassesPlayerLimit}], count, source: "file"} (role: Moderator 1, Gamemaster 2, Admin 3, Owner 4) POST /api/servers/:name/ops {player, level?} (1-4, default 4) → {success, operator, source}; edits ops.json only; 404 when Mojang has no UUID PATCH /api/servers/:name/ops/:player {level} (1-4); 404 if not an operator DELETE /api/servers/:name/ops/:player Removes from ops.json; 404 if not an operator POST /api/servers/:name/kick {player, reason?} via RCON; 400 when not running

Worlds (World assignment rules: §5 World Management; 400 invalid name, 404 unknown server or world, 409 refused)

Method Path Notes GET /api/worlds {worlds: [{name, path, isLocked, lockedBy, servers[], size, lastModified, dimensions {nether, end}}], total, assignmentWarnings[]}; <w>_nether/<w>_the_end folded into <w> GET /api/worlds/:name {world}; any directory right under worlds/ incl. legacy names (My%20World); .-prefixed → 400, not a directory → 404 POST /api/worlds {name, seed?, serverName?, autoStart?} → 201 {success, worldName, seed, serverName, started}; creates worlds/<name>/.meta; 400 if no server exists at all or the name is taken POST /api/worlds/upload ?name= + multipart .zip containing level.dat → 201; 409 exists; 413 over WORLD_UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE (1 GiB) POST /api/worlds/:name/assign {serverName}: sets LEVEL of a stopped server; 409 if another server uses the world POST /api/worlds/:name/release Server goes back to its own world <server> → {success, worldName, previousServer, fallbackWorld, fallbackExists} DELETE /api/worlds/:name Deletes worlds/<name> + <name>_nether/<name>_the_end; 409 while a server uses it GET /api/worlds/:name/info {info: {name, level {seed, spawn, gameMode, difficulty, versionName, worldBorder, gameRules, ...}, dimensions, sizeBytes, regionCount, lastModified}} GET /api/worlds/:name/players Last saved player positions from player data GET /api/worlds/:name/map/status {rendered, maps[], lastModified?} POST /api/worlds/:name/map/render BlueMap CLI in Docker (2 GB limit) → maps/<name>/web; {dimensions?, force?}; ?follow=true → SSE progress, done, error GET /api/worlds/:name/map/web/* Rendered map files (<file>.gz served decompressed) POST /api/worlds/:name/map/markers Structure markers → {counts, total}; 409 before a render GET /api/worlds/:name/stats Cached block statistics (stats/<name>.json); 404 before the first analysis POST /api/worlds/:name/stats/analyze Full region scan; ?follow=true → SSE progress, done, cancelled, error; stops after STATS_ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_MS (10 min) or on disconnect

Router

Method Path Notes GET /api/router/status {router {name, status, health, port, uptime?, uptimeSeconds?, mode: "--in-docker (auto-discovery)", routes [{hostname, target, serverStatus, serverType?, serverVersion?, autoScaleUp?, autoScaleDown?, discoveredByRouter?}], image?, autoScale? {up, down, downAfter?, asleepMotd?}, resolver? {hostIp?, hostIps}}, avahi, playit?}; discoveredByRouter is absent when mc-router or its management API 127.0.0.1:25580/routes is unreadable, and for stopped routes while global AUTO_SCALE_UP is off GET /api/router/status/stream SSE router-status (on connect, then only on change; uptimeSeconds ignored), router-status-error {timestamp}; ?interval= 1000-60000 (5000) GET /api/router/logs/stream SSE connected, router-log {ts?, kind: connect/wake/error/info, hostname?, target?, player?, raw}, end {code, error?}; ?tail= 1-500 (100) POST /api/router/restart docker compose restart router → {success, message}; 500 {error, message}; audit router.restart; the console shows the button to admins only

Backups (GitHub repo from BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO, BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH in .env)

Method Path Notes GET /api/backup/status {configured, repository?, branch, lastBackup?} (branch defaults to main) POST /api/backup/push {message?, allowMissing?} → {success, commitHash?, message} (No changes to backup counts as success); running servers flushed via RCON first; 400 not configured or missing worlds, 409 another backup or unfinished restore, 503 Docker unreachable GET /api/backup/history Last 20 commits {commits: [{hash, message, date, author}], total}; 400 when not configured POST /api/backup/restore {commitHash} (7+ chars); all servers stopped; previous data kept in backups/restore-previous/<timestamp>/ (last 3); 409 / 404 / 503 GET /api/backup/schedules {schedules: [{id, name, cronExpression, cronHumanReadable, retentionPolicy {maxCount?, maxAgeDays?}, enabled, lastRunAt, lastRunStatus, lastRunMessage, createdAt, updatedAt}], total} POST /api/backup/schedules {name, cron, maxCount?, maxAgeDays?, enabled?} → 201 GET /api/backup/schedules/:id One schedule PUT /api/backup/schedules/:id Update name, cron, maxCount, maxAgeDays PATCH /api/backup/schedules/:id/toggle {enabled} DELETE /api/backup/schedules/:id {success, message}

Config snapshots (copies of server.yaml, config.env, docker-compose.yml and other .yml/.yaml/.json/.properties files directly in servers/<name>/, up to 1 MB each)

Method Path Notes GET /api/servers/:name/config-snapshots ?limit=20&offset=0 → {snapshots: [{id, serverName, createdAt, description, files [{path, hash, size}], scheduleId?}], total} POST /api/servers/:name/config-snapshots {description?} → 201 snapshot GET /api/servers/:name/config-snapshots/:id One snapshot (404 if it belongs to another server) DELETE /api/servers/:name/config-snapshots/:id 204 POST /api/servers/:name/config-snapshots/:id/restore {createSnapshotBeforeRestore = true, force = false} → {restored, safetySnapshot?}; 409 while running (without force) or on a world assignment conflict GET /api/config-snapshots/:id1/diff/:id2 {baseSnapshotId, compareSnapshotId, changes [{path, status: added/modified/deleted, ...}], summary, hasChanges} GET /api/config-snapshot-schedules ?serverName= → {schedules: []} POST /api/config-snapshot-schedules {serverName, name, cronExpression, retentionCount? (1-100, default 10), enabled?} → 201 GET /api/config-snapshot-schedules/:id One schedule PUT /api/config-snapshot-schedules/:id Update name, cronExpression, retentionCount PATCH /api/config-snapshot-schedules/:id/toggle {enabled} DELETE /api/config-snapshot-schedules/:id 204; its snapshots are kept

playit.gg

Method Path Notes GET /api/playit/status {enabled, agentRunning, secretKeyConfigured, containerStatus, uptime?, uptimeSeconds?, servers [{serverName, playitDomain, lanHostname}]} POST /api/playit/start Start playit-agent → {success, message}; audit playit.start POST /api/playit/stop Stop playit-agent; audit playit.stop

Platform Settings (<root>/.env; both need X-Role: admin; 404 before mcctl init)

Method Path Notes GET /api/platform-settings {revision, settings [{key, label, group, type, status, source, editable, secret, value? or configured?, restartScope, ...}], runtime []}; secrets return only configured PUT /api/platform-settings {revision, set: {}, remove: []} → {revision, changedKeys, removedKeys, restartScopes}; blank secret = keep; 400 errors[], 409 stale revision (currentRevision) or world-location change (servers); audit by key name only

Audit logs (data/audit.db, shared with the CLI)

Method Path Notes GET /api/audit-logs ?action=&actor=&targetType=&targetName=&status=&from=&to=&limit=&offset=&sort= → {logs, total, limit, offset, filters}; limit 1-200 (50); exact-match filters; only the first of several comma-separated actions applies GET /api/audit-logs/stats No parameters → {total, byAction, byStatus, byActor (newest 1000 entries), recentActivity (10), oldestEntry, newestEntry} GET /api/audit-logs/:id {log, relatedLogs: {sameTarget, sameActor}} (up to 10 each) GET /api/audit-logs/stream SSE connected, audit-log, heartbeat; only entries written by this mcctl-api process (not CLI writes); no filters DELETE /api/audit-logs Needs X-Role: admin; body {before, dryRun?} → {deleted, dryRun, message}

Legacy

Method Path Notes POST /api/auth/login Checks <root>/users.yaml, which current mcctl does not create (console accounts are in the console DB, mcctl console user), so it answers 401 on new installs GET /api/auth/me {username, role} from X-User / X-Role (role defaults to user); 401 without X-User POST /servers/:id/console/exec No /api prefix; {command} → {output, exitCode}; does not check that the server exists

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Errors are {"error": "<Name>", "message": "..."}: BadRequest (route) or Bad Request (schema; some routes add statusCode and code: "FST_ERR_VALIDATION") 400, AuthenticationError 401/403, Forbidden 403, NotFound 404 (unknown route: {"message":"Route GET:/x not found","error":"Not Found","statusCode":404}), Conflict 409, PayloadTooLarge 413, InternalServerError 500, BadGateway 502, ServiceUnavailable 503. Start/stop/restart failures use {success: false, server, action, timestamp, error, message}.
  • Status codes: 201 for creates (server, world, upload, snapshot, schedules), 204 for snapshot and snapshot-schedule deletes.
  • Writes through server.yaml: config, whitelist on/off, hostnames, mods and world assignment update servers/<name>/server.yaml and render config.env and the compose file; a refused write (e.g. hand-edited compose) is 409. Values written to config.env may not contain control characters or start with a quote (400).
  • Create and delete run one at a time inside mcctl-api.
  • SSE: named events (event: + data:) for status, players, router, audit, map render and stats; typed messages (data: {"type": ..., "data": {...}}) for logs and create. : heartbeat every 30 s (audit: event: heartbeat); polling streams take interval 1000-60000 ms (default 5000). The browser EventSource cannot send X-API-Key: use curl -N, fetch with a stream reader, or the console, which proxies /api/sse/<path> to mcctl-api /api/<path>?follow=true for signed-in users.

docs.title: Example: List Servers
docs.text:
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" "http://localhost:5001/api/servers?include=summary"

docs.title: Example: Execute Command
docs.text:
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"command": "list"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/exec
# {"success":true,"output":"There are 3 of a max of 20 players online: ..."}

docs.title: Example: Create Server
docs.text:
# Standard server
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "survival", "type": "PAPER", "version": "1.21.1", "memory": "4G"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/servers

# MODRINTH modpack server
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "cobblemon", "type": "MODRINTH", "modpack": "cobblemon-modpack", "modLoader": "fabric"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/servers

Create Server request body fields:

Field Type Required Description name string Yes 2-32 chars: lowercase letter first, then lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens; router reserved type string No PAPER (default), VANILLA, FORGE, FABRIC, SPIGOT, NEOFORGE, MODRINTH, AUTO_CURSEFORGE version string No Default LATEST; for MODRINTH/AUTO_CURSEFORGE no VERSION is written unless given memory string No ^\d+[MG]$; default 4G (6G for modpack types) seed / worldUrl / worldName string No At most one (400 otherwise); worldName must exist in worlds/ autoStart boolean No Default true sudoPassword string No For adding <name>.local to /etc/avahi/hosts (write-only) modpack string For MODRINTH/AUTO_CURSEFORGE Modrinth modpack slug, ID or URL modpackVersion string No Modpack version (max 128) modLoader string No forge, fabric, neoforge, quilt; with version, an incompatible pair is 400 when Modrinth answers excludeFiles string[] No Up to 100 mods to leave out (MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES / CF_EXCLUDE_MODS)

The JSON reply waits at most 120 s for the container start; after that, or when the first start fails, it is still 201 with status: "created" and a warning.

docs.title: Example: Start/Stop/Restart Server
docs.text:
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/start
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/stop
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/restart

docs.title: Example: Get Server Logs
docs.text:
# Last N lines (JSON)
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" "http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/logs?lines=50"

# SSE streaming logs
curl -N -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" "http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/logs?follow=true"
# data: {"type":"server-log","data":{"log":"[10:30:15] [Server thread/INFO]: Player1 joined the game"}}

docs.title: Example: Player Management via API
docs.text:
# Roster (online + known players)
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/players

# Whitelist add / remove
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"player": "Steve"}' http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/whitelist
curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/whitelist/Steve

# Ban, kick (kick needs a running server)
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"player": "Griefer", "reason": "Griefing"}' http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/bans
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"player": "Troublemaker", "reason": "Breaking rules"}' http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/kick

# Operator with level (1-4, default 4), then change the level
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"player": "TrustedPlayer", "level": 3}' http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/ops
curl -X PATCH -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"level": 2}' http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/ops/TrustedPlayer

docs.title: Example: World Management via API
docs.text:
# List worlds
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/worlds

# Create world
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "newworld", "seed": "12345"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/worlds

# Assign world to the stopped server "survival"
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"serverName": "survival"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/worlds/newworld/assign

# Release world (its server goes back to its own default world)
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  http://localhost:5001/api/worlds/newworld/release

# Delete world
curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  http://localhost:5001/api/worlds/newworld

docs.title: Example: SSE Real-time Status
docs.text:
# Stream all server statuses
curl -N -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" "http://localhost:5001/api/servers-status?follow=true&interval=5000"

# Output format (one event per server every interval, plus ": heartbeat" every 30 s):
# event: server-status
# data: {"serverName":"survival","status":"running","health":"healthy","timestamp":"2026-10-25T10:30:00.000Z"}

docs.title: Example: Audit Logs via API
docs.text:
# List audit logs with filtering
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  "http://localhost:5001/api/audit-logs?action=server.create&limit=20"

# Statistics and one entry
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/audit-logs/stats
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/audit-logs/<id>

# Stream new entries (events: connected, audit-log, heartbeat)
curl -N -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/audit-logs/stream

# Purge entries older than a date (admin only)
curl -X DELETE -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" -H "X-Role: admin" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"before": "2025-11-07T00:00:00.000Z", "dryRun": true}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/audit-logs

docs.title: Example: Backup via API
docs.text:
# Check backup status
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/backup/status

# Push backup
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "Pre-upgrade backup"}' \
  http://localhost:5001/api/backup/push

# Get backup history
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/backup/history

docs.title: API Response Formats
docs.text:
Server object (GET /api/servers items; GET /api/servers/:name adds the detail fields):

Field Type Description name string Server name (no mc- prefix) container string mc-<name> status string running, exited, created, paused, restarting, dead, not_created (directory without a container) health string healthy, unhealthy, starting, none, unknown hostname string The mc-router.host label (comma-separated when several), - when none type, version, memory string From config.env (summary and detail) players object {online, max, players: string[]} (summary: null when RCON fails) stats object Summary: {memoryUsage, memoryLimit} bytes; detail adds memoryPercent, cpuPercent uptime, uptimeSeconds string, number Detail, only while running worldName, worldSize, playitDomain string Detail only

Audit log entry:

Field Type Description id string UUID action string e.g. server.create, player.whitelist.add (49 actions, see the audit FAQ) actor string api:console (most API routes), api:<user> (file routes, Platform Settings), cli:local (CLI), scheduler (retention cleanup after a scheduled backup) targetType string server, world, player, service, system, platform, backup, backup-schedule, config-snapshot-schedule, audit targetName string Server, world, service or schedule name details object or null Context; fields depend on the action status string success, failure errorMessage string or null Error of a failed action timestamp string ISO 8601

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
mcctl-console is a Next.js web application for managing servers, worlds, players, backups, routing and the audit log from a browser (default http://localhost:5000). It needs mcctl-api: mcctl console service start --console starts both under PM2.

Key Technologies: - Next.js 14 (App Router) - React 18 with MUI 5 (dark theme only) - Better Auth: sessions stored in the console database data/mcctl.db (SQLite) behind a session cookie; a session lasts 7 days and is extended at most once a day while used - React Query 5 for data fetching and caching - SSE (Server-Sent Events) for server status, logs, players, router status and log, and audit log updates

Roles: Admin or User. Accounts made on the sign-up page get User and see only servers they were granted on a server's Access tab (per-server Viewer, Operator, Owner); a User who creates a server becomes its Owner. Admin only: Platform Settings, the Users page, Restart mc-router, purging audit logs (API). Users are added and changed with mcctl console user.

docs.title: BFF Proxy Architecture
docs.text:
+------------------+      +-----------------+      +---------------+
|   Web Browser    | ---> | mcctl-console   | ---> |   mcctl-api   |
|   (React Query)  |      | (Next.js BFF)   |      |   (Fastify)   |
+------------------+      +-----------------+      +---------------+
                              |
                              | Session-based auth (Better Auth)
                              | + X-API-Key forwarding to mcctl-api

Why BFF Proxy? 1. API keys stay server-side, never exposed to browser 2. Each BFF route checks the Better Auth session before calling mcctl-api 3. Type-safe shared TypeScript interfaces 4. React Query provides optimistic updates and caching

There is no generic /api pass-through: each mcctl-api call has its own App Router route under app/api/, except SSE (/api/sse/<path>, below).

docs.title: Pages and Features
docs.text: Navigation: top bar Dashboard (/dashboard; / sends signed-in users there, others to /login), Servers (/servers), Worlds (/worlds), Players (/players), Audit (/audit-logs), Backups (/backups), Routing (/routing); user menu Users (/admin/users, admins, read-only), Settings (/settings), Logout. /signup creates a User account (no email verification).

docs.title: Dashboard (/dashboard)
docs.text:
• Status hero: servers online, "All systems operational" or "N servers need attention", Live / Reconnecting (SSE); Create Server opens /servers?create=1
  • Cards: Total Servers (running / stopped), Online Players (online / max over running servers), Worlds (assigned / free), mc-router (:<port>, status, health, routes; red when down or unhealthy)
  • Servers panel: All / Running / Stopped filter, up to five rows with status and health chips, primary hostname (the LAN nip.io address first) with copy, players, memory, TYPE · version; Console (opens /servers/<name>/console), Restart / Stop (confirmed) or Start
  • External Access (playit.gg agent status, up to three server addresses), Recent Activity (audit log; web console actions show the actor console), Recent Updates (latest release in CHANGELOG.md on main, fetched by the console server through GET /api/changelog and cached 1 hour; Update available when newer than the installed console)

Status colors:

Color Status chip Health chip Green running healthy Amber created (container never started) starting Red stopped, exited (server cards: also Not Created) unhealthy Gray other or unknown no health check (Unknown)

docs.title: Servers (/servers)
docs.text:
• Server cards (status, primary hostname with +N, container name, Start/Stop), ALL / RUNNING / STOPPED filter, name search
  • Create Server dialog: name (2-32 characters of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter, no trailing hyphen or --; router is reserved); Standard Server (VANILLA, PAPER, FABRIC, FORGE or NEOFORGE plus a Minecraft version; defaults VANILLA and LATEST) or Modpack (Modrinth search, then a loader and Minecraft version the pack supports; detected client-only mods pre-fill Exclude mods); world (default, seed, or an unassigned existing world); memory (4G, 6G for modpacks); optional Sudo Password for the avahi entry; Auto-start after creation
  • The dialog waits for POST /api/servers, then steps through its stages and ends with Server Created Successfully, Server Created with a Warning (the server exists but its first start failed or is still running; the reason is shown) or Creation Failed

docs.title: Server Detail (/servers/:name)
docs.text:
• Header: Switch server menu; chips for state, health, type, version (and Reconnecting); hostname with copy, uptime; Start, or Stop and Restart; ⋮ Delete Server (type the name; keep the world, moved to worlds/ (default), or delete the server's own world; optional Sudo Password to remove <name>.local; a partial failure shows Server deleted with the warning)
  • Cards above the tabs: CPU usage (High from 70%, Critical from 90%), Memory usage (used / allocated, same marks), World size
  • Ten tabs; ?tab=<Tab> opens one (e.g. ?tab=Options):
  • Overview: live log console with a > prompt, Send, chips /list /tps /save-all /say /whitelist list, Jump to latest, Download logs, Clear console (screen only), Expand console (level filter, Auto-scroll, Hide RCON, quick commands, ↑/↓ history). The RCON reply is not shown, only what the server writes to its log. Panels: Settings (container, memory allocation, world), Players (online players with OP / Whitelisted badges), Connection (every address with port 25565, labeled LAN, Tailscale / VPN, nip.io, External or mDNS, and the playit.gg address)
  • Players (v2.27.0+, online count on the tab): unified online (RCON) + offline (usercache/playerdata/ops/whitelist/banned files) roster, shown even when the server is stopped; real-time via SSE. Avatars (mc-heads.net), badges (Online/Offline, OP, Banned, Whitelisted), per-row menu: Details, Kick, Ban/Unban, Make OP/Remove OP, Add/Remove Whitelist
    • Player Detail Modal: Statistics (play time, deaths, mob/player kills, distance, blocks mined, items crafted, advancements; from stats/+advancements/), Position & Status (XYZ, dimension, health, food, XP level, game mode, inventory summary; from playerdata/<uuid>.dat, live position via RCON polled every 5s while online), Session History (visits, total playtime, last seen, recent 20 sessions)
    • Session history exists only from when the mcctl-api v2.27.0+ collector first runs (first pass backfills up to 24h of container logs)
  • World: info cards (seed, spawn, game mode, difficulty, day, version, size, border, regions, weather), BlueMap Render map / Re-render, Analyze ore and block statistics, player positions
  • Activity: this server's audit entries (Action filter, status toggle, View Full History)
  • Mods (installed-jar count on the tab): search, add and remove Modrinth mods; for modpack servers, Installed Jar Files with an Included / Excluded switch per jar; restart the server to apply
  • Files: browse, upload, create folders, edit, rename, delete, download; form editor for server.properties (edits are lost when the container is recreated; use Options for lasting settings) and a player editor for whitelist.json, ops.json, banned-players.json
  • Config History: config snapshot timeline with diff, compare, restore (safety snapshot by default) and delete
  • Backups: Config Snapshots and World Backups sub-tabs
  • Access: grant, change or remove Viewer / Operator / Owner per user (admins and Owners; the last Owner cannot be removed)
  • Options: Hostnames / Domains (system hostnames read-only; custom domains, including the playit.gg domain; applied after Stop then Start, not Restart), settings cards with advanced fields, Save Changes or Save & Restart, Danger Zone › Reset World (server stopped, type RESET)
  • /servers/:name/console: full-page console (Connected / Connecting / Disconnected (Retry N), breadcrumb, the expanded console's controls)

docs.title: Worlds (/worlds)
docs.text:
• World cards: size with Overworld / Nether / End chips, Available or Assigned, the server using it; a warning alert and an "Assigned to N servers" chip for duplicate assignments left by older installs; ALL / AVAILABLE / ASSIGNED filter and search
  • + Create World: name (letters, digits, hyphens, underscores) and optional seed, or Upload world .zip to import one
  • Assign (stopped servers only; sets the server's LEVEL), Release (the server goes back to its own default world), Delete (type the name; refused while a server uses the world); a card opens World Details (the World tab panel)

docs.title: Players (/players)
docs.text: Server dropdown; tabs Online Players (all servers, Kick), Whitelist (on/off switch, add, bulk add, remove), Operators (levels 1-4), Ban List (ban with reason, pardon). For a stopped server the lists are read from its files and changes apply on the next start.

docs.title: Audit (/audit-logs)
docs.text:
• Live / Disconnected chip (reconnects every 3 s); new entries raise a "N new logs available - Click to refresh" banner (the list does not reload by itself)
  • Cards: Total Logs, Success Rate, Failures, Active Users (refreshed every 30 s)
  • Filters (applied at once, kept in the URL): From/To (UTC days), Action (Create, Delete, Start, Stop, Restart, Whitelist Add/Remove, Ban, Unban, Op, Deop, Kick, Purge, Platform Settings), Target type (All / Server / Player), Status, Target Name, Actor (exact, e.g. api:console)
  • Table: Timestamp, Action, Actor, Target, Status; 25/50/100 rows; failed rows start expanded; a row opens a drawer with the details and Related Logs (same target, same actor)
  • Export CSV or JSON with the current filters (at most 5,000 rows). No purge control: use mcctl audit purge or DELETE /api/audit-logs (Admin)
  • Actor: console for web console actions (recorded as api:console), the user for Platform Settings changes and file operations (api:<user>), local for the CLI (cli:local). Web console player actions are recorded with the server as the target and the player in the details

docs.title: Backups (/backups)
docs.text:
• World Backups: status, Push Backup (commit message; check Remove worlds I deleted on purpose from the backup when a world from the last backup is gone on purpose, like mcctl backup push --allow-missing), schedules (cron, retention, last run), history with restore (refused while any server runs)
  • Config Snapshots: a card per server, Create Snapshot, Manage Schedules (cron preset or expression, retention count)

docs.title: Routing (/routing)
docs.text:
• Header: router status, "N servers · M hostnames", admin-only Restart mc-router (confirmation; players connected through mc-router are disconnected, running servers keep running)
  • Routing Table: a row per server with the primary address (type badge, copy, +N), status (e.g. Sleeping · wakes on connect), N not routed when mc-router lacks some of its hostnames, Wake / Start, Edit hostnames, Open server; expand a row for every hostname; search matches server names and hostnames
  • Routing Flow diagram; Live Router Log (CONNECT / WAKE / ERROR / INFO lines, last 500, Auto-scroll, Clear); mc-router Gateway (status, health, port, active routes, container, mode, uptime, image, auto-scale values, asleep MOTD); Hostname Resolver (host IPs with Primary, a nip.io example, mDNS (Avahi) status); External Access (playit.gg) (start/stop the agent, server domains)

docs.title: Settings (/settings)
docs.text: Account cards (name, read-only email, role, password change). Admins also get Platform Settings, an editor for the platform .env: typed fields in cards (Network & Routing, Server Runtime, RCON, Backup, External Access, Console & Logging), write-only secrets (RCON_PASSWORD, BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET), a read-only Runtime (PM2) card, Advanced Environment for unknown keys, and Legacy / Unused keys. Saving only writes .env (409 when the file changed since it was loaded) and then lists what to restart: servers (stop, then start), mcctl router start, playit (stop, then start), mcctl console service restart --api or --console.

docs.title: BFF Proxy Routes
docs.text:
Examples (the full list is under platform/services/mcctl-console/src/app/api/):

Console Route Method mcctl-api Route Description /api/servers GET/POST /api/servers List / create servers /api/servers/:name GET/DELETE /api/servers/:name Server details / delete /api/servers/:name/start, /stop, /restart, /exec POST same path Lifecycle, RCON exec /api/servers/:name/logs GET /api/servers/:name/logs Logs (JSON) /api/servers/:name/config GET/PATCH /api/servers/:name/config Config /api/servers/:name/world/reset POST /api/servers/:name/world/reset Reset world /api/servers/:name/players GET /api/servers/:name/players Player roster (JSON or SSE with follow=true) /api/servers/:name/players/:uuid GET /api/servers/:name/players/:uuid Player detail (include forwarded; unknown values dropped, not 400) /api/worlds GET/POST /api/worlds List/Create worlds /api/worlds/upload POST /api/worlds/upload Import a world ZIP /api/worlds/:name GET/DELETE /api/worlds/:name World detail/delete /api/worlds/:name/assign, /release POST same path Assign / release world /api/audit-logs GET/DELETE /api/audit-logs List / purge (purge: Admin) /api/audit-logs/stats, /stream, /:id GET same path Stats, SSE, one entry /api/audit-logs/export GET /api/audit-logs CSV/JSON built by the console /api/changelog GET - CHANGELOG.md from GitHub main, cached 1 hour /api/sse/<path> GET /api/<path>?follow=true SSE proxy: servers-status, servers/:name/status, servers/:name/logs, router/status/stream, router/logs/stream

Other routes cover backups and their schedules, config snapshots and schedules, mods, files, hostnames, player lists (whitelist, ops, bans, kick), playit, router status and restart, platform settings, users and per-user server access, and world info, map and stats.

docs.title: React Query Hooks
docs.text:
// Server hooks (hooks/useMcctl.ts unless noted)
useServers()                    // List servers (refetch 60s; live status comes over SSE)
useServer(name)                 // Server details (refetch 30s)
useCreateServer()               // Create server mutation
useDeleteServer()               // Delete server mutation
useStartServer()                // Start server mutation
useStopServer()                 // Stop server mutation
useRestartServer()              // Restart server mutation
useExecCommand()                // Execute RCON command (the console UI does not show the reply)
useServersSSE()                 // hooks/useServersSSE.ts: /api/sse/servers-status
useServerStatus({serverName})   // hooks/useServerStatus.ts: /api/sse/servers/:name/status
useServerLogs({serverName})     // hooks/useServerLogs.ts: /api/sse/servers/:name/logs (keeps 500 lines)
useServerPlayers({serverName})  // SSE player roster (online + offline)
usePlayerDetail(server, uuid)   // Player detail (?include=stats,nbt,sessions; refetch 5s while online)
useRouterStatus()               // /api/router/status (refetch 30s while the router status stream is down)
useRouterLogStream()            // hooks/useRouterLogStream.ts: /api/sse/router/logs/stream (last 500 events)

// World hooks
useWorlds()                     // List all worlds (refetch 30s)
useWorld(name)                  // Get world details
useCreateWorld()                // Create world mutation
useCreateWorldWithZip()         // Import a world ZIP

useReleaseWorld()               // Release world mutation
useDeleteWorld()                // Delete world mutation

// Audit hooks (hooks/useAuditLogs.ts)
useAuditLogs(params)            // List with filters (no polling; reloaded from the new-logs banner)
useAuditLogStats()              // Statistics (refetch 30s)

docs.title: Web Console Environment Variables
docs.text:
Variable Description Default MCCTL_API_URL mcctl-api URL used by the BFF http://127.0.0.1:<api port> (written by mcctl console init) MCCTL_API_KEY Sent to mcctl-api as X-API-Key Written by mcctl console init for the api-key and api-key-ip modes only BETTER_AUTH_SECRET Session secret, read from <MCCTL_ROOT>/.env at startup; while ecosystem.config.cjs still defines it, the ecosystem value wins (mcctl upgrade moves it to .env) Written to .env by mcctl console init BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL Console URL: a trusted sign-in origin, and secure cookies when it starts with https://; same source rules as the secret http://localhost:<PORT> PORT Console listening port 5000 (mcctl console init --console-port) HOSTNAME Console listening host 0.0.0.0 MCCTL_ROOT Platform root directory ~/minecraft-servers DO_NOT_TRACK 1 or true turns off the anonymous usage analytics (as does "telemetry": false in .mcctl.json) -

Sign-in is accepted from localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1, private addresses (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x), .local names, BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL. From any other origin (a Tailscale 100.x address, a domain, an HTTPS reverse proxy), set BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL to that URL in .env and run mcctl console service restart --console.

docs.title: Autopause
docs.text:
Pauses the server process when no players are online. Recovery is instant.

Variable Default Description ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE false Enable autopause AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_EST 3600 Seconds after last player leaves AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_INIT 600 Seconds after start with no connections AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_KN 120 Seconds after port connection attempt AUTOPAUSE_PERIOD 10 Status check interval AUTOPAUSE_KNOCK_INTERFACE eth0 Network interface to monitor MAX_TICK_TIME - Set to -1 to disable watchdog (recommended with autopause)

docs.title: Autostop
docs.text:
Completely stops the container when idle.

Variable Default Description ENABLE_AUTOSTOP false Enable autostop AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_EST 3600 Seconds after last player leaves AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_INIT 1800 Seconds after start with no connections AUTOSTOP_PERIOD 10 Status check interval

docs.title: Autopause vs Autostop Comparison
docs.text:
Feature Autopause Autostop Behavior Pauses JVM process Stops container Recovery Instant resume Requires container restart Resource Savings Medium (CPU only) High (CPU + most memory) Best For Quick response needed Maximum savings

Note: In mcctl, auto-scaling is handled by mc-router (not autopause/autostop). mc-router starts stopped containers on client connect and stops them after idle timeout.

docs.title: Healthcheck
docs.text:
Variable Default Description DISABLE_HEALTHCHECK false Disable the built-in healthcheck SERVER_HOST localhost Monitoring target host SERVER_PORT 25565 Monitoring target port

Recommended healthcheck settings by server type (in docker-compose.yml):

Server Type start_period interval retries Vanilla / Paper 1m 5s 20 Forge / Fabric 3m 10s 30 Large Modpacks 5m 15s 40

mcctl's server template sets no healthcheck:, so the image's built-in check applies. Adding one to servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml is a hand edit outside image and the mc-router.* labels: mcctl keeps it, but a later change that has to rewrite the file stops with compose_edited (mcctl migrate spec <name> --force re-renders it and keeps docker-compose.yml.bak).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
mc-router is a connection multiplexer enabling multiple Minecraft servers to share a single IP and port (25565) using hostname-based routing.

+-------------------------------------------------------+
|                  Minecraft Clients                      |
|        (Connect to server.example.com:25565)           |
+--------------------------+----------------------------+
                           |
+--------------------------v----------------------------+
|                  mc-router (:25565)                     |
|  - Reads hostname from Minecraft handshake packet      |
|  - Routes to correct backend server                    |
|  - Handles auto-scaling (start/stop containers)        |
+--------------------------+----------------------------+
                           |
    +----------------------+---------------------+
    v                      v                     v
+--------+           +--------+           +--------+
|Server1 |           |Server2 |           |Server3 |
| :25565 |           | :25565 |           | :25565 |
+--------+           +--------+           +--------+

In mcctl, the router service of <root>/docker-compose.yml runs itzg/mc-router:1.47.1 (container mc-router) with IN_DOCKER: "true" (label discovery through the read-only Docker socket), the auto-scale values below as literal environment: entries, API_BINDING: ":8080" published as 127.0.0.1:25580 (management API used by mcctl status), and group_add: ["${DOCKER_GID:-999}"] (mc-router 1.46+ runs as non-root). There is no default route, so a client must send a known hostname.

  • Change router settings: edit the router service environment: in <root>/docker-compose.yml (not .env), then mcctl router start (docker compose up -d router recreates the container). mcctl router restart (docker compose restart router) keeps the old values. mcctl upgrade patches only the router image and group_add, so edits survive.
  • Per server: routing.autoScale.up / routing.autoScale.down in servers/<name>/server.yaml become the mc-router.auto-scale-up/down labels (mcctl migrate spec <name>, then recreate the container).
  • Hostnames (mc-router.host): <name>.local, one <name>.<ip>.nip.io per address in HOST_IPS (else HOST_IP), the playit domain and custom hostnames. A container keeps the labels it was created with: apply changes with mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s> (or mcctl start <s> when stopped).
  • Auto-start needs a container: after mcctl create --no-start or mcctl down (which removes containers), run mcctl start <s> (or mcctl up) once.

docs.title: Routing Methods
docs.text:
1. Docker Auto-Discovery (Recommended for Docker Compose):

services:
  mc-router:
    image: itzg/mc-router:1.47.1  # Pin to explicit version for reproducible deployments
    command: --in-docker --auto-scale-up --auto-scale-down
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

  mc-survival:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    labels:
      - "mc-router.host=survival.local,survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io"
      - "mc-router.port=25565"

2. Command-Line Mapping:

mc-router -mapping "server1.example.com=mc-server1:25565,server2.example.com=mc-server2:25565"

3. JSON Configuration File:

{
  "default-server": "vanilla:25565",
  "mappings": {
    "survival.example.com": "mc-survival:25565",
    "creative.example.com": "mc-creative:25565"
  }
}

4. Kubernetes Service Discovery:

Uses annotations on services.

docs.title: Docker Labels
docs.text: Label Description mc-router.host External hostname(s), comma-separated mc-router.port Backend port (default: 25565) mc-router.auto-scale-up Per-container override for auto-scale-up mc-router.auto-scale-down Per-container override for auto-scale-down mc-router.auto-scale-asleep-motd / mc-router.auto-scale-loading-motd Per-container MOTDs while stopped / starting (mcctl adds a loading MOTD label) mc-router.default Truthy: this container is the default route (still needs mc-router.host). mcctl does not set it

docs.title: Auto-Scaling Configuration
docs.text:
Flag Environment Variable mcctl value Description -auto-scale-up AUTO_SCALE_UP "true" Start stopped containers on connect -auto-scale-down AUTO_SCALE_DOWN "true" Stop idle containers -auto-scale-down-after AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER "10m" Idle timeout before stopping -docker-timeout DOCKER_TIMEOUT "120s" Wait for container start (Go duration such as 120s, 2m; bare integers fail) -auto-scale-asleep-motd AUTO_SCALE_ASLEEP_MOTD "§e§lServer is sleeping§r\n§7Connect to wake up!" MOTD of a stopped server

Player Allow/Deny Lists:

Flag Description -auto-scale-up-allow-list File of player UUIDs/usernames allowed to wake servers -auto-scale-up-deny-list File of players blocked from waking servers

docs.title: Security
docs.text: Feature Description Port Scanner Blocking Connections without valid hostname are blocked Rate Limiting Configurable connections per second per IP DDoS Mitigation Connection throttling reduces attack surface Flag Environment Variable Default Description -connection-rate-limit CONNECTION_RATE_LIMIT 1 Connections per second limit

docs.text: Flag Environment Variable Description -metrics-backend METRICS_BACKEND prometheus, influxdb, or discard -metrics-bind METRICS_BIND Metrics server bind address -record-logins RECORD_LOGINS Track player login metrics -webhook-url WEBHOOK_URL URL for player login/disconnect notifications

docs.title: 12. docker-compose.yml Examples
docs.text: These are standalone examples. The files mcctl generates differ: its router service sets the auto-scale options as environment: entries (see section 11), and each server's docker-compose.yml is generated from servers/<name>/server.yaml.

docs.title: Basic Paper Server with mc-router
docs.text:
services:
  router:
    image: itzg/mc-router:1.47.1  # Pin to explicit version for reproducible deployments
    command: --in-docker --auto-scale-up --auto-scale-down
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock

  mc-survival:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server:java25  # Use java25 or latest for MC 26+, java21 for MC 1.21.x
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "PAPER"
      VERSION: "LATEST"
      MEMORY: "4G"
      USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
    labels:
      - "mc-router.host=survival.local,survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
