docs.title: 1. Create Survival Server for Friends
docs.text:
mcctl init
mcctl router start
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1
mcctl config survival MOTD "Welcome friends!"
mcctl config survival DIFFICULTY hard
mcctl config survival MAX_PLAYERS 10
mcctl op survival add YourName 4
mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival   # apply the config changes
# Connect: survival.<HOST_IP>.nip.io:25565 (whitelist is off; `mcctl whitelist survival on` to restrict)

docs.title: 2. Set Up Modded Forge Server
docs.text:
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.4
mcctl mod add modded --curseforge jei journeymap create
mcctl config modded MEMORY 8G
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

docs.title: 3. Performance Fabric Server
docs.text:
mcctl create perf -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1
mcctl config perf MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,starlight,krypton"
mcctl config perf MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES required
mcctl config perf USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true
mcctl stop perf && mcctl start perf

docs.title: 4. Move a World to Another Server
docs.text:
mcctl world list
mcctl stop oldserver
mcctl world release myworld
mcctl stop newserver
mcctl world assign myworld newserver
mcctl start newserver

docs.title: 5. Backup Before Major Changes
docs.text:
mcctl server-backup myserver -m "Before 1.22 upgrade"
mcctl backup push -m "Pre-upgrade backup"
# If something goes wrong:
mcctl server-restore myserver
mcctl backup restore abc1234

docs.title: 6. Remote Access via VPN (Tailscale/ZeroTier)
docs.text:
mcctl init --reconfigure
# Choose "Host IP(s)", select the LAN and the VPN address
# (writes HOST_IP=192.168.1.100 and HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5),
# answer yes to "Update existing servers with new IP hostnames?"
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver   # recreate so the container gets the new hostname
# Friends connect: myserver.100.64.0.5.nip.io:25565

docs.title: 7. Add Players to Whitelist
docs.text:
mcctl whitelist myserver on
mcctl whitelist myserver add Steve
mcctl whitelist myserver add Alex
mcctl whitelist myserver list

docs.title: 8. Optimize Performance
docs.text:
mcctl config myserver USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 6G
mcctl config myserver VIEW_DISTANCE 8
mcctl config myserver SIMULATION_DISTANCE 8
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: 9. Set Up Management Console (API + Web Console)
docs.text:
mcctl console init
# Select: [mcctl-api, mcctl-console]
# Enter admin email, name, and password
# Choose API access mode
mcctl console service start --console   # mcctl-api + mcctl-console (without the flag it asks)
# Web Console: http://localhost:5000
# REST API: http://localhost:5001
# Swagger UI (/docs) only with SWAGGER_ENABLED=true in .env

docs.title: 10. Use REST API
docs.text:
mcctl console init
# Select "api-key" access mode
mcctl console service start
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers
curl -X POST -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers/myserver/start

docs.title: 11. Set Up API Only (No Web Console)
docs.text:
mcctl console init
# Select: [mcctl-api] only (deselect mcctl-console)
mcctl console service start
# No prompt (only API available)
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" http://localhost:5001/api/servers

docs.title: 12. Auto-Start Services on Boot
docs.text:
pm2 startup
sudo env PATH=$PATH:/usr/bin pm2 startup systemd -u $USER --hp $HOME
pm2 save

docs.title: 13. Updating Services
docs.text:
# Update everything (CLI + API + Console + shared + server images)
mcctl update            # in a terminal it also offers to recreate stopped servers on an old image
mcctl update --yes      # no questions; prints the recreate commands instead

# Or update only the CLI (services in .services/ stay as they are)
mcctl update --cli-only --yes

# Then sync the platform files
mcctl upgrade

docs.title: 14. Set Up External Access with playit.gg
docs.text:
# One-time setup
mcctl playit setup
mcctl playit start

# Create tunnel at https://playit.gg/account/tunnels
# Get your address: xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

# Register with server, then recreate it so mc-router sees the domain
mcctl playit domain survival xx-xx.craft.playit.gg
mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival

# Share with friends: xx-xx.craft.playit.gg (no port forwarding needed!)

# Check status
mcctl playit status

docs.title: 15. Upgrade Platform After CLI Update
docs.text:
# After updating mcctl:
mcctl update

# Check what changed:
mcctl upgrade --dry-run

# Apply changes (interactive):
mcctl upgrade

# Or apply with defaults (scripts/CI):
mcctl upgrade --non-interactive

docs.title: Platform Not Initialized
docs.text:
Error: Platform not initialized. Run: mcctl init

Solution: 

mcctl init

docs.title: Docker Not Running
docs.text:
Error: mcctl status prints Docker is not available; mcctl init prints a prerequisite table and Docker is not installed (or a version below 24.0.0)

Solution: 

sudo systemctl start docker
# Or on macOS/Windows: Start Docker Desktop

docs.title: Server Won't Start
docs.text:
Check logs first: mcctl logs <server> -n 100

Cause Symptom Fix EULA not accepted Server exits immediately Should be automatic with mcctl Wrong Java version class file version error Use correct image tag (see Java matrix) Insufficient memory OutOfMemoryError Increase MEMORY setting Port 25565 in use (mc-router) mc-router does not start, Address already in use See Port Conflicts below (server containers publish no host ports)

docs.title: Can't Connect to Server
docs.text:
# 1. Check mc-router is running (mcctl init does not start it)
mcctl status
# mc-router should show "running" and "healthy"; if not:
mcctl router start

# 2. Check server status and its hostnames (HOSTNAME column)
mcctl status myserver

# 3. Try the server's hostnames
# nip.io: server.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565  (the IP must be reachable from the client)
# mDNS:   server.local:25565

A bare IP (192.168.1.100:25565) never works: mc-router routes by hostname and mcctl sets no default route. Auto-start on connect needs an existing container: after mcctl create --no-start or mcctl down, run mcctl start <server> once. New or changed hostnames reach mc-router only after the container is recreated (mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s>).

docs.title: mc-router Cannot Read the Docker Socket
docs.text: mcctl logs router shows permission denied for /var/run/docker.sock and nothing is routed. mc-router 1.46+ runs as non-root and reads the socket through group_add: ["${DOCKER_GID:-999}"]; DOCKER_GID in .env must match stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock. Run mcctl upgrade (sets DOCKER_GID and patches the router service), then mcctl router start.

docs.title: mDNS Not Working
docs.text:
Linux: 

sudo apt install avahi-daemon
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

Windows: Install Bonjour Print Services from Apple

mcctl create registers <name>.local in /etc/avahi/hosts with sudo (--sudo-password, MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD, the prompt, or sudoers NOPASSWD for tee -a /etc/avahi/hosts, sed -i * /etc/avahi/hosts, systemctl restart avahi-daemon). If sudo failed, the server was still created with a warning: add <ip> <name>.local to /etc/avahi/hosts and restart avahi-daemon.

Fallback: Use nip.io hostname instead of .local

docs.title: World Already Assigned
docs.text:
Error: World 'myworld' is assigned to 'otherserver'; assign another world to 'otherserver' or delete it first (API: 409)

mcctl stop otherserver
mcctl world release myworld
mcctl stop myserver
mcctl world assign myworld myserver

If the error mentions an unreadable world assignment, fix the LEVEL line in that server's config.env (plain LEVEL=<name>); every assignment change is refused until then. If the server keeps its world inside servers/<name>/data, stop it and run mcctl migrate worlds --server <name> first. A container in the created state (for example after mcctl update recreated it) counts as not stopped, and mcctl stop does not change it: run mcctl start <name> && mcctl stop <name>.

docs.title: Out of Memory
docs.text: Scenario Recommended Memory Vanilla / Paper (1-10 players) 2-4G Paper (10-30 players) 4-6G Paper (30+ players) 6-8G Forge / Fabric (light mods) 4-6G Forge / Fabric (heavy mods) 6-8G Large modpacks (100+ mods) 8-12G

docs.title: Console service won't start
docs.text:
• Check prerequisites: mcctl console init checks Node.js >= 18, Docker, Docker Compose and a pm2 >= 6.0.0 on PATH (npm install -g pm2)
  • Verify PM2: pm2 --version
  • Check ecosystem config: ls ~/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs
  • View PM2 logs: pm2 logs mcctl-api or pm2 logs mcctl-console
  • Check port conflicts: netstat -tlnp | grep -E "5000|5001". Ports are set only by mcctl console init --api-port/--console-port (written to PORT in ecosystem.config.cjs)
  • mcctl console service start and restart wait up to 15 s for the health checks and exit 1 if a service is not healthy. mcctl console service status checks GET /health on mcctl-api (2xx) and /api/auth/get-session on mcctl-console (below 500), prints Health: HTTP 500 or Health: unreachable for a failed check, and then exits 1 ("Some services need attention")

docs.title: mcctl-console shows "not installed (skipping)"
docs.text:
• Install console package: npm install @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console in ~/minecraft-servers/.services/
  • Or reinitialize: mcctl console init --force and select mcctl-console
  • Verify: ls ~/minecraft-servers/.services/node_modules/@minecraft-docker/mcctl-console/ (older installs: ~/minecraft-servers/node_modules/...)

docs.title: API connection issues
docs.text:
• Check service: mcctl console service status
  • Verify API key (shown only once during init; prefix mctk_). The key in use is AUTH_API_KEY in ecosystem.config.cjs; get a new one with mcctl console init --force
  • Test health: curl http://localhost:5001/health returns {"status":"ok","timestamp":"..."}
  • Check access mode: grep AUTH_MODE ~/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs (mcctl console api status shows api-config.json, not the running API's settings; see #633)
  • Web console requests fail with 403 under ip-whitelist or api-key-ip: the console calls mcctl-api from the same host, so the list must contain 127.0.0.1 (an entry localhost matches nothing). Re-run mcctl console init --force to change the list

docs.title: Can't log in to Web Console
docs.text:
• Verify user: mcctl console user list
  • Reset password: mcctl console user reset-password admin@example.com
  • Signing in from an origin other than localhost, a private LAN address or a .local name (a Tailscale 100.x address, a domain, an HTTPS reverse proxy) fails until BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL=<that URL> is set in ~/minecraft-servers/.env; then mcctl console service restart --console. If ecosystem.config.cjs still defines BETTER_AUTH_*, run mcctl upgrade first (until then the ecosystem value wins)
  • View logs: mcctl console service logs -f

docs.title: PM2 process keeps restarting
docs.text:
• Check crashes: pm2 logs mcctl-api --lines 100
  • Verify dependencies: cd ~/minecraft-servers/.services 2>/dev/null || cd ~/minecraft-servers; npm ls @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api
  • PM2 restarts a service that grows past max_memory_restart (500M): raise it in ecosystem.config.cjs
  • A plain mcctl console service restart keeps the env and options PM2 already has. After editing ecosystem.config.cjs, use mcctl console service restart --force (deletes the processes, kills the PM2 daemon and starts the selected services from the file); .env changes need only a plain restart

docs.title: Console returns 500 after a Node.js change
docs.text: pm2 logs mcctl-console shows NODE_MODULE_VERSION or ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED: the native better-sqlite3 module was built for another Node.js version than the PM2 daemon runs. mcctl console service status prints the steps: pm2 kill, switch to the Node.js version mcctl was installed with (e.g. nvm use 22), then mcctl console service start --console.

docs.title: SSE not working (real-time updates)
docs.text:
• Ensure mcctl-api is running
  • Check if proxy/firewall blocks SSE connections
  • Verify the stream on mcctl-api: curl -N 'http://localhost:5001/api/servers-status?follow=true' (add -H 'X-API-Key: <key>' in the api-key modes). /api/sse/servers-status is the console's proxy path, not an mcctl-api route

docs.title: World management issues
docs.text:
• Ensure server is stopped before world reset
  • Check world assignments and warnings: mcctl world list
  • Free a world another server uses: stop that server, then mcctl world release <world>
  • Leftover worlds/.locks is unused and can be removed: rm -rf worlds/.locks

docs.title: Version mismatch
docs.text:
• Verify all mods support the server's Minecraft version
  • Check mod compatibility with server type (Forge mods on Forge, Fabric mods on Fabric)

docs.title: Missing dependencies
docs.text:
mcctl config <server> MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES required

For Fabric servers, always include fabric-api in MODRINTH_PROJECTS.

docs.title: Mod compatibility
docs.text:
• Review logs: mcctl logs <server>
  • Remove incompatible mods: mcctl mod remove <server> <mod>

docs.title: Java Version Errors
RCON Connection Issues
docs.text:
Symptoms: - mcctl exec or mcctl console commands fail - "Connection refused" errors - Player management commands (whitelist, ban, op) fail

Diagnosis: 

# 1. Verify RCON is enabled
mcctl config <server> ENABLE_RCON
# Should show: true

# 2. Verify the server is running and healthy
mcctl status <server> -d

# 3. Check RCON password is set (servers get it through servers/global.env)
grep RCON_PASSWORD ~/minecraft-servers/.env

mcctl console / mcctl rcon connect over TCP to the container's IP on the Docker network (the server must be fully started; Docker Desktop on macOS may not expose that IP). mcctl exec and the player commands run rcon-cli inside the container with docker exec, so use mcctl exec <server> <command> when the TCP session cannot connect.

Fix: 

# Ensure RCON is enabled
mcctl config <server> ENABLE_RCON true

# Restart server to apply
mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>

docs.title: Autopause / Autostop Issues
docs.text:
Symptoms: - Server pauses unexpectedly - Server does not wake up on client connect - Watchdog timer kills paused server

Fix: 

# Disable watchdog when using autopause (critical!)
mcctl config <server> MAX_TICK_TIME -1

# Check network interface (must match container's interface)
mcctl config <server> AUTOPAUSE_KNOCK_INTERFACE eth0

# Enable debug logging for autopause
mcctl config <server> DEBUG_AUTOPAUSE true
mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>
mcctl logs <server>

Note: In mcctl, auto-scaling is handled by mc-router (not autopause/autostop). Its AUTO_SCALE_UP/AUTO_SCALE_DOWN are set in the router service environment: of docker-compose.yml (apply with mcctl router start); per server, use routing.autoScale in server.yaml.

docs.title: CurseForge Mod Download Failures
docs.text:
Symptoms: - "API key required" errors - Mods fail to download from CurseForge - 403 Forbidden errors

Fix: (Java 17+ images have a built-in key; this applies to java8/pre-17 tags or a custom key) 1. Get a key from CurseForge for Studios 2. Set it per server (do not escape $; mcctl quotes the value), then recreate the server: 

mcctl config <server> CF_API_KEY '<key>'
mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>
For every server instead, add a CF_API_KEY line to servers/global.env and put the value in .env in single quotes. A key only in .env does not reach servers. 3. Some mods are restricted from third-party downloads; use manual download

docs.title: Common config.env Mistakes
docs.text:
Mistake Symptom Fix GAMEMODE=creative Game mode unchanged The image reads MODE: mcctl config <server> MODE creative, or save Game Mode in the console (it writes MODE and removes GAMEMODE) Unquoted # in a value Value cut at the # (MOTD=Hi #1 sets Hi) Quote it (MOTD='Hi #1'), or set it with mcctl config, which quotes it A list continued on the next line Only the first line is the value One comma-separated line (MODRINTH_PROJECTS=fabric-api,lithium,sodium) A value that starts with a quote set through mcctl Refused Pass the value without surrounding quotes; mcctl quotes what needs it CF_API_KEY (or another key) only in .env Not in the container mcctl config <server> CF_API_KEY '<key>', or add the name to servers/global.env TYPE misspelled The server does not run as the intended type mcctl config does not check TYPE; use a name from Section 6

EULA=TRUE is set by each server's compose environment:, and EXTRA_ARGS (--universe /worlds/) is written from world.storage in server.yaml, so neither needs to be added by hand.

docs.title: nip.io DNS Not Resolving
docs.text:
Symptoms: - server.192.168.1.100.nip.io does not resolve - DNS lookup timeout

Causes & Fixes:

Cause Fix DNS firewall/filter blocking nip.io Use alternative DNS (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1) ISP DNS blocking wildcard Switch to public DNS Wrong HOST_IP in .env Verify with ip addr or ifconfig Private IP used from public network Use Tailscale/ZeroTier VPN

docs.title: Port Conflicts
docs.text:
Error: Address already in use for port 25565, 5000, or 5001

# Check what is using the port
sudo lsof -i :25565
sudo lsof -i :5000
sudo lsof -i :5001

# Or use netstat
netstat -tlnp | grep -E "25565|5000|5001"

Fix: Stop the conflicting service or change the port in configuration.

docs.title: General
docs.text:
Q: What is mcctl? A: A CLI tool for managing Docker-based Minecraft Java Edition servers with hostname routing, auto-scaling, and web management.

Q: What Minecraft editions does it support? A: Java Edition only. Bedrock Edition is not supported.

Q: Where is data stored? A: Default: ~/minecraft-servers/. Set MCCTL_ROOT, or pass --root <path> to every command (it is not stored).

Q: How many servers can I run? A: Unlimited, limited only by system resources.

Q: What are the system requirements? A: Node.js >= 18.0.0, Docker Engine >= 24.0.0, Docker Compose >= 2.20.0 (mcctl init checks these). git >= 2.31 for GitHub backups; pm2 >= 6 on PATH for the web console (npm install -g pm2).

docs.title: Server
docs.text:
Q: What server types are supported? A: mcctl create -t accepts PAPER, VANILLA, FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC, SPIGOT, BUKKIT, PURPUR, QUILT, LEAF, FOLIA, PUFFERFISH, MODRINTH and AUTO_CURSEFORGE (the last two with --modpack <slug>). itzg also supports MOHIST, ARCLIGHT, MAGMA_MAINTAINED, KETTING, SPONGEVANILLA, FTBA, CUSTOM (set TYPE with mcctl config).

Q: What's the default server type? A: PAPER - a high-performance fork with plugin support. Defaults of mcctl create: version LATEST, memory 4G (6G for modpacks), image tag by VERSION (java25 for LATEST), whitelist off.

Q: How do I change Minecraft version? A: mcctl config myserver VERSION 1.20.4, then mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver. Check that the image's Java fits the version (older versions need e.g. java17).

Q: Do servers auto-start? A: Yes, with mc-router auto-scaling, a stopped server starts when a player connects, if mc-router runs (mcctl router start) and the server's container exists (after mcctl create --no-start or mcctl down, run mcctl start <server> once).

Q: Do servers auto-stop? A: Yes, after 10 minutes of no players. Change AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER in the router service environment: of <root>/docker-compose.yml and apply it with mcctl router start (not .env, not mcctl router restart).

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
Q: What port do I use? A: Always 25565. mc-router handles routing.

Q: Why can't I connect with just IP? A: mc-router needs a hostname to route. Use nip.io or mDNS.

Q: What is nip.io? A: A magic DNS service. server.192.168.1.100.nip.io resolves to 192.168.1.100.

Q: Do clients need mDNS/avahi? A: Only for .local hostnames. nip.io works without client setup.

docs.title: Mod/Plugin
docs.text:
Q: How do I add mods? A: mcctl mod add <server> <mod-name>. Default source is Modrinth. Use --curseforge for CurseForge.

Q: What mod sources are supported? A: Modrinth (default), CurseForge, Spiget (SpigotMC), and direct URLs.

Q: Do I need an API key for CurseForge? A: No on Java 17+ images (key built in). Only java8/pre-17 tags or your own key need CF_API_KEY (key from console.curseforge.com): set it per server with mcctl config <server> CF_API_KEY '<key>'. A key only in .env does not reach servers.

Q: Where are mods stored? A: Downloaded automatically by the server container based on config.env settings.

Q: Are mod dependencies downloaded automatically? A: Yes. By default MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=required is set. When you add iris, its dependency sodium is auto-downloaded.

Q: How do I disable automatic dependency download? A: Set MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=none in config.env.

Q: What dependency options are available? A: required (default, recommended), optional (required + optional deps), none (manual).

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Q: What does backup include? A: The worlds/ directory with all world data.

Q: What does server-backup include? A: Server configuration files: config.env, docker-compose.yml and, when present, server.yaml, data/ops.json, data/whitelist.json, data/banned-players.json, data/banned-ips.json, data/server.properties. Not world data.

Q: Is a GitHub account required for backups? A: Only for the GitHub backup feature. Manual backups don't require it.

docs.title: World
docs.text:
Q: Can I share a world between servers? A: No. One world is used by one server. To move a world, stop both servers, run mcctl world release <world> (the old server goes back to its own default world), then mcctl world assign <world> <server>.

Q: What happens when I delete a server? A: mcctl delete asks first (-y skips; --force also deletes with players online). The world is kept: a world inside the server folder is moved to worlds/, unless --delete-world.

Q: How do I import an existing world? A: Place it in ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/ and use mcctl create --world <name>.

Q: What happens when I run mcctl world new without --server? A: The world directory is created with a .meta file (seed, timestamp). Actual Minecraft world files are generated when a server first uses the world.

docs.title: Management Console
docs.text:
Q: What is the Management Console? A: mcctl-api (REST API on port 5001) + mcctl-console (Web UI on port 5000).

Q: Why PM2 instead of Docker? A: Lower overhead, faster startup, easier debugging, automatic process recovery.

Q: How do I start the web console? A: mcctl console init then mcctl console service start --console (without --console it asks which services).

Q: What access modes are available? A: internal (default), api-key, ip-whitelist, api-key-ip, open. mcctl console init writes them as mcctl-api AUTH_MODE values: internal → ip-whitelist (loopback only), api-key-ip → combined, open → disabled, the others unchanged.

Q: Where is the API documentation? A: docs/api/endpoints.md. The Swagger UI at http://localhost:5001/docs is served only when mcctl-api does not run with NODE_ENV=production (the PM2 setup does) or when SWAGGER_ENABLED=true is set in .env (apply with mcctl console service restart --api). It needs the same authentication as the other routes (X-API-Key in the api-key modes).

Q: Can I run just the API without the Web Console? A: Yes. During mcctl console init, select only mcctl-api. Or use mcctl console service start --api.

Q: How does service selection work? A: Since v1.13.0, mcctl console service start/stop/restart shows interactive prompt when both services are installed. Console always requires API. Use --api or --console flags to skip prompt; without a terminal the command exits 1 unless one of them is given.

Q: How do I check if the console is running? A: mcctl console service status

Q: How do I view console logs? A: mcctl console service logs or mcctl console service logs -f for real-time.

Q: Why is a player's session history empty or short? A: Session history (v2.27.0+) is collected by mcctl-api from Docker logs (joined/left the game) every 30s into data/players.db. It starts when the collector first runs; the first pass backfills at most 24h of container logs. Older sessions, or logs of a recreated container, cannot be recovered. Stats/position come from world files and are not affected.

Q: Can I see players of a stopped server? A: Yes (v2.27.0+). GET /api/servers/:name/players returns the file-based roster with running: false; online/max/players are 0/empty.

Q: How does SSE work in the Web Console? A: The browser opens Server-Sent Events streams to the console, which checks the session and proxies /api/sse/<path> to mcctl-api /api/<path>?follow=true. Server status comes from GET /api/servers-status?follow=true: mcctl-api checks Docker every 5 seconds and sends a server-status event per server, plus a heartbeat every 30 seconds. Logs, a single server's status and the router status and log use the same proxy; the player roster (/api/servers/:name/players?follow=true) and the audit log (/api/audit-logs/stream) have their own routes.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Q: How do I optimize performance? A: Use mcctl config <server> USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true. For modded servers, increase MEMORY to 6-8G. Reduce VIEW_DISTANCE and SIMULATION_DISTANCE.

Q: What are Aikar flags? A: Recommended JVM garbage collection tuning for Minecraft. Reduces GC pause times.

docs.title: Audit Log
docs.text:
Q: What are audit logs? A: A record of operations from the CLI, mcctl-api and the web console (servers, players, worlds, mods, playit, router, settings, files, schedules). View with mcctl audit list or in Web Console. Logs are kept until mcctl audit purge or the optional auto-cleanup removes them.

Q: How do I configure audit retention? A: AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP=true (default off) and AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90) in .env, read by mcctl-api (the CLI reads only its shell environment). Cleanup runs while logs are written (every 100 entries or 24 hours). Or run mcctl audit purge --days <n>.

Q: What actions are tracked? A: server. create, delete, start, stop, restart, config, hostname; player. whitelist.add, whitelist.remove, whitelist.toggle, ban, unban, op, op.level, deop, kick; world. create, delete, assign, release, map.render; mod. add, remove; playit. start, stop; router.restart; platform.settings.update; file. read, write, delete, mkdir, rename, upload, download; backup.schedule. create, update, delete, enable, disable, run; config.snapshot. create, delete, restore; config.snapshot.schedule. create, update, delete, enable, disable; audit.purge. Filter with the full name, e.g. mcctl audit list --action player.ban.

Q: Where is the audit database stored? A: SQLite database at ~/minecraft-servers/data/audit.db using WAL mode for concurrent read/write.

docs.title: Docker / Infrastructure
docs.text:
Q: Can I run mcctl on Windows? A: Only through WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux). Native Windows is not supported.

Q: Can I run mcctl on macOS? A: Yes. Docker Desktop for Mac is required. mDNS works natively via Bonjour.

Q: How do I use mcctl with Docker Desktop? A: Docker Desktop provides Docker Engine and Docker Compose. After installing Docker Desktop, mcctl works normally.

Q: Can I use Podman instead of Docker? A: Not officially supported. mcctl relies on Docker Compose and Docker socket for mc-router auto-discovery.

Q: How do I check Docker Compose version? A: Run docker compose version. mcctl requires version >= 2.20.0 for the include feature.

Q: What is the include feature in Docker Compose? A: Docker Compose include allows composing multiple compose files together. mcctl uses this to include per-server compose files from the main docker-compose.yml.

docs.title: Networking
docs.text:
Q: Can friends outside my network connect? A: Yes, via playit.gg (mcctl playit), a VPN (Tailscale, ZeroTier) with the VPN IP in HOST_IPS, or port forwarding.

Q: How does Tailscale/ZeroTier work with mcctl? A: Run mcctl init --reconfigure, choose "Host IP(s)", select the LAN and VPN addresses (written to HOST_IPS), answer yes to updating existing servers, then recreate each server (mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s>). Friends connect via server.<vpn-ip>.nip.io:25565.

Q: Can I use a custom domain instead of nip.io? A: Yes. Point your domain's DNS A record to the server IP, then add the domain as a custom hostname: web console > server > Hostnames / Domains > Custom Domains, or routing.customHostnames in servers/<name>/server.yaml followed by mcctl migrate spec <name>. Recreate the container to apply (mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s>).

Q: Why is nip.io recommended over mDNS? A: nip.io works everywhere without client setup. mDNS requires avahi-daemon (Linux) or Bonjour (macOS/Windows) on both server and client.

Q: Can I have a default server (no hostname needed)? A: mcctl configures none, so a client that sends a hostname without a route (or a bare IP) gets no server. mc-router (1.47.1) has two options: the DEFAULT environment variable (flag -default, the host:port of the server used when no mapping matches), for example DEFAULT: "mc-survival:25565" in the router environment: of <root>/docker-compose.yml followed by mcctl router start; or the container label mc-router.default: "true" on one server, which still needs its mc-router.host label. mcctl renders the server labels from server.yaml, which has no field for this one, so a hand-added mc-router.default label is dropped the next time mcctl changes that server.

docs.title: External Access (playit.gg)
docs.text:
Q: What is playit.gg? A: A free tunneling service that lets external players connect to your server without port forwarding or a static IP.

Q: How do I set up playit.gg? A: Run mcctl playit setup with your SECRET_KEY (skip it if you enabled playit in mcctl init), then mcctl playit start, create a tunnel at playit.gg, register it with mcctl playit domain <server> <domain>, and recreate the server (mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s>). Turn on the whitelist before sharing the domain.

Q: Can multiple servers use playit.gg? A: Yes. Each server needs its own tunnel domain. mc-router routes connections to the correct server based on hostname.

Q: Is playit.gg free? A: Yes, the basic plan is free and supports Minecraft Java tunneling. Premium plans offer custom domains and more tunnels.

Q: How do I add a playit domain to an existing server? A: mcctl playit domain <server-name> <your-playit-domain>. This sets PLAYIT_DOMAIN and the server's mc-router.host label; it applies after mcctl stop <server-name> && mcctl start <server-name> (a restart does not apply it). --remove removes it.

docs.title: Migration and Updates
docs.text:
Q: How do I update mcctl? A: mcctl update --yes updates the CLI and the installed services. To update only the CLI, use mcctl update --cli-only --yes or npm update -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl.

Q: How do I update everything (CLI + services)? A: mcctl update --yes. This updates mcctl, mcctl-api, mcctl-console, and shared packages (and pulls Docker images). --all is a deprecated alias for this default behavior.

Q: Do I need to stop servers before updating? A: No. Minecraft server containers are independent of mcctl; only Management Console services are restarted. mcctl update pulls new server images: running servers keep their image until mcctl stop <s> && mcctl start <s>, and in a terminal it offers to recreate stopped servers that still use an old image (default No).

Q: How do I migrate from an old version? A: Follow the Upgrade Runbook (docs/advanced/upgrade-runbook.md; from v2.x use upgrade-v3.sh). mcctl migrate status / mcctl migrate worlds --all move worlds out of server folders; mcctl migrate spec --all imports servers into server.yaml.

Q: What is mcctl upgrade? A: A command that appends new environment variables from the bundled .env.example to your .env (existing values are kept), sets DOCKER_GID, syncs servers/_template/, updates only the router service's image and group_add in your root docker-compose.yml (diff, confirmation, timestamped .bak), creates servers/global.env and points servers at it, moves BETTER_AUTH_* from ecosystem.config.cjs into .env, lists servers without server.yaml, and offers to delete a leftover <root>/scripts.

Q: When should I run mcctl upgrade? A: After updating mcctl to a new version via mcctl update or npm update -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl.

Q: Is mcctl upgrade safe? A: Yes. It appends new .env variables and keeps existing values (except DOCKER_GID when missing or the default, and the moved BETTER_AUTH_* keys); the root docker-compose.yml patch is limited to router.image and group_add, is backed up first, and is restored if validation fails; ecosystem.config.cjs is backed up before the auth keys move. Use --dry-run to preview changes first.

Q: What is the difference between mcctl update and mcctl upgrade? A: mcctl update updates the CLI and service packages to newer versions. mcctl upgrade updates your platform configuration files (.env, templates) to match the new version's template.

docs.title: 17. Glossary
docs.text: Term Definition mcctl Minecraft Control - the CLI management tool mcctl-api REST API service for programmatic server management (Fastify, port 5001) mcctl-console Web-based management console (Next.js, port 5000) mc-router Hostname-based connection router that directs traffic to correct servers PM2 Node.js process manager used to run Management Console services avahi-daemon Linux mDNS service for .local hostname discovery nip.io Magic DNS service that maps x.y.z.w.nip.io to IP x.y.z.w RCON Remote Console protocol for executing Minecraft server commands Paper High-performance Minecraft server fork with plugin support (recommended) Forge Original mod loader for Minecraft, supports vast mod library NeoForge Community fork of Forge (1.20.1+), increasingly popular Fabric Lightweight, modern mod loader with fast updates Modrinth Open-source mod hosting platform (default source in mcctl) CurseForge Popular mod hosting platform (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+ images) Spiget API for SpigotMC plugin resources Auto-scale mc-router feature that starts/stops servers based on player activity World assignment A world belongs to the one server whose LEVEL in config.env names it; prevents simultaneous server access to a world (replaced the former lock files) ecosystem.config.cjs PM2 configuration file generated by mcctl console init Access Mode API authentication method (internal, api-key, ip-whitelist, api-key-ip, open) BFF Backend-for-Frontend pattern used by mcctl-console to proxy mcctl-api SSE Server-Sent Events for real-time streaming (server status, audit logs) Better Auth Authentication library used by mcctl-console for session management playit.gg Free tunneling service for external access without port forwarding mcctl upgrade Platform configuration migration command (appends new .env keys, patches the router service, moves servers to servers/global.env) templateVersion Version tracking field in .mcctl.json to track which template version was last applied

docs.title: Advanced Features
docs.text: This section covers advanced configuration and features for the Docker Minecraft Server platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The platform provides several advanced features for production deployments and complex setups:

  • Networking - nip.io magic DNS, mDNS, mc-router configuration
  • External Access - playit.gg tunneling for internet-wide access without port forwarding
  • Backup - Automatic GitHub backup for world data
  • Upgrade Runbook - Release-independent procedure to upgrade every component, with post-upgrade verification
  • RCON - Remote console protocol for server administration
  • World Management - Assigning worlds to servers (one world, one server)
  • Auto-scaling - Automatic server start/stop based on player activity

docs.title: Feature Guides
docs.text:
• :material-network:{ .lg .middle } Networking

    Configure hostname routing with nip.io, mDNS, and mc-router

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Networking Guide

  • :material-earth:{ .lg .middle } External Access (playit.gg)

    Allow external players to join without port forwarding via playit.gg tunneling

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: External Access Guide

  • :material-backup-restore:{ .lg .middle } Backup

    Set up automatic GitHub backup for world data

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Backup Guide

  • :material-update:{ .lg .middle } Upgrade Runbook

    Upgrade CLI, API, Console, router, servers and maps in order, then verify

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Upgrade Runbook

  • :material-console:{ .lg .middle } RCON

    Remote console protocol for server administration

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: RCON Specification

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
1. Client connects to myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565
  2. nip.io resolves hostname to 192.168.1.100
  3. mc-router receives connection on port 25565
  4. mc-router routes based on hostname to mc-myserver container
  5. If server stopped, mc-router starts it (auto-scale-up)
  6. Server accepts connection after startup

docs.title: Auto-scaling Behavior
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    A[Player connects] --> B[mc-router]
    B --> C{Server stopped?}
    C -->|No| D[Route to server]
    C -->|Yes| E[Start server]
    E --> F[Wait DOCKER_TIMEOUT]
    F --> D
    D --> G[Player connected]

docs.title: World Assignment
docs.text:
A world is assigned to a server by the server's LEVEL in servers/<name>/config.env (legacy WORLD_NAME is read when LEVEL is unset; unset means itzg's default world). One world is used by one server, which prevents data corruption from simultaneous access. A world and its <world>_nether / <world>_the_end folders count as one world.

sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Server A
    participant W as World
    participant B as Server B

    A->>W: assign world (LEVEL=survival)
    Note over W: Used by A
    B->>W: try assign
    W--xB: DENIED
    A->>W: release (A stopped)
    Note over W: Free, A uses its own world
    B->>W: assign world (B stopped)
    Note over W: Used by B

Manage world assignments with mcctl:

# List all worlds with the servers they are assigned to
mcctl world list

# Assign a world to a stopped server (sets its LEVEL)
mcctl world assign survival myserver

# Switch the server using the world back to its own default world
mcctl world release survival
  • There is no lock file. worlds/.locks is no longer read, written or created; an existing directory is harmless and rm -rf worlds/.locks is safe.
  • Assign and release need a stopped server. Nothing is stopped automatically.
  • A server that keeps its world inside servers/<name>/data cannot get another world until mcctl migrate worlds moves it to worlds/.
  • Deleting a server frees its world for reuse. mcctl world delete refuses a world a server uses, even with --force.
  • If a server's config.env cannot be read or its LEVEL cannot be interpreted safely, every assignment change and world delete/reset is refused until it is fixed. Duplicate assignments from older installs are reported by mcctl world list, not fixed.

See World Assignment Rules for the full rules.

docs.title: JVM Optimization
docs.text:
Use Aikar's flags for optimal performance:

mcctl config myserver USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

For large servers, adjust G1GC parameters (edit config.env directly):

# In config.env
JVM_OPTS="-XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=100 -XX:G1NewSizePercent=40"

docs.title: Network Optimization
docs.text:
For high-player-count servers:

mcctl config myserver NETWORK_COMPRESSION_THRESHOLD 256
mcctl config myserver VIEW_DISTANCE 8
mcctl config myserver SIMULATION_DISTANCE 6

docs.title: Container Resources
docs.text:
For Docker resource limits, edit the server's docker-compose.yml directly:

services:
  mc-myserver:
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '4'
          memory: 8G
        reservations:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 4G

Then restart:

mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

Hand-edited compose files

servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml is generated from servers/<name>/server.yaml. After a hand edit like this, a later change that rewrites the file (for example an image retag by mcctl update, mcctl playit domain, hostname edits or mcctl init --reconfigure) fails with compose_edited. mcctl migrate spec <name> --force renders the file again and drops your edit, keeping a copy in docker-compose.yml.bak. See server.yaml hand edits.

docs.title: RCON Password
docs.text:
mcctl init writes a random 24-character RCON_PASSWORD to .env. Installs created before 2.32.0 may still have changeme; replace it:

RCON_PASSWORD=your-very-secure-password-here

Servers get it through servers/global.env when their container is created, so recreate each server's container:

mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver                          # a running server
cd ~/minecraft-servers && docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-otherserver   # a stopped server, left stopped

mcctl down && mcctl up also applies it, but mcctl up starts every server.

docs.title: Whitelist
docs.text:
Enable whitelist for private servers:

mcctl whitelist myserver on
mcctl whitelist myserver add Steve
mcctl whitelist myserver add Alex
mcctl whitelist myserver status

docs.title: Online Mode
docs.text:
Keep online mode enabled unless you specifically need offline:

mcctl config myserver ONLINE_MODE true

docs.title: Server Status
docs.text:
# Basic status
mcctl status

# Detailed status with resources
mcctl status --detail

# Real-time monitoring
mcctl status --watch

# JSON output for scripting
mcctl status --json

docs.title: Server Logs
docs.text:
# View recent logs
mcctl logs myserver

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl logs myserver -f

# View last N lines
mcctl logs myserver -n 100

docs.title: Resource Usage
docs.text:
# Check specific server
mcctl status myserver

# Output includes:
#   Resources: 3.1 GB / 8.0 GB (38.8%) | CPU: 15.2%
#   Players:   2/20 - Steve, Alex

docs.title: Online Players
docs.text:
# Single server
mcctl player online myserver

# All servers
mcctl player online --all

docs.text:

mcctl status --detail

# Check router health
mcctl status router

# Check specific server logs
mcctl logs myserver -n 100

# Test RCON connection
mcctl console myserver

docs.title: Backup Guide
docs.text: Set up automatic world data backup to a private GitHub repository.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The backup system provides:

  • Git-based backup - Full version history of world data
  • GitHub integration - Secure storage in a private repository
  • Interactive and CLI modes - Flexible backup management
  • Restore capability - Roll back to any previous backup

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• GitHub account
  • Private repository for backups
  • Personal Access Token with repo scope
  • git 2.31 or newer on the host (git --version); older git is refused with a clear error

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Private Repository
docs.text:
1. Go to github.com/new
  2. Enter repository name (e.g., minecraft-worlds-backup)
  3. Select Private
  4. Click Create repository

docs.title: Step 2: Create a Personal Access Token
docs.text:
1. Go to GitHub Settings > Developer settings > Personal access tokens
  2. Click Generate new token (classic)
  3. Give it a descriptive name (e.g., "Minecraft Backup")
  4. Select scope: repo (Full control of private repositories)
  5. Click Generate token
  6. Copy the token immediately - it won't be shown again!

Token Security

  • Never commit your token to version control
  • Store it only in the .env file
  • Regenerate if compromised

docs.title: Step 3: Configure Backup
docs.text:
Run mcctl backup init. It asks for the token, the repository, the branch and whether to back up when a server stops, and writes them to .env (if backup is already configured it asks before overwriting; --force skips that question).

Or edit ~/minecraft-servers/.env yourself:

# GitHub Backup Configuration
BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN=ghp_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO=yourusername/minecraft-worlds-backup
BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH=main
BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true
Variable Description Required BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN Personal Access Token Yes BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO Repository as username/repo Yes BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH Target branch No (default: main) BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP Auto backup on server stop No (default: false)

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Configuration
docs.text:
mcctl backup status

Expected output:

Backup Configuration:

  Status: Configured
  Repository: yourusername/minecraft-worlds-backup
  Branch: main
  Auto backup: enabled

docs.title: Interactive Mode
docs.text:
mcctl backup push

You'll be prompted to enter a commit message.

docs.title: CLI Mode
docs.text:
mcctl backup push -m "Before server upgrade"
mcctl backup push -m "Weekly backup"

docs.title: View Backup History
docs.text:
mcctl backup history

Output:

Backup History:

  abc1234  Before server upgrade    2024-01-15
  def5678  Weekly backup            2024-01-08
  ghi9012  Initial backup           2024-01-01

JSON output for scripting:

mcctl backup history --json

docs.title: Interactive Mode
docs.text:
mcctl backup restore

Shows a list of backups to choose from.

docs.title: CLI Mode
docs.text:
mcctl backup restore abc1234          # asks for confirmation
mcctl backup restore abc1234 --force  # no prompt (scripts)

Restore rules:

  • Stop every server first. Restore is refused while any server is running, and when Docker cannot be queried.
  • The result is exactly the backup commit: files added after that commit are removed, not mixed in.
  • worlds/.locks is never touched.
  • Server-internal worlds (servers/<name>/data/<LEVEL>) are restored only for servers in the commit. A server whose current LEVEL differs from the world in the commit is refused (restore_conflict).
  • The data that was replaced is kept in ~/minecraft-servers/backups/restore-previous/<timestamp>/. The three newest are kept; older ones are deleted after a successful restore.

Auto-scale during restore

mc-router can start a server when a player connects. Restore checks for running servers twice, but a server that starts between the last check and the end of the restore is not prevented. Stop mc-router (or make sure no one connects) before restoring.

Data Overwrite Warning

Restore replaces the current world data. Consider backing up first: 

mcctl backup push -m "Backup before restore"
mcctl backup restore abc1234

docs.title: On Server Stop
docs.text:
Enable automatic backup when servers stop:

# .env
BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true

mcctl stop <server>, and a stop from the web console or the API, back up after the server has stopped, like mcctl backup push --auto: no prompt, and a wait of up to 10 minutes when another backup is running. A failed backup is a warning (CLI) or a log entry (API); it never fails the stop. The API runs it in the background, so the stop request returns first; when mcctl-api shuts down it waits for a running backup, and after 90 seconds aborts it so auto-save is turned back on (save-on) before it exits (2 minutes at most in all). Installs set up with mcctl console init before this release need kill_timeout in ecosystem.config.cjs for that wait (Upgrade runbook, step 4-2). mcctl stop --all does not back up.

docs.title: Scheduled Backups
docs.text:
Use mcctl backup schedule add (or the web console) for scheduled backups with a retention policy, for example mcctl backup schedule add --cron daily --name nightly --max-count 7. Commands: mcctl backup schedule.

The schedules run inside mcctl-api, so the web console services must be set up (mcctl console init) and running. Changes made in the web console apply at once; mcctl-api checks the schedules every minute, so a change made with the CLI applies within a minute.

Without mcctl-api, use a plain cron job:

# Daily backup at 4 AM (--auto: no prompt, waits for a running backup)
0 4 * * * /usr/local/bin/mcctl backup push --auto

docs.title: What Gets Backed Up
docs.text:
• The whole worlds/ directory, except worlds/.locks
  • Server-internal worlds: servers/<name>/data/<LEVEL> (with <LEVEL>_nether and <LEVEL>_the_end when present) for servers whose world is not in worlds/

Running servers are flushed before the copy: save-off, save-all flush, copy, then save-on. save-on is sent even when the backup fails. If a running server does not answer RCON, the backup fails instead of copying a world that is being written.

When nothing changed since the last backup, the backup succeeds with "No changes to backup".

docs.title: Excluded from Backup
docs.text:
• Server configuration files (servers/*/config.env, compose files)
  • Plugins/mods (shared/*)
  • Container data (logs, temp files)

Backup Server Config Separately

Use mcctl to backup server configurations: 

mcctl server-backup myserver
mcctl server-backup myserver --list
mcctl server-restore myserver

docs.title: Deleted Worlds
docs.text:
If a world that is in the last backup is missing, the backup stops instead of recording the deletion (a missing mount would otherwise delete every world from the backup). If you deleted the world on purpose, consent once:

mcctl backup push --allow-missing

In the web console, check Remove worlds I deleted on purpose in the push dialog. Scheduled backups never pass this flag; their failure message names the command. Deleting a whole servers/<name>/ directory counts as intentional.

docs.title: Repository Structure
docs.text:
minecraft-worlds-backup/
├── README.md                 # Auto-generated
├── worlds/
│   ├── survival/
│   └── creative/
└── servers/
    └── myserver/
        ├── world/            # server-internal world
        └── world_nether/

The local working copy is ~/minecraft-servers/backups/worlds. Do not edit it by hand.

docs.title: Repository Size
docs.text:
GitHub has the following limits for repositories:

Limit Value Recommended max size 1 GB Hard limit 5 GB Individual file limit 100 MB

For larger worlds, consider:

  • Using Git LFS for large files
  • Compressing backups
  • Using alternative storage (S3, Backblaze)

docs.title: Reducing Backup Size
docs.text:
# Check world sizes
du -sh ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/*

# Output:
# 256M  ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/survival
# 128M  ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/creative

docs.title: Authentication Failed
docs.text:
Error: Authentication failed
  1. Verify token has repo scope
  2. Check token hasn't expired
  3. Regenerate token if needed

docs.title: Repository Not Found
docs.text:
Error: Repository not found
  1. Check repository name spelling
  2. Verify repository is private (not public)
  3. Ensure token has access to the repository

docs.title: Another Backup Is Running
docs.text:
Error: Another backup operation is running (push, pid 1234 on host, since ...)

Push, restore and retention pruning share one lock, ~/minecraft-servers/backups/.backup.lock. If no backup is running (for example after a crash on another host), check that the listed process is gone and delete the file.

docs.title: Worlds Missing From the Source
docs.text: See Deleted Worlds: use mcctl backup push --allow-missing only when the deletion was intended.

docs.title: Stop the Running Servers
docs.text: Restore is refused while servers run. Stop them (mcctl stop <server>) and retry.

docs.title: A Restore Did Not Finish
docs.text:
Error: A restore did not finish; recover manually from .../backups/restore-previous/<timestamp>

A restore failed and could not be fully rolled back. Every later push and restore is blocked until you recover:

  1. Open backups/restore-previous/<timestamp>/INCOMPLETE. It lists each target (live) and where its previous data was kept (previous).
  2. For each target, move the previous path back to live if live is missing or wrong. Data that the restore had already moved in is under .new/.
  3. Delete the INCOMPLETE file.

docs.title: Unsupported Layout
docs.text:
unsupported_layout means one of:

  • A world contains a symbolic link (symlinks are not backed up or restored).
  • worlds/, servers/<name>/ and backups/ are on different filesystems (restore moves directories and needs them on one filesystem).

docs.title: Old worlds.bak.<timestamp> Directories
docs.text:
Earlier versions left worlds.bak.<timestamp> copies next to worlds/ on every restore. They are no longer created. Delete them by hand when you no longer need them:

ls -d ~/minecraft-servers/worlds.bak.*
rm -rf ~/minecraft-servers/worlds.bak.<timestamp>

docs.title: Large File Error
docs.text:
Error: File exceeds 100MB limit

Use Git LFS for large files:

cd ~/minecraft-servers/backups/worlds
git lfs install
git lfs track "*.dat"
git lfs track "*.mca"
git add .gitattributes
git commit -m "Enable Git LFS"

docs.title: Local Backup
docs.text:
# Simple tar backup
tar -czvf backup-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/

# With rsync
rsync -av ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/ /backup/minecraft/worlds/

Worlds are a host directory bind-mounted into the servers, not a Docker volume. Stop the servers before copying, so no world is written during the copy.

docs.title: Cloud Storage
docs.text:
# AWS S3
aws s3 sync ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/ s3://my-bucket/minecraft/

# Backblaze B2
b2 sync ~/minecraft-servers/worlds/ b2://my-bucket/minecraft/

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Regular backups - Daily automatic + manual before changes
  2. Test restores - Periodically verify backups work
  3. Multiple destinations - GitHub + local/cloud backup
  4. Document changes - Use meaningful commit messages
  5. Monitor size - Watch repository growth

docs.title: See Also
docs.text:
• CLI Commands - All backup commands
  • Quick Start - Basic setup
  • GitHub Docs: Personal Access Tokens

docs.title: External Access with playit.gg
docs.text: Allow external players to join your Minecraft servers without port forwarding, firewall changes, or a static IP address using playit.gg tunneling.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: By default, servers created with mcctl are accessible only on your local network (via nip.io or mDNS). playit.gg provides a free tunneling service that gives your server a public domain name, allowing anyone on the internet to connect.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
External Players (Internet)
        |
  playit.gg cloud
  (TCP tunnel relay)
        |
  playit-agent container
  (network_mode: host)
        |
  forwards to localhost:25565
        |
  mc-router (:25565)
  reads hostname from Minecraft handshake
        |
   +----+----+
   |         |
 mc-aa    mc-bb
  1. External players connect to your playit.gg domain (e.g., xx-xx.craft.playit.gg)
  2. playit.gg cloud relays the TCP connection to the playit-agent running on your host
  3. playit-agent forwards traffic to localhost:25565 where mc-router listens
  4. mc-router reads the hostname from the Minecraft handshake packet and routes to the correct server

docs.title: What playit.gg Provides
docs.text:
Feature Free Tier Premium TCP tunnels Unlimited Unlimited Domain xx-xx.craft.playit.gg Custom domain support Bandwidth Unlimited Unlimited Players No limit No limit Regions Auto-selected Selectable

playit.gg vs Other Tunneling Solutions

playit.gg is specifically designed for game server tunneling and supports raw TCP passthrough, which is required for Minecraft's protocol. Generic HTTP tunnels (ngrok, Cloudflare Tunnels) do not work with Minecraft.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before setting up external access, ensure you have:

  • [x] mcctl installed and platform initialized (mcctl init)
  • [x] At least one Minecraft server created (mcctl create)
  • [x] Docker running
  • [x] A playit.gg account (free)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Set up external access in 6 steps:

# 1. Create a playit.gg agent and get your SECRET_KEY
#    Visit: https://playit.gg/account/agents/new-docker

# 2. Configure playit.gg in your platform
mcctl playit setup
# Enter your SECRET_KEY when prompted

# 3. Start the playit-agent
mcctl playit start

# 4. Create a Minecraft Java tunnel in the playit.gg dashboard
#    Visit: https://playit.gg/account/tunnels
#    - Click "Add Tunnel"
#    - Select "Minecraft Java"
#    - Local Address: localhost:25565
#    - Save and note the assigned domain (e.g., xx-xx.craft.playit.gg)

# 5. Register the playit domain with your server
mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --playit-domain xx-xx.craft.playit.gg
# Or for an existing server (then stop and start it):
# mcctl playit domain myserver xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

# 6. Share your domain with friends!
#    They connect to: xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

docs.title: Step 1: Create a playit.gg Agent
docs.text:
1. Go to playit.gg and sign up for a free account
  2. Navigate to Account > Agents > New Docker Agent
  3. Name your agent (e.g., "minecraft-host")
  4. Copy the SECRET_KEY displayed on the page

Keep Your SECRET_KEY Safe

The SECRET_KEY is shown only once. Save it in a secure location. If lost, you must create a new agent.

docs.title: Step 2: Configure playit.gg in mcctl
docs.text:
You can configure playit.gg during initial platform setup or afterwards.

During mcctl initAfter Platform SetupSkip playit.gg 
# With the --playit-key flag
mcctl init --playit-key YOUR_SECRET_KEY

# Or interactively (you will be prompted)
mcctl init
# When asked "Enable playit.gg tunneling?", select Yes
# Enter your SECRET_KEY when prompted

# Then add the playit-agent service (enter the SECRET_KEY again)
mcctl playit setup

# Run the playit setup command
mcctl playit setup
# Enter your SECRET_KEY when prompted

# Explicitly disable during init
mcctl init --no-playit

mcctl playit setup saves PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY to your .env file, sets playitEnabled in .mcctl.json, and adds the playit service (Compose profile playit) to docker-compose.yml, which mcctl playit start needs.

docs.title: Step 3: Start the playit-agent
docs.text:
mcctl playit start

Verify the agent is running:

mcctl playit status

Expected output:

=== playit.gg Agent Status ===

  Agent:      running
  SECRET_KEY: configured ✓

REGISTERED SERVERS

  No servers with playit.gg domains configured

  Dashboard: https://playit.gg/account/tunnels

docs.title: Step 4: Create a Minecraft Java Tunnel
docs.text:
1. Go to playit.gg Dashboard
  2. Click Add Tunnel
  3. Select Minecraft Java as the tunnel type
  4. Set Local Address to localhost:25565
  5. Click Create
  6. Note the assigned domain (e.g., xx-xx.craft.playit.gg)

One Tunnel for All Servers

You only need one playit.gg tunnel pointing to localhost:25565. mc-router handles routing to the correct server based on the hostname in the Minecraft handshake.

However, for multiple servers to be independently accessible from external players, each server needs its own playit.gg tunnel and domain.

docs.title: Step 5: Register the Domain with Your Server
docs.text:
New ServerExisting Server 
# Create a server with playit domain
mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --playit-domain xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

Register the domain with mcctl playit domain. It sets PLAYIT_DOMAIN for the server and adds the domain to its mc-router.host label:

mcctl playit domain myserver xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

Then recreate the container (a restart does not apply hostnames):

mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver   # or `mcctl start myserver` if it is stopped

Run mcctl playit domain without arguments to pick the server and type the domain, or mcctl playit domain myserver --remove to remove it. A domain added to the label by hand counts as a custom hostname, so mcctl playit status and the web console do not show it as the external address.

docs.title: Step 6: Connect and Share
docs.text:
External players can now connect to your server using the playit.gg domain:

Server Address: xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

No port number is needed since playit.gg maps to the standard Minecraft port (25565).

LAN players can still use the original addresses:

LAN: myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565
External: xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

docs.title: Custom Domain Setup (Premium)
docs.text: With a playit.gg premium plan or a domain you own, you can configure a custom domain for your server.

docs.title: DNS Configuration
docs.text:
You have two options for DNS records:

A/CNAME RecordSRV Record

Point your domain directly to the playit.gg tunnel:

# A record (if playit provides an IP)
minecraft.example.com    A      <playit-tunnel-ip>

# CNAME record (if playit provides a domain)
minecraft.example.com    CNAME  xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

Players connect with: minecraft.example.com

Use an SRV record to specify a non-standard port or add a subdomain:

_minecraft._tcp.mc.example.com    SRV    0 5 <port> xx-xx.craft.playit.gg

Players connect with: mc.example.com

SRV Record Fields

Field Value Description Service _minecraft Service identifier Protocol _tcp Minecraft uses TCP Priority 0 Lowest priority wins Weight 5 Load balancing weight Port <port> The port assigned by playit.gg Target xx-xx.craft.playit.gg playit.gg tunnel domain

docs.title: A/CNAME vs SRV Comparison
docs.text: Feature A/CNAME SRV Setup complexity Simple Moderate Custom port No (must be 25565) Yes Subdomain support Direct Via service record Client compatibility All clients Most clients (some older launchers may not support SRV) TTL propagation Fast May take longer

docs.title: Update mc-router Label
docs.text:
After configuring your custom domain, register it as the server's playit domain, then recreate the container:

mcctl playit domain myserver minecraft.example.com
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

To keep the xx-xx.craft.playit.gg domain as well, add the custom domain as a custom hostname instead: web console > server > Options > Hostnames / Domains > Custom Domains, or routing.customHostnames in servers/myserver/server.yaml followed by mcctl migrate spec myserver.

docs.title: CLI Commands
docs.text:
Command reference: mcctl playit.

Command Description mcctl playit start Start the playit-agent container mcctl playit stop Stop the playit-agent container mcctl playit status Show agent status and registered servers mcctl playit setup Configure or reconfigure SECRET_KEY and add the playit service mcctl playit domain <server> [domain] Set a server's playit.gg domain (--remove removes it; no arguments: prompts)

docs.title: Checking Status
docs.text:
mcctl playit status

Output with registered servers:

=== playit.gg Agent Status ===

  Agent:      running
  SECRET_KEY: configured ✓
  Uptime:     2d 5h 30m

REGISTERED SERVERS

  SERVER              EXTERNAL DOMAIN
  ------              ---------------
  myserver            xx-xx.craft.playit.gg
  creative            yy-yy.craft.playit.gg

  Dashboard: https://playit.gg/account/tunnels

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
For scripting and automation:

mcctl playit status --json

{
  "agentStatus": "running",
  "agentRunning": true,
  "secretKeyConfigured": true,
  "enabled": true,
  "uptime": "2d 5h 30m",
  "servers": [
    {
      "serverName": "myserver",
      "playitDomain": "xx-xx.craft.playit.gg"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Web Console Management
docs.text: If you have the Management Console set up, you can monitor and control playit.gg from the web interface.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
The main dashboard shows playit.gg status alongside other platform information. The PlayitSummaryCard displays:

  • Agent running/stopped status
  • Number of servers with playit.gg domains
  • Quick link to the playit.gg dashboard

docs.title: Server Detail Page
docs.text:
Each server's detail page includes a ConnectionInfoCard that shows:

  • LAN connection address (nip.io/mDNS)
  • External connection address (playit.gg domain, if configured)
  • Connection status indicators

docs.title: Routing Page
docs.text:
The routing page shows the PlayitSection with:

  • Agent status and uptime
  • All registered servers and their external domains
  • Start/stop controls for the playit-agent

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text:
The Management Console API provides these playit.gg endpoints:

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/playit/status Get agent status and server domains POST /api/playit/start Start the playit-agent POST /api/playit/stop Stop the playit-agent

docs.title: Agent Won't Start
docs.text:
1. Check SECRET_KEY is configured: 

    mcctl playit status
# SECRET_KEY should show "configured"

  2. Verify Docker is running: 

    docker ps

  3. Check agent logs: 

    docker logs playit-agent

  4. Reconfigure if needed (also when mcctl playit start reports no such service: playit): 

    mcctl playit setup   # adds the playit service to docker-compose.yml if it is missing

docs.title: External Players Can't Connect
docs.text:
1. Verify the agent is running: 

    mcctl playit status
# Agent should show "running"

  2. Check the tunnel exists in the playit.gg dashboard:

  3. Visit https://playit.gg/account/tunnels

  4. Ensure a Minecraft Java tunnel exists with localhost:25565

  5. Verify mc-router.host label includes the playit domain: 

    docker inspect mc-myserver | grep mc-router.host
# Should include the playit.gg domain

  6. Test local connection first: 

    # If LAN connection works but external doesn't, the issue is in the tunnel
mcctl status myserver

  7. Check mc-router logs: 

    mcctl logs router -n 200 | grep playit

docs.title: Connection Timeout
docs.text:
• The playit.gg agent needs a few seconds to establish the tunnel after starting
  • Wait 10-15 seconds after mcctl playit start before testing
  • Check your internet connection on the host machine

docs.title: Domain Not Resolving
docs.text:
• Ensure the tunnel is active in the playit.gg dashboard
  • For custom domains, verify DNS records have propagated: 
    nslookup minecraft.example.com
# or
dig minecraft.example.com
  • DNS propagation can take up to 48 hours for new records

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
Security Considerations

Opening your server to the internet exposes it to potential abuse. Follow these practices to stay safe.

docs.title: Enable Whitelist
docs.text:
New servers have the whitelist off unless it was turned on at creation (for example mcctl create --enable-whitelist), so anyone with the domain can join until you turn it on. Restrict who can join your server:

mcctl whitelist myserver on
mcctl whitelist myserver add TrustedPlayer1
mcctl whitelist myserver add TrustedPlayer2

docs.title: Keep Online Mode Enabled
docs.text:
Online mode verifies player identities through Mojang servers:

mcctl config myserver ONLINE_MODE true

Never Disable Online Mode on Public Servers

Disabling online mode (ONLINE_MODE=false) allows anyone to join with any username, including impersonating administrators.

docs.title: Change Default RCON Password
docs.text:
mcctl init generates a random RCON password. Installs created before 2.32.0 may still use changeme; replace it, then recreate each server's container (see RCON Password):

# In ~/minecraft-servers/.env
RCON_PASSWORD=a-very-secure-random-password

docs.title: Monitor Server Activity
docs.text:
# Check who is online
mcctl player online myserver

# View server logs for suspicious activity
mcctl logs myserver -f

# Review audit logs
mcctl audit list --limit 20

docs.title: Protect Your SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
• Never share your playit.gg SECRET_KEY publicly
  • The key is stored in ~/minecraft-servers/.env which is gitignored by default
  • If compromised, revoke the agent in the playit.gg dashboard and create a new one

docs.title: Free Tier Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Details Domain name Auto-assigned (e.g., xx-xx.craft.playit.gg) Region selection Automatic (nearest region) Custom domains Not available Priority routing Standard

docs.title: Technical Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Details Latency Adds ~10-50ms depending on region and distance Protocol TCP only (sufficient for Minecraft) Bedrock Edition Not supported by this setup (Java Edition only) network_mode playit-agent uses host mode (required for localhost forwarding)

docs.title: Comparison with Other Solutions
docs.text:
Solution Port Forwarding Setup Difficulty Latency Cost playit.gg Not needed Easy Low-Medium Free Tailscale/ZeroTier Not needed Medium Low Free (limited) Port Forwarding Required Medium None Free Cloud Hosting Not needed Complex Varies Paid

When to Use playit.gg vs VPN Mesh

  • playit.gg: Best for public or semi-public servers where you want anyone with the domain to connect
  • Tailscale/ZeroTier: Best for private servers with a fixed group of trusted friends (see Networking Guide)

docs.title: Docker Configuration Reference
docs.text:
mcctl playit setup adds the playit-agent to your platform's docker-compose.yml with a Docker Compose profile:

services:
  playit:
    image: ghcr.io/playit-cloud/playit-agent:0.16
    container_name: playit-agent
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - SECRET_KEY=${PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY:?PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY must be set in .env}
    restart: unless-stopped
    profiles:
      - playit

Key points:

  • network_mode: host: Required so the agent can forward to localhost:25565 where mc-router listens
  • profiles: [playit]: The agent only starts when explicitly activated (via mcctl playit start or docker compose --profile playit up -d)
  • image: ghcr.io/playit-cloud/playit-agent:0.16: Pinned to version 0.16 for stability

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Required Description PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY Yes (if enabled) Agent authentication key from playit.gg PLAYIT_DOMAIN No Per server, in servers/<name>/config.env (set by --playit-domain or mcctl playit domain): the playit.gg domain added to the server's router hostnames

docs.text:
