  • Quick Start - Basic server setup
  • CLI Commands - Full command reference
  • Management Console - Web-based server management
  • playit.gg Documentation - Official playit.gg documentation

docs.title: Networking Guide
docs.text: Configure hostname-based routing for your Minecraft servers using nip.io, mDNS, and mc-router.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The platform supports these hostname methods:

Method URL Example Client Setup Reachable From nip.io (Recommended) myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565 None Networks that can reach the IP in the name (LAN, VPN) mDNS myserver.local:25565 avahi/Bonjour LAN only

mc-router picks the server by the hostname the client sends, so a bare IP such as 192.168.1.100:25565 does not reach a server. For access from the internet, see External Access.

docs.title: nip.io Magic DNS
docs.text:
Recommended for all users.

nip.io is a magic DNS service that automatically resolves hostnames containing IP addresses:

myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io → 192.168.1.100
creative.192.168.1.100.nip.io → 192.168.1.100
modded.192.168.1.100.nip.io   → 192.168.1.100

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Client connects to myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565
  2. DNS query goes to nip.io service
  3. nip.io extracts 192.168.1.100 from hostname
  4. Returns 192.168.1.100 as the IP address
  5. Client connects to 192.168.1.100:25565
  6. mc-router receives connection with hostname myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io
  7. mc-router routes to the correct server based on hostname

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Set your host IP in .env:

# ~/minecraft-servers/.env
HOST_IP=192.168.1.100

When you create a server, mcctl puts both hostnames in its mc-router.host label:

  • myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565 (nip.io, one per address in HOST_IPS, else HOST_IP)
  • myserver.local:25565 (mDNS)

mcctl status shows them in the HOSTNAME column.

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
• No client configuration - Works immediately
  • Works across your networks - From any network that can reach the IP in the name, such as your LAN or a VPN address in HOST_IPS
  • Simple setup - Just set HOST_IP in .env
  • Multiple servers - Each server gets a unique hostname

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Internet access for DNS resolution
  • HOST_IP correctly set in .env
  • mc-router must be running

docs.title: mDNS (Multicast DNS)
docs.text: mDNS allows .local hostnames to work on local networks.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. avahi-daemon broadcasts hostname on local network
  2. Clients with mDNS support discover the hostname
  3. No manual /etc/hosts configuration needed

docs.title: Install avahi-daemon
docs.text:
Ubuntu/DebianCentOS/RHELArch Linux 
sudo apt install avahi-daemon
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

sudo dnf install avahi
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

sudo pacman -S avahi nss-mdns
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

docs.title: Register Hostnames
docs.text:
mcctl create registers <name>.local when avahi-daemon is installed. It appends <ip> <name>.local to /etc/avahi/hosts and restarts avahi-daemon with sudo, using the first host address (HOST_IPS, else HOST_IP; IPv4 only):

  • It asks for your sudo password when /etc/avahi/hosts exists. For scripts, pass --sudo-password or set MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD. Press Enter to try sudo without a password.

  • For passwordless operation, allow the commands mcctl runs, for example in /etc/sudoers.d/mcctl:

    %docker ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/tee -a /etc/avahi/hosts
%docker ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/sed -i * /etc/avahi/hosts
%docker ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /usr/bin/systemctl restart avahi-daemon

  • If sudo fails, the server is still created and mcctl prints a warning; add the line by hand (below).

  • mcctl delete removes the <name>.local line the same way.

Manual registration:

# Add entry
echo "192.168.1.100 myserver.local" | sudo tee -a /etc/avahi/hosts

# Restart avahi
sudo systemctl restart avahi-daemon

docs.title: Client Setup
docs.text: OS Setup Required Linux Install avahi-daemon (usually pre-installed) macOS None (Bonjour built-in) Windows Install Bonjour (iTunes or Bonjour Print Services)

docs.title: Windows Client
docs.text:
1. Download Bonjour Print Services
  2. Install and restart
  3. .local hostnames will resolve

docs.title: Linux Client
docs.text:
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install avahi-daemon libnss-mdns

# Verify nss-mdns is configured
grep mdns /etc/nsswitch.conf
# Should show: hosts: files mdns4_minimal [NOTFOUND=return] dns

docs.title: Troubleshooting mDNS
docs.text:
# Check if avahi is running
systemctl status avahi-daemon

# List registered hostnames
cat /etc/avahi/hosts

# Test resolution
avahi-resolve -n myserver.local

# Check network interface
avahi-daemon --check

docs.title: mc-router Configuration
docs.text:
mc-router handles hostname-based routing and auto-scaling.

Pinned version

The platform pins itzg/mc-router to 1.47.1 in docker-compose.yml for reproducible deployments. Compared to 1.42.0, this release adds event-based Docker polling (faster auto-scale reactions), timezone (TZ) support, and a --log-level option. There are no breaking changes, and the label-based --in-docker auto-scale workflow used here needs no configuration changes.

Since 1.46, mc-router runs as a non-root user. The compose file adds the Docker socket's group via group_add: ["${DOCKER_GID:-999}"]; mcctl init/mcctl upgrade detect and write DOCKER_GID to .env.

docs.title: Router Management with mcctl
docs.text:
# Check router status
mcctl status router

# Start router (also recreates it after docker-compose.yml changes)
mcctl router start

# Restart the running container (keeps its current settings)
mcctl router restart

# Stop router
mcctl router stop

docs.title: Docker Labels
docs.text:
Each server uses Docker labels for mc-router discovery. These are automatically configured by mcctl create:

# servers/myserver/docker-compose.yml (auto-generated)
services:
  mc-myserver:
    labels:
      mc-router.host: "myserver.local,myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io"

docs.title: Auto-scaling Settings
docs.text:
mc-router's settings are in the router service of ~/minecraft-servers/docker-compose.yml, not in .env:

services:
  router:
    environment:
      IN_DOCKER: "true"
      AUTO_SCALE_UP: "true"          # Start servers on connect
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN: "true"        # Stop idle servers (see note)
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER: "10m"   # Idle time before a server is stopped
      DOCKER_TIMEOUT: "120s"         # Wait time (Go time.Duration: 120s, 2m; bare integers fail)

After editing, recreate the router (mcctl router restart keeps the old settings):

mcctl router start

mcctl upgrade changes only the router image and group_add, so your edits stay.

To turn auto-scaling off for one server, set routing.autoScale.up or routing.autoScale.down to false in servers/<name>/server.yaml, run mcctl migrate spec <name>, then recreate its container: mcctl stop <name> && mcctl start <name> when it runs, mcctl start <name> when it is stopped. These become the server's mc-router.auto-scale-up / mc-router.auto-scale-down labels.

AUTO_SCALE_DOWN

Auto scale down is fully enabled and supported since mc-router v1.39.1. Servers will automatically stop after the configured idle timeout (default: 10 minutes). The race condition that previously caused player disconnections has been fixed. See mc-router #507 for details.

docs.title: Multiple Hostnames
docs.text:
To allow connections from multiple networks (LAN + VPN), configure multiple IPs:

# ~/minecraft-servers/.env
HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5

This creates hostnames for each IP: - myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io (LAN) - myserver.100.64.0.5.nip.io (VPN)

HOST_IP vs HOST_IPS

  • HOST_IP: Single IP address (default)
  • HOST_IPS: Comma-separated multiple IPs (for VPN mesh)

When HOST_IPS is set, it takes precedence over HOST_IP.

docs.title: VPN Mesh Networks
docs.text: Using a VPN mesh like Tailscale or ZeroTier allows access to your server from anywhere.

docs.title: Why Use VPN Mesh?
docs.text: Scenario Solution Friends on different networks VPN mesh creates virtual LAN Access home server remotely VPN access without port forwarding Connect from multiple locations Multiple IPs support all networks

docs.title: Tailscale Setup
docs.text: Tailscale is a free VPN mesh service.

docs.title: 1. Install Tailscale
docs.text:
Ubuntu/DebianArch Linux 
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up

sudo pacman -S tailscale
sudo systemctl enable --now tailscaled
sudo tailscale up

docs.title: 2. Get Tailscale IP
docs.text:
tailscale ip -4
# Example: 100.64.0.5

docs.title: 3. Configure Multiple IPs in mcctl
docs.text:
# ~/minecraft-servers/.env
# LAN IP + Tailscale IP
HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5

docs.title: 4. Recreate Servers or Update Labels
docs.text:
# New servers automatically get a hostname for each IP
mcctl create myserver

# Existing servers: choose "Host IP(s)", select every address,
# and answer yes to "Update existing servers with new IP hostnames?"
mcctl init --reconfigure

# Make sure mc-router runs
mcctl router start

# Recreate each running server so its container gets the new hostnames
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

A container keeps the hostnames it was created with; a restart does not apply new ones. mcctl start <name> recreates and starts a stopped server; to recreate it and leave it stopped, run docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<name> in ~/minecraft-servers.

docs.title: 5. Client Connection
docs.text:
Have friends install Tailscale and invite them to your network, then:

# Add server in Minecraft
myserver.100.64.0.5.nip.io:25565

docs.title: ZeroTier Setup
docs.text: ZeroTier is another free VPN mesh service.

docs.title: 1. Install ZeroTier
docs.text: curl -s https://install.zerotier.com | sudo bash

docs.title: 2. Create and Join Network
docs.text:
1. Create network at my.zerotier.com
  2. Copy Network ID (e.g., 8056c2e21c000001)
  3. Join the network: 
    sudo zerotier-cli join 8056c2e21c000001

docs.title: 3. Get ZeroTier IP
docs.text:
sudo zerotier-cli listnetworks
# or
ip addr show zt*
# Example: 10.147.20.1

docs.title: 4. Configure Multiple IPs in mcctl
docs.text:
# ~/minecraft-servers/.env
HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,10.147.20.1

docs.title: Using Multiple VPNs Simultaneously
docs.text:
You can use both Tailscale and ZeroTier at the same time:

# ~/minecraft-servers/.env
# LAN + Tailscale + ZeroTier
HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5,10.147.20.1

Accessible from all networks: - myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565 (LAN) - myserver.100.64.0.5.nip.io:25565 (Tailscale) - myserver.10.147.20.1.nip.io:25565 (ZeroTier)

docs.title: VPN Mesh Troubleshooting
docs.text:
# Check Tailscale status
tailscale status

# Check ZeroTier status
sudo zerotier-cli listnetworks

# Verify hostname labels
docker inspect mc-myserver | grep mc-router.host

# Check mc-router logs for hostname
mcctl logs router -n 200 | grep myserver

When VPN IP Changes

If your VPN IP changes, run mcctl init --reconfigure, select the new IPs, accept updating existing servers, then recreate each server as in step 4. If the first address changed, also fix the <name>.local lines in /etc/avahi/hosts; mcctl does not rewrite them.

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Add DEBUG: "true" to the environment: of the router service in ~/minecraft-servers/docker-compose.yml:

services:
  router:
    environment:
      DEBUG: "true"

Then recreate the router and follow its log:

mcctl router start
mcctl logs router -f

docs.title: Docker Network
docs.text:
All Minecraft containers run on a shared Docker network. mcctl init creates it as a bridge network named minecraft-net with subnet 172.28.0.0/16, and the compose file uses it as an external network:

# docker-compose.yml
networks:
  minecraft-net:
    external: true
    name: ${MINECRAFT_NETWORK:-minecraft-net}

MINECRAFT_SUBNET in .env is not used.

docs.title: Port Mapping
docs.text:
Only mc-router exposes port 25565:

services:
  router:
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"            # Public port
      - "127.0.0.1:25580:8080"   # mc-router management API (localhost only)

Individual Minecraft servers don't expose ports - they're accessed through mc-router.

docs.title: Container Discovery
docs.text:
mc-router uses the Docker socket to discover containers:

volumes:
  - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro

docs.title: Custom Domain Setup
docs.text: For production deployments, use your own domain.

docs.title: DNS Configuration
docs.text:
Add A records pointing to your server:

survival.minecraft.example.com  A  192.168.1.100
creative.minecraft.example.com  A  192.168.1.100

docs.title: Server Configuration
docs.text:
Add the domain as a custom hostname of the server:

  • Web console: server detail > Options > Hostnames / Domains > Custom Domains, then Save
  • Or add it under routing.customHostnames in servers/survival/server.yaml and run mcctl migrate spec survival

mcctl keeps survival.local and the nip.io hostnames in the mc-router.host label next to your domain. Then recreate the container, since a restart does not apply hostnames: mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival when it runs, mcctl start survival when it is stopped.

docs.title: HTTPS/TLS
docs.text: Minecraft uses its own protocol, not HTTPS. TLS is not needed for the game connection.

docs.title: Required Ports
docs.text: Port Protocol Purpose 25565 TCP Minecraft client connections 5353 UDP mDNS (local network only)

docs.title: UFW (Ubuntu)
docs.text:
sudo ufw allow 25565/tcp comment "Minecraft"
sudo ufw allow 5353/udp comment "mDNS"

docs.title: firewalld (CentOS/RHEL)
docs.text:
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=25565/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-service=mdns
sudo firewall-cmd --reload

docs.title: Connection Refused
docs.text:
1. Check mc-router is running: 

    mcctl status router
mcctl router start   # if it is not running

  2. Check hostname is configured: 

    mcctl status myserver --detail

  3. Test DNS resolution: 

    nslookup myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io

docs.title: Server Not Starting
docs.text:
1. Check DOCKER_TIMEOUT of the router service in docker-compose.yml, then recreate the router with mcctl router start: 

    # ~/minecraft-servers/docker-compose.yml (router environment)
DOCKER_TIMEOUT: "180s"   # Increase if server takes long to start

  2. Check server logs: 

    mcctl logs myserver

docs.title: mDNS Not Working
docs.text:
1. Verify avahi is running on server
  2. Check client has mDNS support
  3. Ensure same network subnet
  4. Check firewall allows port 5353/udp

docs.title: RCON Protocol Specification
docs.text: Remote Console (RCON) is a TCP/IP-based protocol for remote server administration. Originally developed by Valve for Source engine games, it's also used by Minecraft servers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
RCON allows administrators to execute server commands remotely without direct console access. This is essential for automated server management and CLI tools like mcctl.

Security Notice

RCON transmits data unencrypted. Never expose RCON ports directly to the internet. Use RCON only within trusted networks or through secure tunnels.

docs.title: Packet Structure
docs.text:
All integers are little-endian (unlike Minecraft's main protocol which uses big-endian).

┌────────────┬────────────┬────────────┬─────────────────┬──────┐
│   Length   │ Request ID │    Type    │     Payload     │ Pad  │
│  (4 bytes) │ (4 bytes)  │ (4 bytes)  │   (variable)    │ (2)  │
│  int32 LE  │  int32 LE  │  int32 LE  │ null-terminated │ 0x00 │
└────────────┴────────────┴────────────┴─────────────────┴──────┘
Field Size Type Description Length 4 bytes int32 Length of remainder of packet (excludes this field) Request ID 4 bytes int32 Client-generated ID for matching responses Type 4 bytes int32 Packet type (see below) Payload Variable ASCII string NULL-terminated command or response Padding 2 bytes byte[2] Two NULL bytes (0x00 0x00)

docs.title: Packet Types
docs.text:
Type Value Direction Description SERVERDATA_AUTH 3 Client → Server Authentication request (password) SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE 2 Server → Client Authentication response SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND 2 Client → Server Command execution request SERVERDATA_RESPONSE_VALUE 0 Server → Client Command execution response

Type Value Overlap

Note that SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE and SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND share the same value (2). The direction of the packet determines the meaning.

docs.title: Size Limits
docs.text: Direction Max Payload Max Total Packet Client → Server 1446 bytes 1460 bytes Server → Client 4096 bytes 4110 bytes

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server

    C->>S: SERVERDATA_AUTH (password)
    S->>C: SERVERDATA_RESPONSE_VALUE (empty)
    alt Authentication Success
        S->>C: SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE (request_id matches)
    else Authentication Failed
        S->>C: SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE (request_id = -1)
    end

Authentication Request: 

Length:     14 + password_length
Request ID: client_generated_id
Type:       3 (SERVERDATA_AUTH)
Payload:    "your_password\0"
Padding:    0x00 0x00

Authentication Response (Success): 

Length:     10
Request ID: same_as_request (matches client ID)
Type:       2 (SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE)
Payload:    "\0"
Padding:    0x00 0x00

Authentication Response (Failure): 

Length:     10
Request ID: -1 (indicates failure)
Type:       2 (SERVERDATA_AUTH_RESPONSE)
Payload:    "\0"
Padding:    0x00 0x00

docs.title: Command Execution
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant S as Server

    Note over C,S: After successful authentication
    C->>S: SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND ("list")
    S->>C: SERVERDATA_RESPONSE_VALUE (result)
    Note over S,C: Large responses may be fragmented

Command Request: 

Length:     14 + command_length
Request ID: client_generated_id
Type:       2 (SERVERDATA_EXECCOMMAND)
Payload:    "list\0"
Padding:    0x00 0x00

Command Response: 

Length:     10 + response_length
Request ID: same_as_request
Type:       0 (SERVERDATA_RESPONSE_VALUE)
Payload:    "There are 2 of a max 20 players online: Steve, Alex\0"
Padding:    0x00 0x00

docs.title: Response Fragmentation
docs.text:
Large responses (>4096 bytes) are split across multiple packets. Detecting the end of a multi-packet response is challenging:

  1. Payload Size Check: If payload < 4096 bytes, it's likely the last packet
  2. Timeout: Wait for a period with no new data
  3. Dummy Packet: Send a dummy command and wait for its response

docs.title: server.properties
docs.text:
# Enable RCON
enable-rcon=true

# RCON port (default: 25575)
rcon.port=25575

# RCON password (required)
rcon.password=your_secure_password

# Broadcast RCON commands to operators (optional)
broadcast-rcon-to-ops=false

docs.title: Docker Configuration (This Project)
docs.text:
# ~/minecraft-servers/.env (passed to every server through servers/global.env)
RCON_PASSWORD=<random, generated by mcctl init>
RCON_PORT=25575

# ~/minecraft-servers/servers/<server>/config.env
ENABLE_RCON=true

A RCON_PASSWORD or RCON_PORT line in a server's config.env overrides the platform value for that server. A server gets a changed value when its container is recreated (see RCON Password).

The itzg/minecraft-server image includes rcon-cli, a built-in RCON client.

docs.title: Common RCON Commands
docs.text: RCON takes the Minecraft server commands without the leading /. For the commands you can send (players, time, weather, game rules and more), see RCON Commands.

docs.title: Using mcctl CLI
docs.text:
# Execute single command (docker exec <container> rcon-cli)
mcctl exec myserver list
mcctl exec myserver say "Server restarting in 5 minutes!"

# Interactive RCON console (TCP to the container IP; same as mcctl rcon)
mcctl console myserver

# Player management (RCON while the server runs)
mcctl whitelist myserver add Steve
mcctl op myserver add Steve
mcctl kick myserver Steve "AFK too long"
mcctl ban myserver add Griefer "Griefing"

docs.title: Using Docker Directly
docs.text:
# Single command
docker exec mc-myserver rcon-cli list

# Interactive mode
docker exec -it mc-myserver rcon-cli

# With explicit password
docker exec mc-myserver rcon-cli --password mypassword list

docs.title: Using rcon-cli Options
docs.text:
# Basic usage
rcon-cli <command>

# With host and port (for remote connections)
rcon-cli --host localhost --port 25575 --password mypassword list

# Environment variables
RCON_HOST=localhost RCON_PORT=25575 RCON_PASSWORD=mypassword rcon-cli list

docs.title: Character Encoding
docs.text:
Some servers (like CraftBukkit/Spigot) send color codes using byte 0xA7 (section sign). For better compatibility:

  • Use ISO-8859-1 (ISO-LATIN-1) charset instead of US-ASCII
  • Handle color codes (§) in responses

docs.title: Request ID Handling
docs.text:
• Generate unique request IDs for each command
  • Match responses by request ID
  • Handle request ID -1 as authentication failure

docs.title: Connection Management
docs.text:
• Keep connections open for multiple commands
  • Implement timeouts for unresponsive servers
  • Handle connection drops gracefully

docs.title: Network Security
docs.text:
1. Never expose RCON to the internet - Use only on localhost or trusted networks
  2. Use strong passwords - At least 16 characters, random
  3. Firewall rules - Block external access to RCON port
# UFW (Ubuntu)
sudo ufw deny 25575/tcp

# iptables
sudo iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 25575 -j DROP

docs.title: Docker Security
docs.text:
No server publishes its RCON port on the host. mcctl reaches RCON in two ways:

  • mcctl exec runs rcon-cli inside the container with docker exec, so it needs only access to the Docker socket.
  • mcctl console (same as mcctl rcon) connects over TCP to the container's IP address on the minecraft-net network, with the container's RCON_PASSWORD. This works on a Linux host; Docker Desktop (macOS) may not expose container IPs, so use mcctl exec there.
# No port exposure needed
services:
  mc-myserver:
    # ports:
    #   - "25575:25575"  # Don't expose RCON port

docs.title: Secure Alternatives
docs.text:
For remote administration over the internet:

  1. SSH: Log in to the host and run mcctl there 

    ssh user@server
mcctl exec myserver list

  2. VPN: Access server network through VPN

  3. Web Panel: Use a web-based management panel with HTTPS

docs.title: Connection Refused
docs.text:
# Check RCON is enabled
docker exec mc-myserver cat /data/server.properties | grep rcon

# Check container is running
docker ps | grep mc-myserver

docs.title: Authentication Failed
docs.text:
# Password the server uses (from its container)
docker exec mc-myserver printenv RCON_PASSWORD

# Platform value, passed to servers through servers/global.env
grep RCON_PASSWORD ~/minecraft-servers/.env

# Check server.properties
docker exec mc-myserver cat /data/server.properties | grep rcon.password

docs.title: Empty Response
docs.text:
Some commands return empty responses. This is normal for commands like:

  • say - Just broadcasts, no response
  • tell - Private message sent
  • whitelist add - Player added (some servers return empty)

docs.title: Timeout Issues
docs.text:
# Increase timeout in rcon-cli
rcon-cli --timeout 30 <command>

# Check server is responsive
docker logs mc-myserver --tail 50

docs.title: Upgrade Runbook (every release)
docs.text:
The same procedure for every release: upgrade the whole system (CLI, API, Console, platform config, router, servers, maps) in a fixed order. It is version-independent; only the NEW variable changes. Read the release's CHANGELOG and release notes first for release-specific notes.

Read first

  • mcctl update upgrades the packages (CLI/API/Console/shared) and pulls the server images (step 5). It does not run mcctl upgrade (.env, servers/_template, root compose router). Run mcctl upgrade separately.
  • Run every command in a shell using the same Node version PM2 uses (step 0). If they differ, the native better-sqlite3 module can hit an ABI mismatch and the Console returns 500.

docs.title: v3.0.0 upgrade script
docs.text:
For v2.x to v3.0.0, scripts/upgrade-v3.sh walks through the steps below and asks before each change. Look first, then run it:

# 1. Dry run: checks and shows the plan, changes nothing
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager/main/scripts/upgrade-v3.sh | bash -s -- --dry-run
# 2. Real run (asks before each change)
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager/main/scripts/upgrade-v3.sh | bash

To read the script before running it:

curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager/main/scripts/upgrade-v3.sh
less upgrade-v3.sh
bash upgrade-v3.sh --dry-run

It is safe to pipe into bash: questions are read from the terminal, every command it starts gets empty input, and a download cut short runs nothing. Linux and macOS (bash 3.2) are supported. Without a terminal and without --yes, steps that change something are skipped. The full output is also written to upgrade.log (in the backup folder, or in a temporary folder on a dry run).

Option Meaning --root <dir> Platform root (default $MCCTL_ROOT, else ~/minecraft-servers) --yes Do not ask; use each question's default answer --dry-run Check and show the plan; change nothing --skip-update Do not run mcctl update (CLI already updated, or a local build) --remove-scripts Delete <root>/scripts after it was backed up, without asking --help Show the options

Before the first step the script reads mcctl --version and npm view @minecraft-docker/mcctl version. If the CLI is already 3.x the update is skipped. If npm latest is not 3.x it stops (use --skip-update with a v3 build).

Step What it does Kind (default answer) 0 Pre-flight Root files, which -a mcctl and whether the first one is under npm prefix -g, PM2 vs shell Node, git 2.31 for backups, cron and timers that call scripts/*.sh or player lookup\|uuid, macOS mcctl console note automatic, read only 1 Backup Copies the files of step 1 and <root>/scripts to <root>/backups/upgrade-v3-<time>/; optional mcctl backup push optional (yes; push: no) 2 Update mcctl update --yes (also pulls server images), then checks the version is 3.x optional (yes) 3 Upgrade Shows mcctl upgrade --dry-run, then mcctl upgrade --non-interactive optional (yes) 4 <root>/scripts Keeps or removes the folder (only after the backup; a link is unlinked) optional (keep) 5 ecosystem.config.cjs Before v2.32.0, rewrites old AUTH_MODE values (4-1); adds kill_timeout to mcctl-api (4-2); then mcctl console service restart --console --force optional (AUTH_MODE: no; kill_timeout: yes if BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true; restart: yes) 6 ServerSpec Shows mcctl migrate spec --all --dry-run, optionally runs it optional (no) 7 Worlds Shows mcctl world list, highlights duplicate or warning lines automatic 7b Stopped servers Lists running servers (restart them yourself) and stopped ones already on the local image their compose service names (up to date). On yes, recreates each other stopped one with docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server>, so its next start uses the pulled image; otherwise the summary lists those commands. Without such servers it does not ask optional (no) 8 Verify mcctl --version, docker compose config -q, PM2 status, PM2's mcctl-api kill_timeout equals the one in ecosystem.config.cjs, API /health (only when ecosystem.config.cjs exists) automatic 9 Summary Result of each step, what is left (including mcctl installs still on the old version), rollback, log path automatic

If step 2 is skipped (you answer no, or there is no terminal and no --yes) or fails, the script runs no later step and stops with "The upgrade did not finish": the later steps need the v3 CLI. Fix the cause and run the script again. A failed backup or mcctl upgrade stops it the same way. Any failed step makes the exit code 1.

Step 0 also stops, before anything changes, when the update would run and the first mcctl on PATH is not under npm prefix -g: mcctl update installs with npm install -g, so it would update another install. Put the bin directory of PM2's Node first on PATH (for example nvm use 22, or the directory of interpreter in ecosystem.config.cjs) and run the script again. With --skip-update this check is skipped.

On a dry run with a v2 CLI, the mcctl upgrade --dry-run preview is the plan of the v2 CLI installed now; the v3 plan appears after the update.

Step 5 loads ecosystem.config.cjs with node (so it runs the file, like PM2 does), edits it only if the mcctl-api name: line is name: 'mcctl-api', alone on its line, loads it again to check the result and puts the original back if the check fails (no restart then). A symbolic link or a one-line app object is not edited; the script tells you what to add by hand. The restart uses --console: without --console or --api the CLI asks which services to restart, and the script gives commands no input.

Step 7b is there because mc-router starts a stopped server with docker start, which keeps the image the container was created from. Recreating keeps worlds and config (bind mounts and volumes) and leaves the server stopped, but a regression in the new image then shows on the next start, so the default is no (also with --yes). Without recreating, the summary lists docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server> for each stopped server to run in the platform directory when you are ready; until then auto-scale wakes them on the old image. After recreating, the summary prints, for each recreated server, docker tag <old image ID> <image> && docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server> to go back.

What the script does not do (the summary repeats these):

  • Restart running servers. Do it at a quiet time: mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>.
  • Replace cron jobs, timers or your own scripts that called <root>/scripts/*.sh. It only warns; use the table in 3-1.
  • Roll back. The summary prints step 8 with this run's values: the files to copy back from the backup folder (then docker compose up -d router), npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl@<old version>, npm install of the installed mcctl-api, mcctl-console and shared at the old version in .services/ (or the root on older installs), and mcctl console service restart --console --force.

Test hook: MCCTL_UPGRADE_TTY replaces /dev/tty (a readable file gives the answers, a path that cannot be opened means "no terminal").

docs.title: 0. Pre-flight
docs.text:
# Variables: current version / target version / platform root
export OLD=$(mcctl --version | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+')   # for rollback
export NEW=3.1.0
export ROOT=~/minecraft-servers          # directory with docker-compose.yml, .env, .mcctl.json

# Check PM2's Node version, then switch the shell to the same one (e.g. 22)
pm2 jlist | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(p['name'],p['pm2_env']['version'],p['pm2_env']['node_version']) for p in json.load(sys.stdin)]"
nvm use 22 && node --version

# If several mcctl installs exist, check which one runs
which -a mcctl && mcctl --version
npm view @minecraft-docker/mcctl version      # must equal $NEW (registry can lag 1-2 min after publish)

Gate: shell Node major equals PM2 Node major, and npm view returns $NEW.

docs.title: 1. Backup
docs.text:
cd $ROOT
S=pre-$NEW; B=$ROOT/backups-$S
mkdir -p $B                                   # keep it OUTSIDE servers/ (see warning below)
cp docker-compose.yml $B/docker-compose.yml
cp .env $B/.env
cp .mcctl.json $B/.mcctl.json
cp -r servers/_template $B/_template
mcctl status                                  # record current state
mcctl server-backup <server> -m "Before v$NEW"   # server config files (server.yaml, config.env, compose)
mcctl backup push -m "Before v$NEW"              # worlds, if GitHub backup is set up

Gate: $B contains docker-compose.yml, .env, .mcctl.json and _template.

Never put backups inside servers/

mcctl update treats every directory under servers/ as a server and checks/changes its image tag. A copy such as servers/_template.pre-… is mistaken for a server and modified, so a rollback would restore tampered values.

docs.title: 2. Update packages
docs.text:
mcctl update --check          # exits 1 when an update is available
mcctl update --yes            # CLI + api/console/shared, restarts PM2
hash -r && mcctl --version    # = $NEW
  • If you see Updated (restart manually), do step 4.
  • If mcctl update retags a server's compose image, note the ⚠ <server>: A → B output. A pinned tag is kept: a tag that starts with a release version (for example 2026.10.0-java21) or a digest (java21@sha256:…) prints - <server>: <tag> - pinned tag, keeping, or ⚠ <server>: <tag> is pinned, but VERSION=<version> needs <tag> - keeping when its Java is older than VERSION needs. mc-router auto-scale only starts existing containers and never recreates them, so a stopped server keeps its old image until its container is recreated. When the CLI that starts it is v3.0.1 or later, mcctl update offers to recreate the stopped servers (default No; --yes skips it, see step 5).

Rollback point: npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl@<previous> then mcctl console service restart --console --force.

docs.title: 3. Migrate configuration
docs.text:
mcctl upgrade --dry-run       # preview only

Check the dry run for new .env variables, compose changes (router.image, router.group_add) and anything unexpected. Stop and report if something looks wrong.

mcctl upgrade                 # accept defaults for new .env vars, y to apply compose changes
mcctl upgrade --non-interactive   # apply defaults without prompting (automation)
  • New .env variables are added (e.g. DOCKER_GID), docker-compose.yml.bak-<timestamp> is created, and docker compose up -d router runs automatically when the router changes.
  • servers/_template/* is overwritten and templateVersion in .mcctl.json is updated.
  • (v2.32.0+) If servers/global.env is missing, it is created and existing servers are repointed from - ../../.env to - ../global.env, so platform secrets stop reaching server containers. Containers keep the old environment until recreated: stop, then start each server in step 5. See Environment Variables.
  • (v2.33.0+) If ecosystem.config.cjs still defines BETTER_AUTH_SECRET / BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL, they are moved into .env (the secret is kept, so sessions stay valid), the keys are removed from the ecosystem file, and ecosystem.config.cjs.bak-<timestamp> is written next to it. Step 4 (mcctl console service restart --console) applies it. --dry-run only shows it; a second run changes nothing (#699).
  • If .mcctl.json has no installId, it is added once (an existing value is kept). The web console uses it for anonymous usage analytics; to opt out, set "telemetry": false in .mcctl.json (see Usage Analytics).
  • If the router image is the untagged itzg/mc-router, mcctl upgrade does not bump the image. Pin image: in docker-compose.yml to the version named in the release notes, then run docker compose config -q && docker compose up -d router.

docs.title: 3-1. Upgrading to v3.0.0: the scripts folder is gone (#736)
docs.text:
v3.0.0 removes every Bash script (#715). mcctl no longer reads <root>/scripts, and the MCCTL_SCRIPTS environment variable is ignored.

  • mcctl upgrade prints the path of <root>/scripts, a warning that it is unused since v3.0.0 and may hold files you edited yourself, and a link to this table. In a terminal it asks Remove <path>? and deletes only after you answer y (default N). With --non-interactive or without a terminal (cron) it prints rm -r <path> as a hint and deletes nothing; --dry-run only says Would ask before removing <path>.. A symbolic link is unlinked, not followed. There is no option to skip the question. You can also delete the folder yourself; nothing else in the platform root depends on it.
  • Before you delete it, copy any script you edited (for example cp -r $ROOT/scripts ~/scripts-backup). Deleting cannot be undone.
  • If cron jobs, systemd units or your own scripts called <root>/scripts/*.sh directly, change them before you delete the folder. Use this table:
Old script (<root>/scripts/) v3.0.0 mcctl.sh start / stop / status / logs mcctl start / mcctl stop / mcctl status / mcctl logs mcctl.sh console mcctl console <server> (TCP RCON) RCON commands (rcon-cli through the script) mcctl exec <server> <command...> create-server.sh mcctl create delete-server.sh mcctl delete backup.sh push / status / history / restore mcctl backup push / status / history / restore lock.sh mcctl world (list, assign, release; see World Assignment Rules) player.sh lookup / uuid mcctl player info <name> [--offline] logs.sh mcctl logs init.sh mcctl init render-map.sh No CLI command. Use Render map in the web console, or the API (BlueMap) migrate-nip-io.sh No dedicated command. After the host IP changes, run mcctl init --reconfigure and answer yes to "Update existing servers with new IP hostnames?"; it renders every server again and the nip.io router hosts follow the new HOST_IPS (custom hosts stay). Then recreate each server's container (mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>, or mcctl start <server> when it is stopped); until then it keeps its old hostnames lib/common.sh None. It was the scripts' own helper library; the name rules are in TypeScript
  • Servers keep working. The first command that changes a server writes servers/<name>/server.yaml and rewrites config.env and the server's compose.yml; see server.yaml.

Gate: ls $ROOT/scripts reports no such folder (or you chose to keep it), and nothing in crontab -l or systemctl list-timers still names a .sh file from it.

docs.title: 4. Restart API / Console (if needed)
docs.text:
mcctl console service restart
# if the new build does not come up or you see an ABI error (NODE_MODULE_VERSION)
mcctl console service restart --console --force
cd $ROOT/.services 2>/dev/null || cd $ROOT     # where mcctl-api and mcctl-console are installed
npm rebuild better-sqlite3 && mcctl console service restart --console --force

docs.title: 4-1. Upgrading to v2.32.0 or later: check the console access mode (#633)
docs.text:
Do this once when upgrading from v2.31.0 or earlier to v2.32.0 or later, and only on hosts where mcctl console init was run.

Up to v2.31.0, mcctl console init wrote the chosen access mode to AUTH_MODE as is. mcctl-api does not recognise internal, api-key-ip or open, and falls back to api-key under NODE_ENV=production (disabled otherwise). From v2.32.0, mcctl console init writes a value mcctl-api recognises. mcctl update and mcctl upgrade do not rewrite ecosystem.config.cjs, so an existing install keeps the old value until you change it.

grep -nE "AUTH_MODE|AUTH_IP_WHITELIST" $ROOT/ecosystem.config.cjs
Current AUTH_MODE Change to Effect api-key, ip-whitelist, disabled, basic, combined nothing to do - internal ip-whitelist + AUTH_IP_WHITELIST: '127.0.0.1,::1,::ffff:127.0.0.1' only clients on the host itself (the Console) can call the API api-key-ip combined (keep AUTH_API_KEY and AUTH_IP_WHITELIST) the IP whitelist is now enforced; clients outside it get 403 open disabled authentication is really off; development only 
cd $ROOT
cp ecosystem.config.cjs $B/ecosystem.config.cjs     # for rollback (step 8)
sed -i \
  -e "s/^\( *\)AUTH_MODE: 'internal',/\1AUTH_MODE: 'ip-whitelist',\n\1AUTH_IP_WHITELIST: '127.0.0.1,::1,::ffff:127.0.0.1',/" \
  -e "s/AUTH_MODE: 'api-key-ip',/AUTH_MODE: 'combined',/" \
  -e "s/AUTH_MODE: 'open',/AUTH_MODE: 'disabled',/" \
  ecosystem.config.cjs
grep -nE "AUTH_MODE|AUTH_IP_WHITELIST" ecosystem.config.cjs
mcctl console service restart --console --force     # plain restart keeps the old env

The sed leaves the other modes untouched. Instead of editing the file, you can re-run mcctl console init --force, which rewrites the whole file and asks every setup question again.

Gate: AUTH_MODE is one of disabled, api-key, ip-whitelist, basic, combined; API /health returns 200 and the Console can list servers (step 7-6).

docs.title: 4-2. Give mcctl-api time to finish an auto-backup (#734)
docs.text:
Do this once on hosts where mcctl console init was run before this release and BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true is set.

A stop from the API or the Console runs the auto-backup in the background, and mcctl-api waits up to 2 minutes for it when it shuts down, so the backup can turn auto-save back on (save-on) on the servers it flushed. PM2 kills a process 1.6 seconds after asking it to stop unless the app sets kill_timeout. mcctl console init now writes kill_timeout: 130000 for mcctl-api; mcctl update and mcctl upgrade do not rewrite ecosystem.config.cjs, and a plain PM2 restart keeps the old setting.

cd $ROOT
grep -n "kill_timeout" ecosystem.config.cjs || echo "missing: add it"
# add the line to the mcctl-api app, next to max_memory_restart:
#       kill_timeout: 130000,
mcctl console service restart --console --force     # re-registers the apps from the file

Instead of editing the file, you can re-run mcctl console init --force, which rewrites the whole file and asks every setup question again.

Gate: pm2 describe mcctl-api shows kill timeout 130000 (or grep kill_timeout ecosystem.config.cjs shows it before the restart).

docs.title: 4-3. Bind mcctl-api to loopback in the internal access mode (#833)
docs.text:
Do this once on hosts where mcctl console init was run before this release with the internal access mode (AUTH_MODE: 'ip-whitelist' with only loopback addresses in AUTH_IP_WHITELIST). Recommended.

internal allows only clients on the host itself, so mcctl-api does not need to listen on other interfaces. mcctl console init now writes HOST: '127.0.0.1' for mcctl-api in that mode (other modes keep 0.0.0.0) and points the console at MCCTL_API_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:<api port>'. mcctl update and mcctl upgrade do not rewrite ecosystem.config.cjs.

cd $ROOT
grep -nE "AUTH_MODE|AUTH_IP_WHITELIST|HOST:|MCCTL_API_URL" ecosystem.config.cjs
cp ecosystem.config.cjs $B/ecosystem.config.cjs     # for rollback (step 8)
sed -i \
  -e "s/^\( *\)HOST: '0.0.0.0',/\1HOST: '127.0.0.1',/" \
  -e "s#MCCTL_API_URL: 'http://localhost:#MCCTL_API_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:#" \
  ecosystem.config.cjs
mcctl console service restart --console --force     # re-registers the apps from the file

Run the sed only when the access mode is internal: other modes allow clients on other hosts, which need 0.0.0.0. Instead of editing the file, you can re-run mcctl console init --force, which rewrites the whole file and asks every setup question again.

Gate: ss -ltnp | grep 5001 shows 127.0.0.1:5001; API /health returns 200 on the host and the Console can list servers (step 7-6).

docs.title: 5. Apply server images
docs.text:
Stopped servers are not updated by starting them: auto-scale only runs docker start on the existing container, so it wakes up on the old image. After pulling, mcctl update checks each stopped server: one whose container already uses the pulled local image is reported as up to date; the others are listed as still using their old image, and in a terminal it asks whether to recreate their containers (without starting them). The default is No, because a new image can be a regression; --yes or no terminal never recreates, it only prints the commands. On yes it reports recreated (with the previous image ID), up to date or the failure per server, and prints how to roll back: docker tag <old image ID> <image> && docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server>. A recreated server shows as created until it starts. The whole update runs in the CLI process that started it, so if that CLI was older than v3.0.1 (this includes v3.0.0 → v3.0.1), this step did not run: run mcctl update once more in a terminal and answer yes, or run this in the platform directory for each stopped server that still uses its old image:

docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server>

Running servers are left alone. Restart them at a quiet time with mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server> (worlds are preserved).

docs.title: 6. Re-render maps (BlueMap) — only if the release notes mention map changes
docs.text: For worlds that have a map, run Render map again from the world detail page in the Console. The renderer regenerates the map config on every render, so --force is usually not needed.

docs.title: 7. Post-upgrade verification
docs.text: Everything must pass. If anything fails, go to step 8 (rollback).

docs.title: 7-1. Versions
docs.text:
hash -r
mcctl --version                                   # = $NEW
pm2 jlist | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(p['name'],p['pm2_env']['version'],p['pm2_env']['status'],p['pm2_env']['node_version'],'restarts=',p['pm2_env']['restart_time']) for p in json.load(sys.stdin)]"
# expect: mcctl-api / mcctl-console both $NEW, online, same Node as PM2, restarts not climbing
mcctl update --check                              # nothing left to update (incl. shared)

docs.title: 7-2. Config files
docs.text:
cd $ROOT
python3 -c "import json;c=json.load(open('.mcctl.json'));print('templateVersion =',c.get('templateVersion'),'| installId present =','installId' in c)"
diff <(grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' .env | sort) <(grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+=' $B/.env | sort)   # only added variables
docker compose config -q && echo "compose OK"

docs.title: 7-3. router
docs.text:
stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock                   # socket GID
grep '^DOCKER_GID=' .env                          # must match
docker inspect mc-router --format '{{.Config.Image}} {{.HostConfig.GroupAdd}}'   # expected tag, GroupAdd has the GID
docker logs --tail 30 mc-router                   # no "permission denied", routing started

docs.title: 7-4. API / Console
docs.text:
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'console %{http_code}\n' http://localhost:5000          # 200 or 3xx
curl -s -o /dev/null -w 'api %{http_code}\n'     http://localhost:5001/health   # 200
mcctl console service status                      # both online
pm2 logs mcctl-console --lines 30 --nostream      # no better-sqlite3 / NODE_MODULE_VERSION errors

docs.title: 7-5. Servers / auto-scale
docs.text:
mcctl status
# connect to a stopped server (<server>.<HOST_IP>.nip.io:25565) and confirm it starts
docker logs --tail 30 mc-router | grep -iE "error|denied|scale"
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Image}}\t{{.Status}}'

docs.title: 7-6. UI smoke test
docs.text: In a browser (hard refresh) open http://<host>:5000: log in → server list → world detail (info/stats panels) → map panel (default view must be Overworld). Also check any screen the release notes call out.

docs.title: 7-7. Completion checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] mcctl --version, PM2 api/console = $NEW, online, matching Node
  • [ ] mcctl update --check reports nothing left
  • [ ] .mcctl.json templateVersion updated, docker compose config -q passes
  • [ ] router image tag / DOCKER_GID / GroupAdd consistent, no errors in logs
  • [ ] API /health 200, Console 200, PM2 restarts not increasing
  • [ ] a stopped server starts on connect (auto-scale)
  • [ ] UI smoke test passes
  • [ ] (v2.31.0 or earlier → v2.32.0+) AUTH_MODE in ecosystem.config.cjs is a value mcctl-api recognises (step 4-1)
  • [ ] once stable, delete $B (backups-pre-$NEW)

docs.title: 8. Rollback
docs.text:
cd $ROOT; B=$ROOT/backups-pre-$NEW
cp $B/docker-compose.yml docker-compose.yml
cp $B/.env .env
cp $B/.mcctl.json .mcctl.json
rm -rf servers/_template && cp -r $B/_template servers/_template
docker compose up -d router
[ -f $B/ecosystem.config.cjs ] && cp $B/ecosystem.config.cjs ecosystem.config.cjs   # if changed in step 4-1
[ -n "$(ls ecosystem.config.cjs.bak-* 2>/dev/null)" ] && echo "restore the latest ecosystem.config.cjs.bak-* if step 3 moved BETTER_AUTH_*"
# packages back to $OLD (in the PM2-Node shell)
npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl@$OLD
cd $ROOT/.services 2>/dev/null || cd $ROOT     # where mcctl-api and mcctl-console are installed
npm install @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api@$OLD @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console@$OLD @minecraft-docker/shared@$OLD
mcctl console service restart --console --force

Note

mc-router 1.46+ runs as non-root, so group_add (DOCKER_GID) is required. Do not remove it unless you are also reverting the router image to an older version.

docs.title: REST API Overview
docs.text:
mcctl-api is the REST API behind the Web Console. It manages servers, worlds, players, backups and mc-router with the same code as the mcctl CLI, and you can call it directly from scripts and other tools.

  • Endpoints: API Endpoints documents every route.
  • Base URL: http://<host>:5001. mcctl-api listens on HOST and PORT (default 5001). mcctl console init writes HOST: '127.0.0.1' for the internal access mode, which allows only clients on the host, and 0.0.0.0 for the other modes; without HOST the API listens on 0.0.0.0.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
mcctl-api and the Web Console run on the host as the PM2 processes mcctl-api and mcctl-console; they are not containers. mcctl-api reads and writes the files under MCCTL_ROOT (default ~/minecraft-servers) and controls containers with the docker and docker compose commands. Minecraft server containers publish no ports: players connect to mc-router on port 25565, which routes each connection by hostname.

flowchart LR
    subgraph Clients["Clients"]
        P["Minecraft clients"]
        B["Browser"]
        R["REST clients<br/>curl, scripts"]
    end

    subgraph Host["Host"]
        subgraph PM2["PM2"]
            CON["mcctl-console :5000"]
            API["mcctl-api :5001"]
        end
        FILES[("MCCTL_ROOT<br/>servers/ worlds/ backups/ data/")]
        subgraph Docker["Docker network minecraft-net"]
            ROUTER["mc-router :25565"]
            S1["mc-survival"]
            S2["mc-creative"]
        end
    end

    P -->|":25565"| ROUTER
    ROUTER --> S1 & S2
    B --> CON
    CON -->|"HTTP with X-User, X-Role"| API
    R -->|"HTTP"| API
    API -->|"docker, docker compose"| Docker
    API --> FILES

docs.title: Request flows
docs.text:
Start a server

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as mcctl-api
    participant D as Docker

    C->>A: POST /api/servers/survival/start
    A->>A: Authenticate, check the server name
    A->>D: docker compose up -d mc-survival
    D-->>A: exit code 0
    A-->>C: { success: true, action: "start", ... }

Run an RCON command

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as mcctl-api
    participant MC as mc-survival

    C->>A: POST /api/servers/survival/exec<br/>{ command: "list" }
    A->>MC: docker exec mc-survival rcon-cli -- list
    MC-->>A: "There are 3 of a max of 20 players online: ..."
    A-->>C: { success: true, output: "There are 3 ..." }

Assign a world

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as mcctl-api
    participant W as WorldManagementUseCase

    C->>A: POST /api/worlds/survival/assign<br/>{ serverName: "myserver" }
    A->>W: assignWorldByName("survival", "myserver")
    W->>W: 1. Check the world name and that worlds/survival exists
    W->>W: 2. Read every server's LEVEL; refuse if another server uses the world
    W->>W: 3. Refuse unless mc-myserver is stopped
    W->>W: 4. Write LEVEL=survival (server.yaml and config.env)
    W-->>A: success
    A-->>C: { success: true, worldName: "survival", serverName: "myserver" }

Follow server logs (SSE)

sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant A as mcctl-api
    participant D as Docker

    C->>A: GET /api/servers/survival/logs?follow=true
    A-->>C: 200 text/event-stream
    A-->>C: data: {"type":"server-log","data":{"log":"..."}} (last 100 lines)
    A->>D: docker logs -f --tail 0 mc-survival
    loop Each new line
        D-->>A: log line
        A-->>C: data: {"type":"server-log","data":{"log":"..."}}
    end
    loop Every 30 seconds
        A-->>C: : heartbeat
    end

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
mcctl-api checks every request except the paths in AUTH_EXCLUDE_PATHS (default /health). The mode is set with AUTH_MODE:

Mode Requirement Request header disabled None (development only) - api-key AUTH_API_KEY X-API-Key: <key> ip-whitelist The source address of the connection is in AUTH_IP_WHITELIST (behind a reverse proxy, that is the proxy's address) - basic A user in AUTH_USERS Authorization: Basic <base64 of user:password> combined API key and IP whitelist, both checked X-API-Key: <key> 
# api-key or combined mode
curl -H "X-API-Key: mctk_your_key_here" http://localhost:5001/api/servers

# basic mode
curl -u admin:password http://localhost:5001/api/servers

The API key is read only from X-API-Key; an Authorization: Bearer header is not accepted.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
These are environment variables of the mcctl-api process. mcctl console init writes them to the env block of the mcctl-api app in <MCCTL_ROOT>/ecosystem.config.cjs.

Variable Description AUTH_MODE One of the modes above. When unset or unknown: api-key if NODE_ENV=production, otherwise disabled AUTH_API_KEY Key compared with X-API-Key. Required for api-key and combined AUTH_IP_WHITELIST Comma-separated addresses or CIDR ranges, for example 127.0.0.1,192.168.1.0/24. Required for ip-whitelist and combined AUTH_USERS JSON array of {"username": "...", "passwordHash": "<bcrypt hash>"}. Required for basic AUTH_EXCLUDE_PATHS Comma-separated paths that skip authentication. Default /health,/health/

mcctl-api does not start when the selected mode lacks its required variable.

mcctl console init asks for an access mode and writes it as follows (Access Modes):

mcctl console init mode AUTH_MODE written internal (default) ip-whitelist with 127.0.0.1,::1,::ffff:127.0.0.1: only clients on the host itself, such as the Web Console api-key api-key with a generated key, printed once ip-whitelist ip-whitelist with the addresses you enter api-key-ip combined with a generated key and the addresses you enter open disabled

To change the mode or the key later, run mcctl console init --force. The mcctl console api commands only update api-config.json, which the running API does not read.

Authentication failures:

Status Body 401 {"error": "AuthenticationError", "message": "Missing X-API-Key header"} (also Invalid API key, Missing or invalid Authorization header, Invalid credentials) 403 {"error": "AuthenticationError", "message": "IP address not allowed"}

docs.title: User and role headers
docs.text:
When the Web Console forwards a request that needs them, it adds the signed-in user's name and role as X-User and X-Role. Other clients send the same headers to use these routes:

Header Used by X-Role DELETE /api/audit-logs, GET /api/platform-settings and PUT /api/platform-settings answer 403 with error: "Forbidden" unless the value is admin. GET /api/auth/me returns it as role X-User Audit log actor api:<user> for the file routes and PUT /api/platform-settings (other routes record api:console). Required by GET /api/auth/me

In the Web Console, more actions are limited to administrators by the console itself, for example restarting mc-router.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors use one JSON shape:

{
  "error": "NotFound",
  "message": "Server 'unknown' not found"
}
error Status Meaning BadRequest 400 The route refused the input, for example two world options at once Bad Request 400 The request does not match the route's schema (type, range, pattern, required field) AuthenticationError 401, 403 See Authentication Forbidden 403 The route needs X-Role: admin, or a path leaves the allowed directory (file and map routes) NotFound 404 Server, world, player, file, schedule or entry not found Not Found 404 Unknown route Conflict 409 Refused because of the current state: the server exists or is running, the world is used by another server, another operation holds a lock PayloadTooLarge 413 File or upload over the size limit InternalServerError 500 The operation failed; message says why BadGateway 502 Client-only mod detection failed (GET /api/mods/:slug/client-only) ServiceUnavailable 503 Docker could not be queried (backup routes)

A few routes use other names (the legacy routes, block statistics, server actions); their sections say so.

Schema violations name the field in message. Some routes also return statusCode and code:

{
  "statusCode": 400,
  "code": "FST_ERR_VALIDATION",
  "error": "Bad Request",
  "message": "querystring/limit must be <= 200"
}

An unknown route answers 404 with {"message": "Route GET:/api/unknown not found", "error": "Not Found", "statusCode": 404}.

docs.title: Status codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 200 Success 201 Created (server, world, world upload, config snapshot, backup or snapshot schedule) 204 Deleted, no body (config snapshot, config snapshot schedule) 400 Invalid request 401 Not authenticated 403 Address not allowed, admin role required, or path outside the allowed directory 404 Not found 409 Conflict with the current state 413 Too large 500 Operation failed 502 Upstream mod source failed 503 Docker could not be queried

docs.title: Server-Sent Events
docs.text:
Routes that stream use Content-Type: text/event-stream. There are two message styles:

Style Wire format Routes Named events event: <name> and data: <JSON> Server status, player roster and live positions, router status and logs, audit logs, map render, block statistics Typed messages data: {"type": "<type>", "data": {...}} without an event: line Server logs (server-log, connection-closed), server create (server-create, server-create-log)
  • Heartbeat. Long-lived streams send the comment line : heartbeat every 30 seconds. The audit log stream sends event: heartbeat with {"timestamp": "..."} instead. The map render and block statistics streams end with their job and send no heartbeat.
  • Polling interval. Streams that poll take interval in milliseconds (1000 to 60000, default 5000): server status, player roster, live player positions and router status.
  • Disconnect. Closing the connection stops the polling or the docker logs process behind it. A server create keeps running after the client disconnects; a block statistics analysis is cancelled.
  • Browsers. The browser EventSource API cannot add request headers, so it cannot send X-API-Key. Use it only when the API needs no header (disabled or ip-whitelist); otherwise read the stream with a client that sets headers, such as curl -N or fetch with a stream reader. The Web Console relays the streams to signed-in users through its own routes.
curl -N -H "X-API-Key: mctk_your_key_here" \
  "http://localhost:5001/api/servers/survival/logs?follow=true&lines=50"

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Set up mcctl-api and the Web Console.
#    Choose the API access mode; the api-key modes print the key once.
mcctl console init

# 2. Start mcctl-api
mcctl console service start --api

# 3. Health check (no authentication)
curl http://localhost:5001/health

# 4. List servers. In the default internal mode, requests from the host itself need no key
curl http://localhost:5001/api/servers

# In api-key or api-key-ip mode, send the key
curl -H "X-API-Key: <key>" http://localhost:5001/api/servers

The key is also stored as AUTH_API_KEY in the mcctl-api env block of ecosystem.config.cjs.

docs.title: OpenAPI and Swagger UI
docs.text:
Swagger UI (/docs) and the OpenAPI document (/docs/json) are served only when NODE_ENV is not production or when SWAGGER_ENABLED=true. mcctl console init sets NODE_ENV=production for installed packages, so a normal install does not serve them. To enable them, add SWAGGER_ENABLED=true to <MCCTL_ROOT>/.env (mcctl-api reads that file when it starts, because PM2 runs it in MCCTL_ROOT) and run mcctl console service restart --api.

Both paths use the same authentication as the other routes. In api-key mode a browser cannot open /docs directly; fetch the document with curl -H "X-API-Key: <key>" http://localhost:5001/docs/json and open it in an OpenAPI viewer.

docs.title: Endpoint groups
docs.text: Group Routes Health GET /health Servers List, detail, status streams, create, delete, start/stop/restart, RCON, logs Server configuration config.env settings, world reset Hostnames Custom hostnames of a server Mods Server mods, installed jars, Modrinth search Files File manager for servers/<name>/data Players and access lists Roster, player detail, live positions, whitelist, bans, operators, kick Worlds List, create, upload, assign, release, delete, world info, map, block statistics Router mc-router status, streams, restart Backups GitHub world backups and backup schedules Config snapshots Snapshots of server configuration files, diff, schedules playit.gg playit-agent status, start, stop Platform Settings The platform .env Audit logs Query, statistics, stream, purge Legacy /api/auth/login, /api/auth/me, /servers/:id/console/exec

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• API Endpoints: every route
  • Installation: set up mcctl-api and the Web Console
  • CLI Commands: mcctl console commands

docs.title: API Endpoints Reference
docs.text:
Every route of mcctl-api, grouped by area. The REST API Overview explains authentication, the error format and Server-Sent Events (SSE) once; this page notes what is specific to each route.

  • Base URL: http://localhost:5001. The paths below are complete; only the legacy /servers/:id/console/exec has no /api prefix.
  • Authentication: send X-API-Key: <key> in api-key and combined mode (Authentication). Routes that need X-Role: admin say so.
  • Bodies are JSON unless a route says otherwise.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Server names. :name in /api/servers/:name/... is the server name without the mc- prefix: survival for the container mc-survival. Existing servers may have names of up to 64 letters, digits, _ and - that start with a letter or digit; new servers follow the stricter rule of POST /api/servers. Request fields that name a server (serverName) take the same name, never the container name.
  • World names. :name in /api/worlds/:name/... is a directory directly under worlds/. Each world route lists the names it accepts.
  • Validation. A body, query or path value outside the documented type, range or pattern is answered with 400 before the route runs (Errors).
  • Values written to config.env (seeds, MOTD, mod slugs and other free text) are refused with 400 when they contain control characters, including line breaks, or start with a quote or backtick.
  • Writes through server.yaml. Routes that change a server's settings (configuration, whitelist on/off, hostnames, mods, world assignment) update servers/<name>/server.yaml and render config.env and the server's docker-compose.yml from it. They answer 409 when that write is refused, for example because the generated docker-compose.yml was edited by hand (server.yaml).

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Returns the service status. It needs no authentication unless AUTH_EXCLUDE_PATHS is changed.

{
  "status": "ok",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-25T10:30:00.000Z"
}

The answer is always 200 while mcctl-api runs.

docs.title: GET /api/servers
docs.text:
Lists every server: the directories under servers/ that have a config.env, and any mc-* container other than mc-router.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Description include string Optional. summary adds type, version, memory, players, stats per server and a top-level totals. Any other value returns 400.

Response:

{
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "survival",
      "container": "mc-survival",
      "status": "running",
      "health": "healthy",
      "hostname": "survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
Field Description name Server name container Container name, mc-<name> status Container state, see below health healthy, unhealthy, starting, none or unknown hostname The server's mc-router.host label, comma-separated when it has several hostnames; - when there is none

Status values:

Status Description running Container is running exited Container has stopped created Container created but not started paused Container is paused restarting Container is restarting dead Docker reports the container as dead not_created The server directory exists but there is no container (health is none, hostname is -)

Response with include=summary:

The default response above is unchanged when include is omitted.

{
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "survival",
      "container": "mc-survival",
      "status": "running",
      "health": "healthy",
      "hostname": "survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io",
      "type": "PAPER",
      "version": "1.21.1",
      "memory": "4G",
      "players": {
        "online": 3,
        "max": 20,
        "players": ["Player1", "Player2", "Player3"]
      },
      "stats": {
        "memoryUsage": 2254857830,
        "memoryLimit": 4294967296
      }
    }
  ],
  "total": 1,
  "totals": {
    "playersOnline": 3,
    "playersMax": 20,
    "running": 1
  }
}

Summary behavior

  • type, version, and memory come from the server's config.env.
  • players and stats are returned only for running servers. players is null when the RCON query fails or times out. stats (memoryUsage, memoryLimit, in bytes) is omitted when docker stats does not answer in time.
  • RCON and stats run in parallel for running servers with timeouts of about 2 seconds (RCON) and 3 seconds (stats), so one slow server only gets players: null (or no stats).
  • Results are cached for about 10 seconds per server.
  • totals.playersOnline and totals.playersMax sum only the servers whose players are known. totals.running is the number of running servers.

docs.title: GET /api/servers/:name
docs.text:
Returns details of one server.

{
  "server": {
    "name": "survival",
    "container": "mc-survival",
    "status": "running",
    "health": "healthy",
    "hostname": "survival.192.168.1.100.nip.io",
    "type": "PAPER",
    "version": "1.21.1",
    "memory": "4G",
    "uptime": "2d 5h 30m",
    "uptimeSeconds": 192600,
    "players": {
      "online": 3,
      "max": 20,
      "players": ["Player1", "Player2", "Player3"]
    },
    "stats": {
      "memoryUsage": 2254857830,
      "memoryLimit": 4294967296,
      "memoryPercent": 52.5,
      "cpuPercent": 15.2
    },
    "worldName": "survival",
    "worldSize": "1.2 GB",
    "playitDomain": null
  }
}
Field Description type, version, memory TYPE, VERSION and MEMORY from config.env uptime, uptimeSeconds Time since the container started; only while it runs players Online players from RCON list; only while the server runs and RCON answers stats From docker stats: memory use and limit in bytes, memory and CPU use in percent; only while the server runs worldName LEVEL (or the legacy WORLD_NAME) from config.env; world when neither is set worldSize Size of worlds/<worldName>; 0 B when that directory does not exist playitDomain PLAYIT_DOMAIN from config.env, or null

A server without a container is answered from its config.env with status: "not_created"; missing TYPE, VERSION and MEMORY are then shown as PAPER, LATEST and 2G.

Errors: 404 when neither the container nor servers/<name>/config.env exists.

docs.title: GET /api/servers-status
docs.text:
Returns the current status of every server. With follow=true it streams instead.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description follow boolean false Stream as SSE interval integer 5000 Poll interval in milliseconds for the stream (1000 to 60000)

Response:

[
  {
    "serverName": "survival",
    "status": "running",
    "health": "healthy",
    "timestamp": "2026-10-25T10:30:00.000Z"
  }
]

status is simplified here: running, exited, created, stopped (paused, dead or no container) or unknown (restarting or not recognized). health is healthy, unhealthy, starting, none or unknown.

Stream: every interval the stream sends one server-status event per server, plus : heartbeat every 30 seconds.

event: server-status
data: {"serverName":"survival","status":"running","health":"healthy","timestamp":"2026-10-25T10:30:00.000Z"}

docs.title: GET /api/servers/:name/status
docs.text:
The same status object as GET /api/servers-status for one server. Takes the same follow and interval parameters; the stream sends a server-status event every interval.

Errors: 404 when the server does not exist.

docs.title: POST /api/servers
docs.text:
Creates a server: writes servers/<name>/ (with server.yaml, config.env and docker-compose.yml), adds <name>.local to /etc/avahi/hosts when the host address is known, and starts the container.

Request body:

{
  "name": "newserver",
  "type": "PAPER",
  "version": "1.21.1",
  "memory": "4G",
  "seed": "12345",
  "autoStart": true
}
Field Type Required Description name string Yes 2 to 32 characters: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens (no trailing hyphen, no --). router is reserved type string No PAPER (default), VANILLA, FORGE, FABRIC, SPIGOT, NEOFORGE, MODRINTH or AUTO_CURSEFORGE version string No Minecraft version such as 1.21.1, LATEST or a snapshot id (letters, digits, ., _, -; up to 64). Default LATEST; for MODRINTH and AUTO_CURSEFORGE no VERSION is written unless you send one memory string No JVM memory such as 4G or 512M. Default 4G, or 6G for MODRINTH and AUTO_CURSEFORGE seed string No World seed, up to 256 characters worldUrl string No URL of a world ZIP to download worldName string No Existing world in worlds/ (letters, digits, -, _) autoStart boolean No Start the container after the files are written (default true) sudoPassword string No Sudo password for adding <name>.local to /etc/avahi/hosts (write-only). Not needed when sudo needs no password modpack string For MODRINTH, AUTO_CURSEFORGE Modrinth modpack slug, ID or URL modpackVersion string No Modpack version, up to 128 characters modLoader string No forge, fabric, neoforge or quilt excludeFiles string[] No Up to 100 mods to leave out (letters, digits, ., _, -), written to MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES or CF_EXCLUDE_MODS

Send at most one of seed, worldUrl and worldName.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description follow boolean false Report progress as SSE instead of one JSON reply

Response (201):

{
  "success": true,
  "server": {
    "name": "newserver",
    "container": "mc-newserver",
    "status": "starting"
  }
}

server.status is starting when the container was started, and created when autoStart is false or the start did not finish. In the second case the reply also has warning:

  • The first start failed: warning carries the error. The server is kept; start it later with POST /api/servers/:name/start.
  • The container start had not finished after 120 seconds (the first start can pull the image or download mods): the reply says so in warning, and the start goes on in the background.

Errors:

Status When 400 Invalid body; MODRINTH or AUTO_CURSEFORGE without modpack; modLoader and version that the modpack does not offer (checked only when both are sent and Modrinth answers); more than one of seed, worldUrl, worldName; worldName not found; a value the server files cannot hold 409 The server exists; the world it would use (worldName, otherwise <name>) is used by another server; another server's config.env cannot be read (World assignment rules) 500 Creation failed; message starts with Failed to create server:

Streaming (follow=true). After the checks above, the reply switches to text/event-stream and sends typed messages:

data: {"type":"server-create","data":{"status":"initializing","message":"Initializing server creation..."}}
data: {"type":"server-create","data":{"status":"creating","message":"Creating server directory..."}}
data: {"type":"server-create","data":{"status":"configuring","message":"Registering mDNS hostname..."}}
data: {"type":"server-create","data":{"status":"starting","message":"Starting container..."}}
data: {"type":"server-create-log","data":{"log":"..."}}
data: {"type":"server-create","data":{"status":"completed","message":"Server created successfully","server":{"name":"newserver","container":"mc-newserver","status":"starting"}}}

When the first start fails, completed says Server created, but it did not start, server.status is created and warning is added. Other failures end with {"status": "error", "message": "Server creation failed: ..."}. The stream waits for the whole start (up to 30 minutes); the server is still created when the client disconnects.

Create and delete requests run one at a time inside mcctl-api; a request waits for the one before it. Each create writes a server.create audit entry.

docs.title: DELETE /api/servers/:name
docs.text:
Deletes a server. The container is stopped and removed even when it is running.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description force boolean false Accepted for compatibility; it changes nothing deleteWorld boolean false Delete the world inside the server (servers/<name>/data/<LEVEL>) instead of moving it to worlds/. Worlds in worlds/ are never deleted

Request body (optional):

Field Type Description sudoPassword string Sudo password for removing the mDNS hostname <name>.local from /etc/avahi/hosts (write-only, never logged). Not needed with the sudoers NOPASSWD rule

By default the world inside the server is moved to worlds/<LEVEL>. If worlds/ already has that name or the world inside the server cannot be located with certainty (see mcctl delete), the request fails with 409 and nothing is deleted; if Docker cannot be queried or the container cannot be stopped, it fails with 500 and nothing is deleted. A 409 after the container was removed (for example servers/compose.yml locked by another mcctl process, or a world move that failed) says so, names the worlds already moved to worlds/, and what is left to clean up. The server leaves servers/compose.yml before its world moves, so a start request cannot bring it back meanwhile; a failed move puts it back. A delete of a server that another process (mcctl delete, say) is deleting fails with 409, and so does a server with a hand-written servers/compose.yml include entry (anything but <name>/docker-compose.yml), before anything is changed. No backup runs before the delete.

Example:

curl -X DELETE "http://localhost:5001/api/servers/myserver" \
  -H "X-API-Key: mctk_xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"sudoPassword": "your-sudo-password"}'

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "server": "myserver",
  "message": "Server deleted successfully"
}

When the server was deleted but its mDNS hostname could not be removed, the response adds warning (for example "mDNS hostname myserver.local was not removed: sudo authentication failed; check the sudo password"). The same goes for files left in servers/<name>/ after it is out of servers/compose.yml (for example files the container wrote as root): the server counts as deleted and warning says to remove them with sudo rm -rf. Both warnings are joined with ;.

Errors: 404 when the server does not exist; 409 and 500 as described above.

Deletes run one at a time with creates, and each writes a server.delete audit entry.

docs.title: POST /api/servers/:name/start
docs.text:
Starts a server with docker compose up -d mc-<name> in MCCTL_ROOT (60-second timeout).

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "server": "survival",
  "action": "start",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-25T10:30:00.000Z",
  "message": ""
}

message carries the standard output of the docker compose command; it may be empty.

Errors use the same object with success: false:

Status When Fields 400 The name breaks the existing-name rule (Conventions) error explains the rule 500 The docker compose command failed, also for an unknown server error: the command error; message: its standard error output

Each request that passes the name check writes a server.start audit entry.

docs.title: POST /api/servers/:name/stop
docs.text:
Stops a server with docker compose stop mc-<name>. Response and errors as for start, with action: "stop" and a server.stop audit entry.

With BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true in the platform .env and backups configured, a successful stop also starts a world backup in the background. Its result goes to the mcctl-api log; it never changes the response. When mcctl-api shuts down it waits up to 2 minutes for such a backup.

docs.title: POST /api/servers/:name/restart
docs.text: Restarts a server with docker compose restart mc-<name>. Response and errors as for start, with action: "restart" and a server.restart audit entry.

docs.title: POST /api/servers/:name/exec
docs.text:
Runs an RCON command with docker exec mc-<name> rcon-cli -- <command>. Because of --, a command that starts with - is passed to the server as it is.

Request body:

{
  "command": "list"
}

command is 1 to 1024 characters.

Response:

{
  "success": true,
  "output": "There are 3 of a max of 20 players online: Player1, Player2, Player3"
}

output is the trimmed standard output of rcon-cli; its standard error is not returned. success is true whenever the container exists, so an empty output can also mean that the command could not run, for example because the server is stopped.

Errors: 404 when the container does not exist.

Common Commands:

Command Description list List online players say <message> Broadcast message give <player> <item> [count] Give item to player save-all Save world whitelist add <player> Add to whitelist op <player> Grant operator

docs.title: GET /api/servers/:name/logs
docs.text:
Returns the container log, or streams it.

Query parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description lines integer 100 Number of recent lines (1 to 10000) follow boolean false Stream as SSE

JSON response:

{
  "logs": "[10:30:15] [Server thread/INFO]: Player1 joined the game\n...",
  "lines": 100
}

lines is the number of non-empty lines returned.

Stream (follow=true). The last lines lines are sent first, then each new line, as typed messages; : heartbeat every 30 seconds. When docker logs ends, a connection-closed message is sent and the stream closes.

data: {"type":"server-log","data":{"log":"[10:30:15] [Server thread/INFO]: Player1 joined the game"}}

data: {"type":"connection-closed","data":{"timestamp":"2026-10-25T10:31:00.000Z"}}

Errors: 404 when the container does not exist, also for a server that has a config.env but no container yet.

docs.title: GET /api/servers/:name/config
docs.text:
Returns the server's settings from config.env. Each field stands for one itzg variable, for example maxPlayers for MAX_PLAYERS, gameMode for MODE and level for LEVEL. Only variables present in config.env appear. A server that has only the older GAMEMODE returns it as gameMode; a PATCH that includes gameMode writes MODE and removes GAMEMODE.

{
  "config": {
    "difficulty": "normal",
    "gameMode": "survival",
    "maxPlayers": 20,
    "motd": "Welcome to survival",
    "memory": "4G",
    "enableWhitelist": false
  }
}
