docs.text: Complete reference for all mcctl commands.

docs.title: mcctl init
docs.text:
Initialize the platform directory structure.

mcctl init [options]

Options:

Option Description --root <path> Custom data directory --skip-validation Skip the prerequisite checks (Node.js, Docker, Docker Compose, avahi) --skip-docker Do not create the minecraft-net Docker network --reconfigure Change the settings of an initialized platform, such as the host IP address(es), timezone and RCON password --playit-key <key> Enable playit.gg with this PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY (no question) --no-playit Do not enable playit.gg (no question) --upgrade Run mcctl upgrade instead

Example:

# Initialize in default location (~/minecraft-servers)
mcctl init

# Initialize in custom location
mcctl --root /opt/minecraft init

What it creates:

~/minecraft-servers/
├── docker-compose.yml
├── .env
├── .gitignore
├── .mcctl.json
├── servers/
│   ├── compose.yml
│   ├── global.env
│   └── _template/
├── worlds/
├── shared/
│   ├── plugins/
│   └── mods/
└── backups/

mcctl init asks which host IP address(es) to use (HOST_IP, HOST_IPS in .env) and whether to enable playit.gg. It writes a random 24-character RCON_PASSWORD to .env. On a platform that is already initialized it changes nothing and points to mcctl init --reconfigure.

docs.title: mcctl up
docs.text:
Start all infrastructure (mc-router and all Minecraft servers).

mcctl up

Example:

mcctl up

Equivalent to docker compose up -d.

docs.title: mcctl down
docs.text:
Stop all infrastructure (mc-router and all Minecraft servers).

mcctl down

Example:

mcctl down

Stops all mc-* containers and runs docker compose down, which removes the containers. The minecraft-net network is declared external and is kept.

docs.title: mcctl router
docs.text:
Manage mc-router independently from Minecraft servers.

mcctl router <action>

Actions:

Action Description start Start mc-router only stop Stop mc-router only restart Restart mc-router

Examples:

# Start mc-router
mcctl router start

# Stop mc-router
mcctl router stop

# Restart mc-router (the container keeps its current settings)
mcctl router restart

mc-router handles hostname-based routing for all Minecraft servers. It must be running for clients to connect to any server.

Configuration:

The auto-scale settings are in the environment: of the router service in <root>/docker-compose.yml:

  router:
    environment:
      AUTO_SCALE_UP: "true"            # Start a stopped server when a player connects
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN: "true"          # Stop idle servers
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER: "10m"     # Idle timeout (1m, 5m, 10m, 30m, 1h)
      DOCKER_TIMEOUT: "120s"           # Container start timeout (Go time.Duration: 120s, 2m)
      AUTO_SCALE_ASLEEP_MOTD: "§e§lServer is sleeping§r\n§7Connect to wake up!"   # MOTD of a stopped server

Apply a change with mcctl router start (docker compose up -d router recreates the container). mcctl router restart keeps the old values. mcctl upgrade patches only the router image and group_add, so these edits survive an upgrade.

docs.title: mcctl update
docs.text:
Full release upgrade procedure with post-upgrade verification: Upgrade Runbook.

Check for updates and update mcctl CLI and services to the latest version.

mcctl update [options]

Options:

Option Description --cli-only Update only the mcctl CLI binary (opt out of the full update) --check Show the available updates for the CLI and the installed services; install nothing --yes Do not ask before updating, and do not recreate stopped servers (see Stopped servers below) --all Deprecated alias — same as the default (kept for backward compatibility)

By default mcctl update updates the CLI, the installed services (mcctl-api, mcctl-console, shared) and the server images. --cli-only updates just the CLI binary.

A server's image tag follows its VERSION (for example java21 for 1.21.1). A release tag such as itzg/minecraft-server:2026.10.0-java21 or a digest (java21@sha256:…) in server.yaml is a pin and is kept, so a server can stay on a known-good image while an upstream regression is open. If the pinned Java is older than VERSION needs, mcctl update warns and still keeps it. Once the fix is released, set the tag back to the one for its VERSION.

Examples:

Check for UpdatesUpdate CLI OnlyUpdate Everything (default)Auto-confirm (CI/CD) 
mcctl update --check

Output (update available): 

mcctl Version Info

  Installed: 3.0.1
  Latest:    3.0.2

  Update available: 3.0.1 → 3.0.2

Output (up to date): 

mcctl Version Info

  Installed: 3.0.2
  Latest:    3.0.2

  You are using the latest version.

Without --cli-only, the services are listed after it (for example Update available or Up to date).

mcctl update --cli-only

After the version info it asks Update mcctl to 3.0.2? (unless --yes), then prints:

✓ mcctl updated successfully!

mcctl update

Output (after the CLI update): 

Updating services...

  mcctl-api        3.0.1 → 3.0.2  ✓ Updated & restarted
  mcctl-console    3.0.1 → 3.0.2  ✓ Updated & restarted

Checking server image compatibility...
  ✓ survival: java21 (VERSION=1.21.1 - compatible)

Updating Docker images...

  ✓ itzg/minecraft-server:java21

Applying new images to stopped servers...
  ✓ survival: up to date

  Completed in 41.8s


mcctl update --yes

Behavior Details:

  • Update check before each command: Before every command except --help and --version, mcctl checks npm for a newer CLI version and prints a notice when there is one. The result is cached for 24 hours in ~/.mcctl-update-check.json; without a fresh cache entry the command waits up to 2 seconds for npm.
  • --check exit codes: Exit code 1 if a newer CLI version is available or npm cannot be reached, 0 if the CLI is up to date. Service updates do not change the exit code. Useful for scripting.
  • Default (full update): After updating the CLI (also when the CLI is already up to date):
    • mcctl-api and mcctl-console: Installs latest version and restarts the PM2 service
    • shared library: Installs latest version (no restart needed)
    • Each server's image tag is set to the tag recommended for its VERSION through server.yaml (pinned tags are kept, see above), then the servers' Docker images are pulled
  • Stopped servers: mc-router auto-scale starts the existing container, so a stopped server keeps its old image until its container is recreated. After pulling, mcctl update lists the stopped (exited or created) servers whose container does not use the pulled image; servers already on it are shown as up to date. In a terminal it asks Recreate the stopped servers now so they use the new image? (default No). Yes runs docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server> for each of them and prints a rollback command (docker tag <old image ID> <image> && docker compose up --no-start --no-deps mc-<server>). With --yes, or without a terminal, nothing is recreated and the docker compose up --no-start --no-deps command is printed for each server. Running servers keep their image until you run mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>.
  • --cli-only flag: Updates only the mcctl CLI binary and skips services/images.

Scripting with --check

Use --check in scripts to conditionally trigger updates:

if ! mcctl update --check > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  mcctl update --yes
fi

update vs upgrade

mcctl update updates the CLI and service packages from npm. mcctl upgrade migrates platform configuration files and templates to a new version.

docs.title: mcctl upgrade
docs.text:
Full release upgrade procedure with post-upgrade verification: Upgrade Runbook.

Migrate platform configuration files to the installed mcctl version.

mcctl upgrade [options]

Options:

Option Description --dry-run Preview changes without modifying files --non-interactive Apply without prompting --root <path> Custom data directory

What it does:

  1. Appends new variables from the bundled .env.example to .env (existing values are never changed). In a terminal it asks for a value for each new variable (Enter keeps the default); --non-interactive writes the defaults
  2. Detects the Docker socket group ID and writes DOCKER_GID to .env (needed by non-root mc-router 1.46+)
  3. Patches the router service in the root docker-compose.yml (see below)
  4. Updates servers/_template/ files and records templateVersion in .mcctl.json
  5. Creates servers/global.env if it is missing and points each server's docker-compose.yml at it instead of the platform .env, so platform secrets no longer reach the servers. Existing containers keep the old environment until they are recreated: run mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server> for each server it lists
  6. Moves BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL from ecosystem.config.cjs into .env (backup: ecosystem.config.cjs.bak-<timestamp>); apply with mcctl console service restart --console
  7. Lists the servers that have no server.yaml yet and writes nothing; they are imported on their next change, or with mcctl migrate spec
  8. Adds installId to .mcctl.json if it is missing (an existing value is kept)
  9. (v3.0.0+) If <root>/scripts exists, prints its path, a warning that it is unused since v3.0.0 and may hold files you edited yourself, and the link to the script to mcctl table. In a terminal it asks Remove <path>? (default N) and deletes only on y. With --non-interactive or without a terminal it prints a hint (rm -r <path>) and deletes nothing. With --dry-run it only prints Would ask before removing <path>.. A symbolic link is unlinked, never followed. There is no option to skip the question.

docker-compose.yml router patch: only the router service's image tag and group_add entry are aligned with the bundled template. Other services, ports, comments, and line endings are kept.

  • A line diff is shown, then you are asked to confirm (--non-interactive applies without asking, --dry-run shows the diff only)
  • The original file is backed up as docker-compose.yml.bak-<timestamp> and restored if writing fails
  • After a successful patch, mc-router is recreated with docker compose up -d router (running servers are not affected)
  • If the file cannot be patched automatically, a warning shows the lines to add by hand
  • If the compose update fails, the remaining steps still run and the command exits with code 1
mcctl upgrade --dry-run
mcctl upgrade
mcctl upgrade --non-interactive

docs.title: mcctl create
docs.text:
Create a new Minecraft server.

mcctl create [name] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description name Server name (optional, prompts if not provided)

Options:

Option Short Description --type -t Server type (default PAPER): PAPER, VANILLA, FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC, SPIGOT, BUKKIT, PURPUR, QUILT, LEAF, FOLIA, PUFFERFISH, MODRINTH, AUTO_CURSEFORGE --version -v Minecraft version: -v 1.21.1, --version 1.21.1 or --version=1.21.1 (default LATEST; modpack types use the modpack's version) --seed -s World seed for generation. A negative seed works (-s -123); --seed=<value> takes any value --world-url -u Download world from ZIP URL --world -w Use existing world from worlds/ directory --modpack <slug> Modpack slug; required with -t MODRINTH or -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack-version <version> Modpack version (default: latest) --mod-loader <loader> Mod loader of the modpack, e.g. fabric, forge, neoforge, quilt (omit to detect it from the modpack) --exclude-files <list> Comma-separated files to leave out of the modpack, e.g. client-only mods --no-start Create without starting --whitelist Enable whitelist and add initial players (comma-separated, e.g. Steve,Alex) --enable-whitelist Enable whitelist without initial players --no-whitelist Disable whitelist (default; overrides the two options above) --playit-domain <domain> playit.gg external domain of the server (e.g. aa.example.com) --sudo-password Sudo password for mDNS registration (automation)

New servers get 4G of memory (6G for modpack types) and the itzg/minecraft-server tag their VERSION needs, for example java8 for 1.16.5 and java21 for 1.21.1 (java25 for LATEST, a modpack without -v and snapshots; see Java Versions and Image Tags). Interactive mcctl create asks for the memory; afterwards change it with mcctl config <name> MEMORY <size>. For modpack details see Modpacks.

One world, one server

--world (and the default world <name> of a new server) is refused when another server already uses that world. See World Assignment Rules.

What create writes

mcctl create writes servers/<name>/server.yaml and renders config.env, docker-compose.yml and the servers/compose.yml entry from it (Server Definition). If anything fails before the server exists, nothing is left behind, so the same command can be run again. If the server is created but does not start, it stays created and the command exits 1 with the cause; start it with mcctl start <name>.

Whitelist is off by default

Servers created without a whitelist option have the whitelist disabled, so anyone with a premium (online-mode) account can join. Use --whitelist or --enable-whitelist to restrict access, or turn it on later with mcctl whitelist <server> on. In interactive mode you are asked "Enable whitelist?" (default No) and only asked for players when you answer Yes. Servers created from the Web Console are also created with the whitelist off.

Premium account authentication (ONLINE_MODE=TRUE) is unchanged and stays on. Servers created before this change keep their existing whitelist setting.

Automation with Sudo Password

When automating server creation in CI/CD pipelines, you can provide the sudo password for mDNS registration:

  • Environment variable: MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD
  • CLI option: --sudo-password

If avahi-daemon is installed and no password is provided, you will be prompted interactively.

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI ModeModpackAutomation (CI/CD) 
mcctl create
# Prompts for all options

# Basic Paper server
mcctl create myserver

# Forge server with specific version
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.4

# Server with world seed
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 -s 12345

# Using existing world
mcctl create legacy -w old-world -v 1.20.4

# Create without starting
mcctl create myserver --no-start

# Whitelist on with initial players
mcctl create private --whitelist Steve,Alex

# Whitelist on, add players later
mcctl create private --enable-whitelist

# Modrinth modpack by slug
mcctl create cobblemon -t MODRINTH --modpack cobblemon

# Pin the modpack version and loader, leave out client-only mods
mcctl create mypack -t MODRINTH --modpack <slug> --modpack-version <version> --mod-loader fabric --exclude-files <file1>,<file2>

# CurseForge modpack by slug
mcctl create mypack -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack <slug>

For a guided setup, run mcctl create without a name and choose Modrinth Modpack or CurseForge Modpack under "Modpack Platforms". It then asks for the modpack slug, the mod loader (Modrinth only; CurseForge has no loader variable and skips the question), the modpack version and the files to exclude.

# Using environment variable for sudo password
export MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD="your-password"
mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Using --sudo-password option
mcctl create myserver --sudo-password "your-password"

Server Types:

Type Description Plugins Mods PAPER High performance (Recommended) Yes No VANILLA Official Minecraft server No No FORGE Modded server for Forge mods No Yes NEOFORGE Modern Forge fork (1.20.1+) No Yes FABRIC Lightweight modded server No Yes SPIGOT Modified Bukkit server Yes No BUKKIT Classic plugin server Yes No PURPUR Paper fork with more features Yes No QUILT Modern modding toolchain No Yes LEAF Lightweight Paper fork Yes No FOLIA Multi-threaded Paper server for large worlds Yes No PUFFERFISH Paper fork for large servers Yes No MODRINTH Modrinth modpack server No Yes AUTO_CURSEFORGE CurseForge modpack server No Yes

docs.title: mcctl delete
docs.text:
Delete a server.

mcctl delete [name] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description name Server name (optional, shows list if not provided)

Options:

Option Short Description --yes -y Skip confirmation --force Delete even if players are online (implies --yes) --delete-world Delete the world inside the server instead of moving it to worlds/ --sudo-password Sudo password for mDNS deregistration (automation)

mcctl delete asks for confirmation. Without a terminal (scripts, CI) it refuses to delete unless you pass --yes or --force.

Worlds outlive their server

  • A world in worlds/ is kept. It is only no longer assigned to the deleted server.
  • A world inside the server (servers/<name>/data/<LEVEL>, plus <LEVEL>_nether and <LEVEL>_the_end) is moved to worlds/<LEVEL> before the server directory is removed. You can assign it to another server afterwards.
  • If worlds/ already has a folder with the same name, the delete stops and nothing is removed. Rename the folder in worlds/, or pass --delete-world.
  • --delete-world deletes the world inside the server. It never deletes worlds in worlds/; use mcctl world delete for those.

Without --delete-world, the delete also stops before removing anything when the world cannot be kept with certainty:

  • The server's world cannot be determined from config.env. LEVEL is read the way Docker Compose reads the file (quotes, a trailing comment and spaces around = are fine; the last LEVEL line wins), and the delete stops when the value is not a world name (letters, digits, -, _), uses $ interpolation, or EXTRA_ARGS puts --universe somewhere mcctl does not support. These are the rules of World Assignment Rules. Without any LEVEL line the world is world.
  • servers/<name>/ or its data/ is a symlink, or only <LEVEL>_nether/<LEVEL>_the_end exist without data/<LEVEL>.
  • Another world folder (one with level.dat, level.dat_old, region/ or *.mca files, such as an old world from a previous LEVEL) would be deleted, or a symlink inside the server points to something inside the server. The message lists them.

If worlds/ resolves to a folder inside the server (for example a symlink into servers/<name>/), the delete stops even with --delete-world. If the server's container cannot be stopped, or Docker cannot be queried, the delete stops and nothing is removed. If the server is running and its online players cannot be read over RCON, mcctl delete <name> refuses unless you pass --force.

No backup runs before the delete: the world is kept in worlds/ (unless --delete-world). Only one delete of a server runs at a time: a second mcctl delete (or API delete) of the same server fails while the first one runs. Delete handles only the servers/compose.yml entry mcctl writes (<name>/docker-compose.yml); if you wrote another include entry for the server by hand (long form, extra compose files), the delete stops before changing anything and asks you to remove that entry first. The mDNS hostname <name>.local is removed from /etc/avahi/hosts after the server files are gone, with sudo sed -i … /etc/avahi/hosts, the command the README's sudoers NOPASSWD lines allow. The sudo password comes from --sudo-password, MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD or the prompt. If the removal fails (no password and no NOPASSWD rule, for example), the server is still deleted and mcctl delete prints a warning; remove the <name>.local line by hand. Files mcctl delete cannot remove from servers/<name>/ (files the container wrote as root, for example) are a warning too, after the server is out of servers/compose.yml; remove them with the printed sudo rm -rf command.

Examples:

# Interactive - shows server list
mcctl delete

# Delete specific server with confirmation
mcctl delete myserver

# Delete without confirmation
mcctl delete myserver --yes

# Delete the server and the world inside it
mcctl delete myserver --yes --delete-world

# Automation with sudo password
MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD="your-password" mcctl delete myserver --yes

docs.title: mcctl start
docs.text:
Start a stopped server or all servers.

mcctl start <name>
mcctl start --all

Options:

Option Short Description --all -a Start all Minecraft servers (not router)

Examples:

# Start single server
mcctl start myserver

# Start all servers
mcctl start --all

mcctl start <name> creates the container if needed and starts it (docker compose up -d mc-<name>). It exits with code 2 and a warning when the server is already running, and with code 1 when servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml does not exist.

Auto-Start

With mc-router, servers automatically start when a player connects.

docs.title: mcctl stop
docs.text:
Stop a running server or all servers.

mcctl stop <name>
mcctl stop --all

Options:

Option Short Description --all -a Stop all Minecraft servers (not router)

Examples:

# Stop single server
mcctl stop myserver

# Stop all servers
mcctl stop --all

mcctl stop <name> exits with code 2 and a warning when the server is not running. start and stop exit with code 1 when Docker cannot be queried.

With BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP=true and a configured backup, mcctl stop <name> backs up the worlds after the server has stopped, the same way as mcctl backup push --auto: it never prompts and waits up to 10 minutes for a running backup. A failed backup prints a warning; the stop still succeeds (exit code 0). Stopping from the web console or the API (POST /api/servers/<name>/stop) runs the same backup in the background. mcctl stop --all does not back up.

docs.title: mcctl logs
docs.text:
View server logs.

mcctl logs <name|router> [options]

Options:

Option Short Description --follow -f Follow log output --lines -n Number of lines to show (default 50). With -f, shows the last N lines, then keeps following --json Print the lines as a JSON array (not combinable with -f)

Examples:

# Show last 50 lines
mcctl logs survival

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl logs survival -f

# Show last 10 lines
mcctl logs survival -n 10

# mc-router logs
mcctl logs router

Press Ctrl+C to end -f; the exit code is 0. mcctl logs does not cover avahi-daemon; run journalctl -u avahi-daemon yourself if needed.

Output Example: 

[22:09:48] [Server thread/INFO]: Steve joined the game
[22:10:15] [Server thread/INFO]: Alex joined the game
[22:15:30] [Server thread/INFO]: <Steve> Hello everyone!
[22:15:45] [Server thread/INFO]: <Alex> Hi Steve!
[22:20:00] [Server thread/INFO]: Steve has made the advancement [Getting Wood]
[22:25:12] [Server thread/INFO]: Saving the game (this may take a moment!)
[22:25:12] [Server thread/INFO]: Saved the game
[22:30:00] [Server thread/INFO]: Alex left the game
[22:35:15] [RCON Listener #1/INFO]: Thread RCON Client started
[22:35:15] [RCON Client #1/INFO]: Thread RCON Client shutting down

docs.title: mcctl console
docs.text:
Connect to server RCON console. This is the same interactive session as mcctl rcon.

mcctl console <name>

The subcommands mcctl console init, service, user, api and remove manage the Management Console instead; see Console CLI Commands. mcctl admin <subcommand> is a deprecated alias for them. A server with one of these names is reached with mcctl rcon <name>.

Since v3.0.0: TCP RCON instead of docker exec

mcctl console connects to the server's RCON port over TCP (the container address, RCON_PORT and RCON_PASSWORD), like mcctl rcon. It used to run docker exec -i mc-<name> rcon-cli. The server must be running and its RCON port reachable from the host running mcctl. Type exit or quit, or press Ctrl+C/Ctrl+D, to leave. Piped input runs line by line (printf 'list\n' | mcctl console myserver). The session ends when the server closes the connection (for example after stop); a connection error exits with code 1.

Example:

mcctl console myserver

> list
There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Steve, Alex
> say Hello everyone!
> tp Steve Alex

Press Ctrl+C to exit.

docs.title: mcctl rcon
docs.text:
Connect to an interactive RCON console for a Minecraft server. This opens a persistent session where you can execute multiple commands.

mcctl rcon <server>

Example:

$ mcctl rcon survival
[INFO] Connecting to RCON console for 'survival'...
[INFO] Connected! Type "help" for commands, "exit" or Ctrl+C to quit.

> list
There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Steve, Alex
> say Server maintenance in 10 minutes!
[Server: Server maintenance in 10 minutes!]
> tp Steve 0 100 0
Teleported Steve to 0.0, 100.0, 0.0
> exit

When to use rcon vs exec:

Command Mode Use Case mcctl rcon <server> Interactive Manual administration, debugging, multiple commands mcctl exec <server> <cmd> Non-interactive Scripts, automation, CI/CD, single commands

For a complete list of available RCON commands, see RCON Commands Reference.

docs.title: mcctl exec
docs.text:
Execute a single RCON command on a server. This is the non-interactive alternative to mcctl rcon, useful for scripts and automation.

mcctl exec <server> <command...>

Negative numbers are passed as they are (mcctl exec myserver tp Steve -1 64 -5). Put a command with other arguments that start with - after --: mcctl exec myserver -- say -h.

Examples:

# Say message to all players
mcctl exec myserver say "Hello everyone!"

# Give items to player
mcctl exec myserver give Steve diamond 64

# List online players
mcctl exec myserver list

# Change weather
mcctl exec myserver weather clear

# Set time
mcctl exec myserver time set day

# Use in scripts
PLAYERS=$(mcctl exec myserver list)
if echo "$PLAYERS" | grep -q "There are 0 of"; then
  mcctl stop myserver
fi

docs.title: mcctl config
docs.text:
View or modify server configuration.

mcctl config <server> [key] [value] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description server Server name key Configuration key (optional) value New value (optional). An empty value ("") removes the key, so the image default applies again

Shortcut Options:

Option Description --cheats Enable cheats (ALLOW_CHEATS=true) --no-cheats Disable cheats --pvp Enable PvP --no-pvp Disable PvP --command-block Enable command blocks --no-command-block Disable command blocks

--json prints the values, or the change (server, key, oldValue, newValue), as JSON.

Examples:

View All ConfigView Single KeySet ValueUse Shortcuts 
mcctl config survival

Output: 

Configuration for survival:

  TYPE=PAPER
  VERSION=1.21.1
  MEMORY=4G
  MODE=survival
  DIFFICULTY=normal
  MAX_PLAYERS=20
  VIEW_DISTANCE=10
  PVP=true
  SPAWN_PROTECTION=0
  LEVEL=survival-world
  ENABLE_RCON=true
  MOTD=Welcome to survival! Your adventure begins here.
  ALLOW_CHEATS=false
  ENABLE_COMMAND_BLOCK=true
  OPS=Steve


mcctl config survival MOTD

mcctl config survival MOTD "Welcome to my server!"
mcctl config survival MAX_PLAYERS 50

mcctl config survival --cheats
mcctl config survival --no-pvp
mcctl config survival --command-block

Restart Required

Some configuration changes require a server restart to take effect.

Removing a key

mcctl config <server> MOTD "" removes MOTD from the server's config and says so; a key that is not set is reported and nothing changes. LEVEL and WORLD_NAME cannot be removed this way: set a world name instead.

Changing LEVEL

LEVEL is the world the server uses (see World Assignment Rules). mcctl config <server> LEVEL <world> is refused while the server is running and when another server uses <world>. The same applies to EXTRA_ARGS when the new value moves the world between worlds/ and servers/<server>/data (--universe).

docs.title: mcctl server-backup
docs.text:
Back up a server's configuration files to backups/servers/<server>/<id>.tar.gz: config.env, docker-compose.yml and, when present, server.yaml, data/ops.json, data/whitelist.json, data/banned-players.json, data/banned-ips.json and data/server.properties. The ID is the creation time (20260120-203357).

mcctl server-backup <server> [options]

Options:

Option Short Description --message -m Backup description --list List all backups for server --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

# Backup with message
mcctl server-backup survival -m "Before upgrade"

# List all backups
mcctl server-backup survival --list

Output Example (--list): 

Backups for survival:

  20260120-203357
    Created: 1/20/2026, 8:33:57 PM
    Size: 3 KB, Files: 7
    Description: Before upgrade

  20260118-150000
    Created: 1/18/2026, 3:00:00 PM
    Size: 3 KB, Files: 7
    Description: Initial setup

docs.title: mcctl server-restore
docs.text:
Restore server configuration from backup.

mcctl server-restore <server> [backup-id] [options]

Options:

Option Description --force Skip confirmation --dry-run Show what would be restored --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

# Interactive - shows backup list
mcctl server-restore myserver

# Restore specific backup
mcctl server-restore myserver 20260120-203357

# Preview restoration
mcctl server-restore myserver 20260120-203357 --dry-run

It asks before restoring unless --force or --json is given. The current files are copied to backups/servers/<server>/.pre-restore/ first. Restart the server to apply the restored files.

docs.title: mcctl config-snapshot
docs.text:
Save and restore copies of a server's configuration files. A snapshot holds the files in servers/<server>/ itself (not data/): server.yaml, config.env, docker-compose.yml and any other .yml, .yaml, .json or .properties file up to 1 MB. Snapshots are stored in backups/meta/config-snapshots.db and backups/meta/config-snapshot-storage/.

mcctl config-snapshot <list|create|show|diff|restore|delete> [args] [options]
Command Description list [server] List snapshots, newest first (--limit <n>, default 20; --json) create <server> Create a snapshot (--description "..."; --json) show <id> Show a snapshot (--files lists its files; --json) diff <id1> <id2> Show what changed between two snapshots (--files-only; --json) restore <id> Write the snapshot's files back to servers/<server>/; asks first unless --force delete <id> Delete a snapshot; asks first unless --force

The other commands need the full snapshot ID, which list, create and list --json print. A restore that changes the server's world follows the World Assignment Rules. Restart the server to apply restored files.

Examples:

mcctl config-snapshot create survival --description "Before mod update"
mcctl config-snapshot list survival
mcctl config-snapshot diff <id1> <id2> --files-only
mcctl config-snapshot restore <id>

docs.title: mcctl config-snapshot schedule
docs.text:
Create snapshots on a schedule. The schedules are run by mcctl-api, which checks them every minute: a change made here applies within a minute.

Command Description schedule list List schedules (--server <name>; --json) schedule add Add a schedule: --server <name>, --cron "<expression>" and --name "<name>" are required; --retention <n> keeps the newest n snapshots of this schedule (default 10); --json schedule remove <id> Remove a schedule; asks first unless --force schedule enable <id> Enable a schedule schedule disable <id> Disable a schedule 
mcctl config-snapshot schedule add --server survival --cron "0 3 * * *" --name "Daily"

docs.title: mcctl op
docs.text:
Manage server operators.

mcctl op <server> <action> [player] [level]

Actions:

Action Description list Show operators with their level and role (read from data/ops.json) add <player> [level] Add operator: OPS in config.env, and over RCON when the server is running (the level is then written to data/ops.json). Without a level it asks in a terminal; with --json it uses 4 remove <player> Remove operator set-level <player> <level> Change an operator's level in data/ops.json. The server must be running; restart it to apply

Levels: 1 Moderator, 2 Gamemaster, 3 Admin, 4 Owner. --json prints the result as JSON.

Examples:

# List operators
mcctl op survival list

# Add operator (asks for the level)
mcctl op survival add Steve

# Add operator with level 2
mcctl op survival add Alex 2

# Change the level
mcctl op survival set-level Alex 3

# Remove operator
mcctl op survival remove Steve

Output Example (list): 

Operators for survival:

  Player       Level             Role
  ------------------------------------------------------------
  Steve                4   Owner
  Alex                 2   Gamemaster

docs.title: mcctl whitelist
docs.text:
Manage server whitelist.

mcctl whitelist <server> <action> [player]

Actions:

Action Description list Show whitelisted players add <player> Add to whitelist remove <player> Remove from whitelist on Enable whitelist off Disable whitelist status Show whitelist status

--json prints the result as JSON.

Examples:

# List whitelisted players
mcctl whitelist survival list

# Add player
mcctl whitelist survival add Steve

# Enable whitelist
mcctl whitelist survival on

# Check status
mcctl whitelist survival status

Output Example (list): 

Whitelist for survival:

  Steve
  Alex
  Notch

Output Example (status): 

Whitelist Status for survival:

  Enabled: Yes
  Players: 3
  Running: Yes

docs.title: mcctl ban
docs.text:
Manage player and IP bans.

mcctl ban <server> <action> [target] [reason]
mcctl ban <server> ip <action> [ip] [reason]

Player Ban Actions:

Action Description list Show banned players add <player> [reason] Ban player remove <player> Unban player

IP Ban Actions:

Action Description ip list Show banned IPs ip add <ip> [reason] Ban IP address ip remove <ip> Unban IP address

--json prints the result as JSON.

Examples:

# List banned players
mcctl ban survival list

# Ban player with reason
mcctl ban survival add Griefer "Griefing spawn area"

# Unban player
mcctl ban survival remove Griefer

# List banned IPs
mcctl ban survival ip list

# Ban IP
mcctl ban survival ip add 192.168.1.100 "Spam"

Output Example (list): 

Banned Players for survival:

  Griefer - Griefing spawn area

docs.title: mcctl kick
docs.text:
Kick a player from the server.

mcctl kick <server> <player> [reason]

The server must be running. --json prints the result as JSON.

Examples:

# Kick player
mcctl kick myserver Steve

# Kick with reason
mcctl kick myserver Steve "AFK too long"

docs.title: mcctl player online
docs.text:
Show online players on servers.

mcctl player online <server>
mcctl player online --all

Options:

Option Short Description --all -a Show players on all servers --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

Single ServerAll Servers 
mcctl player online survival

Output: 

Online Players for survival:

  Status: Running (2/20)

  Steve
  Alex


mcctl player online --all

Output: 

Online Players (All Servers):

  Total: 2 players

  survival (2/20):
    Steve
    Alex

Running servers with no players online are left out.

docs.title: World Assignment Rules
docs.text:
A world is assigned to a server by the server's LEVEL in servers/<name>/config.env. If LEVEL is unset, the legacy WORLD_NAME is read; if both are unset the server uses itzg's default world.

  • No lock file. worlds/.locks is no longer read, written or created (mcctl init does not create it). An existing worlds/.locks directory is harmless; rm -rf worlds/.locks is safe. The lock.sh and mcctl.sh scripts were removed (#670, #734).
  • One world, one server. A world and its <world>_nether / <world>_the_end folders count as one world. A world used by another server cannot be assigned: mcctl world assign, mcctl create --world, a new server's default world <name>, and mcctl config <server> LEVEL <world> are refused. Deleting a server frees its world for reuse.
  • Stopped server only. world assign, world release, world new --server and config LEVEL are refused while the server's container is running, paused, restarting or created. Nothing is stopped automatically (world new --server used to try to stop the server; it now refuses).
  • Fail-closed. If any server's config.env cannot be read, or its LEVEL cannot be interpreted safely, every assignment change and world delete/reset is refused until it is fixed. Unsafe values are path separators, . or .., quotes, control characters, Compose interpolation such as ${VAR} outside single quotes, and an unsupported --universe location. Legacy names such as My World are still accepted as existing values; new names must be letters, digits, - or _.
  • Older installs. Duplicate assignments are reported, not fixed: see mcctl world list.

docs.title: mcctl world new
docs.text:
Create a new world directory with optional seed configuration. The command never starts a server: with --server it only assigns the world (sets LEVEL); run mcctl start <server> afterwards. Only the interactive form asks whether to start the server.

mcctl world new [name] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description name World name (optional, prompts if not provided)

Options:

Option Short Description --seed -s World seed for generation. A negative seed works (-s -123); --seed=<value> takes any value --server Server to assign world to (sets LEVEL, and SEED if given). The server must be stopped --no-start Interactive mode: do not ask whether to start the server, and do not start it --json Print the result as JSON

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl world new
# Prompts for:
# 1. World name
# 2. Optional seed
# 3. Server to assign the world to (must be stopped)
# 4. Whether to start the server

# Create empty world directory
mcctl world new myworld

# Create world with specific seed
mcctl world new myworld --seed 12345

# Create and assign to server
mcctl world new myworld --server myserver

# Create with seed and assign to server
mcctl world new myworld --seed 12345 --server myserver

With a world name the server is not started; start it with mcctl start <server>.

What it does:

  1. Creates world directory in worlds/<name>/ with a .meta file (name, seed, creation time)
  2. If server assigned:
  3. Refuses if the server is running or the world is used by another server (the server is not stopped for you)
  4. Updates server's config.env with LEVEL=<world-name>
  5. Sets SEED=<seed> if provided
  6. In interactive mode, starts the server if you answer yes

mcctl world new needs at least one server; without any it stops with No servers available. Create a server first.

Seed Behavior

The seed is applied via the server's SEED environment variable. The world is generated with this seed when the server first starts.

docs.title: mcctl world list
docs.text:
List all worlds with the servers they are assigned to.

mcctl world list [options]

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

Default OutputJSON Output 
mcctl world list

Output: 

Worlds:

  survival-world

mcctl world list --json

Output: 

[

    "name": "survival-world",
    "path": "/home/myuser/minecraft-servers/worlds/survival-world",
    "isLocked": true,
    "lockedBy": "survival",
    "size": "514.0MB",
    "lastModified": "2026-01-21T13:19:48.853Z",

Duplicate assignments

If an older install has two servers on the same world, mcctl world list shows assigned: a, b and prints a warning for each duplicate (and for each server whose config.env cannot be read). Nothing is fixed automatically: assign another world to all but one of the servers. isLocked and lockedBy remain in the JSON output as aliases for "assigned".

docs.title: mcctl world assign
docs.text:
Assign a world to a server (sets the server's LEVEL).

mcctl world assign [world] [server]

Arguments:

Argument Description world World name (optional, prompts if not provided) server Server name (optional, prompts if not provided)

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl world assign
# Shows world list, then server list

mcctl world assign survival myserver

One world, one server

A world used by another server cannot be assigned, and the target server must be stopped. This prevents data corruption from simultaneous access. A server that keeps its world inside servers/<name>/data is refused too: run mcctl migrate worlds first. See World Assignment Rules.

docs.title: mcctl world release
docs.text:
Switch the server that uses a world back to its own default world <server>.

mcctl world release [world] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description world World name (optional, prompts if not provided)

Options:

Option Description

Examples:

# Interactive - shows assigned worlds
mcctl world release

# Release specific world
mcctl world release survival

The server using the world gets LEVEL=<server>: an existing free worlds/<server> is adopted, otherwise the world is created on the next start. The world itself is kept in worlds/.

Release is refused when the server is running, when the server already uses its own default world, when the world is assigned to more than one server, when the server keeps its world inside servers/<name>/data, and when no server uses the world.

docs.title: mcctl world delete
docs.text:
Permanently delete a world and all its data.

mcctl world delete [world] [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description world World name (optional, prompts if not provided)

Options:

Option Short Description --force Skip the confirmation (does not delete a world a server uses) --yes -y Same as --force for the confirmation --json Output in JSON format (still needs --force or -y to delete)

-f is --follow, not --force.

Permanent Deletion

This command permanently deletes all world data including:

  • World files (level.dat, region data, etc.)
  • Nether and End dimensions
  • Player data for that world

This action cannot be undone. Make sure to backup important worlds before deletion.

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl world delete
# Shows world list for selection
# Asks for confirmation before deletion

# Delete with confirmation prompt (default No; needs a terminal)
mcctl world delete old-world

# Delete without confirmation (scripts, CI)
mcctl world delete old-world --force
mcctl world delete old-world -y

Safety Features:

  • Assignment Check: Cannot delete a world that any server uses, running or not; --force does not override this. Assign another world to the server first. Servers that keep their world inside servers/<name>/data (no EXTRA_ARGS=--universe /worlds/) do not block deleting worlds/<world>
  • Fail-closed: Refused while any server's config.env cannot be read or interpreted (see World Assignment Rules)
  • Confirmation Prompt: Asks for confirmation (yes/no, default No) before deleting, unless --force or -y. Without a terminal (a script, a pipe) and without --force/-y, the command refuses and exits 1; --json alone does not delete either. The REST API DELETE /api/worlds/:name is not affected
  • Size: The confirmation shows the world name and size; after deleting, the freed size is printed

docs.title: mcctl backup init
docs.text:
Set up the GitHub world backup interactively.

mcctl backup init [--force]

It asks for a GitHub personal access token, the repository (username/repo), the branch and whether to back up when a server stops. After testing access to the repository it writes BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO, BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH and BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP to .env. If a backup is already configured it asks before overwriting; --force skips that question. Creating the repository and the token is described in the Backup Guide.

docs.title: mcctl backup status
docs.text:
Show backup configuration status. mcctl backup without a subcommand does the same.

mcctl backup status [options]

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Example:

mcctl backup status

Output (configured):

Backup Configuration:

  Status: Configured
  Repository: myuser/minecraft-backup-repo
  Branch: main
  Last backup: 1/20/2026, 9:06:35 PM
  Auto backup: enabled

Output (not configured):

Backup Configuration:

  Status: Not configured

  To enable backups, set in .env:
    BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN=your-token
    BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO=username/repo

mcctl backup init writes these settings for you.

docs.title: mcctl backup push
docs.text:
Push world data to GitHub repository.

mcctl backup push [options]

Options:

Option Short Description --message -m Commit message --auto No prompt; timestamp message; waits up to 10 min for a running backup (the same rules as the auto-backup on stop) --allow-missing Drop worlds from the backup that were deleted on purpose (see Backup Guide)

Running servers are flushed (save-off, save-all flush, save-on) before the copy. "No changes" is a success.

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl backup push
# Prompts for commit message

mcctl backup push -m "Before server upgrade"

docs.title: mcctl backup history

docs.title: mcctl backup restore
docs.text:
Restore world data from a backup.

mcctl backup restore [commit] [--force]

Arguments:

Argument Description commit Commit hash (optional, shows list if not provided) --force Do not ask for confirmation

Every server must be stopped. The result is exactly the commit, worlds/.locks is kept, and the replaced data is kept in backups/restore-previous/<timestamp>/. See the Backup Guide.

Examples:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl backup restore
# Shows backup history for selection

mcctl backup restore abc1234

Data Overwrite

Restore will overwrite current world data. Make sure to backup before restoring.

docs.title: mcctl backup schedule
docs.text:
Back up the worlds on a schedule. The schedules are run by mcctl-api, which checks them every minute: a change made here applies within a minute.

Command Description backup schedule list List schedules (--json) backup schedule add Add a schedule: --cron <expression or preset> (required; presets hourly, daily, every-6h, every-12h, weekly), --name <name> (default Backup Schedule), --max-count <n>, --max-age-days <n>, --json backup schedule remove <id> Remove a schedule backup schedule enable <id> Enable a schedule backup schedule disable <id> Disable a schedule

After each scheduled backup, backups beyond the newest --max-count and backups older than --max-age-days are removed from the repository history (the latest backup is always kept). See Scheduled Backups.

mcctl backup schedule add --cron daily --name "Daily Backup" --max-count 30

docs.title: mcctl player (Interactive Mode)
docs.text:
Unified player management with interactive workflow.

mcctl player
mcctl player <server>

Examples:

Full InteractiveServer-Specific 
mcctl player
# 1. Select server from list
# 2. Select online player or enter name
# 3. Select action (op/deop, whitelist, ban, kick, info)

mcctl player myserver
# 1. Select online player or enter name
# 2. Select action

The interactive mode provides:

  • Server selection (running servers only; the actions run over RCON)
  • Online player list with easy selection
  • Action menu (op/deop, whitelist add/remove, ban/unban, kick, view info)

docs.title: mcctl player info
docs.text:
Look up player information from Mojang API with encrypted local caching.

mcctl player info <name> [options]

Options:

Option Description --offline Calculate offline-mode UUID instead of Mojang lookup --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

# Look up player info (UUID, skin URL)
mcctl player info Notch

# Offline UUID calculation
mcctl player info Steve --offline

# JSON output for scripting
mcctl player info Notch --json

Output:

Player: Notch
  UUID: 069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5
  Skin: http://textures.minecraft.net/texture/292009a4925b58f02c77dadc3ecef07ea4c7472f64e0fdc32ce5522489362680
  Source: mojang

JSON Output:

{
  "name": "Notch",
  "uuid": "069a79f4-44e9-4726-a5be-fca90e38aaf5",
  "uuidNoDashes": "069a79f444e94726a5befca90e38aaf5",
  "skinUrl": "https://textures.minecraft.net/texture/...",
  "source": "mojang"
}

Player Cache

Player data is cached locally with AES-256-GCM encryption:

  • UUID: Cached permanently (never changes)
  • Username: Cached for 30 days (can change)
  • Skin URL: Cached for 1 day (changes frequently)

Cache location: ~/.mcctl/.player-cache

docs.title: mcctl player cache
docs.text:
Manage the encrypted player data cache.

mcctl player cache <action>

Actions:

Action Description stats Show cache statistics clear Clear all cached player data

Examples:

# View cache statistics
mcctl player cache stats

# Clear all cached data
mcctl player cache clear

Stats Output:

Player Cache Statistics
  Players cached: 5
  Cache size: 2.1 KB

mcctl player online is described under Player Management.

Removed

mcctl player lookup and mcctl player uuid were removed. Use mcctl player info <name> (add --offline for the offline UUID). The old player.sh computed a wrong offline UUID for some names (for example Steve and Alex) because of a variant-bit bug; mcctl player info --offline matches Minecraft.

docs.title: mcctl migrate status
docs.text:
Check migration status for all servers.

mcctl migrate status [options]

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Example:

mcctl migrate status

Output:

Migration Status:

  survival: needs migration
    Missing EXTRA_ARGS=--universe /worlds/
  creative: up to date

1 server(s) need migration.
Run: mcctl migrate worlds to migrate.

docs.title: mcctl migrate worlds
docs.text:
Migrate worlds to the shared /worlds/ directory structure.

mcctl migrate worlds [options]

Options:

Option Description --all Migrate all servers without selection --server <name> Migrate only this server --dry-run Preview changes without applying --backup Create backup before migration --force Skip confirmation prompts

Examples:

Interactive ModeMigrate AllDry RunWith Backup 
mcctl migrate worlds
# Shows servers needing migration, select one or all

mcctl migrate worlds --all

mcctl migrate worlds --dry-run

Output: 

DRY RUN - No changes will be made

Would migrate: survival
  1. Stop server if running
  2. Move world: servers/survival/data/world → worlds/survival
  3. Update config.env:
     - Add: EXTRA_ARGS=--universe /worlds/
     - Set: LEVEL=survival


mcctl migrate worlds --all --backup

What Migration Does:

  1. Stops server if running
  2. Moves world data from servers/<name>/data/world to worlds/<server-name>/
  3. Updates config.env:
  4. Adds EXTRA_ARGS=--universe /worlds/
  5. Sets LEVEL=<server-name>
  6. Detects existing worlds with case-insensitive matching

If the resulting LEVEL is used by another server, or a server's assignment cannot be determined, the migration of that server is refused before any data is moved (see World Assignment Rules).

World Storage Change

New servers created with mcctl create already use the /worlds/ directory structure. This migration command is for existing servers created before this change.

docs.title: mcctl migrate spec
docs.text:
Import servers into their definition file servers/<name>/server.yaml and write the files rendered from it (config.env, docker-compose.yml, the servers/compose.yml entry). See Server Definition.

mcctl migrate spec <server> [options]
mcctl migrate spec --all [options]

Options:

Option Description --all Every server --dry-run Report what would be imported; write nothing --force Re-render from server.yaml over hand edits of the generated files (keeps .bak copies) --json Print the per-server report as JSON

Running it again is safe: a server that is in sync is reported as synced and nothing is rewritten. A server is refused (exit 1) when its world or image cannot be determined, for example a ${...} value in config.env. A changed world.level is checked against the World Assignment Rules and needs the server to be stopped.

You do not have to run this: a server without server.yaml is imported the first time mcctl changes it, and mcctl upgrade lists the servers not imported yet.

docs.title: Mod Management
docs.text: Manage mods and plugins for your Minecraft servers. mcctl integrates with multiple mod sources including Modrinth, CurseForge, Spiget (SpigotMC), and direct URL downloads.

docs.title: mcctl mod search
docs.text:
Search for mods on Modrinth.

mcctl mod search <query> [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description query Search query (mod name, description keywords)

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

# Search for optimization mods
mcctl mod search sodium

# Search for world generation mods
mcctl mod search "world generation"

# JSON output for scripting
mcctl mod search lithium --json

Output Example:

Search results for "sodium" on Modrinth (25 total):

  sodium (12.5M downloads)
    Sodium server client
    A modern rendering engine for Minecraft

  sodium-extra (2.1M downloads)
    Sodium Extra server? client
    Extra options for Sodium

Use: mcctl mod add <server> <mod-slug> to install

The output shows:

  • Mod slug (used for installation)
  • Download count (popularity indicator)
  • Side requirements (server/client/both)
  • Description (truncated)

docs.title: mcctl mod add
docs.text:
Add mods to a server configuration.

mcctl mod add <server> <mod...> [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description server Server name mod... One or more mod slugs/IDs

Options:

Option Description --modrinth Use Modrinth (default) --curseforge Use CurseForge (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+) --spiget Use Spiget (SpigotMC plugins) --url Direct JAR URL download --force Add even if mod not found or server type mismatch --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

Modrinth (Default)CurseForgeSpiget (SpigotMC)Direct URL 
# Add single mod
mcctl mod add myserver sodium

# Add multiple mods at once
mcctl mod add myserver sodium lithium phosphor

# Add to Fabric server
mcctl mod add fabric-server fabric-api sodium lithium

# CF_API_KEY in .env is optional on Java 17+ images
mcctl mod add myserver --curseforge jei journeymap

# Add popular modpack mods
mcctl mod add myserver --curseforge create applied-energistics-2

# Use resource IDs from SpigotMC
mcctl mod add myserver --spiget 9089 1649

# EssentialsX example (resource ID: 9089)
mcctl mod add paper-server --spiget 9089

# Download JAR directly from URL
mcctl mod add myserver --url https://example.com/mod.jar

# Multiple URLs
mcctl mod add myserver --url https://example.com/mod1.jar https://example.com/mod2.jar

How It Works:

  1. Validation: Verifies mod exists on Modrinth (if using Modrinth source)
  2. Server Type Check: Refuses server types without mod or plugin support (for example VANILLA) unless --force
  3. Config Update: Adds mod to appropriate environment variable in config.env
  4. Restart Required: Server must be restarted to apply changes

Environment Variables Used:

Source Environment Variable Server Types Modrinth MODRINTH_PROJECTS All CurseForge CURSEFORGE_FILES All (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+) Spiget SPIGET_RESOURCES Paper, Spigot, Bukkit URL MODS Forge, NeoForge, Fabric, Quilt URL PLUGINS Paper, Spigot, Bukkit

⚠️ Automatic Dependency Download

Mods often require other mods as dependencies (e.g., Iris requires Sodium).

By default, dependencies are automatically downloaded via the MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=required setting in config.env.

Setting Behavior required Download required dependencies automatically (DEFAULT, RECOMMENDED) optional Download required + optional dependencies none Don't download dependencies (manual management)

Example: When you add iris, it automatically downloads sodium (required dependency).

mcctl mod add myserver iris
# ✓ iris added
# ✓ sodium automatically downloaded on server start (required dependency)

Output Example:

Validating mods on Modrinth...
  ✓ Sodium (sodium)
  ✓ Lithium (lithium)

✓ Added 2 mod(s) to myserver

  sodium
  lithium

Config: MODRINTH_PROJECTS=sodium,lithium

Restart the server to apply changes:
  mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: mcctl mod list
docs.text:
List configured mods for a server.

mcctl mod list <server> [options]

Examples:

# List mods for server

docs.title: mcctl mod remove
docs.text:
Remove mods from a server configuration.

mcctl mod remove <server> <mod...> [options]

Arguments:

Argument Description server Server name mod... One or more mod slugs/IDs to remove

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Examples:

# Remove single mod
mcctl mod remove myserver sodium

# Remove multiple mods
mcctl mod remove myserver sodium lithium phosphor

Output Example:

Restart Required

Removed mods will still be present in the server's mods folder until the server is restarted. On restart, the itzg/minecraft-server image will sync the mods folder with the configuration.

docs.title: mcctl mod sources

docs.title: Setting Up a Modded Server
docs.text:
Complete workflow for creating and configuring a modded Fabric server:

# 1. Create a Fabric server
mcctl create modded-server -t FABRIC -v 1.20.4

# 2. Search for mods
mcctl mod search "optimization"

# 3. Add essential mods
mcctl mod add modded-server fabric-api sodium lithium phosphor

# 4. List configured mods
mcctl mod list modded-server

# 5. Restart to apply
mcctl stop modded-server && mcctl start modded-server

docs.title: Setting Up a Plugin Server
docs.text:
Complete workflow for a Paper server with plugins:

# 1. Create a Paper server
mcctl create plugin-server -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# 2. Add plugins from Modrinth
mcctl mod add plugin-server luckperms

# 3. Add plugins from Spiget (SpigotMC)
mcctl mod add plugin-server --spiget 9089  # EssentialsX

# 4. Restart to apply
mcctl stop plugin-server && mcctl start plugin-server

docs.title: CurseForge Configuration
docs.text:
Java 17+ images include a built-in CF_API_KEY; set it only for java8/pre-17 tags or to use your own key. To set your own key:

  1. Get an API key from CurseForge for Studios
  2. Add to your .env file:
CF_API_KEY=your-api-key-here
  1. Now you can add CurseForge mods:
mcctl mod add myserver --curseforge jei journeymap

docs.title: mcctl playit
docs.text:
Manage the playit.gg agent and the servers' external domains. Setting up playit.gg is described in External Access (playit.gg).

mcctl playit <start|stop|status|setup|domain> [args]
Command Description start Start the playit-agent container (needs PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY and playit.gg enabled) stop Stop the agent status Show the agent state, whether PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY is set and the servers with a playit.gg domain (--json) setup Ask for the PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY, save it to .env, enable playit.gg and add the playit service to docker-compose.yml if it is missing domain <server> <domain> Set a server's playit.gg domain (PLAYIT_DOMAIN) domain <server> --remove Remove a server's playit.gg domain

Without arguments, mcctl playit domain asks for the server and the domain. A domain change takes effect after mcctl stop <server> && mcctl start <server>; restarting the container does not apply it.

docs.title: mcctl audit
docs.text:
Show and clean up the audit log of actions taken with the CLI, the API and the web console. Details, action names and settings: Audit Log.

mcctl audit <list|stats|purge> [options]
Command Description list Show entries, newest first: --limit <n> (default 50), --action, --actor, --target, --status <status> (success or failure), --from <date>, --to <date> stats Count the entries by status, action and actor purge Delete entries older than --days <n> (default 90) or before --before <date>; asks first unless --force; --dry-run only counts

docs.title: Global Options Reference
docs.text:
Option Description Example --root <path> Data directory (default: MCCTL_ROOT or ~/minecraft-servers) mcctl --root /opt/mc status --json JSON output, for the commands that support it (listed with each command) mcctl status --json --sudo-password <pwd> Sudo password for the mDNS entry of create and delete (or MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD) mcctl delete myserver --yes --sudo-password "..." -h, --help Show help (the same page for every command) mcctl --help --version Show version mcctl --version

An option that needs a value takes it from the next word (--seed 123) or after = (--seed=123). Switches such as --force, --json and --yes also accept =true or =false. Everything after -- is passed on unchanged (mcctl exec myserver -- say -h).

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Environment variables for automation and CI/CD pipelines.

docs.title: NO_COLOR
docs.text: When NO_COLOR is set to a non-empty value, mcctl prints no ANSI color codes (see no-color.org). An empty value is ignored.

docs.title: MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD
docs.text:
Provides sudo password for operations requiring root access (mDNS registration/deregistration).

export MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD="your-password"

Used by:

  • mcctl create - For registering mDNS hostname with avahi-daemon
  • mcctl delete - For deregistering mDNS hostname

Example (CI/CD):

# GitHub Actions example
- name: Create Minecraft Server
  env:
    MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.SUDO_PASSWORD }}
  run: |
    mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

Security

Store sudo passwords securely using CI/CD secrets. Never commit passwords to version control.

Alternative: Use --sudo-password option directly:

mcctl create myserver --sudo-password "your-password"

docs.title: MCCTL_ROOT
docs.text:
Data directory used when --root is not given (default: ~/minecraft-servers).

export MCCTL_ROOT=/opt/minecraft

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: RCON (Remote Console) allows server administrators to execute Minecraft server commands remotely. This guide covers all available RCON commands you can use with mcctl.

docs.title: mcctl RCON Commands
docs.text: Command Mode Description mcctl rcon <server> Interactive Open RCON console session mcctl console <server> Interactive Same session as mcctl rcon mcctl exec <server> <cmd> Non-interactive Execute single command

docs.title: When to Use Each
docs.text: Use Case Command Manual server administration mcctl rcon myserver Multiple commands in sequence mcctl rcon myserver Debugging and troubleshooting mcctl rcon myserver Shell scripts and automation mcctl exec myserver <cmd> CI/CD pipelines mcctl exec myserver <cmd> Cron jobs mcctl exec myserver <cmd>

docs.title: Interactive Mode (rcon)
docs.text:
$ mcctl rcon survival
[INFO] Connecting to RCON console for 'survival'...
[INFO] Connected! Type "help" for commands, "exit" or Ctrl+C to quit.

> list
There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Steve, Alex
> say Server maintenance in 10 minutes!
[Server: Server maintenance in 10 minutes!]
> tp Steve 0 100 0
Teleported Steve to 0.0, 100.0, 0.0
> exit
$

docs.title: Non-interactive Mode (exec)
docs.text:
# Single command execution
$ mcctl exec survival list
There are 2 of a max of 20 players online: Steve, Alex

# Scripting example
$ mcctl exec myserver say "Backup starting..."
[Server: Backup starting...]

# Use in scripts
PLAYERS=$(mcctl exec myserver list)
if echo "$PLAYERS" | grep -q "There are 0 of"; then
  mcctl stop myserver
fi

docs.title: Configuration Overview
docs.text: This section covers all configuration options for the Docker Minecraft Server platform.

docs.title: Quick Configuration with mcctl
docs.text:
mcctl provides the easiest way to configure servers:

# View all configuration
mcctl config myserver

# View specific setting
mcctl config myserver MOTD

# Change settings
mcctl config myserver MOTD "Welcome to my server!"
mcctl config myserver MAX_PLAYERS 50
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G

# Use shortcuts
mcctl config myserver --cheats        # Enable cheats
mcctl config myserver --no-pvp        # Disable PvP
mcctl config myserver --command-block # Enable command blocks

Recommended Approach

Use mcctl config for most configuration changes. It handles validation and applies changes correctly.

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
For reference, the platform uses these configuration files (under ~/minecraft-servers/):

File Purpose Managed By .env Platform settings. Only the keys named in servers/global.env reach servers mcctl init servers/global.env Names of the .env keys passed to every server mcctl init, mcctl upgrade servers/<name>/server.yaml Server definition mcctl create, mcctl config and every other mcctl change servers/<name>/config.env Server environment variables, generated from server.yaml mcctl docker-compose.yml Main orchestration: mc-router and its settings mcctl init servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml Server container, generated from server.yaml mcctl servers/compose.yml List of the server compose files mcctl

See Server Definition (server.yaml) for how mcctl keeps the generated files in step.

docs.title: Configuration Categories
docs.text:
• :material-cog:{ .lg .middle } Environment Variables

    Complete reference for all environment variables

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Environment Variables

  • :material-server:{ .lg .middle } Server Types

    Paper, Forge, Fabric, and other server platforms

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Server Types

  • :material-file-document:{ .lg .middle } Server Definition

    server.yaml, the file mcctl writes each server's files from

    :octicons-arrow-right-24: Server Definition

docs.title: Change Server Memory
docs.text:
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: Change Minecraft Version
docs.text:
mcctl config myserver VERSION 1.21.1
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

VERSION does not change the server's Java image. A new server gets the tag its VERSION needs; after changing VERSION, run mcctl update or see Java Versions and Image Tags.

docs.title: Enable Mods/Plugins
docs.text:
For mod servers (Forge/Fabric):

# Modrinth mods
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# CurseForge mods (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+ images)
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap"

For plugin servers (Paper/Spigot), place plugins in shared/plugins/ directory.

docs.title: Configure Auto-Scaling
docs.text:
mc-router reads its auto-scaling settings from the router service in ~/minecraft-servers/docker-compose.yml, not from .env:

services:
  router:
    environment:
      AUTO_SCALE_UP: "true"         # Auto-start servers on player connect
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN: "true"       # Auto-stop idle servers
      AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER: "10m"  # Idle timeout
      DOCKER_TIMEOUT: "120s"        # Server startup timeout (Go time.Duration: 120s, 2m)

# Show mc-router status and routes
mcctl status router

# After editing docker-compose.yml, recreate mc-router
mcctl router start

mcctl router restart keeps the old settings; mcctl router start recreates the container from the edited file. mcctl upgrade changes only the router image and group_add in this file, so your edits stay. To turn auto-scaling off for one server, set routing.autoScale in its server.yaml.

docs.title: Change Server Properties
docs.text:
# Game settings
mcctl config myserver DIFFICULTY hard
mcctl config myserver MODE survival
mcctl config myserver MAX_PLAYERS 30

# World settings
mcctl config myserver SPAWN_PROTECTION 0
mcctl config myserver VIEW_DISTANCE 12

# Enable whitelist
mcctl whitelist myserver on
mcctl whitelist myserver add Steve

docs.title: Configuration Priority
docs.text:
Settings are applied in this order (later overrides earlier):

  1. Default values - Built into itzg/minecraft-server image
  2. servers/global.env - The platform keys it names (TZ, EXTRA_ARGS, RCON_PASSWORD, RCON_PORT), with their values from .env
  3. Server config.env - Per-server values, generated from server.yaml (via mcctl config)
  4. environment in the server's docker-compose.yml - Only EULA=TRUE

Other .env keys do not reach servers. To pass one to every server, add its name to servers/global.env (see Setting Classification).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
After configuration changes, verify the server status:

# Check server configuration
mcctl config myserver

# Check server status
mcctl status myserver

# View logs for any errors
mcctl logs myserver -n 50

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
For settings not supported by mcctl config, edit config files directly:

# Edit global settings
nano ~/minecraft-servers/.env

# Edit server-specific settings
nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

# Restart to apply changes
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

mcctl writes config.env and the server's docker-compose.yml from servers/<name>/server.yaml. A hand edit of config.env is taken into server.yaml the next time mcctl changes the server. Edits to docker-compose.yml outside image and the mc-router.* labels, such as resource limits, are kept, but a later change that has to rewrite the file stops with compose_edited. See Hand edits and the value rules for config.env.

When to Edit Files Directly

Direct file editing is only needed for:

  • Advanced JVM options (JVM_OPTS, JVM_DD_OPTS)
  • Custom environment variables
  • Docker resource limits

For standard settings, prefer mcctl config.

docs.text: Complete reference for all environment variables used in the platform.

docs.title: Quick Configuration with mcctl
docs.text:
Most settings can be configured using mcctl config:

# View current configuration
mcctl config myserver

# Change settings
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G
mcctl config myserver MOTD "Welcome!"
mcctl config myserver MAX_PLAYERS 50

# Shortcuts for common settings
mcctl config myserver --cheats        # Enable cheats
mcctl config myserver --no-pvp        # Disable PvP
mcctl config myserver --command-block # Enable command blocks

Recommended Approach

Use mcctl config for standard settings. Edit config files directly only for advanced options not supported by the CLI.

docs.title: Configure from the Web Console
docs.text: Administrators can edit the platform .env in the Web Console under Settings → Platform Settings. Keys are grouped into cards, secrets are write-only, and saving only writes .env. A dialog then lists what to restart. Per-server values stay in each server's Options tab. See Platform Settings.

docs.title: Global Variables (.env)
docs.text: These variables are set in ~/minecraft-servers/.env. Only the keys listed in servers/global.env reach server containers. See Setting Classification for who reads each key.

docs.title: Network Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl HOST_IP Host machine IP address Auto-detected mcctl init HOST_IPS Multiple IPs for VPN mesh (comma-separated) - Manual DOCKER_GID Docker socket group ID for non-root mc-router (1.46+) 999 mcctl init / mcctl upgrade MINECRAFT_NETWORK Name of the Docker network the compose files join. mcctl init creates minecraft-net minecraft-net Manual MINECRAFT_SUBNET Not read by mcctl: mcctl init creates minecraft-net with subnet 172.28.0.0/16 172.28.0.0/16 -

Multi-Network Access (Tailscale/ZeroTier)

To allow connections from both LAN and VPN, use HOST_IPS: 

# LAN IP + Tailscale IP
HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5
See VPN Mesh Networks Guide for detailed setup.

docs.title: Default Server Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default mcctl TZ Timezone of the server containers. mcctl init copies TZ=Asia/Seoul from the template; set your own IANA time zone Asia/Seoul Manual RCON_PASSWORD RCON console password. Randomly generated by mcctl init; after changing it, recreate containers (mcctl down && mcctl up) random mcctl init RCON_PORT RCON port 25575 Auto EXTRA_ARGS Extra arguments for servers that have no server.yaml yet. A server with a server.yaml always sets its own EXTRA_ARGS in config.env (from world.storage and env.EXTRA_ARGS), so this value does not reach it. Saving it in the console is refused (409, with the servers) when it would move the world of a running server that inherits it, or put an inheriting server on a world another server uses - Manual
