docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN GitHub Personal Access Token - mcctl backup init BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO Target repository - mcctl backup init BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH Target branch main mcctl backup init BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP Auto-backup on server stop false mcctl backup init

Backup Setup

After configuring backup variables, verify with: 

mcctl backup status

docs.title: External Access and Console
docs.text: Variable Description Default mcctl PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY playit.gg agent secret key - mcctl playit setup LOG_LEVEL mcctl-api log level info Manual BETTER_AUTH_SECRET Signs console login sessions. Changing it signs everyone out random mcctl console init BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL Public URL of the console for auth callbacks http://localhost:<console port> Manual

docs.title: mcctl-api Limits
docs.text:
mcctl-api reads these keys from .env at startup; apply a change with mcctl console service restart --api. The console's world upload route also reads WORLD_UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE from .env, so after changing it run mcctl console service restart --console too. Platform Settings lists them under Unknown.

Variable Description Default WORLD_UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE Largest world ZIP accepted by POST /api/worlds/upload, in bytes 1073741824 (1 GiB) WORLD_EXTRACT_MAX_SIZE Largest total uncompressed size when a world ZIP is extracted, in bytes 5368709120 (5 GiB) WORLD_EXTRACT_MAX_ENTRIES Most entries allowed in a world ZIP 100000 STATS_ANALYZE_TIMEOUT_MS Time limit for an ore and block statistics scan, in milliseconds 600000 (10 min) SWAGGER_ENABLED true serves the API documentation at /docs under NODE_ENV=production (it is always on in development) -

docs.title: Setting Classification
docs.text:
Every key in .env has exactly one status, decided by which code actually reads it, not by whether a template contains it. The Console Settings page (admin only) shows the same classification. See Platform Settings.

Which .env keys reach server containers

Servers load env_file: [../global.env, config.env]. servers/global.env lists only key names (TZ, EXTRA_ARGS, RCON_PASSWORD, RCON_PORT); Docker Compose fills them from .env. Every other key, including secrets such as BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN and PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY, stays out of the containers. To pass another key to all servers, add its name to servers/global.env. A server's config.env overrides the platform value for that server only. All .env keys are still loaded into the mcctl-api environment at startup.

Upgrading from an earlier version

Servers created before this change load the whole .env (- ../../.env). mcctl upgrade creates servers/global.env and repoints existing servers to it. Containers keep their old environment until recreated, so run mcctl stop <name> && mcctl start <name> for each server afterwards. Keys you relied on being passed through .env (other than the four above) must be added to servers/global.env.

Status Meaning Editable in Console Editable Supported, typed control Yes Read-only Supported, but unsafe to change from the UI No (CLI only) Runtime-managed (PM2) Injected by ecosystem.config.cjs No (mcctl console init) Legacy Not read by any current code Remove only Unknown Not recognized by mcctl Advanced editor

Editable keys

Key Consumer Apply scope HOST_IP, HOST_IPS mcctl create, mcctl init --reconfigure, any later mcctl change to a server next-create: used by the next mcctl create. An existing server takes the new address into its nip.io hostname the next time mcctl rewrites its files; mcctl init --reconfigure re-renders all servers. Stop, then start a server to apply DOCKER_GID compose router.group_add router: mcctl router start (mcctl router restart does not apply it) TZ, EXTRA_ARGS Every server container (servers/global.env); EXTRA_ARGS only reaches servers without server.yaml servers: stop, then start each server RCON_PASSWORD (secret), RCON_PORT Every server container (servers/global.env); CLI rcon servers BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN (secret), BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO, BACKUP_GITHUB_BRANCH CLI and mcctl-api backups (GitWorldBackupAdapter re-reads .env on every operation) none: the next backup operation BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP mcctl stop <server>, API/console stop none: next stop PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY (secret) compose playit service (SECRET_KEY) playit: stop, then start playit LOG_LEVEL mcctl-api only (dotenv, cwd = MCCTL_ROOT) api BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (secret, cannot be removed), BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL mcctl-console reads these two auth keys from .env at startup, and a non-empty value is used only when ecosystem.config.cjs no longer defines that key (while it does, the ecosystem value wins and a warning is logged if .env differs). mcctl upgrade moves them into .env. Changing the secret signs everyone out. Unset base URL = http://localhost:<console port> console: mcctl console service restart --console

Read-only keys: MINECRAFT_NETWORK (mcctl only creates minecraft-net; to rename it, run mcctl down, docker network create <name>, edit .env, then mcctl up), MINECRAFT_SUBNET (not read by mcctl; the network keeps the subnet it was created with) and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME (changing it orphans existing containers and networks; CLI only).

Runtime-managed (PM2): AUTH_MODE (api) comes from ecosystem.config.cjs. Re-run mcctl console init to change it. Ecosystem files generated by earlier versions also inject BETTER_AUTH_SECRET and BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL; while they are defined there, the ecosystem value wins over .env and Platform Settings shows them read-only. Run mcctl upgrade to move both into .env (the secret is kept, so sessions stay valid; a backup ecosystem.config.cjs.bak-<timestamp> is written), then mcctl console service restart --console.

Legacy: API_ACCESS_MODE, BETTER_AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS, BETTER_AUTH_URL, MCCTL_API_IMAGE, MCCTL_CONSOLE_IMAGE, MCCTL_CONSOLE_PORT, MCCTL_CORS_ORIGIN, MCCTL_JWT_EXPIRY, MCCTL_JWT_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_SECRET, NEXTAUTH_URL, DEFAULT_MEMORY, DEFAULT_VERSION. No create path reads DEFAULT_MEMORY or DEFAULT_VERSION.

Unknown: Not recognized by mcctl. Loaded by mcctl-api at startup; Minecraft servers receive it only if its name is listed in servers/global.env.

Legacy and unknown keys whose names match SECRET, TOKEN, PASSWORD, PASSWD, CREDENTIAL, PRIVATE or end in _KEY are treated as secrets and never displayed.

Restart does not reload .env

docker compose restart and mcctl router restart do not re-read .env. Use stop then start (or mcctl router start) so the container is recreated.

docs.title: Server Variables (config.env)
docs.text: These variables are set per-server. Use mcctl config to manage them. mcctl writes config.env from the server's server.yaml; a hand edit is taken into server.yaml the next time mcctl changes the server.

docs.title: Value Rules
docs.text:
config.env is read the way Docker Compose reads an env file:

  • One KEY=value per line. mcctl does not support values that span lines; a following line without = is not part of the value.
  • In an unquoted value, a space followed by # starts a comment: MOTD=Hi #1 sets Hi. Quote such a value (MOTD='Hi #1'), or set it with mcctl config, which quotes it for you.
  • If a key appears twice, the last line wins.
  • mcctl refuses values that contain control characters or start with a quote, and values with $, # or leading or trailing spaces that also contain ' or end with \.

docs.title: Required Settings
docs.text: Variable Description Default mcctl Command EULA Accept Minecraft EULA TRUE Auto-set TYPE Server type PAPER (mcctl create; the Web Console form starts on VANILLA) mcctl create -t TYPE VERSION Minecraft version LATEST mcctl config <server> VERSION

docs.title: Memory Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl Command MEMORY JVM heap memory 4G (6G for modpack types) mcctl config <server> MEMORY INIT_MEMORY Initial heap size Same as MEMORY Manual MAX_MEMORY Maximum heap size Same as MEMORY Manual JVM_OPTS Additional JVM options - Manual JVM_DD_OPTS JVM -D options - Manual

Example - Set memory:

mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: Server Properties
docs.text:
These map directly to Minecraft's server.properties. Defaults are what a new server gets: the values mcctl create writes into config.env from the template, otherwise the image default.

Variable Description Default mcctl Command MOTD Server message Welcome to <name>! Your adventure begins here. mcctl config <server> MOTD MAX_PLAYERS Maximum players 20 mcctl config <server> MAX_PLAYERS DIFFICULTY Game difficulty normal mcctl config <server> DIFFICULTY MODE Default game mode (survival, creative, adventure, spectator). The image reads MODE, not GAMEMODE survival mcctl config <server> MODE LEVEL World/level name Auto-set mcctl config <server> LEVEL SEED World generation seed Random mcctl create -s SEED PVP Enable PvP true mcctl config <server> --pvp/--no-pvp HARDCORE Hardcore mode false mcctl config <server> HARDCORE ALLOW_FLIGHT Allow flying false mcctl config <server> ALLOW_FLIGHT SPAWN_PROTECTION Spawn protection radius 0 mcctl config <server> SPAWN_PROTECTION VIEW_DISTANCE View distance (chunks) 10 mcctl config <server> VIEW_DISTANCE SIMULATION_DISTANCE Simulation distance 10 mcctl config <server> SIMULATION_DISTANCE ONLINE_MODE Authenticate with Mojang true mcctl config <server> ONLINE_MODE ENABLE_COMMAND_BLOCK Enable command blocks false mcctl config <server> --command-block FORCE_GAMEMODE Force default gamemode false mcctl config <server> FORCE_GAMEMODE ENABLE_WHITELIST Enable whitelist false mcctl whitelist <server> on

Example - Configure game settings:

mcctl config myserver DIFFICULTY hard

docs.title: Mod/Plugin Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl Command MODRINTH_PROJECTS Modrinth mod slugs - mcctl config <server> MODRINTH_PROJECTS MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES Download dependencies (none, required, optional; the image default is none) required mcctl config <server> MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES CF_API_KEY CurseForge API key. Needed only for java8 and other pre-Java 17 image tags, or to use your own key. A key only in .env does not reach servers - mcctl config <server> CF_API_KEY CURSEFORGE_FILES CurseForge project slugs - mcctl config <server> CURSEFORGE_FILES SPIGET_RESOURCES Spigot resource IDs - mcctl config <server> SPIGET_RESOURCES MODS Mod download URLs - Manual PLUGINS_SYNC_UPDATE Auto-update plugins false Manual

Example - Add mods:

# Fabric server with performance mods
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES required
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl Command OPS Operator usernames - mcctl op <server> add <player> OPS_FILE Path to ops file - Manual WHITELIST Whitelisted players - mcctl whitelist <server> add <player> WHITELIST_FILE Path to whitelist file - Manual

Example - Manage operators:

# Add operator
mcctl op myserver add Steve

# List operators
mcctl op myserver list

# Remove operator
mcctl op myserver remove Steve

docs.title: Performance Tuning
docs.text:
Variable Description Default mcctl Command USE_AIKAR_FLAGS Use Aikar's JVM flags false mcctl config <server> USE_AIKAR_FLAGS MAX_TICK_TIME Max ms per tick 60000 Manual NETWORK_COMPRESSION_THRESHOLD Compression threshold 256 Manual ENTITY_BROADCAST_RANGE_PERCENTAGE Entity render distance % 100 Manual

mcctl config myserver USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true

docs.text: Variable Description Default mcctl Command UID User ID for file permissions 1000 Manual GID Group ID for file permissions 1000 Manual SKIP_CHOWN_DATA Skip ownership change false Manual TZ Container timezone From .env (servers/global.env) Manual ENABLE_RCON Enable RCON true Auto RCON_PASSWORD RCON password From global .env Auto

docs.text: Variable Description Default mcctl Command DEBUG Enable debug output false Manual DEBUG_EXEC Debug exec commands false Manual DEBUG_MEMORY Debug memory usage false Manual

docs.title: Audit Log Variables
docs.text:
These are set in ~/minecraft-servers/.env for audit log behavior. mcctl-api reads them at startup; the CLI reads them only from its shell environment.

Variable Description Default Management AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP Automatically delete old audit logs false (unset) Manual AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS Number of days to retain audit logs 90 Manual

AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP: - true: While new entries are logged, delete logs older than AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (after every 100 new entries, or once 24 hours have passed since the last cleanup) - Unset or false: No automatic cleanup (manual purge only via mcctl audit purge)

AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS: - Number of days to retain audit logs before auto-cleanup - Recommended: 30-180 days depending on compliance requirements - Production environments: 90+ days

Database Location: 

~/minecraft-servers/data/audit.db

Example: 

# Set custom retention policy
echo "AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS=180" >> ~/minecraft-servers/.env
echo "AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP=true" >> ~/minecraft-servers/.env

# Restart mcctl-api to apply
mcctl console service restart --api

docs.title: mc-router Variables
docs.text:
These are set in the environment block of the router service in ~/minecraft-servers/docker-compose.yml. mc-router does not read them from .env:

Variable Description Default Management IN_DOCKER Enable Docker mode true Auto AUTO_SCALE_UP Auto-start servers on connect true Manual AUTO_SCALE_DOWN Auto-stop idle servers true Manual AUTO_SCALE_DOWN_AFTER Idle timeout 10m Manual DOCKER_TIMEOUT Server startup timeout (Go duration, e.g. 120s) 120s Manual AUTO_SCALE_ASLEEP_MOTD MOTD for sleeping servers §e§lServer is sleeping§r\n§7Connect to wake up! Manual API_BINDING Management API binding :8080 Auto

In a server's server.yaml, routing.autoScale overrides AUTO_SCALE_UP and AUTO_SCALE_DOWN for that server, and routing.asleepMotd overrides AUTO_SCALE_ASLEEP_MOTD. Waking a server on connect also needs AUTO_SCALE_UP set to true here.

After changing mc-router settings:

mcctl router start

mcctl router start recreates the container from the edited file; mcctl router restart keeps the old settings. mcctl upgrade changes only the router image and group_add in this file, so your edits stay.

docs.title: Shell Variables
docs.text:
These are read from the environment of the shell (or PM2) that runs mcctl, not from .env:

Variable Description Default MCCTL_ROOT Platform directory used by mcctl, mcctl-api and mcctl-console. --root <path> overrides it for one command ~/minecraft-servers MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD sudo password the CLI uses to add or remove <server>.local in /etc/avahi/hosts. --sudo-password overrides it -

PLATFORM_PATH is no longer read; use MCCTL_ROOT.

docs.title: Variable Interpolation
docs.text:
When editing config files directly, you can reference other variables:

# .env
HOST_IP=192.168.1.100

# config.env
MOTD=Connect via ${HOST_IP}

This works only for lines you write by hand. Values set with mcctl config, the Web Console or server.yaml are written in single quotes, so ${...} stays literal. Do not use ${...} in TYPE, VERSION, MEMORY, LEVEL, PLAYIT_DOMAIN, EXTRA_ARGS or the server image: mcctl cannot take such a value into server.yaml.

docs.title: Server Types
docs.text: Detailed guide for each Minecraft server platform supported by mcctl.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Create a server with your desired type using mcctl:

# Paper (recommended for most users)
mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Vanilla (pure Minecraft)
mcctl create myserver -t VANILLA -v 1.21.1

# Forge (mods)
mcctl create myserver -t FORGE -v 1.20.4

# NeoForge (modern Forge fork, 1.20.1+)
mcctl create myserver -t NEOFORGE -v 1.21.1

# Fabric (lightweight mods)
mcctl create myserver -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# Modrinth modpack (run `mcctl create` without a name to be asked instead)
mcctl create myserver -t MODRINTH --modpack <modpack-slug>

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Type Plugins Mods Performance Recommended For PAPER Yes No Excellent General use, plugins VANILLA No No Good Pure Minecraft experience FORGE No Yes Varies Forge mod packs NEOFORGE No Yes Varies Modern Forge mods (1.20.1+) FABRIC No Yes Excellent Performance mods MODRINTH No Yes Varies Modrinth modpacks AUTO_CURSEFORGE No Yes Varies CurseForge modpacks SPIGOT Yes No Good Legacy plugin compatibility BUKKIT Yes No Moderate Very old plugins PURPUR Yes No Excellent Advanced customization PUFFERFISH Yes No Varies Paper fork for large servers FOLIA Yes No Varies Multi-threaded Paper fork for large worlds LEAF Yes No Varies Lightweight Paper fork QUILT No Yes Excellent Modern Fabric alternative

These are the types mcctl create -t accepts. For other types the image supports, see Other Server Types.

docs.title: Paper
docs.text:
Recommended for most users.

Paper is a high-performance Minecraft server that supports Bukkit and Spigot plugins while providing significant performance improvements.

docs.title: Create Paper Server
docs.text: mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Significant performance improvements over Vanilla
  • Full Bukkit/Spigot plugin compatibility
  • Async chunk loading
  • Anti-exploit patches
  • Extensive configuration options

docs.title: Recommended Configuration
docs.text:
# Enable Aikar's optimized JVM flags
mcctl config myserver USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true

docs.title: Adding Plugins
docs.text:
# From Modrinth
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "essentialsx,luckperms"

# From Spigot
mcctl config myserver SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,81534"

# Apply changes
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

Or place plugin JAR files in shared/plugins/ directory.

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
• Always enable USE_AIKAR_FLAGS=true for optimal performance
  • Use Paper-specific plugins when available
  • Monitor with Paper's built-in profiler: /timings report

docs.title: Vanilla
docs.text: The official Minecraft server from Mojang.

docs.title: Create Vanilla Server
docs.text: mcctl create myserver -t VANILLA -v 1.21.1

docs.title: Features
docs.text:

  • No modifications

  • Smallest footprint

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:

  • Minimal server requirements

docs.title: Forge
docs.text: Server for running Forge mods.

docs.title: Create Forge Server

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Large mod ecosystem
  • Complex modpacks support
  • Industrial/tech mods
  • RPG mods

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
# Set memory (modpacks need more)
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G

# Add mods (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+ images)
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap,create"

# Or specific Forge version
mcctl config myserver FORGE_VERSION "47.2.0"

# Apply changes

docs.title: Java Version Requirements
docs.text:
Forge needs the Java version of its Minecraft version (see Java Versions and Image Tags), and Forge 1.16.5 and older run only on Java 8.

Forge 1.16.5 and Below

mcctl create -t FORGE -v 1.16.5 gives the server the java8 image. A server whose VERSION you change later keeps its image: set it in servers/<name>/server.yaml, then write the files and start it: 

image: itzg/minecraft-server:java8

mcctl migrate spec myserver
mcctl start myserver

docs.text:
Modpack Size Recommended Memory Light (10-30 mods) 4-6G Medium (30-100 mods) 6-8G Heavy (100+ mods) 8-12G 
mcctl config myserver MEMORY 8G

docs.title: Create NeoForge Server

docs.title: Features
docs.text:

  • Forge mod compatibility (many Forge mods work on NeoForge)
  • Improved performance over legacy Forge
  • Better mod loading and dependency management

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:

# Add mods from Modrinth

docs.text:
• New modded server projects targeting Minecraft 1.20.1+
  • Prefer modern Forge APIs and active community development
  • Want improved performance over legacy Forge

Minecraft Version Requirement

NeoForge requires Minecraft 1.20.1 or newer. For older versions, use FORGE instead.

docs.title: Modrinth Modpack
docs.text: Create a server from a Modrinth modpack. The modpack includes all required mods, configurations, and settings pre-configured.

docs.title: Create Modrinth Modpack Server
docs.text:
# With the modpack slug from its Modrinth URL
mcctl create myserver -t MODRINTH --modpack <modpack-slug>

# Optional: loader, modpack version and mods to leave out
mcctl create myserver -t MODRINTH --modpack <modpack-slug> \
  --mod-loader fabric --modpack-version <version-id> --exclude-files <file1>,<file2>

# Interactive: run without a name and choose "Modrinth Modpack"
mcctl create

The interactive flow asks for:

  1. The modpack slug or URL
  2. The mod loader: Auto-detect, or one of the loaders the modpack supports
  3. The modpack version (empty for the latest)
  4. Mods to exclude (comma-separated)
  5. The world
  6. Memory (default 6G)
  7. The whitelist

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Dynamic loader detection: only shows loaders the modpack supports (Forge, NeoForge, Fabric, Quilt)
  • The modpack decides the Minecraft version: no VERSION is written unless you pass -v
  • Pre-configured mod sets for immediate play

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The modpack server is configured with:

TYPE=MODRINTH
MODRINTH_MODPACK=<modpack-slug>
MODRINTH_VERSION=<version-id>       # optional, --modpack-version
MODRINTH_LOADER=<loader>            # optional, --mod-loader: forge, neoforge, fabric, quilt
MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES=<files>      # optional, --exclude-files

docs.title: Memory Recommendations
docs.text: Modpack Size Recommended Memory Light (10-30 mods) 4-6G Medium (30-100 mods) 6-8G Heavy (100+ mods) 8-12G

docs.title: Web Console
docs.text: The Web Console's Create Server dialog searches Modrinth for the modpack, offers only the loader and Minecraft version pairs the modpack has, and fills Exclude mods with client-only mods it detects. See Excluding Client-Only Mods.

docs.title: CurseForge Modpack
docs.text:
Create a server from a CurseForge modpack:

mcctl create myserver -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack all-the-mods-8

--modpack is written as CF_SLUG, --modpack-version as CF_FILENAME_MATCHER (part of the modpack file name), and --exclude-files as CF_EXCLUDE_MODS. --mod-loader is ignored: the modpack's manifest decides the loader. Java 17+ images include a CurseForge API key, so CF_API_KEY is only needed on older image tags. For CF_PAGE_URL, CF_FILE_ID and the other settings, see CurseForge Modpacks.

docs.title: Other Server Types
docs.text:
The image supports more types than mcctl create -t accepts, for example the hybrids MOHIST, MAGMA_MAINTAINED, ARCLIGHT and KETTING (mods and Bukkit plugins on one server), FTBA (Feed The Beast modpacks) and CUSTOM (your own server jar). Create the server with an accepted type and --no-start, then set TYPE and the type's variables with mcctl config:

mcctl create hybrid -t FORGE -v 1.20.1 --no-start
mcctl config hybrid TYPE MOHIST
mcctl start hybrid
Type Variables MOHIST VERSION MAGMA_MAINTAINED VERSION, FORGE_VERSION ARCLIGHT VERSION, ARCLIGHT_TYPE (FORGE, NEOFORGE or FABRIC) KETTING VERSION FTBA FTB_MODPACK_ID (see FTB Modpacks) CUSTOM CUSTOM_SERVER: URL or container path of the server jar

Check the image tag for the Minecraft version too (see Java Versions and Image Tags).

docs.title: Java Versions and Image Tags
docs.text:
Each server runs the image named by image: in its servers/<name>/server.yaml. A new server gets the tag its VERSION needs from the table below. LATEST, no VERSION (a modpack decides it) and versions mcctl cannot read, such as snapshots and pre-releases, get java25. The tag that matches each Minecraft version:

Minecraft version Java Image tag 26.x, LATEST 25 java25 1.20.5 - 1.21.x 21 java21 1.17 - 1.20.4 17 java17 1.16.5 and older 8 java8

Forge 1.16.5 and older fail on newer Java, so they need java8.

To change the image, edit image: in server.yaml, run mcctl migrate spec <name>, then stop and start the server. An edit of image: in the server's docker-compose.yml is also taken into server.yaml.

mcctl update sets each server's tag to the one in this table for its VERSION. It replaces every itzg/minecraft-server tag that is not pinned, so latest or java21-graalvm is replaced too. A tag that starts with a release version, such as itzg/minecraft-server:2026.10.0-java21, or a digest (itzg/minecraft-server:java21@sha256:…) is pinned: mcctl update keeps it, and warns when its Java is older than VERSION needs. When VERSION is a snapshot or another value mcctl cannot read, the tag is left as it is. Other images are not changed.

Error Cause Fix class file version 69.0 Java 25 required Use the java25 tag class file version 65.0 Java 21 required Use the java21 tag Unsupported class file major version Java too new for the server Use an older tag, for example java8 for Forge 1.16.5 and older

docs.title: Decision Tree
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A{Need mods?} -->|Yes| B{Which type?}
    A -->|No| C{Need plugins?}

    B -->|Modpack from Modrinth| M[MODRINTH modpack]
    B -->|Forge mods| D{Minecraft version?}
    D -->|1.20.1+| N[NEOFORGE or FORGE]
    D -->|Older| O[FORGE]
    B -->|Fabric/Quilt| E{Priority?}
    E -->|Cutting-edge| F[QUILT]
    E -->|Compatibility| G[FABRIC]

    C -->|Yes| H{Priority?}
    C -->|No| I[VANILLA]

    H -->|Performance| J[PAPER]
    H -->|Customization| K[PURPUR]
    H -->|Legacy| L[SPIGOT/BUKKIT]

docs.title: Server Definition (server.yaml)
docs.text:
Each server is defined by one file: servers/<name>/server.yaml. mcctl writes the files Docker Compose reads from it:

File Written from server.yaml servers/<name>/config.env yes (comments and untouched lines are kept) servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml yes (rendered from the bundled template) servers/compose.yml the <name>/docker-compose.yml include entry is added; other entries are kept

Platform files (.env, the main docker-compose.yml, .mcctl.json) are not part of it.

docs.title: What the file holds
docs.text:
specVersion: 1
name: survival
type: PAPER
version: "1.21.1"
memory: 4G
image: itzg/minecraft-server:java21
world:
  level: survival
  storage: universe        # worlds/<level>; "data" = servers/<name>/data/<level>
routing:
  customHostnames:
    - mc.example.com
  playitDomain: aa.example.com
  autoScale:
    up: true
    down: true
  asleepMotd: "§e§lServer is sleeping§r\n§7Connect to wake up!"   # optional
  loadingMotd: "§a§lServer is starting...§r\n§7Please wait!"       # optional
env:                       # every other config.env key, unchanged
  MODE: survival
  ENABLE_RCON: "true"
  MOTD: Welcome to survival! Your adventure begins here.
  • TYPE, VERSION, MEMORY, LEVEL and PLAYIT_DOMAIN are fields of their own; they cannot appear in env.
  • EXTRA_ARGS is written from world.storage (--universe /worlds/ for universe) plus env.EXTRA_ARGS. It is always written, so a server no longer inherits it from .env.
  • image is the server's container image; a new server gets the itzg/minecraft-server tag its VERSION needs (java25 for LATEST). mcctl update changes it to the Java tag VERSION needs unless the tag is pinned; see Java Versions and Image Tags.
  • The mc-router hosts are <name>.local, <name>.<ip>.nip.io for each address in HOST_IPS (else HOST_IP, else the detected host address), the playit domain, then the custom hosts.
  • routing.autoScale sets whether mc-router starts the server on connect (up) and stops it when idle (down). asleepMotd and loadingMotd set the MOTD shown while the server sleeps or starts; without them the template's MOTDs are used.
  • Quote values YAML would read as numbers or booleans (version: "1.21", ENABLE_RCON: "true"). mcctl reports the field otherwise.
  • Unknown keys are errors. env keys must be shell variable names, and their values one line without control characters, not starting with a quote. env.EXTRA_ARGS must not contain --universe (set world.storage instead). Host names must be valid DNS names.

docs.title: Who writes it
docs.text: Every mcctl command and Web Console action that changes a server goes through server.yaml: mcctl create, mcctl config, whitelist, op, mod, playit domain, update, init --reconfigure, world assignment, migrate worlds, and the console's settings, whitelist, mods and hostnames pages.

docs.title: Existing servers
docs.text:
A server created before this change has no server.yaml. It keeps working as before; it is imported the first time mcctl changes it. To import now and see the report:

mcctl migrate spec --all --dry-run   # what would be imported
mcctl migrate spec --all             # import and write the files

Add --json for a machine-readable report. The import keeps every config.env key. A docker-compose.yml environment entry moves into env (Compose gave it precedence over config.env; a clash is reported). A server whose world or image is set through ${...} interpolation cannot be imported until the value is literal. An empty value such as VERSION= stays empty (version: ""), because it still overrides servers/global.env. mcctl writes a $ in a config.env value inside single quotes (such a value must not end with \) and a $ in the compose image or router labels as $$, so Docker Compose does not interpolate it. mcctl upgrade lists the servers that have no server.yaml yet.

docs.title: Hand edits
docs.text:
The first line of the generated files is a header with a hash, so mcctl can tell a hand edit:

  • config.env edited: the edit is taken into server.yaml the next time mcctl changes the server.
  • docker-compose.yml image or mc-router.* labels edited: taken into server.yaml the same way.
  • docker-compose.yml edited elsewhere (ports, volumes, ...): the file is protected. Changes that do not affect it leave it alone; a change that would rewrite it fails with compose_edited and names the edited fields.
  • server.yaml edited by hand: applied the next time mcctl changes the server, or with mcctl migrate spec <name>.
  • config.env and server.yaml both edited: edit_conflict. Undo one edit, or re-render from server.yaml with mcctl migrate spec <name> --force (keeps config.env.bak / docker-compose.yml.bak).

mcctl start does not render files; it starts what is on disk.

Other errors a write can stop with:

  • storage_change: the change would move the world between worlds/ and the server's data/ (world.storage); mcctl refuses it and points to mcctl migrate worlds.
  • invalid_spec: a field is invalid; the message names each field.
  • unsupported_spec_version: the file was written by a newer mcctl; upgrade mcctl.
  • locked: another mcctl process is changing servers/compose.yml or deleting the server; retry when it is done.

docs.title: Creating a server
docs.text: mcctl create and the Web Console write server.yaml and the files above, register <name>.local with avahi (a failure is a warning), and start the server unless --no-start is given. If anything fails before the server exists, nothing is left behind and the same create can be retried at once. If the server is created but does not start, it stays created: the CLI exits 1 with the cause, and the console says so; start it with mcctl start <name>.

docs.title: Management Console Overview
docs.text:
Management Console provides a web-based management interface and REST API for Docker Minecraft servers. It enables remote server management, monitoring, and administration through a modern web console.

Status

mcctl-api (REST API) and mcctl-console (Web UI) are published on npm with each mcctl release. Install them with mcctl console init.

docs.title: mcctl-api (REST API Server)
docs.text:
A Fastify-based REST API server that provides:

  • Server Management: List, start, stop, restart Minecraft servers
  • Server Information: Health status, players, resource usage
  • RCON Integration: Execute console commands remotely
  • Swagger Documentation: Auto-generated API docs at /docs when NODE_ENV is not production or SWAGGER_ENABLED=true is set (off after mcctl console init, which runs the API with NODE_ENV=production)
  • Health Checks: Built-in health endpoint at /health

Default port: 5001

docs.title: mcctl-console (Web Management UI)
docs.text:
A Next.js web application that provides:

  • Dashboard: Servers, players, worlds and mc-router at a glance, with real-time SSE status, quick server actions and recent activity
  • Servers: Server list, server creation, and a detail page with console, players, world, activity, mods, files, config history, backups, access and options tabs
  • Worlds: List, create or upload, assign, release, and delete worlds; world details with map and block statistics
  • Players: Whitelist, operators and bans per server, and the players online on all servers
  • Audit: Activity log with filters, statistics, live updates and export
  • Backups: World backups to a Git repository, backup schedules, and config snapshots
  • Routing: mc-router routing table, router status and restart, live router log, and playit.gg external access
  • Settings and Users: Account settings for every user; Platform Settings (the platform .env) and a read-only user list for administrators
  • User Authentication: Secure login with Better Auth
  • BFF Proxy: Backend-for-Frontend pattern for secure API access
  • React Query Hooks: Type-safe data fetching with automatic caching

Default port: 5000

docs.title: BFF Proxy Routes
docs.text:
The console proxies all API requests through Next.js server routes under /api/. Examples:

Route Description /api/servers/* Server management (list, create, delete, start/stop/restart) /api/servers/:name/exec Execute RCON commands /api/servers/:name/logs Fetch server logs /api/worlds/* World management (list, create, upload, delete, assign/release, map, statistics) /api/players/* Whitelist, operators, bans and kicks /api/backup/* World backups, restore and backup schedules /api/router/* mc-router status and restart /api/sse/* Real-time streams (server status, logs, router log); requires a signed-in session

This architecture ensures API keys never reach the browser. For the mcctl-api endpoints behind these routes, see the API Reference.

docs.title: Authentication Modes
docs.text:
Management Console supports multiple authentication modes:

Mode Description Use Case internal Internal access only, no external exposure (most secure) Default production api-key External access with X-API-Key header Automation/scripts ip-whitelist IP-based access control Known client IPs api-key-ip Both API key and IP required High security open No authentication Development only

Note

mcctl console init writes the access mode to AUTH_MODE as the value mcctl-api recognises: internal → ip-whitelist limited to loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1), api-key-ip → combined, open → disabled; api-key and ip-whitelist are written as is.

Security Warning

Never use open mode in production. It disables all authentication and exposes your servers to unauthorized access.

docs.title: Server Management
docs.text:
• View all Minecraft servers with status
  • Start, stop, and restart servers
  • View server logs in real-time
  • Monitor player counts and server health

docs.title: Console Integration
docs.text:
• Execute RCON commands through the web interface
  • Follow the server log in real time (the RCON reply to a command is not shown)
  • Supports all standard Minecraft commands

docs.title: User Management
docs.text:
• Multiple user accounts with role-based access
  • Admin role: Full access to all features
  • User role: Access limited to the servers granted to the account (Viewer, Operator, or Owner permission per server)

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Note: mcctl admin commands are deprecated. Use mcctl console instead. The admin command alias still works for backward compatibility but will be removed in a future release.

docs.title: 1. Initialize Management Console
docs.text:
mcctl console init

Follow the interactive prompts to configure:

  1. Select services to install (mcctl-api, mcctl-console)
  2. Admin email and name (required if console selected)
  3. Admin password (min 8 characters, requires uppercase, lowercase, number)
  4. API access mode (internal, api-key, ip-whitelist, api-key-ip, open)
  5. IP whitelist (if applicable; include 127.0.0.1 when you also install mcctl-console)

docs.title: 2. Start Management Consoles
docs.text:
mcctl console service start --console

--console starts mcctl-api and mcctl-console. Without a flag, the command asks which services to start when both are installed.

docs.title: 3. Access Web Console
docs.text:
Open your browser and navigate to:

http://localhost:5000

Log in with the admin credentials created during initialization.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• mcctl platform initialized (mcctl init)
  • Docker running (Docker Engine 24 or later, Docker Compose 2.20 or later)
  • Node.js 18 or later and PM2 6 or later installed globally (npm install -g pm2); mcctl console init checks both
  • Ports 5000 and 5001 available (or the ports you pass to mcctl console init --api-port / --console-port)

docs.title: Configuration Files
docs.text:
After initialization, the following files are created:

File Description ~/minecraft-servers/.mcctl-admin.yml Management Console configuration ~/minecraft-servers/data/mcctl.db Console user database (SQLite, Better Auth; created when mcctl-console is selected) ~/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs PM2 ecosystem configuration ~/minecraft-servers/.env mcctl console init adds BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, the console session secret, when mcctl-console is selected (an existing secret is kept)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The mcctl-api reference moved to the REST API section:

  • REST API Overview: base URL, authentication, errors, Server-Sent Events, Swagger
  • API Endpoints: every route

docs.title: Audit Log API Reference
docs.text:
The audit log routes are now documented in the REST API reference: Audit logs.

Former section New location Authentication Authentication GET /audit-logs GET /api/audit-logs GET /audit-logs/stats GET /api/audit-logs/stats GET /audit-logs/:id GET /api/audit-logs/:id DELETE /audit-logs/purge DELETE /api/audit-logs (JSON body, needs X-Role: admin) GET /audit-logs/stream GET /api/audit-logs/stream Data Types Audit log entries Error Responses Errors

See also CLI - Audit Log Commands and Web Console - Audit Log UI.

docs.title: Audit Log Web Console Guide
docs.text: The Audit page of the web console shows the audit log that mcctl-api and the mcctl CLI write: server lifecycle, player management, worlds, backups, configuration and file operations. For the same data on the command line or over HTTP, see CLI - Audit Log Commands and the API Reference.

docs.title: Accessing the Audit Log
docs.text:
• Click Audit in the top navigation bar, or View All in the dashboard's Recent Activity card.
  • URL: http://localhost:5000/audit-logs

Every signed-in user, with the Admin or the User role, can view and export the audit log. The per-server permissions (Viewer, Operator, Owner) do not limit it.

docs.title: Live Updates
docs.text:
The page header shows Live with a green dot while the real-time (SSE) connection is open, and Disconnected with a gray dot while it is not. The page reconnects on its own every 3 seconds.

The list does not reload by itself. When new entries arrive, a banner above the filters says "N new logs available - Click to refresh"; click it to load them. Changing a filter also reloads the list.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
Four cards at the top summarize the whole audit log, whatever filters are set. They refresh every 30 seconds.

Card Value Total Logs Number of entries Success Rate Share of entries with the status success Failures Number of failed entries Active Users Number of distinct actors in the latest 1,000 entries

docs.title: Filters
docs.text:
The Filters panel can be collapsed, shows how many filters are active, and has a Clear All button. A filter applies as soon as you change it and is kept in the page URL, so a filtered view can be bookmarked.

Filter Description From / To Date range in whole days (UTC) Action One action: Create, Delete, Start, Stop, Restart, Whitelist Add, Whitelist Remove, Ban, Unban, Op, Deop, Kick, Purge or Platform Settings. Choosing a target type narrows the list to server or player actions Target type All, Server or Player Status All, Success or Failure Target Name Exact name of the target, such as a server, world or player Actor Exact actor as recorded, for example api:console or cli:local

Other recorded actions (worlds, backups and their schedules, config snapshots, mods, files, playit.gg, mc-router) are not in the Action list. Find them with Target Name or Actor, or with mcctl audit list --action <action>.

Player actions done in the web console are recorded with the server as the target and the player name in the details; the CLI records the player as the target. The Player target type therefore shows only player actions from the CLI.

docs.title: Log Table
docs.text:
Column Description Timestamp Relative time such as "21m ago"; hover for the exact time Action Action label in a colored chip (see Action Colors) Actor console for actions from the web console (recorded as api:console), the user name for Platform Settings changes and file operations (recorded as api:<user>), and a local chip for CLI commands (recorded as cli:local) Target Name of the target, such as a server, world or player. A server links to its detail page, a player to the Players page Status OK (green) or Error (red)
  • A row with details or an error message has an arrow at the start; click it to show them below the row. Failed entries start expanded.
  • Click a row to open the detail drawer (see Log Details).
  • Choose 25, 50 (default) or 100 rows per page.

The server Activity tab shows the same table for one server, without the Target column, with an Action filter, a status toggle and a View Full History link to this page (see the Web Console Guide).

docs.title: Log Details
docs.text:
The drawer on the right shows the entry's ID, Timestamp (to the second, with the time zone), Action, Status, Actor, Target (<type>/<name>), the error message of a failed entry, and a Details table with the recorded fields. For a server creation the details are type, version, memory, modpack, modpackVersion, modLoader and excludeFiles.

Related Logs has two tabs: up to 10 other entries with the Same Target and up to 10 with the Same Actor, newest first.

docs.title: Export
docs.text:
Click Export in the Filters panel to open Export Audit Logs:

  1. Choose CSV or JSON.
  2. Check Applied Filters and Estimated Rows. The export uses the filters currently set.
  3. Click Export CSV or Export JSON. The file is saved as audit-logs-<timestamp>.csv or audit-logs-<timestamp>.json.

An export has at most 5,000 rows. When more entries match, the dialog says so; narrow the filters to export the rest.

CSV example:

ID,Timestamp,Action,Actor,Target Type,Target Name,Status,Error Message,Details
7c1d2e3f-4a5b-4c6d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f,2026-10-24T14:32:15.123Z,server.start,api:console,server,survival,success,"",""
2b8e9f10-1a2b-4c3d-9e4f-5a6b7c8d9e0f,2026-10-24T14:30:45.020Z,player.whitelist.add,cli:local,player,Steve,success,"","{""server"":""survival""}"

The JSON file contains exportedAt, filters, total and the logs array.

docs.title: Action Colors
docs.text: Color Actions Green Create, Whitelist Add, Unban Red Delete, Ban, Kick Blue Start, Op Amber Stop, Whitelist Remove, Deop, Platform Settings Purple Restart Gray Purge, and every action without its own label (shown by its name, such as world.create)

docs.title: Purging Old Logs
docs.text: The web console has no purge control. Delete old entries with mcctl audit purge (--dry-run shows what would be deleted) or with DELETE /api/audit-logs, which requires the Admin role. With AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP=true in the platform .env, entries older than AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS (default 90) are deleted automatically.

docs.title: Logs Not Updating
docs.text:
Symptoms: - The header shows Disconnected - New actions do not raise the "new logs available" banner

Solutions: 1. Wait a few seconds: the page reconnects every 3 seconds 2. Reload the page (F5) 3. Check that mcctl-api and mcctl-console are running: mcctl console service status

docs.title: Slow Page
docs.text:
Symptoms: - The table loads slowly with many entries

Solutions: 1. Narrow the date range 2. Filter by action, target or actor 3. Choose fewer rows per page

docs.title: Missing Logs
docs.text:
Symptoms: - Expected entries do not appear

Possible Causes: 1. Automatic cleanup deleted old entries (AUDIT_AUTO_CLEANUP, AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS) 2. A manual purge was run 3. Filters hide them: click Clear All 4. The action is not in the Action list: search by Target Name or Actor instead 5. A player action from the web console is filed under the server, not under the Player target type

  • Audit Log Variables

docs.title: CLI Commands Reference
docs.text:
Note: mcctl admin commands are deprecated. Use mcctl console instead. The admin command alias still works for backward compatibility but will be removed in a future release.

Complete reference for all mcctl console subcommands.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The mcctl console command group provides management capabilities for the Management Console:

mcctl console <subcommand> [options]

docs.title: Command Summary
docs.text: Command Description mcctl console init Initialize Management Console configuration mcctl console remove Remove Management Console processes and configuration (keeps the console database) mcctl console user Manage admin console users mcctl console api Manage API configuration mcctl console service Manage Management Console lifecycle

docs.title: mcctl console init
docs.text: Initialize Management Console configuration and create the first admin user.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: mcctl console init [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --root <path> Custom data directory --force Skip the reinitialize confirmation and replace an existing admin user with the same email (see Reinitializing below) --api-port <port> API server port (default: 5001) --console-port <port> Console server port (default: 5000)

docs.title: Interactive Flow
docs.text:
The command guides you through:

  1. Services to install - mcctl-api is selected by default; also select mcctl-console to install the web console
  2. Admin email - Used to sign in to the web console (e.g., admin@example.com)
  3. Admin name - Default: Administrator
  4. Admin password - Password requirements:
    • Minimum 8 characters
    • At least one uppercase letter
    • At least one lowercase letter
    • At least one number
  5. API access mode - Choose security level:
    • internal - Internal access only, no external exposure (recommended)
    • api-key - Requires X-API-Key header
    • ip-whitelist - IP-based access control
    • api-key-ip - Both API key and IP required
    • open - No authentication (development only)
  6. Additional configuration - Based on selected mode

The admin email, name, and password are asked only when mcctl-console is selected. The admin account is created with the admin role.

Access modes

mcctl console init writes the access mode to AUTH_MODE as the value mcctl-api recognises: internal → ip-whitelist limited to loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1), api-key-ip → combined, open → disabled; api-key and ip-whitelist are written as is.

The command does not ask for ports. To use ports other than the defaults, pass --api-port and --console-port (see the examples below).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Standard initialization
mcctl console init

# Reinitialize with force
mcctl console init --force

# Custom data directory
mcctl console init --root /opt/minecraft

# Custom ports
mcctl console init --api-port 8001 --console-port 8000

docs.title: Reinitializing
docs.text:
If the console is already initialized, the command asks whether to reinitialize. --force skips that question. Reinitializing:

  • stops the mcctl-api and mcctl-console PM2 processes,
  • deletes .mcctl-admin.yml and ecosystem.config.cjs, so the API access mode is chosen again, a new API key is generated for the api-key modes, and the ports return to the defaults unless you pass --api-port and --console-port,
  • keeps data/mcctl.db, so other users are not touched,
  • keeps the console session secret BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in .env, so signed-in users stay signed in.

If the admin email you enter already exists in data/mcctl.db, the command fails with User '<email>' already exists and suggests mcctl console init --force. With --force, that user is deleted (including its sessions) and created again with the new name and password.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text:
All paths are relative to the data directory (MCCTL_ROOT, default ~/minecraft-servers).

File Description .mcctl-admin.yml Main Management Console configuration data/mcctl.db Console user database (created only when mcctl-console is selected) ecosystem.config.cjs PM2 process configuration .env Gets BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, the console session secret, when mcctl-console is selected. A secret already in use is kept

docs.title: mcctl console remove
docs.text: Remove the Management Console PM2 processes and configuration files. The console database (data/mcctl.db) is kept on purpose.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: mcctl console remove [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Description --root <path> Custom data directory --force Skip confirmation prompt --keep-config Keep configuration files for later reinstall

docs.title: What Gets Removed
docs.text:
Component Description PM2 processes mcctl-api, mcctl-console processes are stopped and removed .mcctl-admin.yml Main configuration file ecosystem.config.cjs PM2 ecosystem configuration users.yaml Legacy user credentials file (removed only if it exists)

With --keep-config, the three files above are kept; only the PM2 processes are removed.

docs.title: What Is Kept
docs.text:
Component Description data/mcctl.db Console database: users, sessions and per-user server permissions. Not removed on purpose, so accounts survive a reinstall .services/ The installed mcctl-api and mcctl-console packages api-config.json Settings written by mcctl console api (if present)

Minecraft servers and worlds are not touched.

docs.title: Reinstalling After Removal
docs.text:
Because data/mcctl.db is kept, running mcctl console init again with the same admin email fails with User '<email>' already exists. Use mcctl console init --force to replace that user, or enter a different email.

To start completely from scratch, delete the database yourself:

This cannot be undone

Deleting the database removes every console user, session and per-user server permission.

# Replace ~/minecraft-servers with your data directory (MCCTL_ROOT)
rm -f ~/minecraft-servers/data/mcctl.db*

The * also removes the SQLite -wal and -shm files that sit next to the database.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Interactive removal (prompts for confirmation)
mcctl console remove

# Force removal without confirmation
mcctl console remove --force

# Keep configuration files
mcctl console remove --keep-config

docs.title: Output Example
docs.text:
This will remove:
    - PM2 processes (mcctl-api, mcctl-console)
    - Configuration files (.mcctl-admin.yml, users.yaml)
    - PM2 ecosystem config (ecosystem.config.cjs)

? Are you sure you want to remove Console Service? Yes

Stopping and removing PM2 processes...  Stopped and removed: mcctl-api, mcctl-console
Removing configuration files...  Removed 2 configuration file(s)

Console Service removed successfully

  To reinstall, run: mcctl console init

The confirmation prompt still names users.yaml, but that file is only deleted if it exists, so a current installation reports 2 removed files (.mcctl-admin.yml and ecosystem.config.cjs).

docs.title: mcctl console user
docs.text:
Manage admin console users.

These commands work on data/mcctl.db in the data directory given by MCCTL_ROOT (default ~/minecraft-servers). They do not take --root; for another data directory, set the variable, for example MCCTL_ROOT=/opt/minecraft mcctl console user list.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Subcommand Description list List all users add Add a new user remove Remove a user update Update user role reset-password Reset user password

docs.title: mcctl console user add
docs.text:
Add a new user account. Users are identified by their email address.

mcctl console user add [email] [options]

Options:

Option Description --role <role> User role: admin or user --password <password> User password

Interactive mode:

mcctl console user add

? Email: operator@example.com
? Name: Operator
? Role: User - Standard access
? Password: ********
? Confirm password: ********

User 'operator@example.com' created successfully!

The interactive password prompt requires at least 8 characters.

CLI mode:

mcctl console user add operator@example.com --role user --password "SecurePass123"

{"success":true,"email":"operator@example.com"}

CLI mode applies only when [email], --role, and --password are all given; otherwise the interactive prompts are shown. The user's name is set to the part of the email before @, and the password given with --password is not checked against the 8-character minimum.

Roles:

Role Permissions admin Full access to all features user Standard access, limited to the servers granted to the account

docs.title: mcctl console user remove
docs.text:
Remove a user account.

mcctl console user remove [email] [options]

Options:

Option Description --force Skip confirmation prompt

Interactive mode:

mcctl console user remove

? Select user to remove: operator@example.com (user)
? Are you sure you want to delete user 'operator@example.com'? Yes

User 'operator@example.com' deleted successfully.

CLI mode:

mcctl console user remove operator@example.com --force

Protection

You cannot delete the last admin user. This prevents accidental lockout.

docs.title: mcctl console user update
docs.text:
Update a user's role.

mcctl console user update [email] [options]

Options:

Option Description --role <role> New role: admin or user

Example:

# Promote to admin
mcctl console user update operator@example.com --role admin

# Demote to user
mcctl console user update operator@example.com --role user

docs.title: mcctl console user reset-password
docs.text:
Reset a user's password.

mcctl console user reset-password [email] [options]

Options:

Option Description --password <password> New password (for non-interactive use)

Interactive mode:

mcctl console user reset-password operator@example.com

? New password: ********
? Confirm password: ********

Password for 'operator@example.com' has been reset.

CLI mode:

mcctl console user reset-password operator@example.com --password "NewSecurePass456"

docs.title: mcctl console api
docs.text:
Manage API configuration and access control.

These commands read and write api-config.json in the data directory (MCCTL_ROOT, default ~/minecraft-servers), a separate file from the .mcctl-admin.yml written by mcctl console init. Like mcctl console user, they do not take --root. Until a command saves a change, the defaults are used: mode internal, port 5001, empty IP whitelist.

Changes do not reach the running mcctl-api

These commands only change api-config.json. The running mcctl-api takes its access mode, API key and IP whitelist from the env block of ecosystem.config.cjs (AUTH_MODE, AUTH_API_KEY, AUTH_IP_WHITELIST), which they do not touch. A change made here therefore has no effect on the API, even after mcctl console service restart, and mcctl console api status shows the contents of api-config.json, not necessarily what the running API uses.

The mode and key in effect are the ones chosen during mcctl console init. For now, change them by reinitializing with mcctl console init --force.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text: Subcommand Description status Show API configuration key regenerate Regenerate API key mode Change access mode whitelist Manage IP whitelist

docs.title: mcctl console api status
docs.text:
Show current API configuration.

mcctl console api status [options]

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Example output:

API Configuration

  Access Mode: api-key
  Port: 5001
  API Key: mctk_a1b...9f3c

  IP Whitelist: (empty)

  Mode: External access with X-API-Key header

docs.title: mcctl console api key regenerate
docs.text:
Generate a new API key. All existing clients must be updated.

mcctl console api key regenerate [options]

Options:

Option Description --force Skip confirmation prompt

Example:

mcctl console api key regenerate

? Are you sure you want to regenerate the API key? All existing clients will need to be updated. Yes
Note: saved to /home/user/minecraft-servers/api-config.json only. mcctl-api reads AUTH_* from ecosystem.config.cjs (written by `mcctl console init`), so this does not change the running API. Re-run `mcctl console init` to apply an access mode.
API key regenerated successfully.

New API Key: mctk_0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f00f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0

Please update all clients with the new API key.

docs.title: mcctl console api mode
docs.text:
Change the API access mode.

mcctl console api mode [mode] [options]

Modes:

Mode Description internal Internal access only, no external exposure (most secure) api-key External access with X-API-Key header ip-whitelist IP-based access control api-key-ip Both API key and IP required open No authentication (development only)

Options:

Option Description --force Skip the confirmation shown when switching to open

On success the command prints Access mode changed to: <mode>.

Examples:

# Interactive selection
mcctl console api mode

# Direct mode change
mcctl console api mode api-key

# Force open mode (development only!)
mcctl console api mode open --force

docs.title: mcctl console api whitelist
docs.text:
Manage IP whitelist for ip-whitelist and api-key-ip modes.

mcctl console api whitelist [action] [ip] [options]

Actions:

Action Description list List whitelisted IPs (default when [action] is omitted) add <ip> Add IP or CIDR range (IPv4 only; prompts for the value if <ip> is omitted) remove <ip> Remove IP from whitelist (prompts for a choice if <ip> is omitted)

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format (list only)

Examples:

# List whitelist (same as "whitelist" with no action)
mcctl console api whitelist list

# Add single IP
mcctl console api whitelist add 192.168.1.100

# Add CIDR range
mcctl console api whitelist add 10.0.0.0/8

# Remove IP
mcctl console api whitelist remove 192.168.1.100

docs.title: mcctl console service
docs.text:
Manage Management Console lifecycle via PM2.

Without a terminal

When both the API and the Console are installed, start, stop, restart and logs ask which services to act on. Without a terminal (cron, CI, a pipe) they cannot ask, so they exit with code 1 unless you pass --console (API + Console) or --api. Nothing is chosen for you.

docs.title: Subcommands
docs.text:
Subcommand Description start Start Management Console via PM2 stop Stop Management Console restart Restart Management Console status Show service status logs View service logs

Without a subcommand, mcctl console service shows the status.

docs.title: mcctl console service start
docs.text:
Start Management Console processes (API and Console) via PM2.

mcctl console service start [options]

Options:

Option Description --api Start only mcctl-api --console Start mcctl-console. mcctl-api is started too, because the console depends on it

Without --api or --console, the command asks whether to start "API only" or "API + Console" when both services are installed.

Examples:

# Start services (asks which ones when both are installed)
mcctl console service start

# Start API only
mcctl console service start --api

# Start console (together with the API)
mcctl console service start --console

After starting, the command waits up to 15 seconds for the health checks to pass, prints the status, and exits with code 1 if a started service is not healthy.

Output Example:

[INFO] Starting console services via PM2...
[INFO]   Started mcctl-api
[INFO]   Started mcctl-console
[INFO] Console services started successfully

  Console Service Status (PM2)

  mcctl-api
    Status: online
    PID: 12345
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 50.2 MB
    Uptime: 5s
    Restarts: 0

  mcctl-console
    Status: online
    PID: 12346
    URL: http://localhost:5000
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 80.5 MB
    Uptime: 3s
    Restarts: 0

  All services healthy

docs.title: mcctl console service stop
docs.text:
Stop Management Console processes.

mcctl console service stop [options]

Options:

Option Description --api Stop mcctl-api. mcctl-console is stopped too, because the console cannot run without the API --console Stop only mcctl-console --force Delete the PM2 processes and kill the PM2 daemon (this stops every process PM2 manages, not only the mcctl services)

Without --api or --console, the command asks whether to stop "All services" or "Console only" when both services are installed.

Examples:

# Stop services (asks which ones when both are installed)
mcctl console service stop

# Stop the console only
mcctl console service stop --console

# Stop the API (this also stops the console)
mcctl console service stop --api

docs.title: mcctl console service restart
docs.text:
Restart Management Console processes.

mcctl console service restart [options]

Options:

Option Description --api Restart only mcctl-api --console Restart mcctl-console. mcctl-api is restarted too, because the console depends on it --force Delete the mcctl PM2 processes, kill the PM2 daemon, start the selected mcctl services again, then save the PM2 process list (pm2 save). Everything else PM2 manages (other apps, and an mcctl service you did not select) is stopped with the daemon, is not started again, and is missing from the saved list

Without --api or --console, the command asks whether to restart "API only" or "API + Console" when both services are installed.

A restart without --force keeps the environment and options PM2 already has. After editing ecosystem.config.cjs (for example its env block or max_memory_restart), use --force so the processes are created again from the file. Values that the services read from the platform .env at startup only need a plain restart.

Like start, the command waits up to 15 seconds for the health checks and exits with code 1 if a restarted service is not healthy.

Examples:

# Restart services (asks which ones when both are installed)
mcctl console service restart

# Restart API only
mcctl console service restart --api

# Recreate both processes from ecosystem.config.cjs
mcctl console service restart --console --force

docs.title: mcctl console service status
docs.text:
Show Management Console status via PM2.

mcctl console service status [options]

Options:

Option Description --json Output in JSON format

Example output:

  Console Service Status (PM2)

  mcctl-api
    Status: online
    PID: 12345
    CPU: 2%
    Memory: 52.1 MB
    Uptime: 2h 15m
    Restarts: 0

  mcctl-console
    Status: online
    PID: 12346
    URL: http://localhost:5000
    CPU: 1%
    Memory: 85.3 MB
    Uptime: 2h 15m
    Restarts: 0

  All services healthy

JSON output:

{
  "api": {
    "name": "mcctl-api",
    "status": "online",
    "pid": 12345,
    "cpu": 2,
    "memory": "52.1 MB",
    "uptime": "2h 15m",
    "restarts": 0
  },
  "console": {
    "name": "mcctl-console",
    "status": "online",
    "pid": 12346,
    "cpu": 1,
    "memory": "85.3 MB",
    "uptime": "2h 15m",
    "restarts": 0,
    "url": "http://localhost:5000"
  },
  "healthy": true
}

A service that is not registered in PM2 is null in the JSON output.

docs.title: Health Checks and Exit Codes
docs.text:
For each online service, the command checks over HTTP that it answers: mcctl-api must return a 2xx status for GET /health, and mcctl-console a status below 500 for GET /api/auth/get-session. A failed check adds a line such as Health: HTTP 500 or Health: unreachable to that service ("health" in the JSON output), and the summary changes to Some services need attention.

  • status exits with code 1 when an installed service is not online or fails its check. When neither service is registered in PM2, it prints Services not running and exits with 0.
  • start and restart repeat the checks for up to 15 seconds and exit with code 1 if a service is still not healthy.
  • If the PM2 error log shows a native module built for another Node.js version (NODE_MODULE_VERSION or ERR_DLOPEN_FAILED), the command also prints how to recover: run pm2 kill, switch to the Node.js version used to install mcctl (for example nvm use 22), then run mcctl console service start.

docs.title: mcctl console service logs
docs.text:
View Management Console logs via PM2.

mcctl console service logs [options]

Options:

Option Description -f, --follow Follow log output (stream) --api Show only mcctl-api logs --console Show mcctl-console logs (mcctl-api logs are included as well)

The CLI help describes --console as "Target console service only". For logs, the current behavior also includes mcctl-api, the same selection as start and restart.

Examples:

# View recent logs
mcctl console service logs

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl console service logs -f

# View API logs only
mcctl console service logs --api

# Follow console logs (API logs are included)
mcctl console service logs --console -f

Press Ctrl+C to stop following logs.

docs.title: Common Workflows
docs.text:
Initial Setup:

mcctl console init
mcctl console service start

Add Operator User:

mcctl console user add operator@example.com --role user --password "SecurePass123"

Switch to API Key Mode:

# Choose "api-key" when asked for the API access mode
mcctl console init --force
# Save the API key printed at the end (it is only shown once)
mcctl console service start

mcctl console api mode and mcctl console api key regenerate only change api-config.json, so they do not switch the running API (see the warning under mcctl console api).

Configure IP Whitelist:

# Choose "ip-whitelist" and enter the allowed IPs, comma-separated
mcctl console init --force
mcctl console service start

mcctl console api whitelist likewise only edits api-config.json for now.

Check Service Health:

mcctl console service status
mcctl console service logs --api

Restart After Configuration Change:

# After changing the platform .env (for example in Platform Settings)
mcctl console service restart --console

# After editing ecosystem.config.cjs (a plain restart keeps the old env and options)
mcctl console service restart --console --force

Auto-Start on Boot:

pm2 startup
pm2 save

Remove (keeps data/mcctl.db):

mcctl console remove

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide covers installing and configuring the Management Console for Docker Minecraft servers.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before installing Management Console, ensure you have:

  • [x] Node.js 18 or higher 

    node --version  # Should be v18.0.0 or higher

  • [x] PM2 6 or higher installed globally 

    npm install -g pm2
pm2 --version  # Should be 6.0.0 or higher

  • [x] Docker Engine 24+ and Docker Compose 2.20+ 

    docker --version
docker compose version

  • [x] mcctl installed and initialized 

    npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl
mcctl init

  • [x] At least one Minecraft server created 

    mcctl status

  • [x] Ports available

  • Port 5000 for web console
  • Port 5001 for API

docs.title: Method 1: CLI Installation (Recommended)
docs.text: The simplest way to install Management Console is using the mcctl CLI.

docs.title: Step 1: Initialize Management Console
docs.text:
mcctl console init

This interactive command will prompt you for:

  1. Services to install - mcctl-api is selected by default; also select mcctl-console to install the web console
  2. Admin email - Used to sign in to the web console (e.g., admin@example.com)
  3. Admin name (default: Administrator)
  4. Admin password - Must contain:
    • At least 8 characters
    • At least one uppercase letter
    • At least one lowercase letter
    • At least one number
  5. API access mode - Choose based on your security needs
  6. Additional configuration based on selected mode

The admin email, name, and password are asked only when mcctl-console is selected. Ports are not asked; to change them, see Method 2.

Example session:

$ mcctl console init
Checking prerequisites...
  ✓ Node.js            v20.10.0  (>= 18.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Engine      v24.0.7  (>= 24.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Compose     v2.24.5  (>= 2.20.0)
  ✓ PM2                v6.0.14  (>= 6.0.0)

Initialize Console Service

  Node.js: v20.10.0
  PM2: 6.0.14

? Select services to install: mcctl-api, mcctl-console

  Selected services:
    ✓ mcctl-api
    ✓ mcctl-console

? Admin email? admin@example.com
? Admin name? Administrator
? Admin password? ********
? API access mode? internal - Local network only (default, most secure)

Creating admin user...  Admin user created
Checking mcctl-api installation...  mcctl-api ready
Checking mcctl-console installation...  mcctl-console ready
Resolving service script paths...  Using production node_modules paths
Generating PM2 ecosystem config...  PM2 ecosystem config generated
Saving configuration...  Configuration saved

Console Service initialized!

  Configuration:
    Config file: /home/user/minecraft-servers/.mcctl-admin.yml
    Console DB:  /home/user/minecraft-servers/data/mcctl.db
    PM2 config:  /home/user/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs
    Access mode: internal

  Endpoints:
    API:     http://localhost:5001
    Console: http://localhost:5000

  Next steps:
    1. Start the service: mcctl console service start
    2. Access the console in your browser

  Console usage analytics is on (anonymous install ID and page paths, sent to Google Analytics). To turn it off, set "telemetry": false in /home/user/minecraft-servers/.mcctl.json.

The last line appears only while usage analytics is on (see Usage Analytics).

docs.title: Step 2: Start Services
docs.text:
mcctl console service start --console

--console starts mcctl-api and mcctl-console. Without a flag, the command asks which services to start when both are installed.

Wait for services to start. The command checks each service over HTTP for up to 15 seconds before it prints the status, and exits with code 1 if a service is not healthy:

[INFO] Starting console services via PM2...
[INFO]   Started mcctl-api
[INFO]   Started mcctl-console
[INFO] Console services started successfully

  Console Service Status (PM2)

  mcctl-api
    Status: online
    PID: 12345
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 50.2 MB
    Uptime: 5s
    Restarts: 0

  mcctl-console
    Status: online
    PID: 12346
    URL: http://localhost:5000
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 80.5 MB
    Uptime: 3s
    Restarts: 0

  All services healthy

docs.title: Method 2: Custom Port Configuration
docs.text:
For environments with port conflicts, specify custom ports during initialization:

mcctl console init --api-port 8001 --console-port 8000

mcctl console init never asks for ports interactively; the --api-port and --console-port flags are the only way to set them. The defaults are 5001 for the API and 5000 for the console.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Default MCCTL_ROOT Data directory path ~/minecraft-servers PORT Listening port of each service, set in its env block 5001 (mcctl-api), 5000 (mcctl-console) HOST mcctl-api listening address 127.0.0.1 for the internal access mode, 0.0.0.0 for the others HOSTNAME Console server hostname 0.0.0.0 MCCTL_API_URL Internal API URL http://127.0.0.1:5001 NODE_ENV Environment mode production LOG_LEVEL mcctl-api log level: fatal, error, warn, info, debug, trace, silent info when NODE_ENV=production, otherwise debug WORLD_UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE Max world ZIP size in bytes for POST /api/worlds/upload 1073741824 (1 GB) BETTER_AUTH_SECRET Console session secret, written to <root>/.env by mcctl console init. Changing it signs everyone out Generated BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL Public URL of the console, read from <root>/.env. Set it when users open the console from an address other than localhost, a private LAN address, or a .local name (see Can't Log In) http://localhost:<console port>

docs.title: PM2 Ecosystem Configuration
docs.text:
The mcctl console init command generates ecosystem.config.cjs in the data directory (<root>/ecosystem.config.cjs, where <root> is MCCTL_ROOT, default ~/minecraft-servers). The service packages are installed under <root>/.services/, and the file points to them with absolute paths. The values below are an example for <root> = /home/user/minecraft-servers:

// ecosystem.config.cjs
module.exports = {
  apps: [
    {
      name: 'mcctl-api',
      script: '/home/user/minecraft-servers/.services/node_modules/@minecraft-docker/mcctl-api/dist/index.js',
      cwd: '/home/user/minecraft-servers',
      env: {
        NODE_ENV: 'production',
        PORT: 5001,
        HOST: '127.0.0.1', // internal access mode; 0.0.0.0 for the other modes
        MCCTL_ROOT: '/home/user/minecraft-servers',
        AUTH_MODE: 'ip-whitelist', // written for the "internal" access mode, see the note below the example
        AUTH_IP_WHITELIST: '127.0.0.1,::1,::ffff:127.0.0.1',
        // AUTH_API_KEY is added for the api-key access modes
      },
      instances: 1,
      exec_mode: 'fork',
      watch: false,
      autorestart: true,
      max_memory_restart: '500M',
      // Shutdown waits for a running auto-backup to re-enable auto-save (#734)
      kill_timeout: 130000,
    },
    {
      name: 'mcctl-console',
      script: '/home/user/minecraft-servers/.services/node_modules/@minecraft-docker/mcctl-console/.next/standalone/platform/services/mcctl-console/server.js',
      cwd: '/home/user/minecraft-servers',
      env: {
        NODE_ENV: 'production',
        PORT: 5000,
        HOSTNAME: '0.0.0.0',
        MCCTL_API_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:5001',
        MCCTL_ROOT: '/home/user/minecraft-servers',
        // MCCTL_API_KEY is added for the api-key access modes
        // BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is written to .env, not here
      },
      instances: 1,
      exec_mode: 'fork',
      watch: false,
      autorestart: true,
      max_memory_restart: '500M',
    },
  ],
};

AUTH_MODE values

mcctl console init writes the access mode to AUTH_MODE as the value mcctl-api recognises: internal → ip-whitelist limited to loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1), api-key-ip → combined, open → disabled; api-key and ip-whitelist are written as is.

Only the services you selected during mcctl console init appear in the file. Installations that predate the .services/ directory keep their packages in <root>/node_modules/, and mcctl console init still uses that location when the packages are found there.

kill_timeout: 130000 gives mcctl-api time to finish a running auto-backup when it shuts down. Files written by versions before v3.0.0 do not have it; see Give mcctl-api time to finish an auto-backup.

docs.title: Access Modes
docs.text: mcctl console init asks for the access mode during setup. The mode, API key and IP whitelist are written to the env block of ecosystem.config.cjs (AUTH_MODE, AUTH_API_KEY, AUTH_IP_WHITELIST), which is what the running mcctl-api reads. The mcctl console api commands do not change those values yet (see the warning in CLI Commands), so to switch modes, change the key or change the IP whitelist today, reinitialize with mcctl console init --force.

docs.title: internal (Recommended for Production)
docs.text:
Internal access only, no external exposure. The most secure option for home/local deployments.

mcctl console init
# Select "internal" when prompted for API access mode

docs.title: api-key
docs.text:
Requires X-API-Key header for all API requests.

mcctl console init
# Select "api-key" when prompted
# An API key will be generated and displayed

After initialization, your API key will be displayed. Save it securely.

To get a new API key, reinitialize with mcctl console init --force. mcctl console api key regenerate currently does not change the key the running API uses.

docs.title: ip-whitelist
docs.text:
Only allows access from specified IP addresses or CIDR ranges.

mcctl console init
# Select "ip-whitelist" when prompted
# Enter allowed IPs when prompted (comma-separated)

To change the allowed IPs, reinitialize with mcctl console init --force and enter the new list. mcctl console api whitelist currently does not change the whitelist the running API uses.

Include 127.0.0.1 when you install mcctl-console

The web console calls mcctl-api from the same host, so a list without 127.0.0.1 makes every console request fail with HTTP 403. Write the address: an entry localhost is accepted by the prompt but does not match any request. The same applies to api-key-ip.

docs.title: api-key-ip
docs.text: Requires both a valid API key AND a client IP from the whitelist.

docs.title: open (Development Only)
docs.text:
Security Risk

This mode disables all authentication. Never use in production!

docs.title: Add Users
docs.text:
# Interactive mode
mcctl console user add

# CLI mode
mcctl console user add operator@example.com --role user --password "SecurePass123"

docs.title: List Users
docs.text:
mcctl console user list

Output:

Users:

Email                         Name                Role        Created
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
admin@example.com             Administrator       admin       2025-01-15
operator@example.com          operator            user        2025-01-16

Total: 2 user(s)

docs.title: Update User Role
docs.text: mcctl console user update operator@example.com --role admin

docs.title: Reset Password
docs.text:
# Interactive
mcctl console user reset-password operator@example.com

# CLI
mcctl console user reset-password operator@example.com --password "NewSecurePass456"

docs.title: Remove User
docs.text:
mcctl console user remove operator@example.com

Last Admin Protection

You cannot delete the last admin user. This prevents accidental lockout.

docs.title: Check Service Status
docs.text: mcctl console service status

docs.title: Verify API Health
docs.text:
curl http://localhost:5001/health

Expected response:

{"status":"ok","timestamp":"2026-10-25T12:00:00.000Z"}

docs.title: Access Web Console
docs.text:
1. Open browser to http://localhost:5000
  2. Log in with admin credentials
  3. Verify server list is displayed

docs.title: Services Won't Start
docs.text:
1. Check Node.js version: 

    node --version  # Must be v18.0.0 or higher

  2. Check PM2 is installed: 

    pm2 --version

  3. Check for port conflicts: 

    netstat -tlnp | grep -E "5000|5001"
# or on macOS
lsof -i :5000
lsof -i :5001

  4. View service logs: 

    mcctl console service logs -f

  5. Check PM2 process list: 

    pm2 list
pm2 logs mcctl-api
pm2 logs mcctl-console

docs.title: Can't Log In
docs.text:
1. Verify user exists: 

    mcctl console user list

  2. Reset password: 

    mcctl console user reset-password admin@example.com

  3. Check configuration file (it lives in the data directory, ~/minecraft-servers by default): 

    cat ~/minecraft-servers/.mcctl-admin.yml

  4. Check the address you sign in from: The console accepts sign-ins from localhost, private LAN addresses (10.x, 172.16.x-172.31.x, 192.168.x), .local names, and the URL in BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL. For any other address, such as a Tailscale 100.x address, a domain name, or an HTTPS reverse proxy, set BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL to that URL in ~/minecraft-servers/.env and restart the console: 

    mcctl console service restart --console
    See Login Fails for details.

docs.title: API Returns 401 Unauthorized
