docs.text:
1. Check access mode (the running API reads it from ecosystem.config.cjs; mcctl console api status shows api-config.json instead): 

    grep AUTH_MODE ~/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs

  2. Verify API key (if using api-key mode):

  3. Ensure X-API-Key header is included in requests

  4. The key in use is AUTH_API_KEY in ecosystem.config.cjs. To get a new one, reinitialize with mcctl console init --force

  5. Check IP whitelist (if using ip-whitelist mode): a client IP that is not in the list gets HTTP 403 

    grep AUTH_IP_WHITELIST ~/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs

docs.title: PM2 Process Keeps Restarting
docs.text:
1. Check logs for errors: 

    pm2 logs mcctl-api --lines 100
pm2 logs mcctl-console --lines 100

  2. Check if the service packages are installed (they are installed in the .services/ directory of your data directory): 

    cd ~/minecraft-servers/.services
npm ls @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console
    Installations without a .services/ directory keep the packages in ~/minecraft-servers/node_modules; run npm ls in ~/minecraft-servers instead.

  3. Restart services: 

    mcctl console service restart

docs.title: Auto-Start on Boot
docs.text:
Configure PM2 to start services automatically on system boot:

# Generate startup script
pm2 startup

# Follow the instructions to run the displayed command
# For example:
sudo env PATH=$PATH:/usr/bin pm2 startup systemd -u $USER --hp $HOME

# Save current process list
pm2 save

Now your services will automatically start when the system boots.

docs.title: Update mcctl and Services
docs.text:
mcctl update

mcctl update updates the mcctl CLI and the services installed in <root>/.services/ (mcctl-api, mcctl-console and the shared library) in one step. Each updated PM2 service is restarted automatically; if the output shows Updated (restart manually) for a service, run mcctl console service restart. Installations without a .services/ directory keep the packages in <root>/node_modules, and mcctl update updates them there. When at least one service package is installed, the command also aligns the image tags of your Minecraft servers and pulls the Docker images; this is skipped with --check and --cli-only, and when no service package is installed.

Option Description --check Only check for updates, install nothing --cli-only Update only the CLI and leave the services as they are --yes Skip the confirmation prompt

npm update -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl updates only the CLI package and does not touch the services in .services/. See the mcctl update reference for all options.

docs.title: Reinitialize After Major Update
docs.text:
If there are breaking changes, reinitialize the console:

# Reinitialize: stops the services and deletes the console settings
mcctl console init --force

# Start services
mcctl console service start --console

--force does not preserve your settings. It stops the PM2 services and deletes .mcctl-admin.yml and ecosystem.config.cjs, so you choose the API access mode again, the ports return to the defaults unless you pass --api-port and --console-port, and a new API key is generated for the api-key modes. The console database data/mcctl.db is kept: other users stay as they are. The session secret BETTER_AUTH_SECRET in .env is kept as well, so other users stay signed in. If you enter the email of an existing admin, that user is deleted (including its sessions) and created again with the password you enter now. If you enter a different email, the existing admin stays and a new admin is added.

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text:
To remove Management Console:

# Remove console service (interactive)
mcctl console remove

# Or force remove without confirmation
mcctl console remove --force

# Keep configuration files for later reinstall
mcctl console remove --keep-config

This will:

  • Stop and remove PM2 processes (mcctl-api, mcctl-console)
  • Delete configuration files (.mcctl-admin.yml, and the legacy users.yaml if it exists)
  • Delete PM2 ecosystem config (ecosystem.config.cjs)

Data Preservation

Removing Management Console does not affect your Minecraft servers or world data.

Console database is kept

data/mcctl.db (console users, sessions and per-user server permissions) and the packages in .services/ are not removed. This is intentional, so accounts survive a reinstall. To run mcctl console init again with the same admin email you need --force; without it the command fails with User '<email>' already exists.

To start completely from scratch, also delete the database:

This cannot be undone

Deleting the database removes every console user, session and per-user server permission.

rm -f ~/minecraft-servers/data/mcctl.db*

See mcctl console remove for the full list of removed and kept items.

docs.title: Clean Up PM2 (Optional)
docs.text:
If you want to completely remove PM2 configuration:

# Remove saved process list
pm2 unstartup

# Kill PM2 daemon
pm2 kill

docs.title: Complete Setup Guide: From Init to Console
docs.text: This guide walks you through the complete one-stop setup process, from initializing the mcctl platform to launching the Management Console with a web-based admin interface. By the end, you will have a fully operational Minecraft server management platform with both CLI and web-based management capabilities.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The setup process consists of three main phases:

flowchart LR
    A["mcctl init"] --> B["mcctl console init"]
    B --> C["mcctl console service start"]

    A --- A1["Platform Setup"]
    B --- B1["API + Console Setup"]
    C --- C1["Launch Services"]
Phase Command What It Does 1. Platform Init mcctl init Creates directory structure, configures Docker network, sets up host IP 2. Console Init mcctl console init Installs API/Console services, creates admin user, configures authentication 3. Service Start mcctl console service start Starts PM2-managed API and Console processes

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before starting, ensure you have the following installed:

  • [x] Node.js 18 or higher 

    node --version  # Should be v18.0.0 or higher

  • [x] Docker Engine 24.0.0 or higher 

    docker --version
docker compose version  # v2.20.0 or higher required

  • [x] mcctl CLI installed globally 

    npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl
mcctl --version

New Installation?

If you haven't installed mcctl yet, see the Installation Guide for detailed instructions on setting up Node.js, Docker, and mcctl.

docs.title: Phase 1: Platform Initialization (mcctl init)
docs.text: The mcctl init command sets up the foundational platform for running Minecraft servers.

docs.title: Running the Command
docs.text:
mcctl init

The initialization process goes through 6 steps:

docs.title: Step 1: Prerequisite Check
docs.text:
mcctl automatically checks that all required software is installed and meets version requirements.

[1/6] Checking prerequisites...
  ✓ Node.js            v20.10.0  (>= 18.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Engine      v24.0.7  (>= 24.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Compose     v2.24.5  (>= 2.20.0)
  ✓ avahi-daemon       running  (>= any)

avahi-daemon is optional: when it is missing the line shows ⚠ with an install hint, and init continues.

Prerequisite Failures

If any check fails, the init process stops and displays instructions on how to install the missing component. Fix the issue and run mcctl init again.

docs.title: Step 2: Directory Structure
docs.text:
mcctl creates the platform directory structure at ~/minecraft-servers/ (default):

[2/6] Creating directory structure...

  Created: ~/.minecraft-servers/servers
  Created: ~/.minecraft-servers/servers/_template
  Created: ~/.minecraft-servers/worlds
  Created: ~/.minecraft-servers/shared/plugins
  Created: ~/.minecraft-servers/backups

Custom Data Directory

To use a different location, specify --root: 

mcctl --root /path/to/data init

docs.title: Step 3: Template Files
docs.text:
Configuration templates are copied to the data directory:

[3/6] Copying template files...

  Copied: docker-compose.yml
  Copied: .env
  Copied: .gitignore
  Copied: servers/compose.yml
  Copied: servers/global.env
  Copied: servers/_template/docker-compose.yml
  Copied: servers/_template/config.env
  ✓ Set DOCKER_GID from docker socket

servers/global.env lists the platform .env keys that are passed to every server container. DOCKER_GID is the group of the Docker socket, which mc-router needs to read it.

docs.title: Step 4: Host IP Configuration
docs.text:
You are prompted to select the host IP address(es) used for server hostname routing (nip.io):

[4/6] Configuring host IP address(es)...

  Detected network interfaces:
    192.168.1.100 (eth0)
    172.17.0.1 (docker0)

? Select host IP address(es):
  ✓ 192.168.1.100 (eth0)

  ✓ Set HOST_IP=192.168.1.100

Multiple IPs

If you have multiple network interfaces (e.g., LAN + VPN), you can select multiple IPs. The first becomes the primary HOST_IP, and all are stored in HOST_IPS for multi-hostname routing.

docs.title: Step 4.5: playit.gg Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
You can optionally enable playit.gg tunneling for external access without port forwarding:

[4.5/6] Configuring playit.gg (optional)...

  playit.gg enables external access without port forwarding.
  Setup: https://playit.gg/account/agents/new-docker

? Enable playit.gg tunneling? No
  ✓ playit.gg disabled

Skip for Now

You can always configure playit.gg later with mcctl init --reconfigure. For the initial setup, it is fine to skip this step.

docs.title: Step 5: Configuration File
docs.text:
The platform configuration file .mcctl.json is created:

[5/6] Creating configuration...

  Created: .mcctl.json

docs.title: Step 6: Docker Network
docs.text:
mcctl creates a dedicated Docker bridge network for Minecraft servers:

[6/6] Setting up Docker network...

  ✓ Created network: minecraft-net

docs.title: Init Complete
docs.text:
After all steps complete successfully, you see:

════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ✓ Platform initialized successfully!
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  Next steps:

  1. Edit configuration (optional):
     nano ~/minecraft-servers/.env

  2. Create your first server:
     mcctl create myserver

  3. Connect via Minecraft:
     myserver.local:25565

  For help:
     mcctl --help

At this point, your platform is ready to create and manage Minecraft servers via the CLI. To add the web-based management interface, continue to Phase 2.

docs.title: Phase 2: Console Initialization (mcctl console init)
docs.text: The mcctl console init command installs and configures the Management Console, which provides a REST API (mcctl-api) and an optional web management UI (mcctl-console).

docs.title: Running the Command
docs.text: mcctl console init

docs.title: Step 1: Prerequisite Check
docs.text:
Console init verifies additional prerequisites beyond the platform init:

Checking prerequisites...
  ✓ Node.js            v20.10.0  (>= 18.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Engine      v24.0.7  (>= 24.0.0)
  ✓ Docker Compose     v2.24.5  (>= 2.20.0)
  ✓ PM2                v6.0.14  (>= 6.0.0)

PM2 Required

mcctl console init stops when the pm2 command is not on your PATH or is older than 6.0.0. Install PM2 globally: 

npm install -g pm2
mcctl also ships the PM2 library for its own calls (for example mcctl console service), but that does not put a pm2 command on your PATH, so it does not satisfy this check.

docs.title: Step 2: Service Selection
docs.text:
You are prompted to select which services to install:

Initialize Console Service

  Node.js: v20.10.0
  PM2: 6.0.14

? Select services to install:
  ✓ mcctl-api       - REST API server for managing Minecraft servers
  ○ mcctl-console   - Web UI for server management
Service Description Default Port mcctl-api Fastify REST API server that manages Minecraft servers via Docker and RCON 5001 mcctl-console Next.js web application with dashboard, server management, and admin features 5000

API-Only Mode

If you only need the REST API (for automation, scripts, or building your own UI), select only mcctl-api. You can always add mcctl-console later by running mcctl console init again.

docs.title: Step 3: Admin User Setup (Console Only)
docs.text:
If you selected mcctl-console, you are prompted to create an admin account:

Admin Email:

? Admin email? admin@example.com

The email is used for authentication via Better Auth.

Admin Name:

? Admin name? Administrator

A display name for the admin account.

Admin Password:

? Admin password? ********

Password requirements:

  • At least 8 characters
  • At least one uppercase letter (A-Z)
  • At least one lowercase letter (a-z)
  • At least one number (0-9)

API-Only Mode

If you only selected mcctl-api (without mcctl-console), the admin user setup is skipped entirely. Authentication is handled via API access modes instead.

docs.title: Step 4: API Access Mode
docs.text:
Select the authentication mode for the REST API:

? API access mode?
  ● internal       - Local network only (default, most secure)
  ○ api-key        - External access with API key
  ○ ip-whitelist   - IP-based access control
  ○ api-key-ip     - Both API key and IP required
  ○ open           - No authentication (development only)
Mode Security Level Best For internal Highest Home/local network deployments api-key High Remote access, automation scripts ip-whitelist High Known client IPs, corporate networks api-key-ip Maximum High-security environments requiring both open None Local development/testing only

Access modes

mcctl console init writes the access mode to AUTH_MODE as the value mcctl-api recognises: internal → ip-whitelist limited to loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1), api-key-ip → combined, open → disabled; api-key and ip-whitelist are written as is.

open Mode Warning

The open mode disables all authentication. If you select it, a confirmation prompt appears: 

WARNING: Open mode has no authentication. Use only for local development!
? Are you sure you want to use open mode? No
Never use open mode in production or on networks accessible from the internet.

docs.title: Step 5: API Key Generation (Conditional)
docs.text:
If you selected api-key or api-key-ip mode, an API key is automatically generated:

Generating API key...  API key generated

The API key is displayed at the end of initialization. Save it securely -- it is shown only once.

docs.title: Step 6: IP Whitelist Configuration (Conditional)
docs.text:
If you selected ip-whitelist or api-key-ip mode, you are prompted for allowed IPs:

? Allowed IPs (comma-separated)? 127.0.0.1, 192.168.1.0/24

You can enter individual IPv4 addresses or CIDR ranges, separated by commas.

Include 127.0.0.1 when you install mcctl-console

The web console calls mcctl-api from the same host, and mcctl-api refuses requests from addresses that are not in the list (HTTP 403). If you also install mcctl-console, include 127.0.0.1. Write the address: an entry localhost is accepted by the prompt but does not match any request.

docs.title: Step 7: Service Installation
docs.text:
When mcctl-console is selected, the admin user is created in data/mcctl.db first. Then the selected packages (mcctl-api, mcctl-console) are installed from npm if they are not installed yet:

Creating admin user...  Admin user created
Checking mcctl-api installation...  mcctl-api ready
Checking mcctl-console installation...  mcctl-console ready

The packages are installed in the .services/ directory under your data root.

docs.title: Step 8: PM2 Ecosystem Configuration
docs.text:
A PM2 ecosystem configuration file is generated:

Resolving service script paths...  Using production node_modules paths
Generating PM2 ecosystem config...  PM2 ecosystem config generated

This creates ecosystem.config.cjs in the data directory (~/minecraft-servers by default), which tells PM2 how to run the API and Console processes.

When mcctl-console is selected, this step also writes the console session secret BETTER_AUTH_SECRET to .env in the data directory. The secret already in use is kept, so signed-in users stay signed in.

docs.title: Step 9: Configuration Save
docs.text:
The admin configuration is saved:

Saving configuration...  Configuration saved

docs.title: Console Init Complete
docs.text:
After all steps, a summary is displayed:

Console Service initialized!

  Configuration:
    Config file: /home/user/minecraft-servers/.mcctl-admin.yml
    Console DB:  /home/user/minecraft-servers/data/mcctl.db
    PM2 config:  /home/user/minecraft-servers/ecosystem.config.cjs
    Access mode: internal

  Endpoints:
    API:     http://localhost:5001
    Console: http://localhost:5000

  Next steps:
    1. Start the service: mcctl console service start
    2. Access the console in your browser

If you chose api-key or api-key-ip mode, the API key is also displayed:

  API Key (save this, shown only once):
    mctk_a1B2c3D4e5F6g7H8i9J0...

For ip-whitelist and api-key-ip, the summary also lists the allowed IPs. While usage analytics is on, a notice about it is printed at the end (see Usage Analytics).

Save Your API Key

The API key is only shown once during initialization. Copy and store it in a secure location. The key the running API uses is AUTH_API_KEY in ecosystem.config.cjs; to get a new one, reinitialize with mcctl console init --force. mcctl console api key regenerate currently does not change that key (see the warning in CLI Commands).

docs.title: Phase 3: Starting Services (mcctl console service start)
docs.text:
Now that everything is configured, start the services. --console starts mcctl-api and mcctl-console; without a flag the command asks which services to start when both are installed:

mcctl console service start --console

docs.title: Service Startup
docs.text:
PM2 starts the configured services:

[INFO] Starting console services via PM2...
[INFO]   Started mcctl-api
[INFO]   Started mcctl-console
[INFO] Console services started successfully

docs.title: Status Verification
docs.text:
After starting, the command checks each service over HTTP (waiting up to 15 seconds) and displays a status report. If a service does not become healthy, the report shows a Health: line for it and the command exits with code 1:

  Console Service Status (PM2)

  mcctl-api
    Status: online
    PID: 12345
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 50.2 MB
    Uptime: 5s
    Restarts: 0

  mcctl-console
    Status: online
    PID: 12346
    URL: http://localhost:5000
    CPU: 0%
    Memory: 80.5 MB
    Uptime: 3s
    Restarts: 0

  All services healthy

docs.title: Verify API Health
docs.text:
Test the API endpoint:

curl http://localhost:5001/health

Expected response:

{"status":"ok","timestamp":"2026-10-25T12:00:00.000Z"}

docs.title: Access the Web Console
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:5000
  2. Log in with the admin email and password you created during mcctl console init
  3. You should see the Dashboard with your Minecraft server list

docs.title: Complete Setup Example
docs.text:
Here is the entire setup flow from start to finish:

# Step 1: Install mcctl
npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl

# Step 2: Initialize platform
mcctl init
# Follow interactive prompts (IP selection, playit.gg)

# Step 3: Create your first Minecraft server
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Step 4: Initialize Management Console
mcctl console init
# Select services -> Create admin user -> Choose access mode

# Step 5: Start Console services
mcctl console service start --console

# Step 6: Verify everything is running
mcctl status                    # Check Minecraft servers
mcctl console service status    # Check Console services
curl http://localhost:5001/health  # Check API health

# Step 7: Open web console
# Navigate to http://localhost:5000 in your browser

docs.title: Configuration Files Reference
docs.text:
After completing the full setup, the following files exist in your data directory:

File Created By Description .mcctl.json mcctl init Platform configuration (version, defaults, features) .env mcctl init Environment variables (HOST_IP, timezone, RCON password, and more). mcctl console init adds BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, the console session secret docker-compose.yml mcctl init Main Docker orchestration for mc-router .mcctl-admin.yml mcctl console init Console service configuration (access mode, ports) data/mcctl.db mcctl console init SQLite database for user accounts (Better Auth) ecosystem.config.cjs mcctl console init PM2 process configuration for API and Console

docs.title: Auto-Start on Boot
docs.text:
To ensure your services start automatically when the system boots:

# Generate PM2 startup script
pm2 startup

# Run the command that PM2 displays (example):
sudo env PATH=$PATH:/usr/bin pm2 startup systemd -u $USER --hp $HOME

# Save current process list
pm2 save

docs.title: Custom Port Configuration
docs.text:
If the default ports (5000, 5001) conflict with other services, specify custom ports:

mcctl console init --api-port 8001 --console-port 8000

The ports are written to ecosystem.config.cjs, and the services always start on them. To change the ports of an existing installation, reinitialize with the new values: mcctl console init --force --api-port 8001 --console-port 8000.

docs.title: Reconfigure Platform Settings
docs.text:
To change platform settings (IP, memory, timezone) without full reinitialization:

mcctl init --reconfigure

docs.title: Reinitialize Console
docs.text:
To reset the Console configuration (useful after major updates):

mcctl console init --force

The --force flag skips the confirmation prompt and cleans up existing configuration before reinitializing.

docs.title: mcctl init Says "Already Initialized"
docs.text:
[WARN] Platform is already initialized

Solution: Use --reconfigure to change settings, or delete the data directory to start fresh:

# Option 1: Reconfigure existing setup
mcctl init --reconfigure

# Option 2: Full reset (WARNING: deletes all server data)
rm -rf ~/minecraft-servers
mcctl init

docs.title: Docker Network Creation Fails
docs.text:
[WARN] Failed to create Docker network (may already exist)

Solution: The network may already exist. Check with:

docker network ls | grep minecraft-net

docs.title: "Platform not initialized" Error
docs.text:
[ERROR] Platform not initialized. Run: mcctl init

Solution: Run mcctl init first before running mcctl console init.

docs.title: PM2 Not Installed
docs.text:
✗ PM2                not found  (>= 6.0.0)
    npm install -g pm2

[ERROR] PM2 is not installed

With a PM2 older than 6.0.0 the line shows its version, and the error is PM2 version <version> does not meet minimum requirement >= 6.0.0.

Solution:

npm install -g pm2

docs.title: Package Installation Fails
docs.text:
[ERROR] Failed to install mcctl-api: ...
[INFO] Try installing manually: npm install @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api

Solution: Try installing manually:

cd ~/minecraft-servers/.services
npm install @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api@latest
npm install @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console@latest

docs.title: Ecosystem Config Not Found
docs.text:
[ERROR] Ecosystem config not found.
[INFO] Please run 'mcctl console init' to initialize console services

Solution: Run mcctl console init to generate the ecosystem configuration.

docs.title: Port Already in Use
docs.text:
# Check which process is using the port
lsof -i :5000
lsof -i :5001

# Or use netstat
netstat -tlnp | grep -E "5000|5001"

Solution: Either stop the conflicting process or use custom ports with --api-port and --console-port.

docs.title: Services Keep Restarting
docs.text:
# Check logs for errors
mcctl console service logs -f

# Or check PM2 logs directly
pm2 logs mcctl-api --lines 100
pm2 logs mcctl-console --lines 100

Common causes:

  • Missing dependencies: Run mcctl console init again
  • Port conflicts: Use custom ports
  • Memory limit: PM2 restarts a service that grows past max_memory_restart (500M in ecosystem.config.cjs). Raise the value there, then apply it with mcctl console service restart --console --force, because a plain restart keeps the previous PM2 settings

docs.title: Cannot Log In to Web Console
docs.text:
1. Verify the admin user was created: 

    mcctl console user list

  2. Reset the admin password: 

    mcctl console user reset-password admin@example.com

  3. Check that mcctl-console is running: 

    mcctl console service status

  4. If you open the console from an address other than localhost, a private LAN address, or a .local name (for example a Tailscale 100.x address, a domain name, or an HTTPS reverse proxy), set BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL to that URL in .env and run mcctl console service restart --console. See Login Fails.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
After completing the setup:

  • Web Console Guide - Learn how to use the web management interface
  • CLI Commands - Complete Console CLI reference
  • API Reference - REST API documentation
  • Quick Start - Create and manage Minecraft servers

docs.title: Web Console Guide
docs.text: Complete user guide for the mcctl-console web management interface -- a modern, full-featured dashboard for managing Docker Minecraft servers from your browser.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The mcctl-console is a Next.js web application that provides a graphical interface to every aspect of your Minecraft server infrastructure. Instead of running CLI commands, you can manage servers, worlds, players, backups, audit logs, and routing through an intuitive dark-themed UI with real-time updates powered by Server-Sent Events (SSE).

Default URL: http://localhost:5000

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
mcctl-console uses a Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) proxy pattern for secure API communication:

+------------------+      +-------------------+      +---------------+
|   Web Browser    | ---> |   mcctl-console   | ---> |   mcctl-api   |
|   (React/Query)  |      |   (Next.js BFF)   |      |   (Fastify)   |
+------------------+      +-------------------+      +---------------+
       ^                          |
       |                   Session Auth +
       |                   X-API-Key forwarding
       |
   React Query
   (auto-refresh)

docs.title: Why BFF Proxy?
docs.text:
1. Security: API keys stay server-side, never exposed to the browser
  2. Session Management: Better Auth keeps sessions in the console database (data/mcctl.db) and identifies them with a session cookie
  3. Type Safety: Shared TypeScript interfaces between frontend and backend
  4. Caching: React Query provides optimistic updates and intelligent caching

docs.title: Signing In
docs.text:
1. Start the Management Console services. --console starts mcctl-api and mcctl-console; without a flag the command asks which services to start when both are installed: 

    mcctl console service start --console

  2. Open your browser and navigate to http://localhost:5000. You are redirected to the Welcome Back sign-in page.

  3. Enter your credentials:

    • Email: The admin email you entered during mcctl console init
    • Password: The admin password (use the eye icon to show or hide it)

  4. Click Sign In. After a successful login you land on the Dashboard.

Session Persistence

A session stays valid for 7 days and is extended automatically (at most once every 24 hours) while you keep using the console. Click Logout in the user avatar menu (top-right corner) to end your session manually.

docs.title: Signing Up
docs.text:
If you do not have an account yet, click Sign up under the sign-in form ("Don't have an account? Sign up") to open the Create Account page:

  1. Enter your Name and Email
  2. Choose a Password (at least 8 characters) and type it again in Confirm Password
  3. Click Sign Up

The account is created, you are signed in immediately, and you land on the Dashboard. Use Sign in under the form to go back to the sign-in page.

New accounts start with the User role

New accounts get the User role. A User sees only the servers that an administrator or a server Owner has granted access to (see Access Tab), so the Servers page stays empty until access is granted. A server created by a User automatically gives that User the Owner permission on it. The sign-up page does not send a verification email.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: The Dashboard is your command center -- it gives you an at-a-glance overview of your entire Minecraft server infrastructure.

docs.title: Status Hero
docs.text:
Since v2.28.0, the Dashboard opens with a status hero that summarizes platform health: how many servers are online (for example, "2 of 3 servers online" with a progress bar), how many servers need attention (not running, or unhealthy; "All systems operational" when none), and a Live / Reconnecting chip that reflects the real-time (SSE) connection. When server data cannot be loaded, the hero says so instead of showing zero.

The Create Server button in the hero opens the Servers page with the Create New Server dialog already open.

docs.title: Statistics Cards
docs.text:
Below the status hero, four cards provide key metrics:

Card Description Total Servers The number of configured servers, with a running / stopped breakdown and a bar for the running share Online Players Players online on the running servers, shown as online / max, with "Across N running servers" (plus "M not responding" when a running server does not answer the player query). Shows — and "Player data unavailable" when no player data is available Worlds The number of worlds in your world storage, with an assigned / free breakdown mc-router The router's listening port (for example :25565) with its container status, health and number of routes. The card is green while the router runs, red while it is down or unhealthy, and amber in other states such as starting or restarting

docs.title: Servers Panel
docs.text:
The left side of the Dashboard displays a Servers panel with a status filter (All, Running, Stopped, each with a count) and up to five servers. Each row shows:

  • Server name, a status chip (such as running, exited, or created) and, when the container reports a health state, an outlined health chip (healthy, unhealthy, or starting)
  • The primary hostname (the LAN nip.io address when the server has one) with a copy button; click the +N chip to list all hostnames
  • Players (online / max) and Memory (used / limit) for a running server, the memory allocation for a stopped one, and Type (TYPE · version)
  • Action buttons: Console (opens the server console page), Restart and Stop for a running server, and Start for a stopped one. Restart and Stop ask for confirmation first, because connected players are disconnected

Click a row to open the server's detail page. When you have more than five servers, a View All (N) link in the panel header opens the full Servers page.

docs.title: External Access Card
docs.text:
On the right side, the External Access card shows your playit.gg tunnel status:

  • How many servers have external domains configured (e.g., "1 / 3 servers")
  • Current agent status (Running or Stopped) and, while the agent runs, its uptime, or a Not configured chip when playit.gg is not set up
  • Up to three servers with their external address and a copy button
  • A Manage link to navigate to the Routing page for detailed configuration

docs.title: Recent Activity Feed
docs.text:
The Recent Activity feed displays the latest management actions performed on your servers, such as:

  • Server start/stop events
  • Backup schedule changes
  • Configuration modifications
  • Player management actions

Each entry shows a colored dot (red for a failure, blue for backups, purple for configuration changes, config snapshots and Platform Settings, green for other server actions, gray for the rest), the action type (with a color-coded badge), the target server or resource, who performed the action, and how long ago it occurred (hover to see the exact time). Actions done in the web console show console as the actor (see Audit Log). Failed actions carry an extra status badge. Click View All to navigate to the full Audit Log page.

docs.title: Recent Updates Feed
docs.text:
The Recent Updates card shows the latest release from the project's CHANGELOG.md on the GitHub main branch: its version, date, and Added, Fixed, and Changed items. An Update available chip appears when that version is newer than the installed console, and View all opens the full changelog on GitHub.

The console server fetches the changelog itself (through GET /api/changelog) and caches it for one hour. When GitHub cannot be reached it keeps showing the last copy it fetched; without one, the card says "Unable to load updates".

docs.title: Servers
docs.text: The Servers page is where you manage all your Minecraft servers.

docs.title: Server List
docs.text:
A summary panel at the top of the page shows a Live / Reconnecting indicator and the + Create Server button. Below it, three cards show Total servers, Running servers, and Needs attention (stopped or unhealthy servers). Then the page displays all configured servers as cards in a grid layout. Each server card shows:

  • Server name (e.g., botagent, factory, wild-deity)
  • Status badge -- Running (green), Stopped (red), or Created / Not Created
  • Hostname -- the primary address (the LAN nip.io address when the server has one) with the number of additional hostnames (e.g., botagent.192.168.1.10.nip.io +2) -- click the +2 chip to list all hostnames
  • Container name (e.g., mc-botagent)
  • Quick action button -- Start (play) for stopped servers or Stop for running servers, in the bottom-right corner

docs.title: Filtering and Search
docs.text:
Above the cards, you can filter servers by status:

  • ALL -- Show all servers
  • RUNNING -- Show only running servers
  • STOPPED -- Show only stopped servers

A Search servers... box on the right allows you to filter servers by name in real time. The number of matching servers is shown below the filters.

docs.title: Creating a New Server
docs.text:
Click the + Create Server button in the page header to open the Create New Server dialog. The dialog guides you through:

  1. Server Name -- A unique identifier: 2-32 characters of lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, starting with a letter and not ending with a hyphen, without --. router is reserved
  2. Server Type -- Choose a category with the toggle:
    • Standard Server -- Pick a Server Type (VANILLA, PAPER, FABRIC, FORGE, or NEOFORGE) and a Minecraft Version (e.g., 1.21.1 or LATEST). The defaults are VANILLA and LATEST. For other types, pin a version such as 1.21.1 if the loader doesn't support the newest Minecraft release yet
    • Modpack -- Search Modrinth modpacks by name (or type a slug such as cobblemon), then choose a Mod Loader and a compatible Minecraft Version. Client-only mods that are detected are added to Exclude mods (optional) automatically; you can edit that comma-separated list
  3. World Setup -- Default World, Seed (enter a seed), or Existing World (pick an unassigned world)
  4. Memory -- How much RAM to assign (default 4G for standard servers, 6G for modpacks)
  5. Sudo Password -- Required for mDNS hostname registration (avahi). If you leave it empty, Create asks you to confirm: choose Continue without password when sudo on the host doesn't ask for one, or Enter password to go back to the field
  6. Auto-start after creation -- Start the server as soon as it is created

Click Create to start. The dialog waits for mcctl-api to create the server, then steps through a progress view (Initializing, Creating, Configuring, Starting). It ends with one of:

  • Server Created Successfully
  • Server Created with a Warning -- The server exists, but its first start failed or is still running in the background (for example while the image is pulled). The dialog stays open and shows the reason; start or check the server from its detail page
  • Creation Failed -- The error is shown on the Servers page

docs.title: Server Detail Page
docs.text: Click on any server card to open the detailed server management view. The detail page features:

docs.title: Header Section
docs.text:
• An All servers button to go back to the list
  • The server name with a Switch server button next to it, which lists your servers (a green dot marks running ones) and opens the one you pick
  • Chips for the current state (e.g., Running, Exited), the health (e.g., Healthy, Unhealthy, or Unknown when the container has no health check), the server type and the Minecraft version, and a Reconnecting chip while the real-time connection is being restored
  • The hostname (with a copy button and the number of additional hostnames) and the uptime
  • Start for a stopped server, or Stop and Restart for a running server
  • A ⋮ menu with Delete Server. The confirmation dialog requires you to type the server name, and the deletion cannot be undone. A running server is stopped and removed. The dialog also asks what to do with the world: Keep the world (move to worlds/) is the default and moves the server's world to worlds/ (a world already in worlds/ is just unassigned); Delete the world inside the server too removes the server's own world. Worlds in worlds/ are never deleted. If the deletion fails (for example worlds/<name> already exists), nothing is deleted and the error is shown in the page
  • The delete dialog has an optional Sudo Password field, used to remove the server's <name>.local entry from /etc/avahi/hosts. Leave it empty on hosts where sudo needs no password. The password is used only for this request and is cleared when the dialog closes. If the hostname entry or some files could not be removed, the dialog changes to Server deleted and shows the warning; Close returns to the server list

docs.title: Navigation Tabs
docs.text:
The server detail page is organized into ten tabs, each with an icon. The Players tab shows the number of online players, and the Mods tab shows the number of installed mod files once the Mods tab has loaded them. To open a tab directly, add ?tab=<Tab> to the URL, for example /servers/survival?tab=Options.

Tab Description Overview Server console with live log output and RCON command input, plus settings, online players, and connection details Players Online + offline player roster with management actions and a per-player detail view (v2.27.0+) World The assigned world's info, BlueMap web map, ore & block statistics, and player locations Activity Per-server audit history showing all actions performed on this server Mods Mod management -- search, install, and remove mods from Modrinth Files Full file manager for browsing, editing, uploading, and downloading server files Config History Timeline of server configuration snapshots with compare, restore, and delete Backups Config Snapshots and World Backups for this server Access User permission management -- grant, modify, or revoke access per user Options Server configuration editor with hostname management and game settings

docs.title: Resource Monitoring
docs.text:
Above the tabs, three cards display resource usage:

  • CPU usage -- Current CPU utilization with one decimal, marked High from 70% and Critical from 90%
  • Memory usage -- RAM in use against the allocated memory (used / allocated, in GB), with the percentage and the same High / Critical marks
  • World size -- The disk space used by the current world, with the world name

Without resource statistics (for example while the server is stopped), the CPU and memory cards show — and "No data".

docs.title: Overview Tab
docs.text: The Overview tab is the default view when you open a server's detail page. It serves as a real-time command center for monitoring and interacting with your server.

docs.title: Console
docs.text:
The centerpiece of the Overview tab is the Console panel, which provides direct access to the server's live log output and command interface:

  • Live Log Stream -- The console displays server log messages in real time, including timestamped entries for server events such as world loading, player connections, and game state changes. Each log line includes the timestamp and log level (e.g., INFO) for easy troubleshooting. Lines are colored by event: errors red, warnings amber, players joining green, players leaving blue, and the startup "Done" line green. RCON housekeeping lines are filtered out, and the header shows a Connected / Disconnected indicator for the log stream.
  • Command Input -- At the bottom of the console, type a command after the > prompt (e.g., say Hello!, gamemode creative Player1, time set day) and press Enter or click Send to run it through RCON. The chips below the field (/list, /tps, /save-all, /say, /whitelist list) put a command into the field. The RCON reply to a command is not shown: the console shows only what the server writes to its log. The field is disabled while the server is not running or the log stream is connecting or reconnecting, and the reason is shown below it. If a request fails, the error is shown below the field.
  • Toolbar -- The panel header has Jump to latest (shown when you have scrolled up), Download logs (saves the lines the console holds as <server>-console.log), Clear console (screen only), and Expand console.
  • Auto-Scroll -- The console follows new log entries while you are at the bottom. Scroll up to read older lines; Jump to latest takes you back.
  • Expanded Console -- Expand console opens a full-screen Console - <server> dialog with a log level filter (ALL, INFO, WARN, ERROR), Auto-scroll and Hide RCON checkboxes, a clear-logs button, a Reconnect button when disconnected, Quick command buttons (say, give, tp, gamemode), and an Enter command... input with a Send button. Use the Up and Down arrow keys in the input to repeat commands sent in the dialog. The dialog does not show the RCON reply either.

Console Commands

The console supports all standard Minecraft server commands. You do not need to prefix commands with / -- simply type the command name and its arguments directly (e.g., whitelist add Player1).

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The Settings panel below the console lists what the header does not show:

Field Description Container The Docker container name (e.g., mc-botagent) Memory allocation The allocated memory (e.g., 4G) World The world the server uses

The server name, type, Minecraft version, hostname, and uptime are in the header.

docs.title: Players
docs.text: The Players panel shows the online / max player count and one row per online player, with the player's avatar and OP and Whitelisted badges. Click a row to open the player detail modal. When nobody is online, it shows "No players online".

docs.title: Connection
docs.text:
The Connection card shows how clients can reach the server:

  • Addresses -- Every hostname of the server with port 25565 and a copy button, labeled by kind: LAN, Tailscale / VPN, nip.io, External (your own domain), or mDNS (.local). LAN addresses are listed first
  • External Address -- The playit.gg domain assigned to this server (with a copy button), or Not configured. This row appears when playit.gg is enabled

Copy buttons also work when the console is opened over plain HTTP from another machine, and show a message if copying fails.

docs.title: Server Console Page
docs.text: The Console button on a running server in the Dashboard opens /servers/<name>/console, a full-page console for that server. The header shows the connection state (Connected, Connecting, or Disconnected (Retry N)), a breadcrumb (Servers › server name › Console), and a back button to the server's detail page. The console itself works like the expanded console: log level filter, Auto-scroll, Hide RCON, Quick command buttons, and a command input with history. It does not show the RCON reply to a command.

docs.title: Players Tab
docs.text:
Available since v2.27.0.

The Players tab lists every player known to the server, not just those currently online. It combines two sources:

  • Online players -- queried live via RCON while the server is running
  • Known players -- read from the server's files (usercache.json, playerdata/, ops.json, whitelist.json, banned-players.json)

Because the file-based part does not need RCON, the roster is also shown when the server is stopped (everyone then appears as Offline). The list updates in real time over SSE; the dot next to the online / max counter in the header shows whether the live connection is active.

Each row shows the player's avatar (from mc-heads.net), name, and badges:

Badge Meaning Online / Offline Current connection state OP Player is a server operator Banned Player is on the ban list Whitelisted Player is on the whitelist

Offline players also show Last saved, the time their player data was last written by the server.

docs.title: Player Actions
docs.text:
Click the ⋮ menu on a row to manage the player. Only the actions that apply to the player's current state are shown:

Action Shown when Notes Details Player has a UUID Opens the player detail modal (see below) Kick Player is online Confirmation dialog with optional reason Ban / Unban Not banned / banned Ban asks for a reason (default: Banned by administrator) Make OP / Remove OP Not OP / OP Make OP grants permission level 4 Add to Whitelist / Remove from Whitelist Not whitelisted / whitelisted

Players tab vs. Players page

The Players tab manages the players of a single server from its detail page. The Player Management page, reached from the top navigation bar, offers the whitelist/ops/ban lists with a server selector.

docs.title: Player Detail Modal
docs.text:
Select Details in the action menu to open the player detail modal. The header shows the avatar, name, UUID, and the same badges as the list. The body has three sections:

Statistics -- values as last saved by the server (from stats/<uuid>.json and advancements/<uuid>.json in the world folder):

Stat Description Play Time Total in-game play time (Xh Ym) Deaths Number of deaths Mob Kills / Player Kills Kill counts Distance Traveled Total distance (m / km) Blocks Mined Total blocks mined Items Crafted Total items crafted Advancements Completed advancements

If the player has no stats file yet, "No statistics recorded yet." is shown.

Position & Status -- parsed from the player's playerdata/<uuid>.dat:

  • Coordinates (X / Y / Z) and dimension
  • Health and food (out of 20), XP level, game mode
  • Inventory summary: slots used and up to 10 item stacks

While the player is online and the server is running, the position is read live via RCON and labeled Live position with a Live badge. The modal refreshes every 5 seconds while the player is online. Offline players show Last saved position instead.

Session History -- join/leave history collected from server logs:

  • Visits, Total Playtime, and Last Seen
  • The most recent sessions (up to 20, newest first) with join → leave time and duration; a session that is still open shows Online now

Session history starts when the collector is installed

Session history is not read from the world files. mcctl-api parses each running server's Docker logs (<player> joined/left the game) every 30 seconds and stores the events in data/players.db (SQLite, under the platform root). History therefore only exists from the time mcctl-api v2.27.0+ first runs the collector. On its first pass for a server, the collector backfills at most the last 24 hours of that container's logs; older sessions are not recovered. After that it resumes from a per-server cursor, so a gap (for example, while mcctl-api was stopped) is filled in only if those lines are still in the container's logs — logs of a recreated container are lost. When a server is found stopped, its open sessions are closed at that time.

Until data is collected, the section shows "No sessions recorded yet (history is collected from server logs)."

docs.title: World Tab
docs.text:
The World tab shows the world assigned to the server. If no world is assigned, it shows "No world is assigned to this server." The same panel opens as World Details when you click a world card on the Worlds page. It contains:

  • Header -- The world name with Overworld, Nether, and End chips. A chip is filled when the world contains that dimension
  • Info cards -- Seed, Spawn, Game Mode, Difficulty (with "(Hardcore)" when applicable), Day, Version, Size, Border, Regions, and Weather. Click the Seed or Spawn card to copy its value
  • Map -- The BlueMap web map (see below)
  • Ore & Block Stats -- Block statistics for the whole world (see below)
  • Players -- Each known player with an online / offline chip, name, coordinates (click to copy), and dimension. Online players use live positions; offline players use the last saved position, and a notice says so when nobody is online

docs.title: Map
docs.text: Render map generates a BlueMap web map of the world, and Re-render refreshes it. The render runs in a Docker container limited to 2 GB of memory; the first render also builds the BlueMap image. The map is embedded right below the buttons, with a progress bar while rendering. The map opens on the Overworld by default (Nether and End remain selectable in the viewer). Worlds rendered before v2.29.0 pick this up on Re-render. After a render, Show structures marks structures on the map; you can toggle the structure types in the BlueMap legend.

docs.title: Ore & Block Stats
docs.text:
Analyze scans every chunk of the world (it can take minutes on large worlds; progress is shown) and caches the result, and Re-analyze refreshes it. The panel shows when the world was last analyzed, followed by:

  • KPI cards: total blocks, block types, regions scanned, analysis time, dimensions
  • Ores: a donut chart with a legend (count and share), highlight chips for rare ores (gold, diamond, emerald, ancient debris), and a Merge stone/deepslate variants toggle
  • Top blocks: a stacked bar by category (Stone, Earth, Wood, Fluid, Nether, Other) and a top-5 list that Show all expands

docs.title: Activity Tab
docs.text:
The Activity tab shows the audit history of this server in the same table as the Audit Log page, without the Target column:

  • An Action dropdown (All Actions or a specific server action) and a status toggle (ALL, SUCCESS, FAILURE)
  • Rows per page of 25 or 50
  • A View Full History link that opens the Audit Log page already filtered to this server

docs.title: Mods Tab
docs.text:
The Mods tab provides a complete mod management interface for servers running modded platforms (FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC). This tab allows you to browse, install, and remove mods directly from the Modrinth repository without manual file management.

Modded Servers Only

The Mods tab is most useful for modded server types (FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC). While the tab is visible for all servers, mod installation requires a compatible server platform.

docs.title: Installed Mods
docs.text:
The Installed Mods card lists the mods you added, grouped under their source (e.g., Modrinth). Each entry shows:

  • Mod icon -- The mod's thumbnail image from Modrinth
  • Mod name -- The display name of the mod (e.g., Create)
  • Description -- A brief summary of what the mod does (e.g., "Aesthetic Technology that empowers the Player")
  • Download count -- The total number of downloads on Modrinth (e.g., 12.6M), indicating the mod's popularity
  • Author -- The mod creator's username (e.g., simibubi)
  • View on Modrinth button (external link icon) -- Opens the mod's page on Modrinth in a new tab for detailed information, changelogs, and documentation
  • Remove button (red trash icon) -- Removes the mod from the server's mod list immediately, without a confirmation prompt

When no mods have been added, the card says "No mods installed".

docs.title: Adding New Mods
docs.text:
Click the + Add Mods button in the top-right corner of the Installed Mods card to open the Search Mods dialog:

  1. Type a mod name or keyword in Search Modrinth... -- results appear as you type
  2. Review each result's icon, title, description, download count, and author
  3. Click Add to add the mod. Mods that are already on the server show Installed

docs.title: Installed Jar Files
docs.text:
For servers created from a modpack, the Installed Jar Files (from modpack) card lists every .jar in the mods directory. Use the Included / Excluded switch on a row to exclude a mod from the next install -- handy for client-only mods that crash a dedicated server. Before the modpack is first installed, the card says "No jar files found in the mods directory."

Server Restart Required

After adding or removing mods, or changing the exclude list, you need to restart the server for the changes to take effect. The tab shows a "Restart the server to apply mod changes." notice when a change is made.

docs.title: Files Tab
docs.text: The Files tab provides a full-featured file manager for your server's file system.

docs.title: File Browser
docs.text:
The file browser displays the contents of the server's data directory in a familiar list layout:

  • Breadcrumb navigation at the top shows your current path (e.g., root /) and lets you click to jump to parent directories
  • Search files... box to filter files by name within the current directory
  • Each file entry shows the file name, size, and last modified date
  • Folders are listed first, followed by files

docs.title: File Operations
docs.text:
The toolbar provides several actions:

Action Description Upload Upload files to the current directory via a drag-and-drop dialog New Folder Create a new directory in the current path Refresh Reload the file listing

The ⋮ menu at the end of each row provides:

  • Open -- Open a folder (folders only)
  • Edit -- Open an editable file in the editor (text files only)
  • Download -- Download the file to your local machine (files only)
  • Rename -- Change the file or folder name
  • Delete -- Remove the file or folder after a confirmation dialog. For critical files you must type the file name to confirm

docs.title: Smart File Editors
docs.text:
The file manager includes intelligent editors that adapt to the file type:

  • server.properties -- Opens a specialized editor with a Form view (categorized, searchable fields) and a Raw view (plain text)
  • Player data files (whitelist.json, ops.json, banned-players.json) -- Opens a dedicated player editor with Mojang API integration for username lookup
  • Text files (.txt, .md, .json, .yml, .yaml, .properties, .cfg, .conf, .ini, .toml, .xml, .csv, .log, .sh, .bat) -- Opens a code editor with syntax awareness
  • Other files -- Available for download only

Editing server.properties

The server.properties editor changes the file of the running server directly. Those edits do not survive recreating the server container. For persistent settings, use the Options tab.

docs.title: Config History Tab
docs.text:
The Config History tab keeps a timeline of configuration snapshots for this server. A snapshot captures the server's configuration files (server.properties, config.env, etc.), so you can compare versions and roll back. The same snapshots are also available on the Backups page.

  • Create Snapshot -- Save the current configuration. Add an optional description such as "Before modpack update"
  • Timeline -- Snapshots are listed newest first and grouped by date. Each entry shows its time, a Scheduled chip if a schedule created it, its description (or "No description"), and its file count
  • View diff -- Compares a snapshot with the previous one
  • Restore -- Rolls the configuration back to that snapshot
  • Delete -- Click the trash button, then click Confirm within three seconds
  • Compare -- Appears once there are two or more snapshots. In compare mode, select any two snapshots and click View Diff
  • Load More -- Loads older snapshots when the list is long

The Config Diff dialog shows Snapshot A vs. Snapshot B with a file tree on the left, a Unified / Split view switch, and a summary of modified, added, and deleted files. In this tab it also offers Restore to Snapshot A.

The Restore Configuration dialog lists the changes that will be applied and keeps Create safety snapshot before restoring (recommended) checked by default. If the server is running, it warns that a restart may be required for the changes to take effect.

docs.title: Backups Tab
docs.text:
The Backups tab of a server has two sub-tabs:

  • Config Snapshots (default) -- The snapshot summary card for this server (latest snapshot, file count, total snapshots, schedule status) with View History, Create Snapshot, and View Diff buttons. Manage Schedules opens the schedule panel described under Config Snapshots
  • World Backups -- The platform-wide world backup view: Push Backup, backup status, backup schedules, and backup history, exactly as on the Backups page

docs.title: Access Tab
docs.text:
The Access tab controls which users can work with this server. Each row shows the user's avatar, name, email, and a permission badge:

Permission Meaning (as described in the grant dialog) Viewer Can view server status and logs Operator Can start, stop, and configure the server Owner Full control including managing other users
  • Add User opens the Add User Access dialog. Search by name or email (type at least 2 characters), choose a Permission Level, and click Add User
  • The ⋮ menu on a row offers Change to Owner, Change to Operator, Change to Viewer, and Remove Access. The last Owner of a server cannot be demoted or removed
  • Only platform admins and server Owners can manage access. Platform admins can see every server; other users see only the servers they have been granted

docs.title: Options Tab
docs.text: The Options tab provides a comprehensive configuration editor for your server.

docs.title: Hostnames / Domains
docs.text:
At the top of the Options tab, the Hostnames / Domains card shows all the hostnames configured for routing connections to this server:

  • System Hostnames (read-only) -- Automatically generated hostnames (e.g., botagent.local, botagent.192.168.xx.xx.nip.io)
  • Custom Domains -- User-defined custom domain names, each with a remove button. The server's playit.gg domain, if it has one, is listed here with a playit chip: removing it clears the server's playit.gg domain, and replacing it with exactly one new domain in the same save makes that domain the playit.gg domain
  • + Add Domain button to enter an additional custom hostname. Domains ending in .local or .nip.io are reserved for system hostnames
  • A Save Hostnames button to store the list. Hostname changes only take effect after the server container is recreated: stop the server and start it again (Restart does not apply them), or run docker compose up -d

docs.title: Settings Sections
docs.text:
Below the hostnames, the settings are grouped into cards. Each card shows its essential fields first; a Show Advanced Settings (N) toggle at the bottom of the card reveals its additional fields:

Section Essential fields Gameplay Difficulty (Peaceful, Easy, Normal, Hard), Game Mode (Survival, Creative, Adventure, Spectator), Max Players, Enable PvP World MOTD (Message of the Day), World Name, Level Type (Default, Flat, Large Biomes, Amplified, Buffet), World Seed Security Online Mode (Mojang Auth), Enable Whitelist Performance & JVM Memory, Aikar's Flags, View Distance Auto-pause / Auto-stop Enable Auto-pause, Pause Timeout System Timezone, Resource Pack URL, Enable RCON Remote Access Enable WebSocket Console, Enable SSH Console Configuration Repositories Git repository URLs for server.properties and for the Paper, Pufferfish, and Purpur configs (applied at startup)

Advanced fields include, for example, Hardcore, Allow Flight, and Spawn Protection in Gameplay; Simulation Distance, Initial Heap, Max Heap, and JVM -XX Options in Performance & JVM; Enable Auto-stop in Auto-pause / Auto-stop; and RCON Password, RCON Port, UID, and GID in System.

Game Mode is stored as MODE, the variable the server image reads. Servers created by earlier versions have GAMEMODE, which the image ignores: the field shows that value, and saving the settings moves it to MODE, so the game mode applies from the next start.

docs.title: Save and Restart
docs.text:
When you modify settings:

  1. A sticky action bar appears at the bottom of the page showing "N unsaved changes" (and, if needed, which fields require a restart)
  2. Click Save Changes (N) to apply the changes
  3. If the server is running and any changed setting requires a restart (e.g., memory, online mode, world settings), a Restart Required dialog appears with Save Only, Save & Restart, and Cancel
  4. Click Discard to drop unsaved changes

Restart Required

Some settings (like memory allocation, online mode, and world seed) require a server restart to take effect. The UI clearly indicates which settings need a restart after being changed.

docs.title: Danger Zone
docs.text: At the bottom of the Options tab, the Danger Zone card contains Reset World, which permanently deletes the current world and generates a new one. The button is disabled while the server is running ("Stop the server first"), and the confirmation dialog requires you to type RESET. This action cannot be undone.

docs.title: Player Management
docs.text: The Players page provides comprehensive management of players across all your servers.

docs.title: Server Selector
docs.text: At the top of the page, a Server dropdown lets you select which server to manage. The selected server determines which data is displayed in the Whitelist, Operators, and Ban List tabs below. Two cards above it show the number of available and running servers.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: The Player Management page is organized into four tabs:

docs.title: Online Players
docs.text: Lists the players currently connected, grouped by server, with a Kick action (optional reason). This tab covers all servers and does not depend on the Server dropdown. Use the refresh button to reload the list.

docs.title: Whitelist
docs.text:
Manage which players are allowed to join your server:

  • Whitelist toggle -- Enable or disable the whitelist (shown as an ON/OFF switch)
  • Player input field -- Enter a Minecraft username to add to the whitelist
  • Add button -- Add a single player
  • Bulk button -- Switch to a multi-line input (player1, player2, player3) and add several players at once with Add All
  • Player list -- Shows all whitelisted players with their Minecraft avatar and a remove button. A search box appears once the list has five or more players

Offline Server Data

When a server is offline, the Players page reads data directly from the server's files (whitelist.json, ops.json, banned-players.json). An informational banner indicates: "Server is offline. Showing data from whitelist.json. Changes will apply on next server start."

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Manage players with operator (admin) privileges:

  • Add players as operators with configurable permission levels (1-4)
  • Level 1: Can bypass spawn protection
  • Level 2: Can use /clear, /gamemode, etc.
  • Level 3: Can use /ban, /kick, /op, etc.
  • Level 4: Can use /stop, full access

An information panel on the right explains each OP level in detail.

docs.title: Ban List
docs.text:
Manage banned players:

  • Ban players by username with an optional reason
  • View all currently banned players
  • Pardon (unban) players with a single click
  • An information panel explains how bans work

docs.title: Worlds
docs.text: The Worlds page lets you manage all Minecraft worlds stored in your platform.

docs.title: World List
docs.text:
The page header shows the + Create World button and three cards: Total worlds, Assigned worlds, and Free worlds. Worlds are displayed as cards in a grid layout. Each world card shows:

  • World name (e.g., Wild-Deity, botagent, factory)
  • Status badge -- Available (green) for unassigned worlds, Assigned for worlds currently assigned to a server. A red Assigned to N servers chip appears when an older install has several servers on the same world
  • Size -- Disk space used by the world (e.g., 610.2MB, 20.5MB), plus Overworld / Nether / End chips when the world has more than one dimension
  • Servers -- The servers using the world, or "No servers". An assigned world also shows which server it is assigned to
  • Date -- When the world was last modified
  • Action buttons:
    • Assign (link icon) -- Assign an available world to a server
    • Release (unlink icon) -- Switch the server using the world back to its own default world (the world is kept in worlds/)
    • Delete (red trash can icon) -- Delete the world

Click the body of a card to open World Details, which shows the same panel as the server World tab (info cards, map, ore & block stats, and player locations).

docs.title: Filtering and Search
docs.text:
At the top of the list:

  • ALL -- Show all worlds
  • AVAILABLE -- Show only available (unassigned) worlds
  • ASSIGNED -- Show only worlds currently assigned to a server

A Search worlds... box lets you filter worlds by name.

docs.title: Assignment Warnings
docs.text: If an older install has two servers on the same world, or a server's config.env cannot be read, a warning alert at the top of the page lists each problem. Nothing is fixed automatically: assign another world to all but one of the servers. Until a server's config.env is fixed, assigning, releasing and deleting worlds are refused.

docs.title: Creating a New World
docs.text:
Click + Create World in the page header to open the Create New World dialog:

  1. Enter a World Name (letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores)
  2. Optionally specify a Seed (leave it empty for a random seed)
  3. Click Create

To bring in an existing world instead, drop a .zip file on the Upload world .zip (optional) area (or click it to choose a file). The Seed field disappears and the button changes to Import. The Server type dropdown does not affect the result; it only changes the on-screen guidance for how to zip the world:

  • VANILLA, FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC, QUILT -- Zip the world folder (it must contain level.dat; the Nether and End are inside it). Some modpacks store them as <world-name>_nether and <world-name>_the_end; if so, zip all three folders together
  • PAPER, SPIGOT, BUKKIT -- Zip <world-name>, <world-name>_nether, and <world-name>_the_end together; leaving one out loses that dimension

docs.title: Assigning a World to a Server
docs.text:
Click the Assign (link) icon on an available world card to open the Assign World dialog. Select a server in Select Server; stopped servers are listed under Available Servers. Running servers appear under Running Servers (stop them first) and cannot be selected. Click Assign. The server's LEVEL is set to the world and the card is marked Assigned.

A world can be used by one server only, and the server must be stopped. To switch a server back to its own default world, click the Release icon on the assigned world's card; the server must be stopped for this too.

docs.title: Deleting a World
docs.text:
Click the red trash can icon on a world card. A Delete World dialog appears requiring you to type the exact world name to prevent accidental deletion. This action is irreversible. A world that a server uses cannot be deleted: assign another world to that server first.

Data Loss

Deleting a world permanently removes all world data including terrain, player builds, and entities. Always create a backup before deleting a world.

docs.title: Backups
docs.text:
The Backups page manages world backups, automated backup schedules, and server configuration snapshots. A chip in the header shows whether backups are Configured.

The page has two tabs: World Backups (default) and Config Snapshots. The selected tab is kept in the URL (/backups?tab=config-snapshots).

docs.title: Backup Status
docs.text:
The Backup Status card shows the current backup configuration:

  • Status -- Whether the backup system is Configured (green checkmark) or Not Configured. When it is not configured, the card asks you to set BACKUP_GITHUB_REPO and BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN
  • Repository -- The configured Git repository for backup storage (e.g., smallmiro/minecraft-worlds-backup)
  • Last Backup -- When the last backup ran (e.g., "5 minutes ago"), or "No backups yet"

docs.title: Push Backup
docs.text:
The Push Backup button in the page header triggers an immediate manual backup of all worlds to the configured Git repository. A dialog lets you enter an optional Commit Message (prefilled with Backup <date>), then click Push.

A push stops if a world that was in the last backup no longer exists, so a world deleted by mistake is not dropped from the backup. If you deleted it on purpose, check Remove worlds I deleted on purpose from the backup before clicking Push (the same as mcctl backup push --allow-missing).

docs.title: Backup Schedules
docs.text:
The Backup Schedules card manages automated cron-based backup scheduling:

  • Each schedule shows its name, a human-readable frequency (e.g., "Every hour"), and the cron expression
  • A last-run chip (OK or Failed) -- hover for the time and message
  • Retention badge -- indicates whether backup retention policies (maximum count or age) are configured
  • Toggle switch -- Enable or disable individual schedules
  • Edit button (pencil icon) -- Modify the schedule
  • Delete button (trash icon) -- Remove the schedule
  • + Add Schedule button to create new automated backup schedules (name, frequency preset or custom cron expression, maximum backup count, and maximum age in days)

docs.title: Backup History
docs.text: The Backup History card (visible when the backup system is configured) lists past backups with the commit hash, date, message, and author. The restore button on a row opens Restore Backup, which warns that all worlds will be restored from the selected backup and that current world data will be overwritten. Stop all servers first: a restore is refused while any server is running ("Stop all servers before restoring").

docs.title: Config Snapshots
docs.text:
The Config Snapshots tab manages configuration snapshots for every server at once. It lists one card per server with:

  • The latest snapshot ("Latest: 2h ago"), its file count, and the total number of snapshots (or "No snapshots yet")
  • A schedule chip: Schedule: Active, Schedule: Paused, or No schedule
  • View History (needs at least two snapshots), Create Snapshot, and View Diff (shown when the server has two or more snapshots; compares the latest two)

The header has two buttons:

  • Create Snapshot -- Opens Create Config Snapshot. Choose the Server, optionally add a description (e.g., "Before modpack update"), and click Create Snapshot
  • Manage Schedules -- Opens the Config Snapshot Schedules panel. Click Add Schedule and fill in Server, Schedule Name, Cron Preset (Every hour, Every 6 hours, Daily at midnight, Daily at 3 AM, Weekly, or Custom) or a Cron Expression, and Retention Count (the maximum number of scheduled snapshots kept per server). Existing schedules can be enabled or disabled with a switch, edited, or deleted

To work with a single server's snapshot timeline -- compare, restore, delete -- use the server's Config History tab.

docs.title: Audit Log
docs.text:
The Audit page (/audit-logs) lists the management actions recorded by mcctl-api and the CLI. It has a Live / Disconnected indicator with a "new logs available" banner, four summary cards, filters, a table with expandable rows and a detail drawer, and CSV / JSON export (up to 5,000 rows).

In the Actor column, actions done in the web console show console (recorded as api:console); only Platform Settings changes and file operations record the signed-in user's name. CLI commands show local.

See the Audit Log Web Console Guide for the filters, the table, the detail drawer, and export.

docs.title: Routing
docs.text: The Routing page shows how players reach your servers through mc-router. The header shows the router's container status and how many servers and hostnames are routed (for example "3 servers · 8 hostnames"). Administrators also see a Restart mc-router button there (see Restarting mc-router).

docs.title: Routing Table
docs.text:
The Routing Table panel has one row per server. A collapsed row shows:

  • The server name with its type and Minecraft version
  • The primary address with its type badge and a copy button, and +N for the server's other hostnames. The primary address is the first routed hostname in the order nip.io, mDNS, WAN, Custom
  • The status (e.g. Running, Sleeping · wakes on connect) and an N not routed warning when mc-router does not know some of the server's hostnames
  • Wake (or Start) for a stopped server, Edit hostnames (opens the server's Options tab), and Open server

Click a row (or its arrow) to list all of that server's hostnames, each with a copy button, its type, and a Not routed warning if needed. Several servers can be open at once; Expand all / Collapse all opens or closes every server. The search box matches server names and hostnames. When a hostname matches, its server opens and the matching hostname is highlighted.

docs.title: Routing Flow
docs.text: The Routing Flow diagram draws the current routes: the hostname types with their counts (mDNS, nip.io, WAN, Custom), then mc-router with its status and port, then up to eight servers with their status (+N more stands for the rest).

docs.title: Live Router Log
docs.text: The Live Router Log panel follows the mc-router log. Each line shows the time, a kind (CONNECT, WAKE, ERROR, or INFO), the hostname and target server for connections and wake-ups (the log text for other lines), and the player name when the log line has one. The panel keeps the last 500 lines, has an Auto-scroll switch and a Clear button, and shows the stream state (Connecting, Live, Disconnected, or Ended).

docs.title: mc-router Gateway
docs.text: The mc-router Gateway card shows the router container's status and health, the listening Port, Active routes (routes whose server is running, as x / y), and the Container name, Mode (e.g., Auto Discovery), Uptime, and Image. When the router's auto-scale settings can be read, it also shows Auto-scale up, Auto-scale down, Idle time, and a preview of the Asleep MOTD that a sleeping server shows in the server list.

docs.title: Hostname Resolver
docs.text: The Hostname Resolver card lists the host IPs used for nip.io hostnames (marking the primary one Primary), an example nip.io address with a copy button, and the mDNS (Avahi) status. Avahi must be running for .local hostnames to resolve on the local network.

docs.title: Restarting mc-router
docs.text: Restart mc-router in the page header is shown to administrators only. It asks for confirmation first: players connected through mc-router are disconnected and new connections fail until the router is back up; running servers are not stopped. The button is disabled when the router container does not exist.

docs.title: External Access (playit.gg)
docs.text:
The External Access (playit.gg) card manages playit.gg tunnel configuration for making your servers accessible from the internet without port forwarding:

  • Start Agent / Stop Agent buttons for managing the playit agent, and a View Dashboard link to the playit.gg tunnels page
  • Agent Status -- Running or Stopped, with the agent uptime
  • Server Domains table showing which servers have external domains configured (e.g., possible-tracks.gl.joinmc.link), each with a copy button
  • A list of servers without external domains

If playit.gg is not set up, the card shows "Not configured". Set PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY (for example with mcctl playit setup) to enable it.

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
The top navigation bar is consistent across all pages and includes:

Item Description Minecraft Console logo Click to return to the Dashboard Dashboard Infrastructure overview Servers Server management Worlds World management Players Player management Audit Activity audit logs Backups Backup management Routing Network routing configuration User avatar (top-right) Opens the user menu

The currently active page is highlighted in the navigation bar.

The user menu shows your name and email (with an Admin chip for administrators) and offers:

Menu item Description Users User Management -- administrators only Settings Account Settings Logout End the session and return to the sign-in page

The console always uses its dark theme; there is no theme toggle.

docs.title: Account Settings
docs.text:
Open Settings from the user menu to manage your own account. The page has three cards:

  • Profile -- Edit your Name and click Save Changes. The Email is read-only ("Email cannot be changed"), and the Role (Admin or User) is shown for reference
  • Account Information -- Your Account ID, Created time, and Last Updated time
  • Change Password -- Enter your Current Password, a New Password (at least 8 characters, different from the current one), and Confirm New Password, then click Change Password. Other signed-in sessions are not signed out

docs.title: Platform Settings (Admin)
docs.text:
Administrators see an additional Platform Settings section on the Settings page, above the account cards. It edits the platform .env file. Non-admin users only see their own account cards and cannot read or change platform configuration; the API enforces this independently of the UI.

  • Bento cards -- Settings are grouped into cards: Network & Routing, Server Runtime, RCON, Backup, External Access and Console & Logging. Each field uses a typed control (text, switch, select, number, IP list) with field-level validation
  • Secrets are write-only -- Secret fields (RCON_PASSWORD, BACKUP_GITHUB_TOKEN, PLAYIT_SECRET_KEY, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) show Configured or Not configured. The input is never pre-filled; typing a value marks the field changed
  • Console sign-in settings -- Console & Logging holds BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (the console session secret; changing it signs everyone out) and BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL (the console's public URL; see Login Fails)
  • Runtime (PM2) -- A read-only card shows AUTH_MODE from ecosystem.config.cjs, plus BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL / BETTER_AUTH_SECRET (configured only) while an older ecosystem file still injects them. While the ecosystem defines them they win over .env and cannot be changed here; run mcctl upgrade to move them to .env
  • Advanced Environment -- Unknown keys as key/value rows (add, edit, remove). Servers receive one only if its name is listed in servers/global.env
  • Legacy / Unused -- Legacy keys with warning styling ("Not read by any current code."). Nothing is removed unless you remove it explicitly
  • Read-only network identity -- MINECRAFT_NETWORK, MINECRAFT_SUBNET and COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME are displayed with CLI guidance only

Server-specific values stay in each server's Options tab. A server's config.env overrides the platform value for that server, and the UI notes this on server-runtime keys. See Environment Variables for the full classification.

docs.title: Saving and Applying Changes
docs.text:
A sticky bar with Discard and Save Changes appears when any field is changed, and a chip above the cards counts the unsaved fields. Saving only writes .env; it never restarts anything. After saving, a Restart required dialog lists what needs to be restarted, per scope:

Scope What to do Servers Stop, then start each server (Servers page, or mcctl stop <name> && mcctl start <name>).
