Restart does not reload .env. mc-router auto-scale wakes an existing container with its old environment, so a recreate through start is required Router mcctl router start (not restart) playit Stop, then start the playit agent on the Routing page, or mcctl playit stop && mcctl playit start API mcctl console service restart --api. Settings backed by mcctl-api show a "restart pending" chip until it restarts Console mcctl console service restart --console (this also restarts mcctl-api). Nobody is signed out unless the session secret changed Next create Applies to servers created after this change. Existing server hostnames are unchanged

If the file changed since you loaded the page (for example via the CLI), saving returns a 409 conflict and a dialog asks you to reload. Your edits are never overwritten automatically.

docs.title: CLI Equivalents
docs.text: Card CLI Network & Routing mcctl init --reconfigure Backup mcctl backup init External Access mcctl playit setup Runtime (PM2) mcctl console init

docs.title: User Management (Admin)
docs.text:
Administrators see a Users item in the user menu that opens the User Management page (/admin/users). Other users who open this page are redirected to the Dashboard.

  • Three cards summarize Total users, Administrators, and Banned users
  • The user directory lists each account's Email, Name, Role (Admin or User), Status (Active or Banned), and Created At
  • Click a row to open User Details with the same fields plus the User ID

The page is read-only. To add users, change roles, or reset passwords, use the CLI (see CLI Commands):

mcctl console user add user@example.com --role user --password "SecurePass123"
mcctl console user update user@example.com --role admin
mcctl console user reset-password user@example.com

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
1. Use Strong Passwords -- Follow the password requirements during mcctl console init
  2. Limit Access -- Use the Access tab to grant minimal permissions to each user
  3. Use HTTPS -- Configure a reverse proxy with SSL for production deployments, and set BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL to the proxy's URL (see Login Fails)
  4. Review Audit Logs -- Regularly check the Audit Log for unexpected activity

docs.title: Server Management
docs.text:
1. Monitor the Dashboard -- Check server health, player counts, and recent activity regularly
  2. Graceful Shutdowns -- Always use the Stop button instead of force-killing containers
  3. Backup Before Changes -- Push a backup before modifying world data, and create a config snapshot before changing server configuration
  4. Use Scheduled Backups -- Configure automated backup schedules for peace of mind

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
1. Avoid Simultaneous Operations -- Don't start/stop multiple servers at once
  2. Monitor Resource Usage -- Use the resource stat cards on the server detail page to track CPU and memory
  3. Clean Up Unused Worlds -- Delete worlds that are no longer needed to free disk space

docs.title: Usage Analytics
docs.text:
In production mode, the web console sends anonymous usage data to Google Analytics 4 (GA4) so we can see which screens are used. Development mode (pnpm dev) never sends anything.

What is sent:

  • An anonymous installId (random UUID), one per installation, sent as the GA user_id. It is unrelated to your accounts or hostnames.
  • The normalized page path, such as /dashboard, /servers/:name, or /servers/:name/console
  • The mcctl console version (mcctl_version)

What is not sent:

  • The console's hostname or IP address (the page URL is rewritten to http://mcctl-console.invalid/... before sending)
  • Server names, world names, or query strings
  • Accounts or email addresses

Note

Your browser sends the request to Google, so Google receives the connecting IP address. According to Google's documentation, GA4 does not log or store IP addresses.

docs.title: The installId
docs.text:
The installId is stored as installId in <root>/.mcctl.json. It is created once and never changes:

  • New installation: created by mcctl init
  • Upgrade: mcctl upgrade adds it only if it is missing (an existing value is kept)
  • Package-only update with mcctl update: created and saved on the console's first request

mcctl console init and mcctl update print this notice when analytics is on:

Console usage analytics is on (anonymous install ID and page paths, sent to Google Analytics). To turn it off, set "telemetry": false in <root>/.mcctl.json.

docs.title: Turning It Off
Can't Access the Console
docs.text:
1. Check Service Status: 

    mcctl console service status

  2. Verify Port: 

    netstat -tlnp | grep 5000

  3. Check Logs: 

    pm2 logs mcctl-console --lines 100

docs.title: Login Fails
docs.text:
1. Verify Credentials: Sign in with the email shown in the Email column: 

    mcctl console user list

  2. Reset Password: The sign-in page has no self-service reset, so use the CLI with the account's email: 

    mcctl console user reset-password <email>

  3. Check the Address You Sign In From: The console accepts sign-ins from localhost, private LAN addresses (10.x, 172.16.x-172.31.x, 192.168.x), .local names, and the URL in BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL (default http://localhost:<console port>). From any other address, such as a Tailscale 100.x address, a domain name, or an HTTPS reverse proxy, sign-in fails until BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL is set to that URL in the platform .env (or in Platform Settings). Then restart the console: 

    mcctl console service restart --console
    On installs whose ecosystem.config.cjs still defines BETTER_AUTH_BASE_URL, run mcctl upgrade first; until then the ecosystem value is used. The console sets secure cookies only when this URL starts with https://.

docs.title: Server Status Not Updating
docs.text:
1. Check API Health: 

    curl http://localhost:5001/health

  2. Verify Docker Socket: Ensure Docker is running and the mcctl-api process has access to the Docker socket.

  3. Check Network: Ensure mcctl-console can reach mcctl-api on port 5001.

docs.title: Commands Not Working
docs.text:
1. Server Must Be Running -- RCON commands only work when the server is in a running state
  2. RCON Must Be Enabled -- Ensure RCON is enabled in the server configuration
  3. Check API Logs: 
    pm2 logs mcctl-api --lines 100

docs.title: Mobile Access
docs.text:
The web console uses a responsive Material UI layout that adapts to different screen sizes:

  • Phone -- Simplified card layout with collapsible navigation
  • Tablet -- Full dashboard with optimized touch controls
  • Desktop -- Full feature set with side-by-side panels

Mobile Tips

  • Use landscape mode for better command input in the console
  • The navigation collapses into a hamburger menu on small screens
  • Most dialogs are full-screen on mobile for easier interaction

docs.title: Development Guide
docs.text:
This guide covers the development environment, repository layout, and contribution workflow for minecraft-server-manager.

Contributor guide

The canonical contributor guide is DEVELOPMENT.md in the repository root. This page summarizes it for the documentation site.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
Create issue in the original repo → Fork → Create branch → Tests first (TDD) → Implement → Open PR to the original repo → Address review → Merge
Rule Details Unit of work One issue = one branch = one PR Where things live Issues live in the original repository. Work happens in your fork. The PR goes from your fork back to the original repository. Base branch develop (branch from develop, and open the PR against develop) Method TDD (Red → Green → Refactor), Tidy First Architecture Hexagonal / Clean Architecture Documentation Keep English (.md) and Korean (.ko.md) versions together

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Tool Version Purpose Node.js 18 or later (CI uses 20) All packages pnpm 9 (pinned in packageManager) Monorepo management Docker / Docker Compose Engine 24+, Compose 2.20+ Server containers, E2E Git, GitHub CLI (gh) Latest Fork, issues, PRs

Supported operating systems are Linux and macOS. better-sqlite3 (a dependency of mcctl-console) is a native module, so some environments need a build toolchain (gcc, make, python).

docs.title: Fork and Set Up
docs.text:
# 1) Fork smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager on GitHub, then:
git clone https://github.com/<your-account>/minecraft-server-manager.git
cd minecraft-server-manager

# 2) Register the original repository as "upstream"
git remote add upstream https://github.com/smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager.git

# 3) Make gh target the original repository for issues and PRs
gh repo set-default smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager

# 4) Install dependencies and build
pnpm install
pnpm build

Before starting any work, bring develop up to date:

git checkout develop
git fetch upstream
git merge --ff-only upstream/develop
git push origin develop

docs.title: Running the CLI from Source
docs.text:
# Link the local build as the global mcctl command
cd platform/services/cli
pnpm link --global
mcctl --version

# Or run the build output directly
node platform/services/cli/dist/index.js --version

docs.title: Repository Layout
docs.text: Path Description platform/services/shared/ @minecraft-docker/shared: domain entities, value objects, use cases, ports/adapters platform/services/cli/ @minecraft-docker/mcctl: the CLI (Hexagonal Architecture) platform/services/mcctl-api/ @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api: Fastify REST API (port 5001) platform/services/mcctl-console/ @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console: Next.js web UI (port 5000) platform/services/mod-source-modrinth/ @minecraft-docker/mod-source-modrinth: Modrinth adapter platform/services/cli/templates/ Single source of the platform templates copied by mcctl init (platform/docker-compose.yml and platform/servers/_template link to it) e2e/ Playwright E2E tests for the Management Console docs/ MkDocs documentation (English/Korean) website/ Project landing page .github/workflows/ CI, release, and website deployment workflows .claude/ Claude Code subagents, commands, and hooks

docs.title: Packages and Build Order
docs.text:
pnpm build runs pnpm -r build, which builds the workspace packages in dependency order:

1. @minecraft-docker/shared                (no workspace dependencies)
2. @minecraft-docker/mod-source-modrinth   (shared)
3. @minecraft-docker/mcctl                 (shared, mod-source-modrinth)
   @minecraft-docker/mcctl-api             (shared, mod-source-modrinth)
   @minecraft-docker/mcctl-console         (shared)

All five packages are published to npm with the same version when a release tag is pushed. See Git Workflow.

docs.title: Root Level
docs.text: Command Description pnpm install Install all dependencies pnpm build Build all packages in dependency order pnpm dev Run every package's dev script in parallel (tsc --watch for shared/cli, tsx watch for mcctl-api, next dev -p 5000 for mcctl-console) pnpm lint Lint all packages pnpm test Run all unit tests (excludes e2e, same as CI) pnpm clean Remove build outputs pnpm test:e2e Run the Management Console E2E suite (Playwright, mcctl-api + mcctl-console) pnpm test:e2e:ui Run the same suite in Playwright UI mode

docs.title: Build and Test
docs.text:
pnpm build                                   # build everything
pnpm test                                    # all unit tests (excludes e2e)
pnpm lint                                    # lint everything

pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/shared test  # a single package
pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/mcctl test

E2E_BASE_URL=<console> E2E_API_URL=<api> pnpm test:e2e   # Management Console E2E (Playwright); both URLs required, use a disposable instance, never a live host
cd platform/services/cli && pnpm test:e2e    # CLI E2E (Vitest)

Add E2E tests for new REST endpoints in e2e/tests/api-*.spec.ts, for console UI flows in e2e/tests/*.spec.ts, and for new CLI commands or options in platform/services/cli/tests/e2e/cli-*.test.ts.

docs.title: Contribution Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create the issue first, in the original repository. Include Summary, Root Cause (bugs) or Requirements (features), Solution / Implementation Plan, Files to Modify, and Acceptance Criteria as a checkbox list. Trivial one-line changes such as typo fixes may skip the issue.
  2. Branch from develop in your fork: feature/<issue>-<description> or bugfix/<issue>-<description>. Never work directly on develop or main.
  3. TDD: write a failing test, make it pass with minimal code, then refactor. PRs without tests are not accepted, except for documentation-only changes and configuration changes with no logic.
  4. Tidy First: never mix structural changes (refactoring) and behavioral changes (features, fixes) in one commit.
  5. Commit as <type>: <description> (#<issue-number>), where type is feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, or chore.
  6. Open one PR per issue from your fork to develop of the original repository, with Closes #<issue> in the body.
git push -u origin feature/12-add-backup
gh pr create --repo smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager --base develop \
  --head <your-account>:feature/12-add-backup \
  --title "feat: add backup script (#12)" --body "Closes #12 ..."

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
PR checks against develop must pass before merge. ci.yml runs on every PR, with no path filter:

Job What it does lint, typecheck, test Builds every package, then runs pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, the tests of every package except e2e, and the cli verify:package check (the tarball has docker/bluemap/Dockerfile and no scripts/) docker compose config (platform, templates) Validates both compose files

e2e.yml runs daily at 03:00 KST and on manual dispatch, not on PRs: it starts mcctl-api and mcctl-console and runs the Playwright suite. Run pnpm test:e2e locally when you change API or console behavior.

Branch naming, commit rules, versioning, and the release process are described in Git Workflow.

docs.title: Developing with Claude Code
docs.text:
The repository ships Claude Code configuration. Run claude from the repository root and CLAUDE.md plus the subagents, commands, and hooks in .claude/ are loaded automatically.

Command Purpose /plan-work Plan the work before starting (--issue <N>, --milestone <N>, --issues <N1,N2>). Plans only; does not execute. /work Run an issue or milestone through to completion: branch, TDD implementation, PR, and code review. /write-docs Write bilingual (English/Korean) technical documentation. /sync-docs Sync CLAUDE.md, README.md, and other docs with the code. /update-docs Refresh docs/itzg-reference/ from the official documentation. /build-kb Analyze the source in depth and build an LLM knowledge base.

A typical flow: describe the change, create an issue from the analysis, plan larger work with /plan-work --issue <N>, then run /work --issue <N>. See Agent Collaboration for the subagents, the /work routing, and how completion is enforced.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
TypeScript code follows Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) with Clean Architecture layering:

+---------------------+
| Presentation Layer  |  CLI commands, API routes
+----------+----------+
           |
+----------v----------+
| Application Layer   |  Use cases, application services
+----------+----------+
           |
+----------v----------+
|    Domain Layer     |  Entities, value objects, ports
+----------+----------+
           |
+----------v----------+
| Infrastructure      |  Adapters: file system, Docker, external APIs
+---------------------+
  • The domain layer has no external dependencies.
  • All I/O goes through adapters, and dependencies are injected.

See CLI Architecture for details.

docs.title: Agent Collaboration
docs.text:
This page describes how the Claude Code subagents and slash commands in .claude/ work together on this repository: who owns what, how work is planned, how /work routes it, and how completion is enforced.

Source of truth

The behavior described here is defined by the files in .claude/agents/, .claude/commands/, and .claude/hooks/, plus CLAUDE.md and DEVELOPMENT.md in the repository root. If this page and those files disagree, the files win.

docs.title: Overview and Principles
docs.text:
• Issue-driven. Every change starts from a GitHub Issue. One issue = one branch = one PR. See Git Workflow.
  • Plan first, then execute. /plan-work produces a plan and does not change code. /work executes.
  • Specialists own modules. Each agent owns a set of paths. The main session routes work to the owner.
  • No message bus. Agents do not exchange messages through a runtime protocol. Work is handed over through the Agent tool call (the prompt in, the agent's final report out) or, in a team, through SendMessage.
  • Progress lives in Git and GitHub. Local progress is written to task.md (gitignored). Issue checkboxes track completed items.

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
All agent definitions are in .claude/agents/. Agents have no tools: restriction; they inherit all tools. Model names are aliases (opus, sonnet) so files do not need editing when a new model ships.

Agent Owns Model Label orchestrator-agent Entry point for requests. Analyzes, plans, delegates, coordinates. Does not write code. opus agent:orchestrator core-agent platform/services/shared/, platform/services/mod-source-*/ (domain entities, value objects, use cases, ports/adapters) opus agent:core cli-agent platform/services/cli/ sonnet agent:cli backend-agent platform/services/mcctl-api/ (Fastify, OpenAPI) sonnet agent:backend frontend-agent platform/services/mcctl-console/ (Next.js, React, MUI 5.x, Better Auth) sonnet agent:frontend devops-agent Docker files and the rest of platform/, e2e/, .github/workflows/, .claude/hooks/ sonnet agent:devops technical-writer docs/, README*, CHANGELOG.md (English and Korean) sonnet agent:docs release-manager Version bumps, v* tags, GitHub releases, post-release verification sonnet agent:release

The commands /plan-work and /build-kb also run on opus; /work, /write-docs, /sync-docs, and /update-docs run on sonnet.

Notes on specific agents:

  • mcctl-console runs natively under PM2, not in Docker.
  • release-manager handles npm packages, not Docker images. Pushing a v* tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which publishes five packages (shared, mod-source-modrinth, mcctl-api, mcctl-console, mcctl) and creates the GitHub Release.
  • The agent:* values in the Label column are the label each agent definition declares in its Identity table.

Architect agents are not part of this repository

orchestrator-agent.md and /plan-work mention system-architect, backend-architect, frontend-architect, devops-architect, and quality-engineer. These are optional user-level agents and are not shipped in .claude/agents/. The workflow does not depend on them: without them, the main session or the owner agent does the design step.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Request] --> B[orchestrator-agent<br/>intake and analysis]
    B --> C[GitHub Issue]
    C --> D["/plan-work<br/>plan only"]
    D --> E{Plan approved?}
    E -- no --> D
    E -- yes --> F["/work<br/>branch, TDD, PR, review, merge"]
    F --> G[Done: Stop hook verifies]
  1. Intake. By the repository rules in CLAUDE.md, a request is received by orchestrator-agent, which analyzes it and delegates analysis to specialists. No code is modified in this phase.
  2. Issue. The analysis becomes a GitHub Issue (summary, root cause or requirements, plan, files to modify, branch strategy, acceptance criteria).
  3. Plan. /plan-work produces a plan: work breakdown, dependencies, parallel groups, agent assignment, and an execution proposal (Teams or sequential sub-agents). It never edits code or creates branches.
  4. Approval. You review the plan.
  5. Execute. /work carries the work through to completion. Invoking /work is the approval to branch, commit, open the PR, run the review, and merge.

docs.title: /plan-work
docs.text:
/plan-work                           # Plan from the conversation
/plan-work --issue <N>               # One issue
/plan-work --milestone <N>           # Every open issue in a milestone
/plan-work --issues <N1,N2,...>      # Several issues

docs.title: How "plan first" applies
docs.text:
• When a request comes in through orchestrator-agent, planning with /plan-work comes first, then /work.
  • Inside /work, the main session routes by tier (below). It runs /plan-work itself only at tier T4. Smaller tiers use the issue's Files to Modify and go straight to implementation.

docs.title: /work Modes and Routing
docs.text:
/work                         # Context mode: create an issue from the conversation, then execute
/work --issue <N>             # Single issue
/work --milestone <N>         # All issues in a milestone, in dependency order
Option Description --dry-run Print the plan (issues, order, branches) and stop. No state file, no changes. --contributor Fork mode: no merge. See the Contributor Mode section below. --skip-review Skip the code review (emergency fixes only). Records REVIEW=skipped. --parallel Milestone mode only. Run independent issues concurrently, each Agent with isolation: "worktree". Branches are merged one at a time, with tests re-run after each.

For a single issue, /work:

  1. Loads the issue and writes the state file.
  2. Creates feature/<N>-<description> (or bugfix/...) from an updated develop.
  3. Routes the work (below) and implements it with TDD, committing as <type>: <description> (#<N>) at each checkpoint.
  4. Ticks the issue checkboxes as items complete.
  5. Adds E2E tests for new or changed external behavior (REST API: Playwright in e2e/; CLI: Vitest in platform/services/cli/tests/e2e/).
  6. Opens the PR, runs /code-review:code-review, fixes every finding, and sets REVIEW=done.
  7. Merges with a merge commit and returns to develop.

In milestone mode, each issue goes through the same steps. A blocked issue is noted in task.md and revisited after its dependency is merged.

docs.title: Module routing
docs.text:
The main session acts as the orchestrator. The most specific path wins.

Paths in Files to Modify Owner platform/services/shared/**, platform/services/mod-source-*/** core-agent platform/services/cli/** cli-agent platform/services/mcctl-api/** backend-agent platform/services/mcctl-console/** frontend-agent rest of platform/**, e2e/**, .github/workflows/**, .claude/hooks/** devops-agent docs/**, README*, CHANGELOG.md technical-writer .claude/commands/**, .claude/agents/**, CLAUDE.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, prose only handled directly by the main session

If prose files change together with logic files, the logic owner handles both.

docs.title: Routing tiers
docs.text:
Tier Condition Handling T0 direct One module, 2 files or fewer, no new public interface, confirmed root cause; or typo/comment/instruction prose only Main session. The PR body gets one line noting the direct handling. T1 single One module, 3-8 files, confirmed root cause One owner agent, default model T2 hardened Shared domain change, unconfirmed root cause, security label, data-loss risk, or 9+ files Owner agent (analysis first if the cause is unconfirmed), model: opus, effort: high T3 multi-module Two modules Delegate per module, core first, independent parts in parallel (worktrees) T4 design Three or more modules, or architecture change /plan-work plus an architect if available, then T3

model and effort are set on the delegation only when the tier gives a value that differs from the agent's default.

Not every task goes to an agent

Tier T0 work and prose-only files are handled by the main session. Small code-review findings are also fixed directly; large ones go back to the same agent. The rule is not "never touch another agent's files" but "route by the table, and do not edit files a running agent owns".

docs.title: Delegation Contract
docs.text:
A delegation prompt must contain:

  • the issue number and body
  • the branch that is already checked out
  • the files the agent owns
  • TDD, the commit format, and Tidy First (structural and behavioral changes in separate commits)
  • "commit at every checkpoint"

The agent must not: switch branches, create PRs or merge, edit the issue body, touch the work-state file, or invoke /work.

The agent returns: commit SHAs, test results, and the list of completed items.

Delegated agents run in the background. If the Stop hook blocks the main session while one is running, wait for its completion notification and do not edit its files.

docs.title: Parallel Work
docs.text:
Mechanism When Notes Single agent One owner for the issue Works directly on the feature branch. No worktree. Agent tool + isolation: "worktree" Parallel delegation (T3, or --parallel in milestone mode) Each agent gets its own worktree. Merge the branches into the feature branch before the PR. Claude Code Teams Larger parallel plans Needs CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1. Provides TeamCreate, TaskCreate/TaskUpdate (dependencies), and SendMessage.

If the Teams tools are not available, parallelize with the Agent tool and worktrees only.

Worktrees are for parallel delegation, not for every agent. Separately, concurrent /work sessions share one checkout's branch and working tree, so run them in separate git worktree folders.

docs.title: Completion Enforcement
docs.text:
/work declares a Stop hook in its frontmatter: .claude/hooks/work-done-check.sh. When /work starts (not for --dry-run), it writes .claude/work-state.<session_id> (gitignored; one file per session so concurrent sessions do not block each other):

# Issue mode
printf 'MODE=issue
ISSUE=%s
REVIEW=pending
' <N> > .claude/work-state.${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}
# Milestone mode
printf 'MODE=milestone
MILESTONE=%s
' <N> > .claude/work-state.${CLAUDE_SESSION_ID}

Each time Claude tries to stop, the hook checks the real GitHub and git state and, if conditions are unmet, blocks the stop and lists what remains.

Mode Work is complete when Issue No unchecked - [ ] in the issue body, a PR for the issue is merged, REVIEW is done or skipped, no uncommitted changes Issue, ROLE=contributor A non-closed PR for the issue exists, REVIEW is done or skipped, no uncommitted changes Milestone The milestone has no open issues, no uncommitted changes

Safety valves:

  • The hook gives up after 30 blocked stops (WORK_MAX_LOOPS overrides the limit).
  • If gh fails, verification is skipped.
  • On an unresolvable blocker, the session reports it, deletes its state file, and stops.
  • No state file means the hook does nothing.

docs.title: Contributor Mode
docs.text:
For people without write access to the original repository. It turns on with --contributor, or automatically when gh repo view --json viewerPermission reports something other than WRITE, MAINTAIN, or ADMIN. The state file gets ROLE=contributor, and the flow changes as follows:

  • Sync the fork's develop first, then branch.
  • Tick issue checkboxes only if you can edit the issue; otherwise list completed items in the PR body.
  • Push to the fork and open the PR against the original repository's develop.
  • Do not merge. The job is done when the PR is open and the review is done.

See DEVELOPMENT.md (section 7.6) in the repository root for the contributor-facing steps.

docs.title: Handoff Conventions
docs.text:
Some agent prompts use markdown headings as handoff conventions. They are prompt conventions, not a protocol: nothing parses them.

Convention Used by Meaning DEPENDENCY_NEEDED core, cli The agent is blocked on another agent's output DEPENDENCY_READY backend, orchestrator A shared artifact (type, API spec) is available WORK_COMPLETE core, cli, frontend The agent's task is finished BLOCKER_DETECTED orchestrator A blocker and the chosen resolution PROGRESS_REPORT orchestrator Overall and per-agent status STATUS_REQUEST orchestrator Ask an unresponsive agent for status

Example of a completion report:

## WORK_COMPLETE
Task: Mod domain entities (#42)
Commits: a1b2c3d, e4f5a6b
Tests: shared package, all passing
Ready for: cli-agent, backend-agent

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose /plan-work Plan before starting (--issue, --milestone, --issues). Plans only. /work Run an issue or milestone through to completion: branch, TDD, PR, code review, merge. /write-docs Write bilingual (English/Korean) technical documentation. /sync-docs Sync CLAUDE.md, README.md, and other docs with the code. /update-docs Refresh docs/itzg-reference/ from the official documentation. /build-kb Analyze the source in depth and build an LLM knowledge base.

Command definitions are in .claude/commands/. The contributor-facing description is in DEVELOPMENT.md (section 7). For the surrounding development rules, see the Development Guide.

docs.title: Agent Prompt Files
docs.text:
File Agent .claude/agents/orchestrator-agent.md Orchestrator .claude/agents/core-agent.md Core .claude/agents/cli-agent.md CLI .claude/agents/backend-agent.md Backend .claude/agents/frontend-agent.md Frontend .claude/agents/devops-agent.md DevOps .claude/agents/technical-writer.md Technical Writer .claude/agents/release-manager.md Release Manager

To hand a specific area to one agent directly, name it in the conversation, for example: "Use cli-agent to add a --dry-run option to mcctl backup (issue #42)".

docs.title: CLI Architecture
docs.text: This document describes how the @minecraft-docker/mcctl CLI is organized and how to extend it. The CLI follows Hexagonal Architecture (Ports & Adapters) with Clean Architecture layering, but the domain model, ports, use cases and most adapters live in the shared package, not in the CLI package.

docs.title: Package Layout
docs.text:
Three packages matter here:

Package Path Contents @minecraft-docker/mcctl platform/services/cli/ Entry point, command handlers, DI container, CLI-only adapters @minecraft-docker/shared platform/services/shared/ Domain, ports, use cases, most adapters. Used by the CLI and mcctl-api @minecraft-docker/mod-source-modrinth platform/services/mod-source-modrinth/ Modrinth implementation of IModSourcePort

docs.title: CLI (platform/services/cli/src/)
docs.text: Path Role index.ts Entry point. Own parseArgs() and one large switch (command) commands/ Command handlers (create.ts, world.ts, mod.ts, ...). Subdirectories config-snapshot/ and console/ hold grouped commands lib/ Helpers: shell.ts (re-exports ShellExecutor), rcon.ts, console-db.ts, pm2-utils.ts, prompts/ infrastructure/adapters/ CLI-only adapters: ClackPromptAdapter, OpsJsonAdapter, Pm2ServiceManagerAdapter infrastructure/ShellExecutor.ts Compose-project operations only (pull, up/down, start/stop all, router) and config.env access. Not a runtime port (ADR-0001, row 15) infrastructure/di/container.ts Dependency injection container domain/index.ts, application/index.ts Only re-export @minecraft-docker/shared

docs.title: Shared (platform/services/shared/src/)
docs.text: Path Role domain/value-objects/, domain/entities/, domain/mod/ Domain model application/ports/inbound/ Use case interfaces (ICreateServerUseCase, IConfigSnapshotUseCase, ...) application/ports/outbound/ Infrastructure interfaces (IContainerRuntimePort, IServerConsolePort, IWorldBackupPort, IWorldAssignmentPort, IServerSpecRepository, IServerRepository, IPromptPort, IDocProvider, IModSourcePort, ...) application/use-cases/ Use case implementations infrastructure/adapters/ DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter, GitWorldBackupAdapter, ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter, AvahiHostnameRegistrarAdapter, ServerRepository, WorldRepository, DocsAdapter, ApiPromptAdapter, Sqlite*Repository, RconCliAdapter, ... infrastructure/config/, infrastructure/factories/ Pm2EcosystemConfig, ModSourceFactory docker/, prerequisite/, types/, utils/ Docker helpers, prerequisite checks, shared types and utilities

docs.title: Architecture Diagram
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph CLI["cli package"]
        IDX["index.ts<br/>parseArgs + switch"] --> CMD["commands/*.ts"]
        CMD --> DI["Container<br/>getContainer()"]
        CMD -.compose commands.-> SH["infrastructure/ShellExecutor.ts<br/>(compose project only)"]
        CLIAD["ClackPromptAdapter<br/>OpsJsonAdapter<br/>Pm2ServiceManagerAdapter"]
    end
    subgraph SHARED["shared package"]
        UC["Use cases<br/>(application/use-cases)"] --> PORTS["Ports<br/>(inbound / outbound)"]
        ADP["Adapters<br/>DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter,<br/>GitWorldBackupAdapter, ServerRepository,<br/>Sqlite*, ..."] -.implements.-> PORTS
        UC --> DOM["Domain<br/>entities, value objects"]
    end
    API["mcctl-api"] --> UC
    DI --> UC
    DI --> ADP
    DI --> CLIAD

docs.title: Two Kinds of Commands
docs.text:
Be aware of both styles when reading or adding code:

  • Use case commands contain business logic. The handler gets the container, calls a use case from shared, and formats the result. Examples: create, delete, config-snapshot, backup-schedule, world, mod.
  • Thin commands are pass-throughs. They call a runtime port (start, stop, logs), open a TCP RCON session from IServerConsolePort.getEndpoint (rcon, console <server>), run docker compose through ShellExecutor (up, down, --all, router; compose project only), or run RCON through docker exec <container> rcon-cli (lib/rcon.ts, exec). The console init/service/user/api/remove subcommands are separate; see below.

New business logic belongs in a shared use case, not in a file under commands/. A command file should parse options, call the use case and print output.

docs.title: Domain Layer
docs.text:
Lives in platform/services/shared/src/domain/.

Value objects (immutable, validated in a static create()):

Class Rule ServerName 2-32 characters, lowercase, must start with a letter, hyphens allowed but not consecutive. Exposes value; the container and host names come from containerNameOf / serverHostnameOf ServerType Wraps ServerTypeEnum: PAPER, VANILLA, FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC, SPIGOT, BUKKIT, PURPUR, QUILT, LEAF, FOLIA, PUFFERFISH, MODRINTH, AUTO_CURSEFORGE McVersion Minecraft version Memory JVM memory such as 4G or 2048M WorldOptions, ModpackOptions World and modpack setup

Other value objects cover cron expressions, snapshot diffs, roles, player data and so on. See domain/value-objects/.

Entities include Server, World, ConfigSnapshot, BackupSchedule, Player, PlayerSession, User and AuditLog. See domain/entities/.

docs.title: Ports and Use Cases
docs.text:
Inbound ports (application/ports/inbound/) are use case interfaces. Older, interactive use cases expose two entry points:

Interface Methods ICreateServerUseCase execute() (prompts) / executeWithConfig(config) IDeleteServerUseCase execute() (prompts) / executeWithName(name, { force, yes, deleteWorld })

Newer use cases (config snapshots, backup schedules, player management, ...) have plain CRUD-style methods and no interactive mode:

// shared/src/application/ports/inbound/IConfigSnapshotUseCase.ts
export interface IConfigSnapshotUseCase {
  create(serverName: string, description?: string, scheduleId?: string): Promise<ConfigSnapshot>;
  list(serverName?: string, limit?: number, offset?: number): Promise<ConfigSnapshot[]>;
  findById(id: string): Promise<ConfigSnapshot | null>;
  diff(snapshotId1: string, snapshotId2: string): Promise<SnapshotDiff>;
  restore(snapshotId: string, force?: boolean): Promise<void>;
  count(serverName?: string): Promise<number>;
  delete(id: string): Promise<void>;
}

Outbound ports (application/ports/outbound/) include IPromptPort, IContainerRuntimePort, IServerConsolePort, IWorldBackupPort, IWorldAssignmentPort, IServerSpecRepository, IServerRepository, IWorldRepository, IDocProvider, IAuditLogPort, IRconPort, IModSourcePort, IServiceManagerPort and the snapshot/backup repositories. Note that IPromptPort and IDocProvider are outbound ports.

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text: Port Adapter Package IPromptPort ClackPromptAdapter (@clack/prompts) cli IPromptPort ApiPromptAdapter (non-interactive, used by mcctl-api) shared IContainerRuntimePort DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter shared IServerConsolePort DockerServerConsoleAdapter (RCON) shared IWorldBackupPort GitWorldBackupAdapter shared IWorldAssignmentPort ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter shared IServerRepository ServerRepository (filesystem, via Paths) shared IWorldRepository WorldRepository shared IDocProvider DocsAdapter shared IAuditLogPort, backup/snapshot repositories Sqlite*Repository (better-sqlite3) shared IServiceManagerPort Pm2ServiceManagerAdapter cli IModSourcePort ModrinthAdapter mod-source-modrinth

docs.title: Dependency Injection
docs.text:
cli/src/infrastructure/di/container.ts defines class Container with lazily created singletons exposed as typed getters. There is no string-keyed resolve().

const container = getContainer(options.root);   // ContainerOptions | rootDir string
const useCase = container.configSnapshotUseCase; // created on first access

Available getters include promptPort, runtimePort, containerRuntime, serverConsolePort, worldBackupPort, worldAssignmentPort, serverSpecRepository, serverRepository, worldRepository, docProvider, auditLogPort, modSourcePort, createServerUseCase, deleteServerUseCase, worldManagementUseCase, backupUseCase, backupScheduleUseCase, configSnapshotUseCase and configSnapshotScheduleUseCase.

Related helpers:

  • getContainer(options?) returns a process-wide Container.
  • Container.create(options?) builds a fresh one.
  • Container.createWithAdapters(...) injects custom adapters (tests).
  • resetContainer() drops the global instance (tests).

docs.title: Adding a New Command
docs.text:
Commands are registered by hand in cli/src/index.ts. The CLI does not use commander for this (commander is only used by console user and console api).

  1. Write cli/src/commands/<name>.ts exporting <name>Command(options): Promise<number> that returns an exit code.
  2. Re-export it from cli/src/commands/index.ts.
  3. Import it in cli/src/index.ts.
  4. Add a case '<name>': to the switch (command) block.
  5. If it has subcommands, add the command name to the list in parseArgs() that sets result.subCommand. Add any value-less flags to booleanOnlyFlags.
  6. Add help text to printUsage().

If the command needs business logic, first add it in shared:

  1. Add the port interface under application/ports/inbound/ (and outbound ports or adapters if new I/O is needed).
  2. Implement it in application/use-cases/.
  3. Export both from shared/src/index.ts.
  4. Add a getter in cli/src/infrastructure/di/container.ts.

docs.title: Worked Example: config-snapshot
Prompts
docs.text:
IPromptPort provides generic prompts (text, confirm, password), domain prompts (promptServerName, promptServerType, promptMcVersion, promptMemory, promptWorldOptions, promptServerSelection, ...), output helpers (intro, outro, success, error, warn, info, note), spinner() and cancellation helpers.

const name = await this.prompt.promptServerName();   // returns a ServerName
if (this.prompt.isCancel(value)) {
  this.prompt.handleCancel();                         // never returns
}
const spin = this.prompt.spinner();

To add a prompt:

  • Domain prompt used by a use case: add a promptXxx() method to IPromptPort, implement it in ClackPromptAdapter and ApiPromptAdapter, and add it to MockPromptAdapter.
  • Standalone prompt used directly by a command (server select, player select, ...): add a file under cli/src/lib/prompts/ and export it from its index.ts.

docs.title: Mod Sources
docs.text:
IModSourcePort has sourceName, displayName, search(), getProject(), getVersions(), isAvailable(), getEnvKey(), formatForEnv(), plus two optional methods: getProjects?() and getModpackClientOnlyMods?().

Essential model fields (shared/src/domain/mod/):

  • ModProject: slug, title, description, downloads, iconUrl, projectType, serverSide, clientSide, categories, author, license, sourceId, sourceName.
  • ModVersion: version identity plus versionType, downloads, datePublished, optional changelog.

ModSourceFactory (shared/src/infrastructure/factories/ModSourceFactory.ts) is a static registry: register (throws on duplicate), get (throws if unknown), getOrNull, isSupported, getSupportedSources, getAllAdapters, getDefaultSource, clear.

ModrinthAdapter takes ModrinthApiClient and ModrinthMapper through its constructor, with defaults, and registers an instance on import (also exported as modrinthAdapter). The CLI command cli/src/commands/mod.ts resolves sources with ModSourceFactory.getOrNull(source), while the container creates new ModrinthAdapter() for modSourcePort.

To add a source: create a package that implements IModSourcePort, call ModSourceFactory.register() from its index.ts, and import the package where it should be active.

docs.title: How the CLI Relates to the Other Packages
docs.text:
• The CLI does not call mcctl-api over HTTP. Both consume the same shared use cases.
  • mcctl console ... manages mcctl-api and mcctl-console as PM2 processes through Pm2ServiceManagerAdapter and shared/src/infrastructure/config/Pm2EcosystemConfig.ts.
  • mcctl console user writes the console SQLite database directly (cli/src/lib/console-db.ts).
  • SQLite stores (better-sqlite3), relative to the platform root: data/audit.db, backups/meta/backup-schedules.db, backups/meta/config-snapshots.db.
  • There are no bash scripts. Every command is TypeScript (#715); mcctl runs docker, git and avahi through ports and adapters.
  • Some subsystems are only used by mcctl-api: BlueMap rendering, world analysis, player sessions and the RCON adapter (RconCliAdapter).

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The CLI uses vitest. Layout under platform/services/cli/tests/:

Directory Purpose unit/ Domain, lib, infrastructure and command unit tests integration/ Use cases wired with mocks commands/ Command handlers with a mocked container e2e/ cli-*.test.ts spawn node dist/index.js via tests/e2e/helpers.ts (runCli) mocks/ MockPromptAdapter, MockServerRepository, MockWorldRepository, MockWorldAssignmentPort, createMockContainerRuntime

Shared package tests are flat files in platform/services/shared/tests/*.test.ts.

pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/mcctl test              # all
pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/mcctl test:unit
pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/mcctl test:integration
pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/mcctl test:e2e          # needs a build (dist/)

Older tests use node:assert; newer ones use vitest expect and vi.mock(). Use expect in new tests.

Use case integration test (construct the use case directly with mocks and a fake port; see cli/tests/integration/BackupUseCase-port.test.ts):

const prompt = new MockPromptAdapter({ /* scripted answers */ });
const port: IWorldBackupPort = fakeBackupPort();   // a fake that records calls
const useCase = new BackupUseCase(prompt, port);

Command test with a mocked container (see cli/tests/commands/config-snapshot.test.ts):

vi.mock('../../src/infrastructure/di/container.js');
vi.mocked(getContainer).mockReturnValue({
  configSnapshotUseCase: mockUseCase,
} as never);

Container.createWithAdapters(prompt, serverRepo, worldRepo) builds a container from mocks when you need a real Container. Reset any global container between tests with resetContainer().

docs.title: Git Workflow
docs.text: This project follows the Git-Flow branching strategy with Semantic Versioning. Every change starts from a GitHub issue and lands on develop through a pull request.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
main      ← released state, updated from develop by maintainers
  │
develop   ← integration branch; every PR targets develop
  │
  ├── feature/<issue>-<description>   new features, improvements, refactoring
  ├── bugfix/<issue>-<description>    non-urgent bug fixes
  ├── release/<version>               release preparation (maintainers)
  └── hotfix/<version>                urgent production fixes (maintainers)
Type Pattern Example When Feature feature/<issue>-<description> feature/12-add-backup New features, improvements, refactoring Bugfix bugfix/<issue>-<description> bugfix/15-fix-lock Regular, non-urgent bugs Release release/<version> release/2.30.0 Preparing a release Hotfix hotfix/<version> hotfix/2.30.1 Production incidents, urgent bugs, risk of data loss

Never commit directly to develop or main.

docs.title: Standard Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create the GitHub issue in the original repository (smallmiro/minecraft-server-manager) with Summary, Root Cause or Requirements, Solution / Implementation Plan, Files to Modify, and Acceptance Criteria as checkboxes.
  2. Create a branch from an up-to-date develop in your fork, with the issue number in its name.
  3. Implement with TDD and commit with the issue reference (#<issue>). Check off acceptance criteria as you go.
  4. Open one PR per issue against develop of the original repository, with Closes #<issue> in the body.
  5. Address review comments with new commits on the same branch.
  6. After merge, delete the branch locally and on your fork.

Setup commands for the fork and the upstream remote are in the Development Guide.

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
<type>: <description> (#<issue-number>)

<body>

A scope is optional, for example feat(cli): add mod search (#123). Commits written with Claude Code end with a Co-Authored-By: Claude ... <noreply@anthropic.com> trailer.

Type Description Example feat New feature feat: add world backup command (#12) fix Bug fix fix: resolve lock file race condition (#15) docs Documentation docs: update CLI reference (#20) refactor Refactoring with no behavior change refactor: extract validation logic (#25) test Tests test: add world locking tests (#30) chore Maintenance, releases chore(release): bump version to v2.30.0

Avoid vague messages such as "fix", "update", or "changes".

docs.title: TDD
docs.text:
Every feature, bug fix, and improvement follows Red → Green → Refactor:

  1. Red: write a failing test that defines the expected behavior.
  2. Green: write the minimum code that makes it pass.
  3. Refactor: clean up while the tests stay green.

PRs without tests are not accepted, except for documentation-only changes and configuration changes with no logic. Where tests live is listed in the Development Guide.

docs.title: Tidy First
docs.text:
Never mix structural and behavioral changes in the same commit.

Change type Examples Structural Rename, extract function, move file Behavioral New feature, bug fix, logic change 
# Good: two separate commits
git commit -m "refactor: extract validate_world function (#7)"
git commit -m "feat: add world existence check (#7)"

# Bad: mixed in one commit
git commit -m "feat: add validation with new helper function (#7)"

docs.title: Task Checkpoint (task.md)
docs.text:
task.md in the repository root is git-ignored and used for local work-in-progress notes. /work appends a checkpoint to it at each commit.

## Working On
- [ ] Implementing lock.sh (#5)

## Context
- Branch: feature/5-world-locking

## Notes
- lock file format: <server>:<timestamp>:<pid>

Planning happens on GitHub: issue bodies hold the requirements and acceptance criteria, and /plan-work produces the plan for larger work. The root plan.md and the per-package plan.md files are historical roadmaps from the initial build-out.

docs.title: Semantic Versioning
docs.text:
The project follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0. All five npm packages (@minecraft-docker/shared, mod-source-modrinth, mcctl, mcctl-api, mcctl-console) and the root package.json share one version.

Part Increment when Example MAJOR Incompatible or breaking changes 1.9.0 → 2.0.0 MINOR New backward-compatible features 2.29.1 → 2.30.0 PATCH Backward-compatible bug fixes 2.29.0 → 2.29.1

Incrementing MAJOR resets MINOR and PATCH to 0; incrementing MINOR resets PATCH to 0.

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
Releases are run by maintainers, usually through the release-manager agent.

  1. Branch: create release/<version> from develop.
  2. Prepare: in one chore(release): bump version to v<version> commit, bump the version in the root and all five package package.json files, add the version to CHANGELOG.md, copy it to platform/services/cli/CHANGELOG.md, update the Changelog section of platform/services/cli/README.md (shown on the npm page), and update README.md and docs/documentforllmagent.md as needed.

  3. Merge and tag: merge the release branch into develop, then create and push an annotated tag.

    git tag -a v2.30.0 -m "Release v2.30.0"
git push origin v2.30.0

  4. CI: the v* tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which builds the workspace, publishes the five packages to npm, creates the GitHub Release, and deploys the MkDocs site to GitHub Pages.

  5. Verify: check that npm view <package> version returns the new version for all five packages. CI generates the release notes from the commit list, so apply curated notes only after CI finishes (gh release edit v<version> --notes-file ...).

docs.title: CI Workflows
docs.text: Workflow Trigger Purpose ci.yml Every PR to develop/main, push to develop, called by release.yml Build, lint, typecheck and test all packages; script tests on Linux and macOS; compose validation e2e.yml Daily at 03:00 KST, manual dispatch Management Console E2E (Playwright) release.yml Push of a v* tag Runs ci.yml first, then npm publish, GitHub Release, docs deploy deploy-website.yml Push to main touching website/**, manual dispatch Deploy the landing page

docs.title: Code Quality
docs.text:
• Remove duplication by extracting shared logic.
  • Use names that describe intent.
  • Keep each function to one responsibility.
  • Keep commits small and atomic so they are easy to review and revert.

docs.title: ADR-0001: Container Runtime Ports and the Docker Adapter
docs.text: Status Proposed (2026-10-23) Issue #654 (Hardening D1), milestone M2 (#643), epic #640 Follow-ups that change this ADR #665 (D4, port boundary cleanup), #669 (A7), C2, #675 (D5), #641 (k8s adapter), #732 (S3, backup port), #670 (A4: IWorldAssignmentPort final, ADR-0002), #735 (S7, server delete) Consumers #667 (D2, API), #668 (D3, CLI), #666 (E3, contract tests), #715 (script removal)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• platform/services/shared/src/docker/index.ts exports 48 free functions. The CLI and mcctl-api import them directly, so there is no seam for a second runtime.
  • The CLI and mcctl-api also run docker themselves in about 20 places (cli/src/lib/shell.ts, cli/src/lib/rcon.ts, mcctl-api/src/lib/rcon.ts, mcctl-api/src/routes/servers.ts, and others; see Direct call sites).
  • The existing ports (IShellPort, IRconPort, IServerRepository) cover none of status, logs, exec, lifecycle, or stats.
  • The k8s adapter (#641) must be added later, not written by editing call sites again.

This issue is a structural change only (Tidy First). Runtime behaviour, argv, return values, and timing stay as they are.

docs.title: Decision Summary
docs.text:
1. Six runtime ports in D1: IContainerRuntimePort, IServerConsolePort, IRouterStatusPort, IPlayitAgentPort, IHostnameRegistrarPort, IRuntimeEnvironmentPort.
  2. Method rule: a method goes into a port only if a current call site will move to it: a function in docker/index.ts, or a direct docker call in the CLI or API that D2/D3 will migrate. Methods needed only by future k8s or #715 work are deferred. D1 fixes the port surface so that D2 and D3 can work in parallel without editing shared (SYNC-3).
  3. IServerSpecRepository and IWorldAssignmentPort are reserved as type-only files. The issue asks for them "interface only", so D1 creates them with the sketched signatures, marked provisional. They have no implementation and no caller in D1. Their shapes depend on designs that are still open (ServerSpec schema, §9.2; the A4 assignment model), so D5 and A4 may rewrite them. See Reserved ports. Both are now settled: IWorldAssignmentPort by ADR-0002 (#670), IServerSpecRepository by ADR-0003 (#675).
  4. Contracts are provisional until a second adapter exists. Until #641 adds the k8s adapter, D4, A7, C2, and D5 may change signatures. The TypeScript compiler finds every call site. Each change updates this ADR.
  5. Synchronous where the code is synchronous today. Methods backed by execSync/spawnSync/execFileSync stay synchronous. Methods that are async today stay async. C2 converts the port to Promise everywhere.
  6. Error model is unchanged: sentinels ('not_found', 'unknown', '', null, false, '-') and result objects that never throw, exactly as today. "Cannot tell" and "absent" stay conflated until A7 adds RuntimeUnavailableError.
  7. Workload names are Docker container names in D1 (mc-<server>, mc-router, playit-agent). Only then can the facade wrappers delegate without translation, and only then do the #720 argv tests (docker-shell-injection.test.ts) keep passing unchanged. D4 moves the mc- rule into the adapter and changes the parameter to ServerName. Done in #665: the parameter is widened to ServerName | string (see Port Boundary Cleanup).
  8. One adapter class per port. The Docker classes live in one module, infrastructure/adapters/DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.ts, and share private docker inspect helpers. Avahi gets its own file. A single class cannot implement all ports: start()/stop() (playit) collide with start(name)/stop(name) (runtime), and getHealth() (router) collides with getHealth(name).
  9. docker/index.ts becomes a legacy facade. It keeps all 48 exports with the same signatures. The leaf functions that run processes delegate in one line to private adapter instances. Composite functions stay verbatim, and process helpers move to infrastructure/process.ts. The facade no longer imports child_process.
  10. No exported singleton. Composition roots (CLI Container in D3, API container plugin in D2) construct adapters with new. Only the facade holds a private default instance.
  11. Lint: no-restricted-imports + no-restricted-syntax forbid child_process outside src/infrastructure/** in shared, cli, and mcctl-api. The rule starts as warn and becomes error per package once that package has zero violations (after D2/D3).

docs.title: Port Definitions
docs.text:
Files: platform/services/shared/src/application/ports/outbound/<Port>.ts, exported from outbound/index.ts and listed in ports/index.ts, so D2/D3 import them from the package root (one port per file, as in the rest of the directory). Types such as ContainerStatus come from src/types/index.ts.

// IContainerRuntimePort.ts
import type { ContainerStatus, HealthStatus, ContainerStats } from '../../../types/index.js';
import type { ServerName } from '../../../domain/value-objects/ServerName.js';

/** Lifecycle result. Never rejects; failure is `success: false`. */
export interface RuntimeActionResult {
  success: boolean;
  stdout?: string;
  stderr?: string;
  error?: string;
}

/**
 * Per-workload runtime operations.
 * `name` is the server (#665): the adapter maps a ServerName to its workload (Docker: `mc-<server>`).
 * A string is the workload name itself (D1 form; @deprecated for servers; not narrowed in v3.0.0, see #667 and #641).
 * D1 contract: "absent" and "runtime unreachable" are NOT distinguished (A7 changes this).
 */
export interface IContainerRuntimePort {
  /** 'not_found' when absent or when the runtime cannot be queried. */
  getStatus(name: ServerName | string): ContainerStatus;
  /** Added by #665: getStatus as an awaited child process, for request paths. */
  getStatusAsync(name: ServerName | string): Promise<ContainerStatus>;
  /** Added by #764: getStats as an awaited child process (null on failure or timeout), for request paths. */
  getStatsAsync(name: ServerName | string): Promise<ContainerStats | null>;
  /** 'none' without a healthcheck, 'unknown' on failure. */
  getHealth(name: ServerName | string): HealthStatus;
  exists(name: ServerName | string): boolean;
  /** Server workloads (mc-* except mc-router), sorted. [] on failure. */
  /** `strict: true` (added by #732): a failed query throws instead of returning []. */
  list(options?: { running?: boolean; strict?: boolean }): string[];
  /** Last `lines` lines (default 50). '' on failure. */
  getLogs(name: ServerName | string, lines?: number): string;
  getStats(name: ServerName | string): ContainerStats | null;
  getUptime(name: ServerName | string): { uptime: string; seconds: number } | null;

  /** Create the workload if missing, then run it. */
  start(name: ServerName | string): Promise<RuntimeActionResult>;
  stop(name: ServerName | string): Promise<RuntimeActionResult>;
  restart(name: ServerName | string): Promise<RuntimeActionResult>;
  /** #735: stop and remove the workload. Absent = success; a runtime that cannot be queried = failure. Server data is not the runtime's. */
  remove(name: ServerName | string): Promise<RuntimeActionResult>;

  /** Timestamped lines since `since`, at most `tail` lines. Rejects on failure. */
  readLogs(name: ServerName | string, options: { since: string; tail: number }): Promise<string[]>;
  /** New output only by default; `options.tail` emits the last N lines first, then follows; `options.follow: false` prints the last `tail` lines (stdout and stderr) and resolves at exit; `options.onExit(code, error?)` reports docker's exit code or a spawn error once, while the promise still always resolves so the v2.x contract holds (#731). */
  followLogs(name: ServerName | string, onChunk: (chunk: string) => void, signal: AbortSignal, options?: { tail?: number; follow?: boolean; onExit?: (code: number | null, error?: Error) => void }): Promise<void>;
}

// IServerConsolePort.ts
import type { PlayerListResult } from '../../../types/index.js';

export interface ConsoleCommandResult { exitCode: number; stdout: string; stderr: string; }
export interface ConsoleEndpoint { host: string; port: number; password: string; }

export interface IServerConsolePort {
  /** `list` via RCON. null when offline or unparseable. */
  listPlayers(name: ServerName | string): Promise<PlayerListResult | null>;
  /** Runs one RCON command. Never rejects (spawn error → exitCode 1, stderr = message).
   *  `signal` (added by #732) is passed to spawn; abort kills the child. */
  command(name: ServerName | string, args: string[], options?: { signal?: AbortSignal }): Promise<ConsoleCommandResult>;
  /** Address and credentials for a direct RCON TCP session (`mcctl rcon`). null when unknown. */
  getEndpoint(name: ServerName | string): Promise<ConsoleEndpoint | null>;
}

// IRouterStatusPort.ts
import type { HealthStatus } from '../../../types/index.js';

export interface IRouterStatusPort {
  /** 'unknown' if the router is not running; else management API probe result. */
  getHealth(): HealthStatus;
  /** Comma-separated router hostnames of a server workload, '-' when none. */
  getHostnames(name: ServerName | string): string;
}

// IPlayitAgentPort.ts
export interface IPlayitAgentPort {
  start(): Promise<{ success: boolean; error?: string }>;
  stop(): Promise<boolean>;
}

// IHostnameRegistrarPort.ts
export type HostnameRegistrarStatus = 'running' | 'installed (not running)' | 'not installed';
/** Added by #675 (ADR-0003). 'skipped' = no/invalid IPv4, registrar missing, or sudo failed. */
export interface HostnameChangeResult { status: 'changed' | 'unchanged' | 'skipped'; reason?: string; }
export interface IHostnameRegistrarPort {
  getStatus(): HostnameRegistrarStatus;
  /** #675: add `<ip> <hostname>` (exact-match check, #660). Never rejects. */
  register(hostname: string, ip: string): Promise<HostnameChangeResult>;
  /**
   * #735: remove the lines that list exactly `hostname` before any comment; 'unchanged' when none does. Never rejects.
   * Command (README sudoers shape, #751): argv, no shell:
   *   sudo -n sed -i '/^[^#]*[[:space:]]<host>\([[:space:]]\|#\|$\)/d' /etc/avahi/hosts
   * <host> is a validated hostname with `[ ] \ . * ^ $ /` escaped; the field-boundary
   * anchors make the match exact. With a password, `sudo -S -p '' -v` runs first.
   */
  unregister(hostname: string): Promise<HostnameChangeResult>;
}

// IRuntimeEnvironmentPort.ts
export interface ToolVersion { installed: boolean; version?: string; }
export interface IRuntimeEnvironmentPort {
  /** Runtime daemon/cluster reachable. */
  isAvailable(): boolean;
  getEngineVersion(): ToolVersion;
  /** Version without a leading 'v'. */
  getComposeVersion(): ToolVersion;
}

IRconPort (getEntityPosition) stays a separate port. D4 (#665) only widened its first parameter to ServerName | string; re-implementing RconCliAdapter on top of IServerConsolePort.command, or merging the two ports, is left to #736 (it would change the argv: docker exec without --).

docs.title: IServerSpecRepository (#675)
docs.text:
Settled by ADR-0003 (schema in its §1). The v2 contract is kept (release rule, #715/#736): ServerSpec stays { name: string } and the four reserved methods keep their signatures. The full type is the new ServerSpecDocument extends ServerSpec, and the new behaviour comes from two added methods, as #670 did for IWorldAssignmentPort. No new port: write renders the generated files through an infrastructure-internal ServerSpecRenderer, so IContainerRuntimePort needs no apply(spec).

// IServerSpecRepository.ts
export interface ServerSpec { name: string }   // v2 export, unchanged
// ServerSpecDocument (domain/server-spec) extends ServerSpec; re-exported here.
export interface LoadedServerSpec {
  document: ServerSpecDocument;
  revision: string | null;   // sha256 of server.yaml; null = imported in memory, no server.yaml yet
  warnings: string[];        // absorbed edits, protected compose, import notes
}
export interface WriteServerSpecOptions {
  expectedRevision?: string | null; // from load(); mismatch → ServerSpecError 'conflict'
  create?: boolean;                 // claim servers/<n> with mkdir, add the include entry, roll back on failure
  force?: boolean;                  // overwrite hand-edited generated files after writing a .bak
  allowStorageChange?: boolean;     // only `mcctl migrate worlds`
}
export interface IServerSpecRepository {
  // v2 (D1) signatures, unchanged
  /** One `{ name }` per server directory with server.yaml or config.env. */
  list(): Promise<ServerSpec[]>;
  /** The document, typed as the v2 ServerSpec. @deprecated Use load(). Deleted in v3.0.0 (#736): `get` → `load(name)`. */
  get(name: string): Promise<ServerSpec | null>;
  /** write(spec) after checking that `spec` is a full document; a bare { name } → 'invalid_spec' listing the missing fields. */
  save(spec: ServerSpec): Promise<void>;
  /** #735: see [Script Removal S7](#script-removal-s7-delete-serversh-735). `delete(name)` (v2) still compiles. */
  delete(name: string, options?: { deleteWorld?: boolean; dryRun?: boolean }): Promise<ServerSpecDeleteResult>;
  // added by #675
  /** Imports in memory when server.yaml is missing; absorbs hand edits. No writes. */
  load(name: string): Promise<LoadedServerSpec | null>;
  write(doc: ServerSpecDocument, options?: WriteServerSpecOptions): Promise<void>;
}
// Errors: ServerSpecError (domain) with code 'invalid_spec' | 'not_found' | 'already_exists' | 'conflict'
//   | 'edit_conflict' | 'compose_edited' | 'undetermined' | 'storage_change' | 'locked' | 'unsupported_spec_version';
//   the world guard rethrows ADR-0002's WorldAssignmentError. API: invalid_spec → 400, not_found → 404, others → 409.

docs.title: Reserved ports
docs.text:
Created in D1 as type-only files with the sketch from the hardening plan §9.1, each with a "provisional" JSDoc. They are async (new code, no synchronous caller to preserve) and import nothing from infrastructure.

Port Owner D1 signature Why provisional IServerSpecRepository D5 (#675) list(): Promise<ServerSpec[]>, get(name): Promise<ServerSpec \| null> (deleted in v3.0.0, #736: use load(name)), save(spec): Promise<void>, delete(name): Promise<void>; ServerSpec is a placeholder { name: string } Settled by ADR-0003, see IServerSpecRepository (#675) above. IWorldAssignmentPort A4 (#670) getAssignment(world): Promise<string \| null> (deleted in v3.0.0, #736: use snapshot() + holdersOf), listAssignments(): Promise<WorldAssignment[]> ({ world, server }), assign(world, server): Promise<void> (rejects on an R1 violation) Superseded, final below.

IWorldAssignmentPort, final (#670, ADR-0002). Assignments are derived from each server's LEVEL in config.env; there is no separate record. It stays a port (#715: no new ports), and the rules live in pure domain functions (shared/src/domain/services/worldAssignment.ts) that adapters reuse.

interface WorldAssignment { world: string; server: string; internal?: boolean } // internal: world in servers/<n>/data (D-1); optional keeps the v2 shape
interface WorldAssignmentSnapshot { assignments: WorldAssignment[]; undetermined: string[] }

export interface IWorldAssignmentPort {
  /** @deprecated (v2) The holder of the world's folders, or null. Use snapshot() + holdersOf. Deleted in v3.0.0 (#736): `getAssignment` → `snapshot()` + `holdersOf`. */
  getAssignment(world: string): Promise<string | null>;
  /** v2 shape: the readable assignments. */
  listAssignments(): Promise<WorldAssignment[]>;
  /** Rejects only when servers/ cannot be listed. An unreadable config or invalid LEVEL goes to `undetermined`. */
  snapshot(): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>;
  /** The snapshot with one server's config.env replaced (snapshot restore, migrate). Writes nothing. */
  preview(server: string, configEnv: string): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>;
  /** The snapshot with the platform .env replaced (platform settings EXTRA_ARGS). Writes nothing. */
  previewPlatformEnv(dotenv: string): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>;
  /** Writes LEVEL=<world>. Rejects WorldAssignmentError (conflict, undetermined, internal_world, ...); fail-closed (R7). */
  assign(world: string, server: string): Promise<void>;
  /** Unassign (#715): the holder's LEVEL falls back to its own default world `<server>`. Rejects WorldAssignmentError. */
  release(world: string): Promise<{ server: string; fallback: string }>;
}

The v2 members getAssignment (deprecated here; deleted in v3.0.0, #736, in favour of snapshot() + holdersOf) and listAssignments (WorldAssignment[]) keep their shape (#715, #736); snapshot, preview and release were added. Adapter: ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter (infrastructure/adapters/ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter.ts), built by the CLI Container and, until D2, by the API routes.

docs.title: Adapters and the Legacy Facade
docs.text:
application/ports/outbound/I*Port.ts           (interfaces only, no imports from infrastructure)
        ▲ implements
infrastructure/process.ts                       execCommand, execCommandAsync, execScript, execScriptInteractive (moved verbatim)
infrastructure/adapters/DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.ts
   ├─ DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter     → IContainerRuntimePort
   ├─ DockerServerConsoleAdapter      → IServerConsolePort
   ├─ DockerRouterStatusAdapter       → IRouterStatusPort
   ├─ DockerPlayitAgentAdapter        → IPlayitAgentPort
   └─ DockerRuntimeEnvironmentAdapter → IRuntimeEnvironmentPort
infrastructure/adapters/AvahiHostnameRegistrarAdapter.ts → IHostnameRegistrarPort (host OS, not Docker)
        ▲ imported by file path (never via a barrel)
docker/index.ts                                 legacy facade: 48 exports, leaf wrappers + verbatim composites
  • Why Avahi is separate: avahi is a host OS service, not a Docker service. Runtime choice and hostname-registrar choice are independent (Docker + avahi on Linux, Docker + nothing on macOS, k8s + nothing).
  • Constructor options (only where current code needs them):
  • DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter({ root?: string; env?: () => NodeJS.ProcessEnv }). root defaults to resolveMcctlRoot() evaluated per call, as today. env applies only to start/stop/restart. The API passes () => childProcessEnv() in D2.
  • DockerPlayitAgentAdapter({ root?: string }). The playit commands keep inheriting process.env, as today.
  • Legacy extras: three exports have no port equivalent. They stay as @deprecated methods on the adapter, outside every port, and are deleted once they have no callers (D3/D4):
  • startContainer (docker start) has no production caller.
  • stopContainer (synchronous docker stop) had one caller, the API delete route; since #735 the route deprovisions through remove(), so it has none.
  • checkDockerCompose has no caller.
  • Composition: export the classes from infrastructure/adapters/index.ts (and therefore from the package root). Do not export instances. The facade creates its own private instances at module load. The constructors have no side effects, so import-time behaviour is unchanged.

docs.title: Dependency rules (cycle prevention)
docs.text:
1. Adapter modules and infrastructure/process.ts import only node:*, ../../types, ../../utils (resolveMcctlRoot), ../process.js, and port types. They never import docker/index.ts.
  2. docker/index.ts imports adapters by file path, never through infrastructure/index.js or infrastructure/adapters/index.js. The barrel loads ServerRepository, which imports the facade; that is a cycle, and a TDZ error on new at load time.
  3. ServerRepository and WorldRepository keep importing execCommandAsync/getContainerStatus from the facade in D1. world-name-resolution.test.ts mocks the facade's execCommandAsync. D4 switches them to an injected IContainerRuntimePort. Done in #665: both take an optional IContainerRuntimePort (default new DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter(), imported by file path) and no longer import the facade.
  4. Composite functions stay in the facade and call the wrappers. They contain no process code. Docker literals in them ('mc-router', 'playit-agent', --in-docker (auto-discovery), :25565) stay until the composites become a query service (see Open questions).

docs.title: Lifecycle Semantics and argv Rules
docs.text:
Method Docker implementation Matches today's start(name) docker compose up -d <name>, cwd = root, env + COMPOSE_FILE=docker-compose.yml, timeout 60 s mcctl.sh start (:426), API executeServerAction('start') stop(name) docker stop -- <name>, env, no timeout mcctl.sh stop (:464), stopContainer, CLI migrate.ts:557, API delete route restart(name) docker compose restart <name>, cwd = root, env + COMPOSE_FILE, timeout 60 s API executeServerAction('restart') (only caller) remove(name) (#735) docker ps -a --format {{.Names}} (exact name; failure = failure, not "absent"); in the compose project (docker compose ps <name> lists it): docker compose stop <name>, then docker compose rm -f <name> (cwd = root, COMPOSE_FILE, timeout 60 s each); otherwise docker rm -f -- <name>. A failed stop returns before rm delete-server.sh step 1 (removed in #735)
  • start means "create if missing". docker start cannot start a server whose container was never created (not_created in the UI). For k8s, start is a scale to 1 after the k8s IServerSpecRepository adapter has written the spec and applied the manifests (ADR-0003, #641).
  • stop follows the majority (3 of 4 paths use docker stop). The API actions route uses docker compose stop today, so its move in D2 is a behaviour change and needs its own commit (see open questions).
  • argv rule: every Docker command that takes a workload name puts -- before the name, as #720 does. Leaf functions already do this. New methods (stop, readLogs, followLogs, command, getEndpoint) add it. Names that reach these calls are already validated, so the only effect is defence in depth. Compose commands (start, restart) keep the API's current argv.
  • Timeouts stay as they are today (listPlayers 5 s, readLogs 10 s with a 10 MiB buffer, compose 60 s, router probe 3 s, the rest none). C2 sets them uniformly.

docs.title: Error Model and Sync/Async (D1)
docs.text:
Method Sync On failure Source getStatus sync 'not_found' getContainerStatus getHealth sync 'unknown' getContainerHealth exists sync false containerExists list sync [] getMcContainers, getRunningMcContainers getLogs sync '' getContainerLogs getStats / getUptime sync null getContainerStats / getContainerUptime start / stop / restart async { success: false, error }, never rejects API executeServerAction readLogs async rejects API player-session-collector.ts followLogs async resolves on close or spawn error API servers.ts:581 (adds the missing error handler; signal is passed to spawn, which kills the child on abort, and chunks after abort are dropped) listPlayers async (non-blocking since #764: awaits execFile, same 5 s timeout) null getOnlinePlayers command async { exitCode: 1, stderr }, never rejects API lib/rcon.ts execRcon getEndpoint async null CLI commands/rcon.ts (the copy uses execFile and returns null on a spawn error; the original has no error handler) router getHealth sync 'unknown' / 'unhealthy' getRouterHealthViaApi router getHostnames sync '-' getContainerHostname playit start / stop async { success: false, error } / false startPlayitAgent / stopPlayitAgent registrar getStatus sync 'not installed' getAvahiStatus environment methods sync false / { installed: false } checkDocker, getDockerVersion, getDockerComposeVersion

Why D1 keeps the legacy error model: changing it is a behaviour change, and A7 (#669) owns that change. A7 will make getStatus throw RuntimeUnavailableError when the runtime cannot be queried, keeping 'not_found' for "absent". Why D1 stays synchronous: making a synchronous facade wrapper delegate to an async port is impossible without changing every caller. C2 converts the ports and their callers together.

docs.title: Mapping: docker/index.ts (48 exports)
docs.text:
Callers are production imports (src/, tests excluded). "facade" means callers that are other functions in docker/index.ts.

Leaf functions → adapter (facade delegates, 20)

Export Callers Target getContainerStatus api: routes/players, routes/servers, routes/servers/config, services/config-snapshot-service; shared: WorldRepository; facade IContainerRuntimePort.getStatus getContainerHealth api: routes/servers; facade .getHealth containerExists cli: status; api: routes/players, routes/servers; facade .exists getMcContainers cli: status; facade .list() getRunningMcContainers cli: msg, player-online .list({ running: true }) getContainerLogs api: routes/servers .getLogs getContainerStats, getContainerUptime facade .getStats, .getUptime startContainer none DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.startContainer (deprecated extra) stopContainer api: routes/servers (delete) DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.stopContainer (deprecated extra) getOnlinePlayers api: routes/servers; facade IServerConsolePort.listPlayers getRouterHealthViaApi facade IRouterStatusPort.getHealth getContainerHostname facade IRouterStatusPort.getHostnames startPlayitAgent, stopPlayitAgent cli: playit; api: routes/playit IPlayitAgentPort.start / .stop getAvahiStatus api: routes/router; shared: PrerequisiteChecker IHostnameRegistrarPort.getStatus checkDocker cli: status IRuntimeEnvironmentPort.isAvailable getDockerVersion, getDockerComposeVersion shared: PrerequisiteChecker .getEngineVersion, .getComposeVersion checkDockerCompose none DockerRuntimeEnvironmentAdapter.isComposeAvailable (deprecated extra)

Process helpers → infrastructure/process.ts (re-exported by the facade, 4): execCommand (facade only), execCommandAsync (shared ServerRepository, playit), execScript and execScriptInteractive (cli lib/shell, shared ShellAdapter). These are generic process runners, not runtime ports. #715 removes the script runners.

Composites → stay in the facade verbatim (12): getServerInfo, getRouterInfo, getPlatformStatus (cli status), getDetailedServerInfo, getDetailedServerInfoWithPlayers (cli status), getRouterDetailInfo (cli status, api routes/router), getServerInfoFromConfig (api routes/playit, routes/servers), getAllServers (api routes/players, routes/playit, routes/servers), serverExists (7 api files), getDetailedServerInfoFromConfig, getServerDetailedInfo (api routes/servers), getPlayitAgentStatus (cli playit, api routes/playit, routes/router). They combine runtime state with config files. Their target is an application query service that takes ports (see open questions).

Pure or config-file functions → no port (12): parseRconPlayerList (lives in DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.ts next to listPlayers, because adapters cannot import the facade; the facade re-exports it), formatBytes, parseRouterHosts, replaceRouterHosts, resolvePlayitDomain (pure); getWorldsDir, getServersDir, getWorldDirectorySize (plan §9.1: moves to WorldRepository, async); getConfiguredServers, readServerConfigEnv, getServerPlayitDomain, setServerPlayitDomain (config files; their writes move behind IServerSpecRepository in #675, ADR-0003 §6; env parsing is unified by A6).

docs.title: Lint Rule
docs.text:
Config files: platform/services/{shared,cli,mcctl-api}/.eslintrc.json (ESLint 8.57, eslintrc format). mcctl-console uses next lint, has no child_process in src/, and is out of scope.

{
  "rules": {
    // ...existing rules
    "no-restricted-imports": ["warn", { "paths": [
      { "name": "child_process", "message": "child_process is allowed only under src/infrastructure/ (ADR-0001). Use a runtime port." },
      { "name": "node:child_process", "message": "child_process is allowed only under src/infrastructure/ (ADR-0001). Use a runtime port." }
    ]}],
    // no-restricted-imports does not see import() or require() in ESLint 8
    "no-restricted-syntax": ["warn",
      { "selector": "ImportExpression[source.value=/^(node:)?child_process$/]", "message": "..." },
      { "selector": "CallExpression[callee.name='require'][arguments.0.value=/^(node:)?child_process$/]", "message": "..." }
    ]
  },
  "overrides": [
    { "files": ["src/infrastructure/**/*.ts"], "rules": { "no-restricted-imports": "off", "no-restricted-syntax": "off" } }
  ]
}
  • pnpm lint runs eslint src --ext .ts without --max-warnings, and CI (ci.yml) runs pnpm lint. Warnings therefore do not fail CI. Tests are not linted (src only), so tests that mock child_process are unaffected.
  • Measured on 2026-10-23 with this exact config (dry run): shared 2 (docker/index.ts, prerequisite/PrerequisiteChecker.ts), cli 12, mcctl-api 9 (6 files, including 3 dynamic import()s in routes/servers.ts). Total 23. After D1: shared 1, total 22. The override correctly exempts RconCliAdapter and BlueMapCliRenderer.
  • Becoming an error: per package, in the issue that brings the package to zero (cli: D3, mcctl-api: D2, shared: D4). Rows 8, 15, 16, and 19 above are not runtime work but still block the error.
  • cli is an error since #668 (0 findings). No port method was added: the CLI uses getStatusAsync, getStatus, list, stop, and console.command as they are.

docs.text:
Script What it does Covered by D1 ports Deferred (reason) logs.sh (removed in #731) tail, follow, --since, --timestamps getLogs, followLogs({ tail, follow }), readLogs --file/--json formatting is CLI presentation, not a port.
