docs.title: Implementation Plan for #654 (core-agent)
docs.text:
Rules: no behaviour change; refactor/test/chore commits only; tests first (a red commit is fine, as in #720); never touch call sites outside shared; run source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22 first. Baseline: shared 60 files / 988 tests passing (2026-10-23).

  1. refactor(shared): add runtime port interfaces (#654): the six port files and outbound/index.ts exports. Check: pnpm --filter @minecraft-docker/shared typecheck.
  2. refactor(shared): move process helpers to infrastructure/process (#654): move execCommand, execCommandAsync, execScript, execScriptInteractive verbatim; the facade re-exports them. Check: shared tests, especially world-name-resolution.test.ts (its facade mock must still apply to ServerRepository).
  3. test(shared): characterize Docker runtime adapters (#654) (red), then refactor(shared): move docker leaf functions into runtime adapters (#654) (green). Create the five Docker classes by moving 19 leaf bodies (the 20th, getAvahiStatus, moves in step 5), and make the facade leaves one-line delegations. After step 5 the facade has no child_process import. Export the classes from infrastructure/adapters/index.ts. Tests: vi.mock('node:child_process'), and for each method assert the exact (file, argv, options) and both the success mapping and the failure sentinel. Keep docker-shell-injection.test.ts unchanged: its fake docker on PATH proves wrapper → adapter argv end to end.
  4. test(shared): ... (red), then refactor(shared): add lifecycle, log and console methods to Docker adapters (#654) (green): start/stop/restart, readLogs, followLogs, command, getEndpoint, copied from the call sites in the direct call sites table. The originals stay until D2/D3. Test followLogs with a fake child (EventEmitter + PassThrough): close resolves, a spawn error resolves, no chunk is forwarded after abort, and signal reaches spawn. One test runs a real child to prove that abort kills it.
  5. test (red), then refactor(shared): add AvahiHostnameRegistrarAdapter (#654) (green): move getAvahiStatus and mock the three execSync probes.
  6. chore(lint): warn on child_process outside infrastructure (#654): the three .eslintrc.json files. Check: pnpm lint exits 0 with warnings shared 1, cli 12, mcctl-api 9.
  7. Final gate at the repo root: pnpm build && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test. The cli/api tests use vi.mock('@minecraft-docker/shared', ...) and must pass unchanged, because every export name and signature is kept.

Review checklist: git grep -n "docker/index" src/infrastructure/adapters/DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter.ts src/infrastructure/process.ts is empty; docker/index.ts imports adapters by file path; all 48 exports keep their names and signatures (git diff on src/index.ts shows no removals); no --max-warnings added.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + D2, D3, D4, A7, and E3 can start against fixed interfaces, and the k8s adapter becomes an addition.
  • + The review is mechanical: leaf bodies move unchanged and #720's argv tests guard the move.
  • − Port signatures will change three more times (D4: ServerName; A7: unavailable error; C2: async). That cost is accepted; the compiler lists the call sites.
  • − About 150 lines are duplicated between the new adapter methods (step 4) and the API/CLI originals until D2/D3 land.
  • − Docker naming remains in the facade composites until they become a query service.

docs.title: Open Questions
docs.text:
1. Reserved ports (resolved 2026-10-23): created as two type-only files with the sketched signatures and a placeholder ServerSpec that D5 will replace (decision 3). IWorldAssignmentPort was finalized by #670 (ADR-0002).
  2. API stop semantics: moving executeServerAction('stop') (docker compose stop) to runtime.stop (docker stop) is a small behaviour change. The two differ only for containers that are not in the compose project. Option A (recommended): accept it in D2 as a separate, labelled commit. Option B: make stop compose-based and change mcctl.sh-parity callers instead.
  3. Owner of the composites: none of D2, D4, or #667 names the 12 facade composites. D2's acceptance criterion "route tests with a fake container" needs them injectable. Recommendation: add "turn the composites into an application query service built from ports" to D4 (shared, core-agent), and land it before D2's route migration. #665 did not do this: none of its acceptance criteria needs it. It stays open for D2 (#667).
  4. Order of signature changes: D2, D3, and D4 run in parallel (P3), but D4 changes port parameters to ServerName. Option A (recommended): land D4's signature change first, then D2/D3. Option B: run them in parallel and let the compiler-driven fix-ups happen at merge. Resolved by #665: the parameters were widened, not replaced, so D2/D3 compile either way and can move call sites to ServerName at their own pace.
  5. Scope of the error flip: rows 8, 15, 16, and 19 (script, git, npm, and pm2 runners) are not runtime work. Confirm they belong to D2/D3/D4, or else the rule stays a warning for that package. The script part is closed by #736 (v3.0.0): every script runner is gone (execScript, execScriptInteractive, ShellAdapter, IShellPort), so no script row is left in the table above. The git, npm and pm2 runners are not script work; the CLI's moved under src/infrastructure/ in #668.

docs.title: Port Boundary Cleanup (#665, D4)
docs.text: Structural change only (Tidy First). Docker argv, return values and error sentinels are unchanged except where noted below, and no shared export or signature is removed (#715: v2.x only deprecates; #736 deletes in v3.0.0).

docs.title: Naming rules move to infrastructure
docs.text:
infrastructure/adapters/workloadNames.ts holds the runtime naming rules and is exported from the package root:

Function Result containerNameOf(server: ServerName \| string) mc-<server> serverHostnameOf(server: ServerName \| string) <server>.local workloadNameOf(name: ServerName \| string) a ServerName → its container; a string → unchanged (the container name)

The module has no runtime imports, so @minecraft-docker/shared/naming stays browser-safe. ServerName.containerName/hostname and Server.containerName/hostname remained as @deprecated getters that delegate here (state at #665); that was the only domain → infrastructure import. The getters were deleted in v3.0.0 (#736); use containerNameOf / serverHostnameOf. The reserved-name message (conflicts with the mc-router container) is built the same way, so its text is unchanged.

docs.title: Port signature changes
docs.text:
Port Before (D1) After (#665) IContainerRuntimePort getStatus, getHealth, exists, getLogs, getStats, getUptime, start, stop, restart, readLogs, followLogs take name: string name: ServerName \| string. list() is unchanged and still returns container names. Added getStatusAsync(name): Promise<ContainerStatus> (see repositories below) and, in #764, getStatsAsync(name): Promise<ContainerStats \| null> IServerConsolePort listPlayers, command, getEndpoint take name: string name: ServerName \| string IRouterStatusPort getHostnames(name: string) getHostnames(name: ServerName \| string) IRconPort getEntityPosition(container: string, player) getEntityPosition(server: ServerName \| string, player) IShellPort exec(script, args), execInteractive(script, args) unchanged, @deprecated (a port method must not take a script name) IPlatformSettingsPort (new) — load(): McctlConfig \| null
  • Meaning: a ServerName is the server and the adapter picks the workload (workloadNameOf). A string is the workload name itself, as in D1. The string form is deprecated for servers; the router and playit agent keep their container names until the k8s adapter (#641) gives them their own methods.
  • Why a union, not overloads: method parameters are bivariant, so a v2 implementation declared with (name: string) still satisfies (name: ServerName | string). An overload pair (name: ServerName) + (name: string) would reject it. tests/runtimePorts-v2-compat.test.ts compiles a v2 IRconPort implementation and v2 callers to hold this.
  • Released and unreleased ports (#753 review): of the widened ports only IRconPort shipped in v2.33.0 (npm). IContainerRuntimePort, IServerConsolePort, IRouterStatusPort and IHostnameRegistrarPort were added by #654 after v2.33.0, so no released implementation exists and passing a ServerName to them is not a breaking change. Shared does so (checkServerStopped, WorldManagementUseCase start after create, DeleteServerUseCase online players, ServerRepository.getStatus); the cli and mcctl-api test fakes map it with workloadNameOf(name).
  • IRconPort keeps the v2 runtime contract: its callers (WorldInfoUseCase.getLivePlayerLocations, PlayerManagementUseCase options.container, fed by the API) keep passing the container name string mc-<server>, so a v2 implementation receives exactly what it did before. Only RconCliAdapter accepts both forms. tests/rconPort-v2-contract.test.ts pins this with a recording v2 implementation. New code that computes the name in infrastructure or the API uses containerNameOf.

docs.title: Repositories take a runtime port
docs.text:
new ServerRepository(paths?, runtime?) and new WorldRepository(paths?, assignments?, runtime?). The default is new DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter(), the instance the facade delegated to; the CLI Container passes its runtime. Neither repository imports the facade any more.

  • ServerRepository.getStatus awaits runtime.getStatusAsync(ServerName.fromExisting(name)) and keeps the old mapping (not_found, the failed-query sentinel, is STOPPED). getStatusAsync was added to IContainerRuntimePort because the synchronous getStatus (spawnSync, no timeout) blocked the API event loop once per server in findAll() (#753 review). The Docker adapter runs the pre-#665 query through execCommandAsync (docker inspect -f {{.State.Status}} -- <container>; a non-zero exit is not_found, the state is lower-cased); the only argv change is the -- of the #720 rule. A new method was simpler than making getStatus async, which is C2's change across every caller. A name that fromExisting rejects returns UNKNOWN instead of STOPPED; findByName never reaches that, because it rejects such names first.
  • WorldRepository.findAllWithServerStatus passes the container-name string it used before, including the pre-#670 branch that takes a holder starting with mc- as a container name. Changing that would be a behaviour change; it stays until the port is narrowed (#667, #641); v3.0.0 does not narrow it.

docs.title: Platform settings port (CreateServerUseCase)
docs.text:
CreateServerUseCase used Paths only to build a Config and read playitEnabled from .mcctl.json. Its fourth constructor parameter is widened to IPlatformSettingsPort | Paths. The CLI injects new Config(paths); Config satisfies the port structurally, so there is no adapter class. Passing Paths, or nothing, still reads .mcctl.json under those paths (deprecated v2 form). The change is limited to the constructor so that #675 can rebase onto it.

Why a new port: #715 adds no ports unless an issue asks, and #665 names this one. No existing port reads platform settings: IServerRepository reads per-server config.env, IPlayitAgentPort drives the agent container, IServerSpecRepository is the D5 server model. The port has one method, the one current caller needs.

docs.title: Callers still on the string form
docs.text: Caller Why Owner docker/index.ts facade wrappers Same argv as D1 (decision 9) #736 WorldRepository.findAllWithServerStatus Exact pre-#670 container name #736 GitWorldBackupAdapter list() returns container names and they go back to console.command #736 or list() returning server names PlayerManagementUseCase (options.container), WorldInfoUseCase.getLivePlayerLocations(container) The API builds mc-<name>; public signatures unchanged D2 (#667) mcctl logs for the router mc-router is not a server #641 CLI lib/rcon.ts helpers, mcctl exec, the player server prompt, migrate worlds Port calls since #668; they keep the container-name API and convert with serverOfContainer, which passes a ServerName and falls back to the string only for a name that is not a valid server container #736

docs.text:

  • PrerequisiteChecker (direct call site row 19) and the shared lint error flip.
  • ServerStatusUseCase (deprecated as a whole) and the "Connect via" message in CreateServerUseCase still read the deprecated getters (state at #665). #675 rewrote the creation path, and both getters were deleted in v3.0.0 (#736).

docs.title: Deprecated in #665 (removed in v3.0.0, #736)
docs.text:
The string (container-name) form of the server parameter of the ports above is not removed in v3.0.0; it stays until #667 and #641.

ServerName.containerName, ServerName.hostname, Server.containerName, Server.hostname, IShellPort.exec, IShellPort.execInteractive, ShellAdapter.exec, ShellAdapter.execInteractive, and passing Paths (or nothing) to CreateServerUseCase's fourth parameter.

docs.title: Backup Port (#732, S3)
docs.text:
Status: Proposed (2026-10-23). Revised after the system-architect review (APPROVE WITH CHANGES) and the Codex review (R1–R14, S1–S5), then simplified after the architect's re-review of a5d246a (S1–S5). Absorbs #653, #664, #727. The issue fixed these points, and this section does not reopen them:

  • IShellPort.backup* splits into one backup port; no new feature port.
  • RCON is used only for the flush.
  • git runs through execFile argv arrays, copies use fs.cp, and config is read through the env codec.
  • The token never appears in any argv.
  • mcctl.sh calls mcctl backup until #734.

Supported scope: a single local host. worlds/, servers/<n>/data/ and backups/ must be on one filesystem. Regular files and directories only. Anything else is refused before the first change.

docs.title: B1. Port, adapter, composition
docs.text:
File application/ports/outbound/IWorldBackupPort.ts. Every method is async and never rejects. Every failure is a result, including status (S5); unexpected exceptions map to git_failed/io_failed.

import type { BackupRetentionPolicy } from '../../../domain/index.js';

export type WorldBackupErrorCode =
  | 'not_configured' | 'locked' | 'recovery_required'   // B2, B5 step 6
  | 'runtime_unavailable' | 'servers_running' | 'flush_failed'
  | 'missing_worlds'      // B4 step 3: a world in HEAD is missing from the source (server dir still present)
  | 'unsupported_layout'  // symlink, path escape, cross-device, invalid LEVEL
  | 'restore_conflict'    // the commit's world dir for a server ≠ its current LEVEL
  | 'commit_not_found' | 'empty_source'
  | 'auth_failed' | 'repo_not_found' | 'git_too_old' | 'timeout' | 'lease_conflict'
  | 'git_failed' | 'io_failed';
export interface WorldBackupError { code: WorldBackupErrorCode; message: string; paths?: string[]; servers?: string[]; holder?: BackupLockHolder }
export type WorldBackupResult<T> = { ok: true; value: T } | { ok: false; error: WorldBackupError };
export interface BackupLockHolder { pid: number; hostname: string; bootTime: number; nonce: string; op: 'push' | 'restore' | 'prune'; startedAt: string }
export interface LockOptions { lockWaitMs?: number }   // default 0 = fail fast

export interface WorldBackupStatus {
  configured: boolean;           // token AND repo non-empty (#13)
  repository?: string; branch: string; autoOnStop: boolean;
  lastBackup?: { commit: string; date: Date };   // local cache tip (may be unpushed after a failed push)
}
export interface WorldBackupCommit { hash: string; date: Date; author: string; message: string }  // full hash
export interface PushOutcome { changed: boolean; commit?: string; flushed: string[]; skipped: string[]; warnings: string[] }

export interface IWorldBackupPort {
  status(): Promise<WorldBackupResult<WorldBackupStatus>>;
  history(limit?: number): Promise<WorldBackupResult<WorldBackupCommit[]>>;   // newest first, default 20; [] without a cache
  push(options?: { message?: string; allowMissing?: boolean } & LockOptions): Promise<WorldBackupResult<PushOutcome>>;
  restore(commit: string, options?: LockOptions): Promise<WorldBackupResult<{ commit: string; previousDir: string; skipped: string[] }>>;
  prune(policy: BackupRetentionPolicy, options?: LockOptions): Promise<WorldBackupResult<{ removed: number; warnings: string[] }>>;
  testConnection(credentials: { token: string; repository: string }): Promise<WorldBackupResult<void>>;  // no .env, no lock
}
Item Decision Adapter infrastructure/adapters/GitWorldBackupAdapter.ts, new GitWorldBackupAdapter({ root, runtime: IContainerRuntimePort, environment: IRuntimeEnvironmentPort, console: IServerConsolePort, remoteBase? = 'https://github.com/' }). Private helpers (not exported): infrastructure/backup/lock.ts, git.ts (runner and env), restore-slots.ts (swap and slots), support.ts. The adapter may import domain types (BackupRetentionPolicy, the world-name validator) Policy location (B-Q1) Lock, flush and running checks live in the adapter. Every caller routes through it, and the injected ports make it testable with fakes. No later split is promised (S1) Config <root>/.env through parseEnvDocument on every call, falling back to process.env for keys the file lacks. The API no longer reads a stale process.env after backup init Names Ports take container names (mc-<server>, D1). Results report server names. One private serverNameOf()/containerNameOf() pair does the conversion, and D4 moves it CLI root Container.worldBackupPort (built from the Docker adapters); backupUseCase = new BackupUseCase(promptPort, worldBackupPort) API root routes/backup.ts and routes/backup-schedule.ts each build one instance (runtime env: () => childProcessEnv()). BackupSchedulerService takes the port instead of mcctlRoot and loses its git and retention code. These move to the D2 container plugin when it exists. Two instances are fine because the lock is a file BackupUseCase (K1) Parameter 2 widens to IWorldBackupPort \| IShellPort, with the guard 'backupPush' in x. An IShellPort keeps today's code path unchanged; there is no new parsing. #736 narrows the type. Prompts stay in the use case; the port never prompts Deprecated IShellPort.backupPush/Status/History/Restore and the same ShellAdapter methods get @deprecated. They are not delegated. In the PR that deletes backup.sh, they return a clear failure (code: 1, stderr: 'backup.sh was removed; use IWorldBackupPort (GitWorldBackupAdapter)'). The release policy forbids removing exports and changing signatures, not changing behaviour IServerConsolePort command(name, args, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal }). The optional signal is passed to spawn, which kills the local docker exec child on abort (R9). Killing the docker CLI does not necessarily stop rcon-cli inside the container. Backward compatible

docs.title: B2. Lock (push, restore, prune; all four callers)
docs.text:
Step Rule Path <root>/backups/.backup.lock, after mkdir -p backups. It is outside the cache tree and outside worlds/.locks Acquire Write the holder JSON (with a random nonce and bootTime = Date.now() − os.uptime()·1000) to .backup.lock.<nonce>.tmp, then link(tmp, lock) and unlink the tmp. link fails with EEXIST atomically, and the lock file is never partially written Stale Only when hostname matches and either bootTime differs by more than 60 s (the host rebooted) or process.kill(pid, 0) throws ESRCH. EPERM counts as alive. Time is never used (R3). A different host, a live pid, or unparseable content → locked with holder. The manual fix ("delete the file after checking the holder process") is in the docs Takeover rename(lock, lock.<myNonce>.stale), then read the renamed file. If its nonce equals the stale holder's, unlink it and acquire. Otherwise another contender already took over: link it back to lock and report locked Release If the lock holds our nonce and the unlink succeeds, done. Otherwise (not ours, or the unlink lost to a takeover) a late contender may have moved it aside and will put it back: delete any .stale aside copy holding our nonce (the put-back link then fails), then re-read the lock and unlink it if the put-back already happened. No polling or timing window (PR #745 review) Waiting Interactive CLI, API manual push and restore: lockWaitMs: 0 (API → 409 with the holder). push --auto (auto-on-stop) and the scheduler (push and prune): 10 min, polling every 1 s Reads status/history do not lock. During the first clone they see "no cache"

ponytail: takeover is safe for two contenders. With three contenders on one stale lock, the put-back link can fail with EEXIST after a third process acquired the lock, and then two writers exist. Upgrade path: an OS advisory lock (flock through a native binding) if this ever happens.

docs.title: B3. Git environment and token
docs.text:
• One helper builds every git child env. It starts from process.env and removes the repository-local variables (the list printed by git rev-parse --local-env-vars: GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_WORK_TREE, …) plus every GIT_CONFIG_*. User settings such as proxy and CA variables are kept. Then it adds GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, GCM_INTERACTIVE=never, LC_ALL=C, and the backup identity (GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* = Minecraft Backup <minecraft-backup@localhost>) for every commit, the README init commit included. Every git child gets GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=commit.gpgSign / false, so a user's global signing setting cannot break backup commits.
  • Network commands (ls-remote, clone, fetch, push) also get three more entries (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=4):
  • http.<remoteBase>.extraHeader= (an empty value resets the multi-valued list, R14)
  • http.<remoteBase>.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic <base64("x-access-token:"+token)>
  • credential.helper= (empty)
  • Remote normalization on each run: git config --unset-all remote.origin.pushurl (exit 5 is ignored), then git remote set-url origin <remoteBase><repo>.git. This also scrubs the token URL that backup.sh left behind.
  • Git ≥ 2.31 is required (B-Q3). The version is checked once; older git → git_too_old.
  • repository must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$. branch must pass git check-ref-format --branch <b>.
  • Errors carry git's stderr only, never the env.
  • Timeouts (replace the fixed 15 min):
Commands Limit network GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_LIMIT=1000, GIT_HTTP_LOW_SPEED_TIME=300 (abort below 1 KB/s for 5 min) every git child 4 h wall-clock cap ls-remote for testConnection 60 s

docs.title: B4. Push
docs.text:
Repository layout (old repositories hold only worlds/ and stay compatible):

README.md                    worlds/<world>/…  (mirror of <root>/worlds, without .locks)
servers/<n>/<LEVEL>/…        plus <LEVEL>_nether, <LEVEL>_the_end when present

A server has an internal world when servers/<n>/data/<LEVEL>/level.dat is a regular file. LEVEL comes from config.env (env codec) and must pass the world-name validator: no /, .. or empty value. servers/<n>, data and data/<LEVEL> must not be symlinks. A server that fails these checks is reported in skipped and never dropped silently. _template is skipped.

  1. Preconditions: config (not_configured), lock, no INCOMPLETE restore slot (recovery_required), git version and branch check.
  2. Cache <root>/backups/worlds:
  3. No .git: run ls-remote --heads origin refs/heads/<b>. Exit ≠ 0 → auth_failed/repo_not_found/git_failed; a network failure is never treated as "branch absent" (R10).
    • Branch present: clone --depth 50 --branch <b> (as today). Full history is fetched (--unshallow) only by prune and by a restore whose commit is missing (R5).
    • Branch absent: init + checkout -b <b> + README commit.
  4. .git exists: fetch origin +refs/heads/<b>:refs/remotes/origin/<b> (an explicit refspec, so a changed branch works, R10).
    • (a) origin/<b> is an ancestor of local <b> (a failed push left commits): keep local; this push sends them as a fast-forward (R11).
    • (b) Otherwise, if local^{tree} == origin^{tree} (a crash after a prune push, before update-ref): checkout -f -B <b> origin/<b> silently.
    • (c) Any other divergence: add a warning, then checkout -f -B <b> origin/<b>.
  5. Missing-world guard (R7), before any cache change:
  6. tracked = world dirs in HEAD (worlds/*, servers/*/*); source = the scan above.
  7. Any tracked − source → missing_worlds with paths and nothing changed, unless allowMissing: true. A server whose whole servers/<n>/ dir is gone counts as an intentional deletion and is excluded. A missing servers/ or an empty worlds/ still blocks.
  8. Consent comes from CLI --allow-missing and API body allowMissing. The scheduler and auto-on-stop never pass it. The scheduler's failure message names the fix (mcctl backup push --allow-missing).
  9. An empty source with an empty HEAD → empty_source.
  10. Runtime gate (K3): environment.isAvailable() false → runtime_unavailable. Then running = runtime.list({ running: true, strict: true }); a failed docker ps throws → runtime_unavailable. Without strict, D1 returns [] ("nothing running") on failure. worlds/ or servers/ being a symlink → unsupported_layout.
  11. Flush and copy:
  12. Add each server to the cleanup list before sending save-off.
  13. Send save-off, then save-all flush, each with signal: AbortSignal.timeout(60_000). A non-zero exit or an abort → flush_failed, and nothing is copied.
  14. Copy: fs.rm + fs.cp(src, dst, { recursive: true, filter }). .locks is never copied, and a symlink → unsupported_layout with no commit. worlds/ is scanned for symlinks before any RCON; internal worlds are checked by the copy filter.
  15. finally: send save-on to each server in the cleanup list, independently. If the push succeeds, a failure goes to warnings with the server name. If the flush, the copy or a later git step (commit, push) fails, the save-on failures are appended to the error message and their servers are added to servers.
  16. Commit and push:
  17. add -A. If diff --cached --quiet exits 0 → { changed: false }, which is success (#8).
  18. Otherwise commit -m <message> (default Backup: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS), then push origin <b>:refs/heads/<b> with no force.
  19. A failed push keeps the local commit; step 2 of the next run saves it as a recovery ref.

ponytail: rm + cp rewrites every file, so git re-hashes the whole tree each run. This is correct but slow on very large worlds. Size/mtime shortcuts (core.checkStat=minimal) were rejected because they can miss changes (S2).

docs.title: B5. Restore
docs.text:
1. Preconditions: lock (lockWaitMs: 0); no INCOMPLETE slot (recovery_required); delete leftover backups/.restore-* staging dirs, then worktree prune; no cache → run B4 step 2 (needs config).
  2. Commit: commit must match ^[0-9a-f]{4,40}$. fetch. rev-parse --verify <c>^{commit} gives the full OID, which every later command uses. If the commit is missing and the cache is shallow, run fetch --unshallow and retry. Otherwise → commit_not_found.
  3. Runtime gate: isAvailable() false, or the strict list fails → runtime_unavailable. Any running server → servers_running. The check covers every server, not only those using affected worlds, because the world → server map is unreliable until #670.
  4. Stage and plan, without touching live data:
  5. worktree add --detach backups/.restore-<ts> <oid>. This gives the exact tree of the commit (#3) and leaves the cache's HEAD, index and work tree alone.
  6. Validate:
    • There must be at least one restorable payload: a non-empty worlds/, or a servers/<n>/<dir>/level.dat → otherwise empty_source (R8).
    • Any symlink in staging → unsupported_layout. .locks entries in the commit are ignored.
    • The commit's main world dir for server n ≠ its current valid LEVEL → restore_conflict (R8).
    • worlds/, the target data/ dirs and backups/ on different devices → unsupported_layout. There is no copy fallback (S2).
  7. Targets:
    • worlds/ (every entry except .locks), only if the commit has worlds/. Old internal-only snapshots leave live worlds/ alone.
    • For each servers/<n>/ in the commit: data/<dir> for each dir name in the commit, plus the live <LEVEL>{,_nether,_the_end}.
    • Servers not in the commit are untouched. A server whose servers/<n>/ is gone, or whose path is a symlink, goes to skipped.
  8. Before the first rename: worlds/ and servers/ must not be links, and every live target and managed parent (worlds/, servers/<n>/, servers/<n>/data/) is checked with lstat. A link, or a device other than that of backups/, → unsupported_layout.
  9. Re-check the runtime gate (strict) immediately before the first move (K3, R1).
  10. Swap:
  11. Create the slot backups/restore-previous/<ISO-ts>/. Write the planned target list into its INCOMPLETE file once, before the first move; that is the manual recovery record.
  12. For each target, (a) rename live → slot (when it exists), then (b) rename staging → live. Completed steps are kept in memory.
  13. .locks is never moved.
  14. On failure, roll back the in-memory steps in reverse:
  15. Each (b): move live → slot/.new/…. New data is set aside, not deleted.
  16. Each (a): move slot → live.
  17. Full rollback → delete the whole slot (it only holds the parked copy of the commit, which is still in git) and return the original error. Rolled-back slots therefore never count in the rotation. Partial rollback → keep INCOMPLETE and return io_failed with the slot path. Every later push or restore then returns recovery_required until a human recovers by following the target list in INCOMPLETE (documented; no --recover command in S3).
  18. On success: remove INCOMPLETE, then rotate. Keep the 3 newest complete slots and delete older complete ones. An INCOMPLETE slot is never deleted, and nothing is deleted before the swap succeeds (K2).
  19. finally: worktree remove --force, then release the lock. A cleanup error never hides the main error: it is appended to the main error's message, and the code and slot path are kept (withCleanup).

The port never prompts (#4). mcctl backup restore <commit> confirms unless --force, and the interactive BackupUseCase.restore() is unchanged. Legacy worlds.bak.<ts> dirs are left in place, and the docs explain how to remove them (B-Q5).

Known limit (R1, B-Q7): mc-router auto-scale, or a start from the CLI or API, can launch a server between step 5 and the last rename. S3 does not stop mc-router or lock start paths. The docs say: "stop mc-router or disable auto-scale before restoring".

docs.title: B6. History, status, diff, connection test
docs.text:
• history: git log -n <limit> --format=%H%x00%aI%x00%an%x00%s%x1e. | and " in messages are safe. It returns full hashes; the API route keeps its 7-character hash field (#12).
  • status: env codec plus git log -1 --format=%H%x00%aI. configured comes from the keys, not from an exit code (#13). An unreadable .env or a git error is { ok: false }, not configured: false (S5).
  • diff: not ported. This is an explicit scope change (S4). It has no user entry point: mcctl backup has init|status|push|history|restore only (diff in cli/src/index.ts is config-snapshot diff); the API and console have no diff route; the docs do not mention it. It is reachable only by running the repository's mcctl.sh/backup.sh directly.
  • testConnection (#10): ls-remote --heads <remoteBase><repo>.git with the B3 env. Exit 0 → ok. stderr Repository not found/404 → repo_not_found; Authentication failed/401/403 → auth_failed.

docs.title: B7. Retention rewrite (#9)
docs.text:
prune(policy) replaces truncateHistory/applyRetentionPolicy. The scheduler runs it after a push. A prune failure is audited (lease conflicts separately) and does not fail the run.

  1. Preconditions: lock and config. Normalize the remote and fetch (B4 refspec) only, with no checkout. If the untouched local <b> ≠ origin/<b>, skip with a warning and touch no ref (the next push reconciles, B4 step 2). Only a missing cache runs the full B4 step 2.
  2. Full history: if rev-parse --is-shallow-repository is true, fetch --unshallow; if that fails → no prune (R5). Pin oldTip = origin/<b>.
  3. Keep set: walk rev-list --first-parent oldTip in chain order.
  4. The tip is always kept (R6, K5).
  5. Older commits are kept if they are within the newest maxCount and, separately, have author date ≥ now − maxAgeDays × 86 400 000 ms. This fixes --reverse -1 returning the newest commit.
  6. Nothing dropped → { removed: 0 }.
  7. Rebuild in the original chain order: commit-tree <c>^{tree} [-p <prev>] -m <full message>, with the original author/committer name, email and %aI/%cI dates in env. Invariant before pushing: newTip^{tree} == oldTip^{tree} (R6). No ref, index or work tree changes.
  8. Publish:
  9. push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/<b>:<oldTip> origin <newTip>:refs/heads/<b>.
  10. On success: update-ref refs/heads/<b> <newTip> <oldTip>, then delete the state file. The index stays valid because the trees are equal.
  11. Uncertain outcome (R12): on any push error or timeout, ls-remote origin refs/heads/<b>.
  12. = newTip → update-ref and success.
  13. = oldTip → failure, nothing changed.
  14. Anything else → lease_conflict.
  15. The remote is always a complete old or new history, never partial. There is no compensating force push. A crash between push and update-ref is resolved by the next push (B4 step 2, case b: equal trees).

docs.title: B8. Bug → design → proving test
docs.text:
"repo" means real git, a local bare remote (remoteBase = file://…), and a temporary <root>. Tests are grouped in five bundles (Codex): R restore failure injection, L real-process lock, H real git history, U uncertain remote outcome, I integration and transition.

# Bug Fixed by Proving test (red first) 1 copy without flush B4.4–5 fake runtime/console: save-off×n → flush×n → copy → save-on×n; save-on is sent even when flush aborts (child killed) or the copy throws; isAvailable() false → runtime_unavailable, no copy 2 restore over running servers; .locks lost B5.3, B5.5, B5.6 repo: running → refused; a server that starts after the first check is caught by the re-check; .locks byte-identical; .locks in the commit ignored 3 mixed-commit restore B5.4 repo: A {x}, B {x, y}; restore A → y absent, x = A's bytes 4 restore waits on stdin B5, B3 every git env has GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0; API restore resolves 5 no lock B2 L: two child processes, one holding → locked; dead pid → taken over; EPERM, other host, old startedAt with a live pid → locked; two contenders on one stale lock (barrier) → exactly one wins; wait then success 6 internal worlds missing B4 layout, B5.4 repo: servers/a/data/w + w_nether backed up and restored; internal-only commit restorable; old worlds/-only commit leaves them alone; LEVEL change → restore_conflict; symlinked data → skipped 7 npm install: commit without sync B1 I: root without scripts/ → push commits world content; API and scheduler have no backup.sh script lookup 8 "no changes" = failure B4.6 repo: second push → changed: false; route 200; scheduler success; prune after a no-change push works 9 unsafe retention rewrite B7 H: 60+ commits cloned shallow (assert shallow), age-only, count > 50, combined → kept trees match; tip with an old author date is kept; tree invariant holds. U: lease conflict, hook reject, timeout after remote applied → converges to new; crash before update-ref → fixed next run 10 connection test fails; token in argv B6, B3 fake git on PATH records argv/env: no token in argv, header in env, inherited GIT_DIR/GIT_CONFIG_* stripped, proxy vars kept; exit/stderr mapping; BackupUseCase init succeeds 11 token in the backup.sh URL B3 PATH wrapper over real git through clone/fetch/push: token in no argv; .git/config has no token, no stale extraHeader effect, no pushurl 12 history always empty B6 repo: messages with \| and " → exact entries, newest first; BackupUseCase maps them (PR2) 13 status labels/configured B6 .env without keys → configured: false; with keys → real values; unreadable .env → { ok: false }

Bundle R also covers the review cases: the N-th rename fails → original bytes recoverable; partial rollback → INCOMPLETE blocks the next push and restore; rotation keeps 3 slots; push R7 (one world missing → missing_worlds, remote unchanged); a deleted servers/<n>/ is not missing_worlds; R11 (failed push → the next push sends the kept commit as a fast-forward); a crash before update-ref → case (b).

docs.title: B9. Test plan and PR split
docs.text:
• Behaviour is tested with real git and a bare remote. A fake git on PATH is used only where argv and env must be observed. Characterize the kept behaviour first: cache path, default branch, README init, message format, identity, .locks exclusion.
  • PR1 (core): port, adapter, helpers, the IServerConsolePort signal option (with the Docker adapter), bundles L/H/U/R and the adapter rows of B8. Additive only; no call site changes.
  • PR2 (cli + backend):
  • The widened BackupUseCase; CLI Container; mcctl backup push --auto becomes non-interactive with a 10 min wait (today --auto is ignored); --allow-missing; restore confirmation.
  • API route (codes → 400/404/409/500, 7-character hash kept) and scheduler.
  • mcctl.sh: both auto-on-stop and cmd_backup call "${MCCTL_NODE:-node}" "$MCCTL_CLI" backup … when ShellAdapter exported those two vars (process.execPath, process.argv[1]); otherwise mcctl on PATH; otherwise a warning. After PR2 no lockless backup.sh writer is reachable from mcctl.sh (S3).
  • PR3: delete backup.sh and the unused CLI lib/shell.ts backup(); deprecated ShellAdapter.backup* return the clear failure; fix the env-file.ts comment and the EN/KO docs (restore preconditions, manual lock removal, manual recovery from an INCOMPLETE slot); test:scripts and verify:package pass. PR2 and PR3 ship in the same release.

docs.title: B10. Decisions and open questions
docs.text:
Decision (2026-10-23) B-Q1 Policy in the adapter, single port (S1) B-Q2 Widen to IWorldBackupPort \| IShellPort; narrow in #736 (K1) B-Q3 git ≥ 2.31 B-Q4 diff not ported; explicit scope change, no entry point (S4) B-Q5 Keep worlds.bak.*; document removal B-Q6 One flush failure fails the push B-Q7 Docs + isAvailable + re-check before the swap; the race is a known limit B-Q8 A stuck save-off after a crash: accept and document B-Q9 API/console stops never auto-backup; #734 owns it

Not adopted: Promise.race for RCON (an AbortSignal actually kills the child, R9); core.checkStat=minimal (can miss changes) and verbatimSymlinks (symlinks are refused); reflog expire after prune (local disk is not an acceptance criterion; auto gc handles it); stopping mc-router or locking start paths (outside S3, R1).

Settled at re-review: option names CLI --allow-missing / API allowMissing; INCOMPLETE recovery is manual in S3; the two known limits (auto-start during restore, three lock contenders) are accepted.

docs.title: Script Removal S5: mcctl.sh (#734)
docs.text:
mcctl.sh is deleted. No new port; the existing ones gained one optional parameter.

Path Before After CLI start/stop <server> ShellExecutor.mcctl → mcctl.sh IContainerRuntimePort.start/stop with a ServerName (commands/lifecycle.ts). Exit codes kept: 2 = already running (start) / not running (stop), 1 = no servers/<name>/docker-compose.yml or the runtime cannot be queried (not_found confirmed by list({ strict: true }), replacing check_docker) CLI console <server> docker exec -i mc-<name> rcon-cli the mcctl rcon session: getStatus + IServerConsolePort.getEndpoint + rcon-client over TCP (row mcctl.sh in Alignment with #715). Lines run in order; EOF closes after the last reply; the client's end ends the session (0), error exits 1 Auto-backup on stop mcctl.sh stop → mcctl backup push --auto autoBackupOnStop(backup, server) (shared): status() → configured && autoOnStop → push({ lockWaitMs: 600000 }), never allowMissing, never rejects. CLI stop <server> awaits it (warning on failure, exit 0); the API stop route runs it in the background, logs the result, and an onClose hook waits for running ones (at most AUTO_BACKUP_CLOSE_WAIT_MS, 2 min; after 90 s it aborts them through push's signal, and the adapter stops before the next save-off or copied file, sends save-on, and fails with aborted; the generated PM2 config gives mcctl-api kill_timeout API_PM2_KILL_TIMEOUT_MS, 130 s) so the adapter's save-on recovery is not cut off by shutdown (B-Q9 closed). Start, restart, stop --all and server delete (S7) do not back up createWorld SEED IShellPort.setServerConfig → mcctl.sh config IWorldAssignmentPort.assign(world, server, { seed }): one write with LEVEL (through the ServerSpec since #675, ADR-0003 §6); SEED is written even when LEVEL is unchanged. WorldManagementUseCase's shell parameter is unused (@deprecated) Stopped check checkServerStopped passed not_found not_found passes only when list({ strict: true }) succeeds, so an unreachable runtime is undetermined (fail-closed) Pre-delete stop IShellPort.stopServer DeleteServerUseCase(..., runtime?): runtime.stop when given (CLI), then delete-server.sh. Since #735 there is no separate stop: deprovision stops and removes the container with runtime.remove (S7) API new ShellAdapter({ paths }) in lib/world-use-case.ts none: the API no longer resolves <root>/scripts for world operations

IShellPort/ShellAdapter startServer, stopServer, serverStatus, setServerConfig, logs, console, status keep their v2 signatures and return mcctl.sh was removed (#734); use … without running a script (removed in #736). The API stop route keeps executeServerAction (docker compose stop); open question 2 is unchanged.

docs.title: Script Removal S7: delete-server.sh (#735)
docs.text:
mcctl delete and DELETE /api/servers/:name delete in TypeScript. No new port: three existing ports gain a method (none of them shipped in v2.33.0, so this is not breaking).

Step delete-server.sh TypeScript (DeleteServerUseCase.deprovision(name, { deleteWorld })) Plan the worlds plan_worlds, worlds_outside_server before anything specRepo.delete(name, { deleteWorld, dryRun: true }): same rules (see below). An unsafe plan rejects before the container is touched Stop and remove the container docker ps -a, compose stop + compose rm -f, or docker rm -f IContainerRuntimePort.remove(name). A failure rejects with "Nothing was deleted" Plan again (the server may write while it stops), drop the include entry, move the world, delete servers/<n> steps 2 and 4, include before the move specRepo.delete(name, { deleteWorld }): plan, drop the include entry under the servers/.compose.yml.lock lock (#675 acquireFileLock), move (rename; on EXDEV, as mv did, claim worlds/<w> with a non-recursive mkdir, copy, remove the original), then delete servers/<n>. Delete handles only the entry mcctl writes: the server's entries (paths inside servers/<n>/, ./alpha/x normalised, not alphabet/x) must be the one string <n>/docker-compose.yml. A hand-written entry for the server (long form, path group, another file, a custom compose file, the entry twice) is refused with conflict right after the delete lock, dry runs included, before the container is touched; entries of other servers are never changed. The entry goes first, as in the script: mcctl start and POST /api/servers/:name/start skip the delete queue, and docker compose up -d mc-<n> must not recreate the server while its world is copied. The move and the rm stay outside the lock, so a long copy does not make other writers fail with locked. A failed move takes the lock again and puts the entry back (the replaced text when the file is unchanged, else the string entry added unless one names it; skipped when servers/<n>/docker-compose.yml is gone); if that fails too, the error adds how to put it back by hand. The whole delete, dry runs included, holds servers/.<n>.delete.lock (acquireFileLock, no wait), so a second delete of the server from any process (CLI or API) fails with locked. A failure says the container is already gone and which worlds already moved. Files rm cannot remove are a warning with a sudo rm -rf hint (the delete succeeds and the hostname step runs) Hostname step 3, before the directory IHostnameRegistrarPort.unregister('<name>.local') after the files, best effort (a skip is a warning) Validate the compose project docker compose config after the include edit, restore the backup on failure dropped: the include edit is a YAML edit of one key (removeIncludeEntry), which keeps the file valid
  • World plan (infrastructure/adapters/server-spec/serverWorldPlan.ts, #652): data/<LEVEL>, _nether, _the_end (real folders, not symlinks) move to worlds/. Refused, changing nothing: worlds/<w> exists (conflict); dimension folders without data/<LEVEL>; a symlinked servers/<n> or data/; any other world folder in the server (level.dat, level.dat_old, region/, *.mca); a symlink whose target is inside the server (all undetermined). deleteWorld overrides these. worlds/ resolving inside the server is refused even with deleteWorld. LEVEL is read by the ADR-0002 snapshot reader (Compose semantics: quotes, inline comments, last definition), not by the script's "one plain LEVEL= line" rule; a server the reader cannot determine (invalid or interpolated LEVEL, unsupported --universe) aborts unless deleteWorld. The world-folder scan keeps a misread LEVEL from losing data: the other world is found and the delete stops.
  • Assignment release: nothing to call. The assignment is the server's LEVEL (ADR-0002 R3, R5), so it goes with servers/<n>/config.env; IWorldAssignmentPort.release (fall back to <server>) is for servers that stay.
  • No backup before the delete. remove stops the container without the auto-backup on stop (S5), so the delete does not run BACKUP_AUTO_ON_STOP: the world is kept in worlds/ (#652), and --delete-world is an explicit request to drop it.
  • unregister command shape (README sudoers, #751): sudo -n sed -i '/^[^#]*[[:space:]]<host>\([[:space:]]\|#\|$\)/d' /etc/avahi/hosts, then sudo -n systemctl restart avahi-daemon, argv without a shell. <host> is the validated hostname with [ ] \ . * ^ $ / escaped (the expression of the removed avahi_remove_host). A password (CLI --sudo-password / MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD / prompt, API request body sudoPassword) goes to sudo -S -p '' -v on stdin first and never to sed or an environment variable (#682); an empty password is none. No hosts file or no exact entry is unchanged.
  • API: DELETE /api/servers/:name takes an optional JSON body { "sudoPassword": "..." } (write-only, as in create; not a query parameter because URLs are logged). Before #735 the route ran the script without it, so the avahi entry stayed unless sudo needed no password. The 200 body gains an optional warning when the hostname was not removed. force no longer changes anything (remove stops the container). The create/delete queue (#656) is unchanged.
  • Deprecated (removed in #736): IShellPort.deleteServer, ShellAdapter.deleteServer (rejects with "delete-server.sh was removed in #735; …" and runs nothing). DeleteServerUseCase without runtime? (#734) and its new optional trailing parameter deprovision? ({ specRepo, hostnames? }) rejects with the same message.
  • Removed scripts and tests: delete-server.sh, delete-server.bats, sudo-password.bats (its cases are vitest tests of the avahi adapter), tests/fake-bin/docker, and every lib/common.sh and tests/helpers.bash helper that only delete-server.sh, mcctl.sh (S5) or their tests used. lib/common.sh keeps the naming validators that naming-rules.bats tests; platform/scripts/ has no *.sh left at its top level.

docs.title: ADR-0002: World–Server Assignment Derived from LEVEL
docs.text: Status Accepted (2026-10-23), implemented in #670 Issue #670 (Hardening A4, decision D-2), milestone M3 (#644), epic #640; includes #715 S4 (remove lock.sh) Changes ADR-0001: IWorldAssignmentPort is final Related #652 / PR #741 (delete keeps the world), #655 (A5, migrate server-internal worlds), #656 (env parser unification), #669 (A7), #732 (S3, backup adapter; strict runtime lookup), #734 (S5, remove mcctl.sh), #736 (S9, v3.0.0)

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• D-2 rules R1–R7 (see #670) were not enforced. lock.sh wrote worlds/.locks/<world>.lock only from world assign. No start path read it, create and delete never wrote or cleared it, locks went stale after 24 h, a stale lock could not be released (set -e + exit 2), and WorldRepository.getLockStatus treated an unreadable lock as "unlocked".
  • The assignment that actually matters is each server's LEVEL in servers/<n>/config.env: it decides which world directory the container opens.
  • WorldManagementUseCase read server status through ShellAdapter.serverStatus, whose argument mcctl.sh status ignores, so the check always failed and LEVEL changed while the server ran.
  • World delete, the API world reset, config snapshot restore and mcctl migrate did not check which servers use a world.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. LEVEL is the only source of truth (R5). A server's world is resolveWorldName(env) (LEVEL, then the legacy WORLD_NAME, else itzg's world). There is no other record. Deleting a server's config.env releases its world (R3).
  2. IWorldAssignmentPort stays a port (#715: no new ports, methods may be added). The v2 contract stays: getAssignment (deprecated) and listAssignments (WorldAssignment[], internal optional). #670 adds snapshot (with undetermined servers), preview, and release (the unassign method #715 asked for). Callers use snapshot with holdersOf.
  3. The rules are pure domain functions (shared/src/domain/services/worldAssignment.ts), so a future adapter (k8s, IServerSpecRepository) reuses them. The adapter only reads and writes config.env and runs checkAssign on a fresh snapshot right before it writes.
  4. Fail-closed (R7). A server is undetermined when its config.env cannot be read, its resolved world fails EXISTING_WORLD_NAME_PATTERN, the world or EXTRA_ARGS value would be interpolated by Compose, or its --universe points somewhere unsupported. While any server is undetermined, every assignment change and every world delete/reset is refused. Listings still work and show a warning.
  5. A world changes only on a stopped server. Assign, release, world new --server, config LEVEL|WORLD_NAME, PATCH level, snapshot restore and migrate refuse when the runtime status is running, paused, restarting, or created. Nothing stops a server automatically, and force never bypasses this.
  6. world release = fall back to the default world. The holding server switches to its own default world <server> (the LEVEL that create-server.sh writes). --force is accepted and ignored.
  7. worlds/.locks is ignored: never read, written, created or deleted by mcctl. mcctl init stops creating it. Users may delete it.
  8. Duplicates are reported, not fixed: mcctl world list, GET /api/worlds (assignmentWarnings), and the console worlds page. Start paths are unchanged.
  9. lock.sh and lock.bats are deleted. mcctl.sh world printed a removal message until #734 deleted mcctl.sh.
  10. world delete --force no longer deletes a world a server uses; --force only skips the prompt.
  11. Concurrent CLI/API changes: the check-then-write race is accepted (human-driven, millisecond window); findDuplicates reports the result. No mutex file.

docs.title: Assignment Model
docs.text: Case Rule Normal server Holds resolveWorldName(env). LEVEL unset means it holds world. World folders A world name covers three folders: <w>, <w>_nether, <w>_the_end (world delete removes all three). A holder covers its LEVEL and LEVEL_nether/LEVEL_the_end; two names conflict when they share a folder. holdersOf, delete, reset, listWorlds().servers and duplicate reports use this one rule, so deleting w_nether of a used w, deleting w while LEVEL=w_nether is used, and deleting w_nether_nether of a legacy LEVEL=w_nether are refused. assign rejects a name ending in _nether or _the_end (invalid_world). Legacy names WORLD_NAME is read as today and never written by the port. Existing values are checked with EXISTING_WORLD_NAME_PATTERN (no /, \, ./.., quotes, control characters), so names such as My World or world.old keep working. A new LEVEL must match WORLD_NAME_PATTERN. Interpolation Compose interpolates unquoted and double-quoted env_file values, not single-quoted ones. LEVEL=${MC_WORLD:-x} or LEVEL="$W" is undetermined; LEVEL='cash$world' is the literal name. Server-internal world (D-1) The effective EXTRA_ARGS follows the template env_file order: the server's config.env wins (even an empty value), else servers/global.env (a bare EXTRA_ARGS line takes the platform .env value, which gets the same interpolation check). --universe /worlds (with or without a trailing slash or =) means worlds/; no --universe, /data or . means the world lives in servers/<n>/data/<LEVEL> (internal: true); any other location is undetermined. An internal server reserves its name, assign/release refuse it (internal_world) until #655 migrates it, and delete/reset of worlds/<w> ignore it. Server dirs Same filter as ServerRepository.listNames: directories not starting with _ that contain config.env.

docs.title: Port and Adapter
docs.text:
// shared/src/domain/services/worldAssignment.ts  (pure, no I/O)
interface WorldAssignment { world: string; server: string; internal?: boolean } // absent = false (v2 shape)
interface WorldAssignmentSnapshot { assignments: WorldAssignment[]; undetermined: string[] }
type WorldAssignmentErrorCode = 'invalid_world' | 'server_not_found' | 'conflict' | 'undetermined'
  | 'internal_world' | 'not_assigned' | 'default_world' | 'server_running';
class WorldAssignmentError extends Error { code; servers: string[] }

holdersOf(s, world, { includeInternal = true }): string[]
checkAssign(s, world, server, { newServer = false }): WorldAssignmentError | null
planRelease(s, world): { server; fallback } | WorldAssignmentError
checkRemoval(s, world): WorldAssignmentError | null      // world delete
checkReset(s, server): WorldAssignmentError | null       // API world reset
checkProposed(s, server): WorldAssignmentError | null    // snapshot restore, migrate
findDuplicates(s): { world; servers }[]                  // groups of servers sharing a folder
formatAssignmentWarnings({ duplicates, undetermined }): string[]

// shared/src/application/ports/outbound/IWorldAssignmentPort.ts
interface IWorldAssignmentPort {
  /** @deprecated v2: holder of the world's folders or null; rejects undetermined instead of null. */
  getAssignment(world: string): Promise<string | null>;
  listAssignments(): Promise<WorldAssignment[]>;              // v2 shape: readable servers only
  snapshot(): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>;               // + undetermined; rejects only when servers/ cannot be listed
  preview(server: string, configEnv: string): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>; // writes nothing
  previewPlatformEnv(dotenv: string): Promise<WorldAssignmentSnapshot>;          // platform .env replaced; writes nothing
  assign(world: string, server: string): Promise<void>;       // checkAssign on a fresh snapshot; no-op if held
  release(world: string): Promise<{ server: string; fallback: string }>;
}
  • checkAssign order: invalid_world, undetermined, server_not_found, internal_world, conflict (another holder, internal included). newServer (create) skips the two server checks.
  • planRelease order: undetermined, not_assigned, conflict (duplicate), internal_world, default_world, then checkAssign(fallback, holder). The use case reports whether worlds/<holder> already exists (fallbackExists); a release of a world that neither exists nor is assigned is "not found".
  • checkReset order: undetermined, server_not_found, internal_world, conflict (another non-internal holder of the family).
  • Adapter: ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter(paths) reads with parseEnvDocument, writes LEVEL with applyEnvChanges + writeFileAtomic, keeping the file mode; other lines stay byte-identical. server_running is raised by use cases, not by the adapter.
  • Same parser everywhere it matters: the API reset route wipes the world planWorldReset returns, and listWorlds().servers comes from the same snapshot, so a quoted or commented LEVEL is read the same way by the check and the action. The API ConfigService display parser stays until #656.

docs.title: Compatibility (v2.x, #715)
docs.text:
• Constructors only gain optional trailing parameters: WorldManagementUseCase(…, assignments?, runtime?), CreateServerUseCase(…, modSource?, assignments?), ConfigSnapshotUseCaseImpl(…, collector, assignments?, runtime?), WorldRepository(paths?, assignments?) (default: the config.env adapter). Without the assignment port every assignment change, world delete, server create and config.env restore is refused (undetermined); without the runtime port a world change is refused.
  • IWorldManagementUseCase.assignWorldByName gains an optional { requireExisting } (default true). Results gain errorCode; WorldReleaseResult gains fallbackWorld and fallbackExists. WorldManagementUseCase adds planWorldReset and getAssignmentReport.
  • isLocked/lockedBy now mean "assigned" (WorldRepository fills World.lockTo() from one snapshot per call). findAllWithServerStatus maps a missing container to stopped, not available.
  • Deprecated, removal in #736: IWorldAssignmentPort.getAssignment; IShellPort/ShellAdapter worldAssign, worldRelease, worldList (they return a failed result naming the replacement and run no script), serverStatus; WorldRepository.getLockStatus (derived, pid undefined), WorldLockData, Paths.locks, Paths.lockFile.

docs.title: Composition roots
docs.text: Root Wiring CLI Container worldAssignmentPort and containerRuntime getters, passed to WorldRepository, WorldManagementUseCase, CreateServerUseCase and ConfigSnapshotUseCaseImpl. API No container plugin yet (D2). lib/world-use-case.ts (createWorldUseCase, worldFailure) builds the adapter and DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter; the server create route builds the adapter for checkAssign; services/config-snapshot-service.ts passes both ports. D2 moves them into its plugin.

docs.title: Enforcement Points (R1, R6, R7)
docs.text:
Entry Check mcctl create [--world W], interactive create checkAssign(snapshot, W ?? <name>, <name>, { newServer: true }) before create-server.sh. Adopting a free worlds/<name> stays allowed. API POST /api/servers Same check (replaces the listWorlds() block and its ShellAdapter). mcctl world assign, API POST /api/worlds/:name/assign assignWorldByName: checkAssign → runtime check → assignments.assign. The world must exist in worlds/. mcctl config <srv> LEVEL\|WORLD_NAME <v> Only when the effective world (LEVEL, else WORLD_NAME) changes: assignWorldByName(newWorld, srv, { requireExisting: false }). A WORLD_NAME under a set LEVEL changes nothing and is written as before. mcctl config <srv> EXTRA_ARGS <v> checkConfigChange (checkConfigEnvChange): when the proposed config.env changes the server's world or location (--universe), checkProposed and a stopped server are required. The API PATCH config has no EXTRA_ARGS field. API PATCH /api/servers/:name/config with a changed level assignWorldByName(level, name, { requireExisting: false }) before any other field is written; level is then dropped from the config update. Other fields cannot inject a LEVEL line (#726). mcctl world new --server, API POST /api/worlds with serverName Runtime check and checkAssign before creating the directory, then assignments.assign; start uses runtime.start. SEED is written with LEVEL in the same config.env write: assignments.assign(world, server, { seed }) (#734); a seed config.env cannot hold is refused before the directory is created. mcctl world release, API POST /api/worlds/:name/release planRelease → runtime check on the holder → assignments.release. mcctl world delete, API DELETE /api/worlds/:name checkRemoval: refused while a non-internal server uses one of its folders or anything is undetermined; --force/?force no longer bypasses this. API POST /api/servers/:name/world/reset planWorldReset (checkReset), and the route wipes the world it returns. Config snapshot restore (CLI, API POST …/config-snapshots/:id/restore) config.env: checkConfigEnvChange (preview + checkProposed, and a runtime check when the assignment changes, whatever force says). docker-compose.yml (parsed with js-yaml): refused when its environment sets LEVEL, WORLD_NAME or EXTRA_ARGS, when its /worlds or /data mapping or its env_file list (or order) differs from the current file, or when it cannot be parsed. API answers 409. API PUT /api/platform-settings changing or removing EXTRA_ARGS The platform value reaches servers that inherit it (bare key in servers/global.env, no own value). previewPlatformEnv + checkSnapshotChange: every server whose assignment changes must pass checkProposed and be stopped; otherwise 409 with servers. An interpolated value leaves inheritors undetermined and is refused. mcctl migrate worlds The new config.env is built first and checked with preview + checkProposed before any world data moves.
  • Runtime check: checkServerStopped(runtime, server) calls runtime.getStatus('mc-<server>') (D1 naming; D4 switches to ServerName). Known limit: in D1, not_found also means "runtime unreachable", so that case passes and a running server can be changed when Docker cannot be queried. A throw is mapped to undetermined. Follow-up: replace the call with #732's strict runtime lookup once it is merged (A7, #669).
  • Results and HTTP: results carry errorCode; API routes use worldFailure: invalid_world → 400, server_not_found or a missing world → 404, every other code → 409. Messages name the blocking servers and the next step.
  • mcctl start, API start, startAll, and mc-router auto-start are not gated: once config enforces R1, two servers can share a world only through an existing duplicate, and that is reported.

docs.title: worlds/.locks and Backup
docs.text:
• Nothing reads or writes .locks, and WorldRepository.delete no longer unlinks lock files. Existing files are harmless (listNames skips dot directories); rm -rf worlds/.locks is safe. Downgrade is harmless too: the old lock code never enforced anything.
  • Backup (#732): keep .locks in the exclude list, so it is neither backed up, restored, created, nor deleted. Restoring worlds/ does not touch servers/*/config.env, so assignments survive a restore.

docs.title: Reporting and Console
docs.text:
• mcctl world list shows assigned: a, b (or unassigned) and prints one warning per duplicate world and per undetermined server (formatAssignmentWarnings; --json output unchanged, warnings on stderr). mcctl status is unchanged (#655).
  • GET /api/worlds adds assignmentWarnings: string[] (same text). POST /api/worlds/:name/release returns fallbackWorld and fallbackExists.
  • Console: the worlds page shows assignmentWarnings in one warning Alert; WorldCard labels assigned worlds "Assigned" and shows "Assigned to N servers" for duplicates; AssignWorldDialog disables running servers. The BFF forwards the whole API response.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• lock.bats was replaced: "a different server cannot take a held lock" → R1 conflict tests (adapter, use case, API, CLI); unlock/force → release tests; stale locks → undetermined tests (no TTL).
  • Domain (worldAssignment.test.ts), adapter on temp dirs (ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter.test.ts: global.env/.env inheritance, --universe locations, interpolation, EISDIR), use cases with mock ports, API routes (worlds-assignment.test.ts, server-config.test.ts, servers-world-validation.test.ts, config-snapshots.test.ts), CLI commands (world-assignment.test.ts), console components.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + One source of truth; no TTLs, no stale locks, no lock file to back up or migrate to k8s volumes.
  • + The rules are pure functions, so a ServerSpec or k8s adapter (D5, #641) only reimplements read and write.
  • − One broken or interpolated config.env blocks all assignment changes until it is fixed (deliberate, R7).
  • − The cross-process race is accepted, not prevented. The runtime check passes when Docker cannot be queried until #732/#669.
  • − Existing duplicates keep running until the user resolves them.

docs.title: ADR-0003: ServerSpec, the Single Server Definition
docs.text: Status Accepted with changes after system-architect review (2026-10-23); implemented in PR 1 (#754), PR 2 (#754) and PR 3 (feature/675-provision) Issue #675 (Hardening D5, milestone M4 #645), includes #715 S8 (replace create-server.sh) Changes ADR-0001: IServerSpecRepository gains load/write (v2 methods kept), IHostnameRegistrarPort.register/unregister Builds on ADR-0002 (#670, LEVEL is the assignment; merged in PR #750), PR #749 (#656: env codec, atomicWriteFile, API create/delete queue), #651 (single template), #649 (names), #654 (runtime ports), #751 (avahi sudoers shape) Related #735 (S7 delete), #657 (create cleanup), #658 (progress), #736 (S9, v3.0.0), #641 (k8s), #655 (migrate worlds), #737, #726

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
• One server is defined in seven places: config.env, the server docker-compose.yml (image tag, router labels), the servers/compose.yml include list, .env (HOST_IPS), .mcctl.json, /etc/avahi/hosts, and lock files (gone since ADR-0002).
  • More than ten code paths write them (table in Write paths); four edit compose YAML with regexes (B4).
  • create-server.sh (789 lines) builds a server with cp + sed, leaves servers/<n> behind on failure (#657), and prints progress the API cannot parse (#658).
  • The k8s adapter (#641) needs one runtime-neutral definition to render manifests from (plan §12, condition 3).

docs.title: Decision Summary
docs.text:
1. servers/<n>/server.yaml is the definition. config.env, the server docker-compose.yml and the include entry are generated from it. Platform files (.env, main compose, .mcctl.json) stay out of the spec.
  2. Small typed core + env pass-through. Typed fields only for what mcctl reasons about or a renderer must translate (type, version, memory, image, world, routing). Every other config.env key lives in env unchanged, so import is lossless.
  3. Readers do not change in v2.x. Generated files are rewritten on every save, so existing readers (ServerRepository, status, API config) keep reading config.env/compose. Only writers move.
  4. Hand edits are absorbed, not lost. A header hash detects them. config.env edits and edits of spec-owned compose fields (image, mc-router.* labels) are absorbed into the spec before the next write. Any other compose difference is protected: never overwritten silently.
  5. No new port, no broken export (#715, v2.x rule). IServerSpecRepository and ServerSpec keep their v2 shape; the full type is the new ServerSpecDocument, and the new behaviour comes from added methods (load, write), as #670 did for IWorldAssignmentPort. Rendering is an infrastructure detail of the repository adapter. IHostnameRegistrarPort gains register; unregister was added with delete in #735.
  6. No lock file. Create claims the directory with mkdir; updates use an optimistic revision (sha256 of server.yaml). The in-process API queue from #749 stays.
  7. Import is lazy or explicit, never bulk. A server without server.yaml is imported in memory on its first write; mcctl migrate spec imports on request. mcctl upgrade only reports which servers are not imported yet. A server that is never imported keeps working as today.
  8. Provision replaces create-server.sh inside CreateServerUseCase, with progress events named as the API SSE already expects and all-or-nothing cleanup so a retry works.

docs.title: Resolved questions (2026-10-23)
docs.text: # Question Decision 1 Start fails after a successful create The server stays created. CLI prints the cause and exits 1. The API answers success with server.status: 'created' and a warning (SSE completed), so the console does not offer a retry that would hit "already exists". 2 Hand-edited compose Absorb spec-owned fields, protect the rest, --force overwrites after a .bak. An override file can be added later. 3 EXTRA_ARGS inherited from global.env/.env Import pins the effective value into config.env and reports it. 4 Bulk import in mcctl upgrade No. upgrade reports; import is lazy or via mcctl migrate spec. 5 Template for creates The bundled template only (#651); the API stops reading <root>/servers/_template. 6 Deviations from plan §9.2 Accepted (see §1). 7 .mcctl.json avahiEnabled: false Ignored, as the script does. 8 Sudoers shape for unregister sudo -n sed -i <expr> /etc/avahi/hosts, the README shape #751 restored (ADR-0001).

docs.title: 1. Schema
docs.text:
// shared/src/domain/server-spec/ServerSpecDocument.ts (pure, no I/O)
// ServerSpec ({ name: string }) stays the v2 export; the document extends it.
export interface ServerSpecDocument extends ServerSpec {
  specVersion: 1;
  name: string;                      // directory name, mc-<name> container
  type: string;                      // TYPE
  version?: string;                  // VERSION; absent = itzg/modpack decides
  memory?: string;                   // MEMORY
  image: string;                     // compose image, e.g. itzg/minecraft-server:java25
  world: {
    level: string;                   // LEVEL (ADR-0002 resolveWorldName)
    storage: 'universe' | 'data';    // worlds/<level> | servers/<n>/data/<level> (D-1)
  };
  routing: {
    customHostnames: string[];       // user-added mc-router hostnames
    playitDomain?: string;           // PLAYIT_DOMAIN and a router hostname
    autoScale: { up: boolean; down: boolean };
    asleepMotd?: string;             // mc-router.auto-scale-asleep-motd
    loadingMotd?: string;            // mc-router.auto-scale-loading-motd
  };
  env: Record<string, string>;       // every other config.env key, file order kept
}

specVersion: 1
name: survival
type: PAPER
version: "1.21.1"
memory: 4G
image: itzg/minecraft-server:java25
world: { level: survival, storage: universe }
routing:
  customHostnames: [mc.example.com]
  playitDomain: aa.example.com
  autoScale: { up: true, down: true }
  asleepMotd: "§e§lServer is sleeping§r\n§7Connect to wake up!"
  loadingMotd: "§a§lServer is starting...§r\n§7Please wait!"
env:
  GAMEMODE: survival
  ENABLE_RCON: "true"
  MOTD: Welcome to survival! Your adventure begins here.
  SEED: "12345"
  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: fabric-api,lithium

Validation (validateServerSpecDocument, pure). Create uses the strict value objects; import accepts what works today and reports what the strict rules reject (C1 #7: unknown TYPE and snapshot VERSION must not make a server disappear).

Field Create Import / save of an imported spec name ServerName (DNS-1123, reserved words, #649); equals the directory EXISTING_SERVER_NAME_PATTERN world.level WORLD_NAME_PATTERN, not *_nether/*_the_end (ADR-0002) EXISTING_WORLD_NAME_PATTERN type, version, memory ServerType, MC_VERSION_INPUT_PATTERN (releases, LATEST, snapshots and pre-releases, the API create rule), Memory env value rule routing.*Hostnames, playitDomain hostname rule (moved from HostnameService to domain) same env keys / values ENV_KEY_RE / assertEnvFileValue (#726), and a value the config.env writer can write (PR 3 review) ENV_KEY_RE / assertEnvFileValue
  • Managed keys cannot appear in env: TYPE, VERSION, MEMORY, LEVEL, PLAYIT_DOMAIN. env.EXTRA_ARGS is allowed but must not contain --universe (that is world.storage).
  • Strict file: unknown top-level keys and non-string scalars are rejected with the path (version: 1.21 is a float in YAML; the error says to quote it). mcctl itself writes with js-yaml dump, which quotes as needed.
  • Errors are actionable: every ServerSpecError names the server, the file and the field, and the next step (quote the value, run mcctl migrate spec <n> --force, upgrade mcctl). Saving a bare v2 { name } through save fails with invalid_spec listing the missing fields.
  • specVersion: optional fields are added without a bump. A breaking change bumps it and the repository upgrades older files in memory on read (written on the next save). A higher version is refused (unsupported_spec_version).
  • Hand edits of server.yaml are allowed. They take effect on the next mcctl write to that server or on mcctl migrate spec <n>; mcctl start does not render.
  • Secrets: no secretRefs in version 1 (no per-server secret exists; RCON and tokens stay in .env, passed through global.env). A secret a user put in config.env (e.g. CF_API_KEY) lands in env: server.yaml gets config.env's file mode, is collected by config snapshots like config.env, and is never returned by the API. #641 adds secretRefs as an optional field.
  • Deviations from plan §9.2 (accepted): world.source, modpack and whitelist are plain env keys (SEED/WORLD, MODRINTH_*/CF_*, ENABLE_WHITELIST/WHITELIST); image replaces imageTag (lossless for custom images); stopGraceSec and resources wait for A2/C3; an optimistic revision replaces the per-server lock.

docs.title: 2. Repository, Storage and Concurrency
docs.text:
// IServerSpecRepository: v2 methods unchanged, #675 adds load/write (full text in ADR-0001)
list(): Promise<ServerSpec[]>;                       // { name } per server dir with server.yaml or config.env
/** @deprecated Use load(). Removed in v3.0.0 (#736). */
get(name: string): Promise<ServerSpec | null>;       // the document, typed as the v2 ServerSpec
save(spec: ServerSpec): Promise<void>;               // = write(spec) after validating it is a document
delete(name: string, options?: DeleteServerSpecOptions): Promise<ServerSpecDeleteResult>; // #735
load(name: string): Promise<LoadedServerSpec | null>;               // { document, revision, warnings }
write(doc: ServerSpecDocument, options?: WriteServerSpecOptions): Promise<void>; // { expectedRevision?, create?, force?, allowStorageChange? }
  • File: servers/<n>/server.yaml, fixed key order, written with atomicWriteFile (#749).
  • Create: mkdir servers/<n> (not recursive) is the claim; EEXIST → already_exists. Works across CLI and API processes.
  • Update: load returns revision = sha256 of the bytes it read. write compares it when it starts and again right before its first write, after every awaited check (host addresses, import, world snapshot); the generated files it planned against are re-read at the same point. A mismatch is conflict and nothing is written. updateServerSpec(repo, name, mutate) (application helper) retries once with a fresh load. ponytail: the remaining window is the temp-file write and fsync of atomicWriteFile (milliseconds); add a per-server lock only if lost updates are ever observed.
  • World guard (R1, R7): when the rendered LEVEL or storage differs from the current config.env, write runs ADR-0002's pure checkProposed on a snapshot with the rendered config.env. It uses the same snapshot reader as IWorldAssignmentPort.preview directly, not the port, because the assignment adapter itself writes through this repository. A storage change is refused (storage_change) unless allowStorageChange is set, which only mcctl migrate worlds does. The same write also refuses a server that is not stopped (checkServerStopped with the runtime the adapter is built with; no runtime or an unreadable state is undetermined), so a hand edit of world.level rendered by mcctl migrate spec cannot bypass ADR-0002 decision 5. Use cases keep their own stop checks.
  • Write order: server.yaml first, then the generated files. A crash in between leaves generated files with a valid hash but an old spec= (§3), which the next write or mcctl migrate spec re-renders, completing the interrupted write.

docs.title: 3. Rendering
docs.text:
Seam (infrastructure, not a port):

// shared/src/infrastructure/adapters/server-spec/ServerSpecRenderer.ts
export interface RenderContext {
  root: string; templatesDir: string; hostIps: string[];
  read(path: string): string | undefined;   // current file content
}
export interface RenderedFile { path: string; content: string; guarded: boolean }
export interface ServerSpecRenderer {
  render(doc: ServerSpecDocument, ctx: RenderContext): RenderedFile[];
}

FileServerSpecRepository (the IServerSpecRepository adapter) takes a renderer in its constructor. Application code never calls a renderer, so it is not a port. DockerComposeRenderer is implemented now. KubernetesManifestRenderer (StatefulSet, Service, PVC from world.storage) is only this interface until #641, which adds the renderer plus whatever storing the spec and applying manifests need in a k8s repository adapter; ADR-0001's apply(spec) is not needed. Removal (#735) drops the generated include entry <n>/docker-compose.yml with removeIncludeEntry (and include: itself when no entry is left) before moving its world, refusing a hand-written entry for the server, and deletes servers/<n> after; see ADR-0001 S7.

Docker outputs

File How Guarded config.env applyEnvChanges(current ?? bundled _template/config.env, diff, { raw: true }): set keys whose value differs, remove keys the spec lacks. Untouched lines (comments, quoted values) stay byte-identical. yes docker-compose.yml Bundled _template/docker-compose.yml loaded with js-yaml; service key and container_name → mc-<n>, image, router labels set; dump. yes servers/compose.yml js-yaml load, add <n>/docker-compose.yml if no entry equals it, keep all other entries (long form - path: too), dump with a static header. The whole read-merge-write runs under servers/.compose.yml.lock (acquireFileLock, shared with the backup lock: link-based, a holder that provably died on this host is taken over, about 10 s wait, then locked), because CLI and API processes add servers to the same file. Inside the lock the file is read fresh, written, read back and checked for every entry it had plus the new one; retry once on mismatch. A file that fails to load is never overwritten: the write stops with an error before anything is written. no (merge) data/, logs/, servers/global.env mkdir -p; copy global.env from the template if missing (as the script does). —
  • Env projection: TYPE, VERSION (omitted when absent, VERSION= when ''), MEMORY, LEVEL, PLAYIT_DOMAIN, EXTRA_ARGS, then env. EXTRA_ARGS = --universe /worlds/ plus env.EXTRA_ARGS for universe; env.EXTRA_ARGS ?? '' for data (an empty value still overrides global.env, ADR-0002).
  • Router hosts: <n>.local, <n>.<ip>.nip.io for each hostIps, playitDomain, customHostnames (deduplicated, in this order). This one generator replaces build_hostnames, init.ts buildHostnames/mergeHostnames, and the system part of HostnameService (B4).
  • Host IPs (resolveHostIps, shared infrastructure, the script's order): .env HOST_IPS, else HOST_IP (comma list), read with the env codec; else the src address of ip route get 1; else the first address of hostname -I; else (macOS) the first non-internal IPv4 from os.networkInterfaces(). Addresses on docker0, br-*, veth* are skipped in every probe. Avahi gets the first address.
  • Header (first line of guarded files): # Generated by mcctl from server.yaml; edits are detected (ADR-0003). mcctl:sha256=<64 hex> spec=<12 hex> sha256 hashes the rest of the file; spec is the prefix of the server.yaml revision it was rendered from. No other state file.
  • Idempotent: rendering twice gives the same bytes; an unchanged spec means no writes (no mtime churn, no needless container recreation).
  • Who does what (PR 2): the renderer returns file bodies and reads bodies through ctx.read; the repository adds and checks the header, so the renderer never sees it. Every check (revision, storage, edit detection, an unreadable servers/compose.yml) runs before the first write.
