A write that fails part way puts back every file it already changed (a new file is removed) before the error is thrown, but only while the file still holds what it wrote: a file another writer changed meanwhile (e.g. during the include lock wait) is left and named. server.yaml, the definition, is put back only when every generated file was; otherwise it keeps the new spec, so what is left is all earlier content or the new spec with some new generated files, and mcctl migrate spec renders the new spec again. The files it could not put back are on the error (unrestoredFiles(error)); mcctl migrate worlds then places the world where the spec mcctl migrate spec would render (load()) puts it (new: it stays in worlds/; earlier: moved back; otherwise left, with what to check) and says to run mcctl migrate spec before the next start, or, when that spec and server.yaml disagree on the storage (which mcctl migrate spec refuses), to remove server.yaml and run mcctl migrate worlds again (PR 3 review). FileServerSpecRepository.loadFile(name) (adapter only, not the port) reads server.yaml without absorbing; mcctl migrate spec --force uses it to re-render from server.yaml. With server.yaml present, compose environment entries are not spec-owned: they count as edits outside the spec (import still moves them, §4).

Edit detection (on load):

config.env Meaning Action hash ok, spec= current in sync — hash ok, spec= old server.yaml edited by hand, or an interrupted write next write renders it hash bad or no header, spec= current or none config.env edited (or never rendered) absorb into the spec (as import, step 1) hash bad, spec= old both edited edit_conflict; mcctl migrate spec <n> --force re-renders from server.yaml after writing config.env.bak docker-compose.yml Action hash ok overwrite freely (also picks up template changes from a newer mcctl) hash bad or no header 1. absorb spec-owned fields (image, mc-router.* labels) into the spec, as import step 4; 2. normalize known legacy variants (env_file ../../.env #685, missing loading-MOTD label); 3. compare the rest semantically with render(spec). Equal → overwrite. Different → protected: a write that would change the rendered compose fails with compose_edited and the differing YAML paths, other writes leave the file untouched, --force overwrites after docker-compose.yml.bak.

docs.title: 4. Import of Existing Installs
docs.text:
importDockerServer(name, ctx) (infrastructure, next to the renderer):

  1. config.env via parseEnvDocument: TYPE, VERSION, MEMORY, PLAYIT_DOMAIN → typed fields; an empty VERSION, MEMORY or PLAYIT_DOMAIN stays '', so the rendered KEY= keeps overriding global.env (PR 3 review). world.level = resolveWorldName(env) (LEVEL, else legacy WORLD_NAME, else world; WORLD_NAME stays in env). Every other key → env in file order (unknown keys preserved).
  2. Storage from the effective EXTRA_ARGS, with ADR-0002's resolution reused (config.env wins even when empty, else global.env, whose bare key takes the .env value): --universe /worlds[/] → universe; no --universe, /data or . → data. The --universe token is stripped and the rest goes to env.EXTRA_ARGS (pinned, reported when it came from global.env). The directories are only cross-checked (warning when worlds/<level> is missing but servers/<n>/data/<level> exists).
  3. Fail-closed (R7 style): an interpolated managed value (${...} unquoted or double-quoted) or another --universe location is undetermined: the import is refused for that server, it keeps running, and writes to it fail with the reason until the file is fixed.
  4. Compose: one service mc-<n> expected. image and router labels → routing; hostnames are classified as system (<n>.local, <n>.<IPv4>.nip.io, the playit domain) or custom. environment entries other than EULA move to env; Compose gives environment precedence over env_file, so on a key clash the compose value wins and the clash is reported. ${...} in a spec-owned field or a moved environment entry → undetermined; elsewhere → protected. $$ is Compose's literal $ and is read as $; the renderer writes every $ it puts in the compose as $$, and the config.env writer single-quotes a value with $, refusing one that ends with \ (Compose reads \' as an escaped quote; PR 3 review). The semantic comparison of §3 runs on the compose with the moved and absorbed items removed.
  5. Report per server (imported | refused; a protected compose is a warning) with warnings: pinned EXTRA_ARGS, environment clashes, stale nip.io hosts re-derived from the current HOST_IPS, values the strict create rules would reject.

When it runs

  • Lazy: load imports in memory when server.yaml is missing; the first write saves it. Reads never write.
  • mcctl migrate spec [<name>|--all] [--dry-run] [--force]: import or absorb, render, print the report. Idempotent. Same command family as migrate worlds.
  • mcctl upgrade: prints which servers have no server.yaml yet (and the migrate spec --dry-run findings); it writes nothing.
  • Never imported (v2.x): works exactly as today, because readers still read the files. A server directory copied in by hand is adopted on its first write.

docs.title: 5. Provision (replaces create-server.sh)
docs.text:
CreateServerUseCase gains one optional trailing constructor parameter provision?: ServerProvisionDeps ({ specRepo, hostnames?, runtime?, hostIps? }, after #670's assignments?; one object keeps the constructor change small next to #665) and executeWithConfig(config, options?: CreateServerRunOptions) ({ onProgress?, onLog? }). Without it, since the script is deleted, that path and ShellAdapter.createServer fail with a clear error instead of ENOENT: create-server.sh was removed in #675; pass specRepo / use ServerSpec provision. Both execute (interactive) and executeWithConfig use the same flow; the API route calls the use case instead of spawning the script.

# create-server.sh TS provision Progress 0 parse flags, validate names, world exclusivity, env values, modpack slug buildCreateSpec(input) (pure; the repository adds the bundled template's other config.env keys under the document's values on create, so the use case needs no template) + validation (parseCreateServerConfig, pure: an input the value objects refuse, or a spec the create rules refuse, such as a seed config.env cannot hold, is invalid_spec; the API runs it before it opens the SSE stream, so JSON and SSE both answer 400); #670 checkAssign(..., { newServer: true }) (reads the assignment snapshot). No writes before this passes. initializing (API) 1–4 cp -RL _template, sed compose and config.env, add include, docker compose config --quiet, restore .bak on failure one call, specRepo.write(doc, { create: true }): mkdir claim, server.yaml, render, include entry (read back, §3). docker compose config is dropped: the files are generated by js-yaml, and start reports a broken project. creating 5 avahi <n>.local → first IP, best effort hostnames.register('<n>.local', hostIps[0]); a skip is a warning configuring 6 docker compose up -d mc-<n> unless --no-start, sleep 2, ps runtime.start('mc-<n>') unless autoStart === false; no sleep starting
  • Events: onProgress(stage, message) uses the statuses the API server-create SSE event and the console CreateServerStatus already define (creating, configuring, starting); onLog(line) becomes server-create-log. The API sends initializing first and completed/error from the result, never from stderr text (#658: a server named error-test succeeds). A client disconnect stops events, not provisioning (today it kills the script mid-way).
  • Start failure (decision 1): CLI exit 1 with the cause and mcctl start <n>; API 201/SSE completed with server.status: 'created' and warning. PR 3 checks how the console's CreateServerStatus handling shows that warning (a warning dialog). JSON POST /api/servers (no follow) waits for the container start at most createTimeoutMs (120 s) once the files are written; past that it gives the same answer with a warning that the start goes on in the background, and the create/delete queue moves on with the reply. SSE and the CLI keep the 30-minute start limit.
  • Cleanup (#657): write({ create: true }) is all-or-nothing. On any failure after the claim it removes the include entry it added and the directory it created, then rethrows, so the same create can be retried at once. It never touches worlds/ (itzg creates the world on first start). Hostname registration is best effort as today. A process killed mid-create can leave servers/<n>; mcctl delete <n> removes it (ponytail: no marker file).
  • Avahi adapter runs the commands the README.md sudoers lines allow, as argv without a shell: sudo -n tee -a /etc/avahi/hosts (stdin <ip> <host>), then sudo -n systemctl restart avahi-daemon. The sudo password is an adapter option, not an environment variable: the CLI passes --sudo-password, MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD, or what promptSudoPasswordIfNeeded asked for (mcctl prompts, not sudo); the API passes the request's sudoPassword. With a password, sudo -S -p '' -v reads it on stdin first and the command never sees it (#682). Without one, sudo -n relies on NOPASSWD or cached credentials and a failure becomes a warning. Exact-match check (#660), IPv4 check, avahi presence via getStatus.

Option parity (every flag the CLI and API pass today)

Script CLI / API ServerSpec <name> name name -t (default PAPER); bare PAPER positional --type / type type; the positional form is dropped (no caller) -v --version / version version; modpack type without version → no VERSION (a given LATEST is written), otherwise the template default -m --memory / memory memory (closes #737 if still open) -s, -u (exclusive with -w) --seed, --world-url / seed, worldUrl env.SEED, env.WORLD -w --world / worldName world.level; missing world: warning (CLI), 400 (API), as today --modpack same / modpack MODRINTH: env.MODRINTH_MODPACK; AUTO_CURSEFORGE: env.CF_SLUG --modpack-version same / modpackVersion env.MODRINTH_VERSION / env.CF_VERSION --mod-loader same / modLoader env.MODRINTH_LOADER / env.CF_LOADER --exclude-files same / excludeFiles env.MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES / env.CF_EXCLUDE_MODS --whitelist P, --enable-whitelist, --no-whitelist (wins) CLI only env.ENABLE_WHITELIST=TRUE (+ WHITELIST); template whitelist lines dropped --playit-domain D CLI only routing.playitDomain. Intended difference: the script added D to the router hosts only when a host IP was found; TS always adds it. --start — no-op (default) --no-start --no-start / autoStart: false skip start MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD --sudo-password / sudoPassword avahi adapter option defaults MOTD=Welcome to <n>!…, LEVEL=<n> — env.MOTD, world.level

bats → vitest: get_host_ip ×4 → resolveHostIps; register_avahi_hostname ×5 → avahi adapter with fake sudo/avahi-daemon on PATH (as docker-shell-injection.test.ts); create writes dir/config/include, seed/modpack-version rejection, text seed → provision tests on a temp root (plus "retry after failure succeeds"); "aborts when compose config fails" → "aborts and writes nothing when servers/compose.yml fails to load"; symlinked _template → "the renderer never writes templatesDir"; whitelist ×3 → render tests with the bundled template and a legacy one with ENABLE_WHITELIST=TRUE. sudo-password.bats stayed until #735, which moved its cases to the avahi adapter tests and removed it with delete-server.sh.

docs.title: 6. Write Paths
docs.text:
All in PR 3. Every writer goes through updateServerSpec(repo, name, mutate). setEnvKey(doc, key, value) maps managed keys to typed fields, so the generic config writers need no key list.

Writer today Writes PR 3 CLI config, whitelist, op (ShellExecutor.writeConfigValue) any config.env key setEnvKey (LEVEL/WORLD_NAME keep #670's assign path) API PATCH config (ConfigService), PlayerFileService.writeConfigEnv, ModConfigService; CLI mod config.env keys setEnvKey setServerPlayitDomain (CLI and API playit) PLAYIT_DOMAIN + host label routing.playitDomain; body delegates, @deprecated API HostnameService.update host label (regex) routing.customHostnames CLI init --reconfigure (new HOST_IP) every host label (regex) re-render every server, no spec change CLI update image tag, loading-MOTD label doc.image; the label comes from the template CLI upgrade server-env-migration env_file repoint kept until #736: servers that were never imported still need it (decision 4) ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter.assign/release (#670) LEVEL world.level through the repository WorldManagementUseCase → shell.setServerConfig (SEED, LEVEL); since #734 assign(world, server, { seed }) config.env env.SEED in the same write as world.level (row above) mcctl migrate worlds (#655) EXTRA_ARGS, LEVEL world.storage = 'universe' with allowStorageChange config snapshot restore config.env, compose restore server.yaml and render when the snapshot has it (add it to KNOWN_CONFIG_FILES); older snapshots: write the files, then absorb create-server.sh / delete-server.sh everything provision (§5) / #735 via repo.delete

Out of scope: platform files (main compose and its playit service, .env, ecosystem.config.js, .mcctl.json).

One source of truth with #670. server.yaml is the only thing writers change; LEVEL in config.env is its projection. ADR-0002's adapter keeps reading config.env, which is right: it is exactly what the container uses, including a hand edit not yet absorbed. Its writes go through the repository, so assign/release never write config.env directly. The pure rules in worldAssignment.ts do not change, and world.storage === 'data' is ADR-0002's internal: true.

docs.title: 7. Stages
docs.text:
PR Content Behaviour change 1 schema + import ServerSpecDocument, validation; IServerSpecRepository.load/write on server.yaml only (revision check, no rendering yet) and the v2 list/get/save; the importer, which reads world storage through the same effectiveExtraArgs.ts rules as the #670 assignment adapter; mcctl migrate spec (dry run, or write server.yaml only) none: only migrate spec writes, and nothing reads server.yaml yet 2 renderer + write ServerSpecRenderer, DockerComposeRenderer, header and edit detection, write renders (force with .bak, storage guard, the R1/R7 world guard with the stopped check, include read-back), mcctl migrate spec renders only migrate spec writes 3 write paths (#715 S8) golden outputs of today's create-server.sh for each option combination (captured in its bats harness before it is deleted) as the parity oracle; buildCreateSpec; write({ create: true }) (claim, rollback, data/, logs/, global.env); the mcctl upgrade report; IHostnameRegistrarPort.register + avahi adapter; provision; CLI and API create (SSE events, start-failure warning, console check); every writer in §6; delete create-server.sh and its 3 bats files; @deprecated on IShellPort.createServer, ShellAdapter.createServer, Server.toCliArgs, WorldOptions.toCliArgs, setServerPlayitDomain, replaceRouterHosts, IServerSpecRepository.get; the shell create path fails with the clear "removed in #675" error; a test that fails when code outside the repository adapter writes config.env or a server compose (allow-list: server-env-migration); docs EN/KO; test:scripts and verify:package pass. May split into 3a (create) and 3b (other writers). yes

All eight acceptance criteria of #675 are met by PR 3, so #675 closes after PR 3. The former stage 4 ("end of old-format support") is folded into PR 3 as the write guard test and the docs: from PR 3 on, no code path writes the old way except server-env-migration. Servers without server.yaml stay supported through lazy import (also how a hand-copied server is adopted). Deferred to #736 (v3.0.0): removing the @deprecated exports above, IShellPort/ShellAdapter, and server-env-migration. No ServerSpec behaviour changes in v3.0.0.

Order: PR 1–2 after #749 (#656) merges; PR 3 after #670 (merged in PR #750); #735 follows PR 3. A server whose server.yaml was written by PR 1's migrate spec and whose config.env was later changed by a v2 writer has no header, so PR 2 absorbs the config.env change on the next load (§3).

PR 3 notes (as built):

  • The rendered server compose quotes every string, because the v2 label readers (parseRouterHosts, HostnameService) match mc-router.host: "...".
  • Every writer of §6 goes through updateServerSpec/setEnvKeys except: setServerPlayitDomain (deprecated v2 export, no longer called by mcctl), server-env-migration (until #736) and config snapshot restore, which writes a consistent set: snapshots and mcctl server-backup now include server.yaml, and a pre-#675 set without it is absorbed on the next load. The write-guard test lists each exception with its reason.
  • ConfigEnvWorldAssignmentAdapter takes the repository in its constructor; without one that has a runtime, a LEVEL change is refused (R7). A new world's SEED goes in the same write: WorldManagementUseCase passes it to assign (#734).
  • The CLI and API build their repositories through small factories (serverSpecRepositories, serverProvision) that tests replace; no test runs docker, sudo or the real platform root.
  • Provisioning starts the server with a 30-minute docker compose up timeout (DockerComposeRuntimeAdapter startTimeoutMs): the first start can pull the image, and the script had no timeout.
  • A modpack type without a version writes no VERSION (the CLI used to pass LATEST); an explicit LATEST is written. Snapshot and pre-release versions the API accepts are written as given.

docs.title: 8. Tests (TDD, failing test first in each PR)
docs.text:
• v2 compatibility: a type test written against the v2 contract still compiles (const s: ServerSpec = { name: 'a' }; repo.list(), repo.get(n), repo.save(s), repo.delete(n) with v2 types) and the package root still exports ServerSpec and IServerSpecRepository; save({ name }) fails with invalid_spec naming the missing fields.
  • Domain: validation tables (create vs import rules, managed keys in env, --universe in env.EXTRA_ARGS, non-string scalars, specVersion), buildCreateSpec for every row of the parity table, host generator.
  • Import on temp roots: template-created server, legacy template variants, quoted/commented/duplicate keys, WORLD_NAME, global.env/.env inheritance and every --universe form (shared fixtures with ADR-0002), interpolation → refused, compose environment → env with a clash report, ${...} in compose, hand-edited compose image/labels absorbed, other compose edits protected; report text.
  • Render: idempotent bytes, unchanged spec means no writes, comment preservation, header hash, both edit-detection tables, include add/remove by exact name with long-form entries kept, read-back retry, unloadable servers/compose.yml left untouched, atomicWriteFile failure leaves old files.
  • Repository: revision conflict + one retry, create claim against an existing directory, rollback on render/include failure followed by a successful retry, world guard (conflict from checkProposed, storage_change without the option).
  • Host IPs: .env precedence and trimming; ip route get 1 → hostname -I → interfaces order with fake binaries; docker0/br-* skipped.
  • Provision and API: golden parity (parsed config.env and compose equal to the PR 3 fixtures except the header, explicit LEVEL, EXTRA_ARGS and the playit host); event order; --no-start; SSE creating → configuring → starting → completed, start failure → completed + status: 'created' + warning, error with the cause, name containing error; avahi argv exactly as the sudoers lines, password only on -S -v, never in the child environment.
  • Removed script: CreateServerUseCase built without specRepo and ShellAdapter.createServer reject with the "create-server.sh was removed in #675" message, not ENOENT.
  • Writers: one test per row of §6 through the spec; #670's assignment tests keep passing with the repository-backed writes.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• + One definition per server; compose files become output, so the k8s work (#641) adds a renderer instead of editing call sites.
  • + Host generation, env writing and YAML editing each have one implementation; no regex edits YAML.
  • + Create cleans up after itself, reports real progress, and works without bash.
  • + v2 consumers of IServerSpecRepository/ServerSpec keep compiling.
  • − Comments are lost in rendered compose files (header explains) and in servers/compose.yml.
  • − A compose edit outside the spec-owned fields blocks compose-changing writes for that server until the user reverts it or forces a re-render.
  • − Two derived states (header hash, revision) must stay correct; the edit-detection tables are the test contract.
  • − Until v3.0.0 the repository carries the v2 get/save alongside load/write.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Welcome to Docker Minecraft Server Management Platform. This guide will help you set up and manage multiple Minecraft servers using Docker.

docs.title: What is mcctl?
docs.text:
mcctl is a command-line tool for managing Docker-based Minecraft servers. It provides:

  • Easy server creation - Create Paper, Forge, Fabric, or Vanilla servers with a single command
  • Multi-server routing - Run multiple servers on a single machine with hostname-based routing
  • Auto-scaling - Servers automatically start when players connect and stop when idle
  • World management - Assign worlds to servers (one world, one server) and release them
  • GitHub backup - Automatic backup of world data to a private GitHub repository

docs.title: Hostname-based Routing with nip.io
docs.text:
Connect to any server using magic DNS - no client configuration required:

myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565

nip.io automatically resolves the hostname to your server's IP address.

docs.title: Interactive CLI
docs.text:
mcctl provides both interactive and CLI modes:

Interactive ModeCLI Mode 
mcctl create
# Prompts for server name, type, version, etc.

mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

docs.title: Zero-downtime Server Management
docs.text:
• Servers start automatically when players connect
  • Servers stop after configurable idle timeout
  • Only mc-router runs when all servers are idle

docs.title: Complete Server Lifecycle
docs.text:
# Start mc-router (once, after mcctl init)
mcctl router start

# Create a server
mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Configure the server
mcctl config myserver DIFFICULTY hard
mcctl config myserver MAX_PLAYERS 50
mcctl config myserver USE_AIKAR_FLAGS true

# Manage players
mcctl op myserver add Steve
mcctl whitelist myserver add Steve

# Monitor and control
mcctl status myserver
mcctl logs myserver -f
mcctl console myserver

# Backup and restore
mcctl backup push -m "Before upgrade"
mcctl backup restore

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide walks you through installing mcctl and setting up the required dependencies.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
Component Minimum Version Recommended Notes Node.js >= 18.0.0 20 LTS Required for mcctl CLI Docker Engine >= 24.0.0 Latest Container runtime Docker Compose >= 2.20.0 Latest include feature required OS Linux, macOS Ubuntu 22.04+ Windows via WSL2 git >= 2.31 Latest Only for GitHub world backups PM2 >= 6.0.0 Latest Only for the web console: mcctl console init needs pm2 on PATH (npm install -g pm2)

Docker Compose Version

Docker Compose v2.20.0 or higher is required. The include directive used by mcctl was introduced in this version. Check your version with docker compose version.

mcctl init checks Node.js, Docker Engine and Docker Compose and stops if one is missing or too old.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Before installing mcctl, ensure you have the following installed:

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Docker is required to run Minecraft servers. Install Docker Engine:

Ubuntu/DebianCentOS/RHELmacOS 
# Add Docker's official GPG key
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install ca-certificates curl
sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

# Add the repository
echo \
  "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
  $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

# Install Docker
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-compose-plugin

# Add your user to docker group
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
newgrp docker

sudo dnf install -y dnf-plugins-core
sudo dnf config-manager --add-repo https://download.docker.com/linux/centos/docker-ce.repo
sudo dnf install docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-compose-plugin
sudo systemctl enable --now docker
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

Download and install Docker Desktop for Mac.

Verify Docker installation:

docker --version
# Docker version 24.0.0 or higher

docker compose version
# Docker Compose version v2.20.0 or higher

docs.title: Node.js
docs.text:
Node.js 18 or higher is required:

Using nvm (Recommended)Ubuntu/DebianmacOS (Homebrew) 
# Install nvm
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.0/install.sh | bash
source ~/.bashrc

# Install Node.js 20 LTS
nvm install 20
nvm use 20

curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | sudo -E bash -
sudo apt-get install -y nodejs

brew install node@20

Verify Node.js installation:

node --version
# v20.0.0 or higher

npm --version
# v10.0.0 or higher

docs.title: Global Installation (Recommended)
docs.text:
Install mcctl globally via npm:

npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl

Or using pnpm:

pnpm add -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl

mcctl update reinstalls the CLI with npm install -g, so it does not update a pnpm global install. Prefer npm.

Verify installation:

mcctl --version
# mcctl version 3.0.2 (or newer)

docs.title: Using npx (No Installation)
docs.text:
You can also run mcctl without installing:

npx @minecraft-docker/mcctl --help

docs.title: Platform Initialization
docs.text:
After installing mcctl, initialize the platform:

mcctl init

This creates the platform directory structure at ~/minecraft-servers/:

~/minecraft-servers/
├── docker-compose.yml     # Main orchestration (mc-router, server includes)
├── .env                   # Platform settings (HOST_IP, RCON_PASSWORD, ...)
├── .mcctl.json            # mcctl settings (template version, playit, install ID)
├── .gitignore             # Keeps .env, servers, worlds and backups out of git
├── servers/               # Server configurations
│   ├── compose.yml        # Server include list
│   ├── global.env         # .env keys passed to every server
│   └── _template/         # Server template
├── worlds/                # Shared world storage
├── shared/
│   ├── plugins/           # Mounted read-only into every server (/plugins)
│   └── mods/              # Created, but not mounted by the server template
└── backups/               # Backup storage

mcctl init also asks which host IP address(es) to use for nip.io hostnames and whether to enable playit.gg, and creates the Docker network minecraft-net.

Custom Data Directory

Use --root to specify a custom location: 

mcctl --root /path/to/data init

Pass --root to every later command as well, or set MCCTL_ROOT (for example export MCCTL_ROOT=/path/to/data in your shell profile). Otherwise mcctl uses ~/minecraft-servers.

docs.title: Start mc-router
docs.text:
mcctl init does not start mc-router, the router that accepts connections on port 25565. Start it once:

mcctl router start

mc-router has restart: unless-stopped, so Docker starts it again after a reboot until you stop it (mcctl router stop). Creating or starting a server starts only that server. mcctl up starts mc-router and every server.

docs.title: Optional: mDNS Setup
docs.text:
For local network discovery using .local hostnames, install avahi-daemon:

Ubuntu/DebianCentOS/RHELmacOS 
sudo apt install avahi-daemon
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

sudo dnf install avahi
sudo systemctl enable --now avahi-daemon

macOS has built-in Bonjour support - no additional installation needed.

sudo for .local names

mcctl create registers <server>.local in /etc/avahi/hosts with sudo. When that file exists, it asks for your sudo password (or takes --sudo-password / MCCTL_SUDO_PASSWORD); press Enter to try sudo without a password (sudoers NOPASSWD). See Register Hostnames.

nip.io Recommended

nip.io magic DNS is recommended over mDNS as it works without any client configuration. See Networking Guide for details.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit the environment file to customize settings:

nano ~/minecraft-servers/.env

Key settings:

# Your server's IP address (required for nip.io)
HOST_IP=192.168.1.100

# For VPN mesh with multiple IPs (Tailscale/ZeroTier)
# HOST_IPS=192.168.1.100,100.64.0.5

# Timezone
TZ=Asia/Seoul

# RCON password (generated randomly by `mcctl init`; recreate containers after changing it)
RCON_PASSWORD=<random, generated by mcctl init>

docs.title: Verifying Installation
docs.text:
After mcctl router start, run the status command to verify everything is working:

mcctl status

Expected output (no servers yet):

=== Server Status (mc-router Managed) ===

INFRASTRUCTURE
SERVICE              STATUS       HEALTH     PORT/INFO
-------              ------       ------     ---------
mc-router            running      healthy    :25565 (hostname routing)
avahi-daemon         running      (system)   mDNS broadcast

MINECRAFT SERVERS
SERVER               STATUS       HEALTH     HOSTNAME
------               ------       ------     --------
  No Minecraft servers configured

Without avahi-daemon, its row shows not installed.

docs.title: Docker Permission Denied
docs.text:
If you get a permission error:

# Add your user to the docker group
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Apply the group change
newgrp docker

docs.title: Port 25565 Already in Use
docs.text:
Check if another process is using port 25565:

sudo lsof -i :25565

Stop the conflicting service or change the port in docker-compose.yml.

docs.title: mcctl Command Not Found
docs.text:
Ensure npm global bin is in your PATH:

# For npm
export PATH="$PATH:$(npm config get prefix)/bin"

# Add to ~/.bashrc for persistence
echo 'export PATH="$PATH:$(npm config get prefix)/bin"' >> ~/.bashrc

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Create your first Minecraft server in 5 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure you have completed the installation steps:

  • [x] Docker installed and running
  • [x] Node.js 18+ installed
  • [x] mcctl installed (npm install -g @minecraft-docker/mcctl)
  • [x] Platform initialized (mcctl init)
  • [x] mc-router started (mcctl router start)

Start mc-router once

mcctl init does not start mc-router, and creating a server starts only that server. Run mcctl router start once; Docker starts mc-router again after a reboot until you stop it. mcctl up starts mc-router and every server.

docs.title: Interactive Mode (Recommended for Beginners)
docs.text:
Run the create command without arguments for guided setup:

mcctl create

You will be prompted for:

  1. Server name - A unique name (e.g., survival, creative)
  2. Server type - Paper, Vanilla, Forge, Fabric, etc.
  3. Minecraft version - e.g., 1.21.1, 1.20.4 (modpack types ask for the modpack instead)
  4. World - A new world, a new world with a seed, an existing world from worlds/, or a world ZIP URL
  5. Memory allocation - Default is 4GB (6GB for modpacks)
  6. Whitelist - Off by default; if you turn it on, you can add players
  7. playit.gg domain - Only when playit.gg is enabled

When /etc/avahi/hosts exists (avahi-daemon is installed), mcctl first asks for your sudo password to register <name>.local (press Enter to try sudo without a password).

docs.title: CLI Mode (For Automation)
docs.text:
Create a server with a single command:

mcctl create myserver -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

Options:

Option Description Default -t, --type Server type (PAPER, VANILLA, FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC) PAPER -v, --version Minecraft version Latest -s, --seed World seed Random --no-start Create without starting Start automatically --whitelist, --enable-whitelist Turn on the whitelist (with the listed players, or empty) Off

docs.title: Step 2: Wait for Server to Start
docs.text:
The server will download and start automatically. Watch the logs:

mcctl logs myserver -f

Wait until you see:

[Server thread/INFO]: Done (X.XXXs)! For help, type "help"

First Start Takes Longer

The first start downloads Minecraft server files and generates the world. Subsequent starts are much faster.

docs.title: Find Your Server Address
docs.text:
The create command prints only Connect via: myserver.local:25565. mcctl status lists every address of the server in the HOSTNAME column:

mcctl status

MINECRAFT SERVERS
SERVER               STATUS       HEALTH     HOSTNAME
------               ------       ------     --------
myserver             running      healthy    myserver.local,myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io

docs.title: Connect from Minecraft
docs.text:
1. Open Minecraft Java Edition
  2. Click Multiplayer > Add Server
  3. Enter the server address: myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565
  4. Click Done and join!

Connection Methods

nip.io (Recommended)mDNS

Works from networks that can reach 192.168.1.100, usually your LAN (a VPN address in HOST_IPS gets its own hostname): 

myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565

Works on local network (requires avahi/Bonjour): 

myserver.local:25565

A bare IP (192.168.1.100:25565) does not work: mc-router picks the server by the hostname the client sends. To let players join from the internet, see External Access.

docs.title: View Server Status
docs.text:
mcctl status

Output:

=== Server Status (mc-router Managed) ===

INFRASTRUCTURE
SERVICE              STATUS       HEALTH     PORT/INFO
-------              ------       ------     ---------
mc-router            running      healthy    :25565 (hostname routing)
avahi-daemon         running      (system)   mDNS broadcast

MINECRAFT SERVERS
SERVER               STATUS       HEALTH     HOSTNAME
------               ------       ------     --------
myserver             running      healthy    myserver.local,myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io

For type, version, memory and players, use mcctl status myserver (or mcctl status --detail for every server):

=== Server: myserver ===

  myserver
    Container: mc-myserver
    Status:    running (healthy)
    Hostname:  myserver.local,myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io
    Type:      PAPER
    Version:   1.21.1
    Memory:    4G
    Uptime:    5m
    Resources: 1.2 GB / 15.5 GB (7.7%) | CPU: 3.1%
    Players:   0/20 - none

docs.title: View Server Logs
docs.text:
mcctl logs myserver

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl logs myserver -f

docs.title: Stop the Server
docs.text: mcctl stop myserver

docs.title: Start the Server
docs.text:
mcctl start myserver

Auto-Start on Connect

With mc-router, stopped servers automatically start when a player attempts to connect. This needs the server's container: a server created with --no-start, or every server after mcctl down (which removes the containers), starts on connect only after you run mcctl start <name> (or mcctl up) once.

docs.title: Access Server Console (RCON)
docs.text:
mcctl console myserver

This opens an interactive RCON session (the server must be running):

> list
There are 0 of a max of 20 players online:
> help

Type exit or quit, or press Ctrl+C or Ctrl+D to leave.

Docker Desktop (macOS)

mcctl console connects over TCP to the container's IP address on the Docker network, which Docker Desktop may not expose to the host. Use mcctl exec myserver <command> there.

docs.title: Example: Create Multiple Servers
docs.text:
Create additional servers for different game modes:

# Creative server with specific seed
mcctl create creative -t VANILLA -v 1.21.1 -s 12345

# Modded server with Forge
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.4

# Check all servers
mcctl status

Each server gets its own hostname:

  • creative.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565
  • modded.192.168.1.100.nip.io:25565

docs.title: Keeping mcctl Updated
docs.text: mcctl update updates the CLI and the installed services (mcctl-api, mcctl-console and the shared library) from npm.

docs.title: Check for Updates
docs.text: mcctl update --check   # exits 1 when a CLI update is available

docs.title: Update mcctl
docs.text:
# Interactive (prompts for confirmation)
mcctl update

# Auto-confirm (useful for CI/CD)
mcctl update --yes

# Update only the CLI
mcctl update --cli-only

mcctl update also checks each server's image tag against its VERSION, pulls the server images, and in a terminal offers to recreate stopped servers that still use an old image (default No). It does not run mcctl upgrade: run mcctl upgrade next to refresh .env, servers/_template and the router. The Upgrade Runbook has the full procedure.

Automatic Update Checks

Before each command (except --help and --version), mcctl checks npm for a newer version. The result is cached for 24 hours in ~/.mcctl-update-check.json; when the cache is older, the command waits for the check (at most about 2 seconds). If a newer version exists, mcctl prints a notice.

For the full update command reference, see mcctl update.

docs.title: Server Won't Start
docs.text:
1. Check logs for errors: 

    mcctl logs <server> -n 100

  2. Check Java version compatibility:

  3. Minecraft 26.x and LATEST require Java 25
  4. Minecraft 1.20.5–1.21.x requires Java 21
  5. Minecraft 1.17–1.20.4 requires Java 17
  6. Minecraft 1.16.5 and older requires Java 8

docs.title: Can't Connect to Server
docs.text:
1. Verify mc-router is running: 

    mcctl status
# mc-router should show "running" and "healthy"
mcctl router start   # if it is not running

  2. Check server hostname: 

    mcctl status <server>
# Note the hostname (e.g., myserver.192.168.1.100.nip.io)

  3. Ensure server is running: 

    mcctl start <server>

docs.title: Server Crashes
docs.text:
1. Check memory allocation: 

    mcctl config <server> MEMORY
# Increase if needed: mcctl config <server> MEMORY 6G

  2. Check for mod conflicts: 

    mcctl logs <server> | grep -i "error\|exception"

docs.title: Permission Denied Errors
docs.text:
# Fix file ownership (if needed)
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER ~/minecraft-servers/

For more detailed troubleshooting, see the itzg/minecraft-server documentation.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: A guide for building Minecraft servers using Docker.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The itzg/minecraft-server image allows you to easily run a Minecraft Java Edition server in a Docker container.

docs.title: Docker CLI
docs.text:
docker run -d -it --name mc \
  -p 25565:25565 \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
    volumes:
      - ./minecraft-data:/data

docs.title: Required Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description Required EULA Minecraft EULA agreement (must set TRUE) Required

docs.title: Basic Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description TYPE VANILLA Server type VERSION LATEST Minecraft version MEMORY 1G JVM heap memory TZ UTC Timezone

docs.title: Default Ports
docs.text: Port Purpose 25565 Minecraft server (TCP) 25575 RCON (TCP) 19132 Bedrock compatible (UDP, when using GeyserMC)

docs.title: Data Persistence
docs.text:
To persist server data, you must mount the /data volume:

docker run -d -it --name mc \
  -p 25565:25565 \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  -v /path/to/minecraft-data:/data \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: View Server Logs
docs.text: docker logs -f mc

docs.title: Access Server Console
docs.text:
When RCON is enabled (default):

docker exec -i mc rcon-cli

docs.title: Stop Server
docs.text: docker stop mc

docs.title: Data Directory
docs.text: Guide to the /data directory structure and volume management inside the container.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
All server data is stored under the /data path in the container. This path is declared as a Docker volume, so an anonymous volume is created if not explicitly configured.

Warning: Anonymous volumes may result in data loss when the container is deleted.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
/data
├── server.jar          # Server executable
├── server.properties   # Server configuration
├── ops.json           # Operator list
├── whitelist.json     # Whitelist
├── banned-players.json
├── banned-ips.json
├── world/             # Default world
├── world_nether/      # Nether world
├── world_the_end/     # End world
├── plugins/           # Plugins (Paper/Spigot)
├── mods/              # Mods (Forge/Fabric)
├── config/            # Mod configurations
└── logs/              # Server logs

docs.title: Host Directory Bind
docs.text:
docker run -d \
  -v /home/user/minecraft-data:/data \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    volumes:
      - ./minecraft-data:/data
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"

docs.title: Named Volume
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    volumes:
      - mc-data:/data
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"

volumes:
  mc-data:

docs.title: SELinux / Podman Environments
docs.text:
In environments using SELinux or AppArmor, add the :Z option:

docker run -d \
  -v /home/user/minecraft-data:/data:Z \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: Converting Anonymous Volume to Named Volume
docs.text:
Method to migrate data from an existing anonymous volume to a named volume:

# 1. Stop existing container
docker stop mc

# 2. Find anonymous volume location
docker inspect -f "{{json .Mounts}}" mc | jq

# 3. Create new named volume and copy data
docker volume create mc-data
docker run --rm \
  -v OLD_VOLUME_PATH:/source:ro \
  -v mc-data:/dest \
  alpine cp -a /source/. /dest/

# 4. Run new container
docker run -d \
  -v mc-data:/data \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: Permission-Related Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description UID 1000 User ID inside container GID 1000 Group ID inside container SKIP_CHOWN_DATA false Skip /data ownership change

docs.title: Resolving Permission Issues
docs.text:
If permission issues occur between host and container:

environment:
  UID: 1000
  GID: 1000

Or to skip ownership changes:

environment:
  SKIP_CHOWN_DATA: "true"

docs.title: Optional Mount Points
docs.text:
You can mount specific directories separately:

Path Purpose /plugins Plugin files /mods Mod files /config Mod configuration files 
volumes:
  - ./data:/data
  - ./plugins:/plugins:ro  # Read-only
  - ./mods:/mods:ro

docs.title: Environment Variables Reference
docs.text: Complete list of environment variables available in Docker Minecraft Server.

docs.title: General Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Description EULA - Minecraft EULA agreement (Required: TRUE) TYPE VANILLA Server type VERSION LATEST Minecraft version (LATEST, SNAPSHOT, legacy such as 1.21.11-rc1, or new version numbering such as 26.1, 26.1-snapshot-1, 26.1-pre-1, 26.1-rc-1) TZ UTC Timezone (e.g., America/New_York) UID 1000 Container user ID GID 1000 Container group ID

docs.title: Server Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Description MOTD - Server message DIFFICULTY easy Difficulty (peaceful, easy, normal, hard) MODE survival Game mode (survival, creative, adventure, spectator) MAX_PLAYERS 20 Maximum player count HARDCORE false Enable hardcore mode (true/false). Maps to the hardcore server property PVP true Enable PvP LEVEL world World save folder name SEED - World seed VIEW_DISTANCE - View distance SIMULATION_DISTANCE - Simulation distance

docs.title: Memory Settings
docs.text:
Variable Default Description MEMORY 1G Initial/max heap memory INIT_MEMORY - Initial heap size (separate setting) MAX_MEMORY - Maximum heap size (separate setting)

Format: <size>[g|G|m|M|k|K] or percentage <size>%

docs.title: Whitelist
docs.text: Variable Description ENABLE_WHITELIST Enable whitelist (true/false) WHITELIST Player list (comma separated) WHITELIST_FILE Whitelist file path/URL

docs.title: Operators (OPs)
docs.text: Variable Description OPS Operator list (comma separated) OPS_FILE Operator file path/URL

docs.title: RCON
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_RCON true Enable RCON RCON_PASSWORD - RCON password RCON_PASSWORD_FILE - RCON password file (Docker Secrets) RCON_PORT 25575 RCON port

docs.title: Resource Pack
docs.text: Variable Description RESOURCE_PACK Resource pack URL RESOURCE_PACK_SHA1 Checksum RESOURCE_PACK_ENFORCE Enforce on clients (TRUE/FALSE)

docs.title: Server Icon
docs.text: Variable Description ICON Server icon URL or path (64x64 PNG)

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Variable Default Description LOG_LEVEL info Log level LOG_TIMESTAMP false Add timestamp GENERATE_LOG4J2_CONFIG false Generate log4j2 config ROLLING_LOG_FILE_PATTERN - Rolling log file pattern ROLLING_LOG_MAX_FILES 1000 Maximum log file count

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: Variable Default Description SERVER_HOST localhost Monitoring host SERVER_PORT 25565 Monitoring port DISABLE_HEALTHCHECK false Disable healthcheck

docs.title: Proxy
docs.text: Variable Description PROXY HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL PROXY_HOST Proxy host PROXY_PORT Proxy port PROXY_NON_PROXY_HOSTS Proxy exclusion hosts

docs.title: Custom Server
docs.text: Variable Description CUSTOM_SERVER Custom server JAR URL/path EXTRA_ARGS Additional arguments to pass to server JAR

docs.title: Server Control
docs.text: Variable Default Description STOP_SERVER_ANNOUNCE_DELAY - Stop announcement delay (seconds) STOP_DURATION 60 Graceful stop wait time (seconds) STOP_SERVER_DELAY_COMMAND - Full command to run at the start of the stop announce delay, in place of the default announcement (added 2026.6.1; trailing-"s" bug fixed in 2026.8.2) FORCE_REDOWNLOAD false Force re-download server files SETUP_ONLY false Setup only, then exit PRE_START_SCRIPT - Path to an executable (mounted into the container) run after setup and just before the server starts. Runs directly, not through a shell, as the server user from the server's working directory. If it exits non-zero, the server is not started (added 2026.9.2) SERVER_RUNNER - Replace the default mc-server-runner exec. Value is expanded on exec, so the runner can be wrapped by a mounted executable (added 2026.7.2) CLEAN_SERVER_LIBRARIES true Remove stale server libraries during installation for supported server types; set false to disable

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text: Variable Description DEBUG Verbose log output DEBUG_EXEC Show server start command DEBUG_MEMORY Memory allocation debugging

docs.title: JVM Optimization Flags
docs.text: Variable Description USE_AIKAR_FLAGS Aikar's GC tuning flags USE_MEOWICE_FLAGS MeowIce updated flags USE_MEOWICE_GRAALVM_FLAGS GraalVM optimization USE_FLARE_FLAGS Flare profiling USE_SIMD_FLAGS SIMD optimization

docs.title: OpenJ9 Specific
docs.text: Variable Description TUNE_VIRTUALIZED Virtualized environment optimization TUNE_NURSERY_SIZES Nursery size settings

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
Variable Default Description PREFER_IPV6 false Set true to prefer IPv6 addresses and stack. Sets java.net.preferIPv6Addresses and java.net.preferIPv6Stack for mc-image-helper and the Minecraft server (added 2026.7.2)

Note: The variable name is PREFER_IPV6 (upper-case V6), as used in the image scripts and official docs.

docs.title: Miscellaneous
docs.text: Variable Description CONSOLE Set FALSE for noconsole option GUI Set FALSE to disable GUI SKIP_CHOWN_DATA Skip /data ownership change OVERRIDE_ICON Set TRUE to override an already-set server icon (default FALSE) BROADCAST_RCON_TO_OPS Sets the broadcast-rcon-to-ops server property (default false)

docs.title: Loading Environment Variables from Files
docs.text:
Added in 2026.5.3. Values loaded this way override values passed via docker run -e or compose environment:.

Variable Description LOAD_ENV_FROM_FILE Container path or URL of a shell-style env file (KEY=VALUE per line; comments and blank lines allowed) LOAD_ENV_FROM_ARCHIVE Container path or URL of a zip/tar archive containing an env file LOAD_ENV_FROM_ARCHIVE_ENTRY Relative path of the env file inside the archive (default .env) LOAD_ENV_FROM_GENERIC_PACK When true, probe each GENERIC_PACKS entry for a top-level .env and source it

Load order: generic packs, then LOAD_ENV_FROM_FILE, then LOAD_ENV_FROM_ARCHIVE (later overrides earlier).

docs.title: Server Properties
docs.text: How to manage server.properties file through environment variables.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
All server.properties entries can be set via environment variables. Variable names are converted to uppercase with - replaced by _.

Example: max-players → MAX_PLAYERS

docs.title: Basic Settings
docs.text: Variable Default Description MOTD - Server message (supports formatting codes, \n for multiline) DIFFICULTY easy peaceful, easy, normal, hard MODE survival survival, creative, adventure, spectator SEED - World seed (wrap negative numbers in quotes) LEVEL world World save folder name MAX_PLAYERS 20 Maximum player count PVP true Enable PvP

docs.title: View and Performance
docs.text: Variable Description VIEW_DISTANCE Server view distance (chunks) SIMULATION_DISTANCE Simulation distance (chunks) MAX_TICK_TIME Max tick time (-1 to disable watchdog)

docs.title: World Generation
docs.text: Variable Description LEVEL_TYPE World type (default, flat, largeBiomes, amplified) GENERATOR_SETTINGS JSON format generator settings GENERATE_STRUCTURES Generate structures (true/false) SPAWN_ANIMALS Spawn animals SPAWN_MONSTERS Spawn monsters SPAWN_NPCS Spawn NPCs

docs.title: Player Management
docs.text: Variable Description WHITELIST Whitelisted players (comma/newline separated) WHITELIST_FILE Whitelist file path/URL OPS Operator players (comma/newline separated) OPS_FILE Operator file path/URL ENABLE_WHITELIST Enable whitelist ENFORCE_WHITELIST Enforce whitelist

docs.title: RCON
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_RCON true Enable RCON RCON_PASSWORD - RCON password (required) RCON_PASSWORD_FILE - For Docker Secrets RCON_PORT 25575 RCON port

docs.title: Resource Pack
docs.text: Variable Description RESOURCE_PACK Resource pack download URL RESOURCE_PACK_SHA1 Resource pack checksum RESOURCE_PACK_ENFORCE Enforce on clients RESOURCE_PACK_PROMPT Resource pack prompt message

docs.title: Server Icon
docs.text:
environment:
  ICON: "https://example.com/icon.png"

64x64 PNG image URL or container path

docs.title: Datapacks
docs.text: Variable Description INITIAL_ENABLED_PACKS Initially enabled datapacks INITIAL_DISABLED_PACKS Initially disabled datapacks

docs.title: Custom Properties
docs.text:
Set multiple properties at once with CUSTOM_SERVER_PROPERTIES:

environment:
  CUSTOM_SERVER_PROPERTIES: |
    allow-flight=true
    spawn-protection=0
    enable-command-block=true

docs.title: Disable Automatic Management
docs.text: Setting OVERRIDE_SERVER_PROPERTIES=false disables automatic server.properties management via environment variables.

docs.title: Placeholders
docs.text:
Placeholders can be used in configuration files:

Format Description %VAR% Environment variable value %env:VAR% Environment variable value (explicit) %date:FMT% Date format

docs.title: User API Provider
docs.text: Variable Default Description USER_API_PROVIDER playerdb playerdb or mojang

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
environment:
  DUMP_SERVER_PROPERTIES: "true"  # Output settings at startup

docs.title: Example: Complete Server Configuration
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "PAPER"
      VERSION: "1.20.4"

      # Server info
      MOTD: "Welcome to My Server!\nEnjoy!"
      ICON: "https://example.com/icon.png"

      # Game settings
      DIFFICULTY: "normal"
      MODE: "survival"
      PVP: "true"
      MAX_PLAYERS: "50"
      VIEW_DISTANCE: "12"

      # World
      LEVEL: "world"
      SEED: "12345"

      # Security
      ENABLE_WHITELIST: "true"
      WHITELIST: "player1,player2"
      OPS: "admin1"

      # RCON
      RCON_PASSWORD: "secure_password"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"

docs.title: JVM Options
docs.text: Java Virtual Machine memory and performance optimization settings.

docs.title: Basic Memory Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description MEMORY 1G Set initial/max heap memory together INIT_MEMORY - Initial heap size (separate setting) MAX_MEMORY - Maximum heap size (separate setting)

docs.title: Format
docs.text:
• Absolute value: <size>[g|G|m|M|k|K]
  • Examples: 2G, 2048M, 2048m
  • Percentage: <size>%
  • Example: 75% (75% of container memory)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Single value
environment:
  MEMORY: "4G"

# Separate initial/max
environment:
  INIT_MEMORY: "2G"
  MAX_MEMORY: "4G"

# Percentage of container memory
environment:
  MEMORY: "75%"

docs.title: Passing JVM Options
docs.text: Variable Purpose JVM_OPTS General JVM options (space separated) JVM_XX_OPTS -XX options only JVM_DD_OPTS System properties (name=value comma separated)

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
environment:
  JVM_OPTS: "-Dfoo=bar -Xms512M"
  JVM_XX_OPTS: "-XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200"
  JVM_DD_OPTS: "foo=bar,baz=qux"

docs.title: Aikar Flags
docs.text:
Recommended GC tuning flags for Paper/Spigot servers:

environment:
  USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"

Applied options include: - G1GC garbage collector - GC pause time optimization - Improved heap memory management

docs.title: MeowIce Flags
docs.text:
Updated version of Aikar flags:

environment:
  USE_MEOWICE_FLAGS: "true"

docs.title: GraalVM Optimization
docs.text:
When using GraalVM JVM:

environment:
  USE_MEOWICE_GRAALVM_FLAGS: "true"

docs.title: Flare Profiling
docs.text:
Performance profiling support:

environment:
  USE_FLARE_FLAGS: "true"

docs.title: SIMD Optimization
docs.text:
Vector operation optimization:

environment:
  USE_SIMD_FLAGS: "true"

docs.title: JMX Remote Monitoring
docs.text:
Remote profiling through JMX (Java Management Extensions):

Variable Default Description ENABLE_JMX false Enable JMX JMX_HOST - JMX bind host JMX_PORT 7091 JMX port 
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      ENABLE_JMX: "true"
      JMX_HOST: "0.0.0.0"
      JMX_PORT: "7091"
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
      - "7091:7091"

docs.title: OpenJ9 Specific Options
docs.text:
When using IBM OpenJ9 JVM:

Variable Description TUNE_VIRTUALIZED Virtualized environment optimization (TRUE) TUNE_NURSERY_SIZES Automatic nursery size setting (TRUE) 
environment:
  TUNE_VIRTUALIZED: "TRUE"
  TUNE_NURSERY_SIZES: "TRUE"

docs.title: Memory Debugging
docs.text:
Diagnose memory allocation issues:

environment:
  DEBUG_MEMORY: "true"

docs.title: Small Server (1-10 players)
docs.text:
environment:
  MEMORY: "2G"
  USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"

docs.title: Medium Server (10-30 players)
docs.text:
environment:
  MEMORY: "4G"
  USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
  VIEW_DISTANCE: "10"

docs.title: Large Server (30+ players)
docs.text:
environment:
  INIT_MEMORY: "4G"
  MAX_MEMORY: "8G"
  USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
  VIEW_DISTANCE: "8"
  SIMULATION_DISTANCE: "6"

docs.title: Modpack Server
docs.text:
environment:
  MEMORY: "6G"
  USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
  JVM_XX_OPTS: "-XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions -XX:G1NewSizePercent=40"

docs.title: Server Types and Platforms
docs.text: Various Minecraft server types and modpack platform configurations.

docs.title: Server Type Overview
docs.text:
Select server type with the TYPE environment variable:

environment:
  TYPE: "PAPER"  # Specify server type

docs.title: Vanilla
docs.text:
Official Mojang server:

environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "VANILLA"  # Default, can be omitted
  VERSION: "1.20.4"

docs.title: Paper
docs.text:
High-performance Spigot fork with plugin support:

Variable Description TYPE PAPER PAPER_BUILD Specific build number PAPER_CHANNEL experimental - Experimental builds PAPER_DOWNLOAD_URL Custom download URL 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "PAPER"
  VERSION: "1.20.4"

docs.title: Paper-based Alternative Servers
docs.text: Type Description PURPUR Paper fork with additional features PUFFERFISH Performance optimized fork FOLIA Multi-threaded support LEAF Performance optimized lightweight fork

docs.title: Leaf
docs.text:
Performance-optimized Paper fork focused on lightweight server operation:

Variable Description TYPE LEAF LEAF_BUILD Specific build number 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "LEAF"
  VERSION: "1.21.1"

docs.title: Folia
docs.text:
Multi-threaded Paper fork for large-scale servers:

Variable Description TYPE FOLIA FOLIA_CHANNEL experimental or default FOLIA_DOWNLOAD_URL Custom download URL 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "FOLIA"
  VERSION: "1.20.4"
  FOLIA_CHANNEL: "experimental"

docs.title: Configuration Repositories
docs.text:
Automatically download optimized configuration files from Git repositories:

Variable Server Type Description PAPER_CONFIG_REPO PAPER Paper optimized config repository URL PUFFERFISH_CONFIG_REPO PUFFERFISH Pufferfish config repository URL PURPUR_CONFIG_REPO PURPUR Purpur config repository URL SERVER_PROPERTIES_REPO_URL ALL Base server.properties repository (Smart Mode / Direct Mode) 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "PAPER"
  PAPER_CONFIG_REPO: "https://github.com/example/paper-configs.git"

docs.title: Forge
docs.text:
Mod support server:

Variable Description TYPE FORGE FORGE_VERSION Forge version (latest or version number) FORGE_INSTALLER Local installer path FORGE_INSTALLER_URL Installer download URL (also used for Cleanroom server) FORGE_FORCE_REINSTALL Force reinstall (true) 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "FORGE"
  VERSION: "1.20.1"
  FORGE_VERSION: "latest"

Tip: Cleanroom is an alternative Forge-compatible server that can be installed by providing a custom installer URL via FORGE_INSTALLER_URL.

docs.title: NeoForge
docs.text:
Community fork of Forge:

Variable Description TYPE NEOFORGE NEOFORGE_VERSION latest, beta, or specific version number 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "NEOFORGE"
  VERSION: "1.20.4"
  NEOFORGE_VERSION: "latest"  # also supports "beta"
  • NEOFORGE_VERSION can be a specific version, latest, or beta. By default the latest non-beta NeoForge version available for the requested Minecraft version is used.
  • Specific version example: -e TYPE=NEOFORGE -e VERSION=1.20.1 -e NEOFORGE_VERSION=47.1.79

docs.title: Fabric
docs.text:
Lightweight mod loader:

Variable Description TYPE FABRIC FABRIC_LAUNCHER_VERSION Launcher version FABRIC_LOADER_VERSION Loader version FABRIC_LAUNCHER Custom launcher path FABRIC_LAUNCHER_URL Custom launcher URL FABRIC_META_BASE_URL Custom Fabric meta API base URL (for mirrors) FABRIC_FORCE_REINSTALL Force reinstall 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "FABRIC"
  VERSION: "1.20.4"

docs.title: Installing Fabric API
docs.text:
Most mods require Fabric API:

environment:
  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: "fabric-api"

docs.title: Quilt
docs.text:
Fabric-compatible mod loader:

Variable Description TYPE QUILT QUILT_LOADER_VERSION Loader version QUILT_INSTALLER_VERSION Installer version 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "QUILT"
  VERSION: "1.20.4"

docs.title: Bukkit / Spigot
docs.text:
Plugin support servers (Paper recommended):

environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "SPIGOT"  # or BUKKIT
  VERSION: "1.20.4"

Note: Bukkit/Spigot auto-download can be unstable. Paper is recommended.

docs.title: Hybrid Servers
docs.text: Support both mods and plugins:

docs.title: Mohist
docs.text:
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "MOHIST"
  VERSION: "1.20.1"

docs.title: Magma Maintained
docs.text:
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "MAGMA_MAINTAINED"
  VERSION: "1.20.1"
  FORGE_VERSION: "47.2.0"

docs.title: Arclight
docs.text:
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "ARCLIGHT"
  ARCLIGHT_TYPE: "FORGE"  # FORGE, NEOFORGE, FABRIC
  VERSION: "1.20.1"

docs.title: Ketting
docs.text:
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "KETTING"
  VERSION: "1.20.1"

docs.title: Auto CurseForge
docs.text:
Automatic CurseForge modpack installation:

Variable Description TYPE / MODPACK_PLATFORM AUTO_CURSEFORGE CF_API_KEY CurseForge API key. Built into the image on Java 17+ (since 2026.7.1); you may still supply your own. Required on java8 and other pre-Java 17 tags CF_API_KEY_FILE Path to a file in the container containing the API key (e.g., Docker secret) CF_FILENAME_MATCHER Substring, or regex surrounded by /, to select a modpack file by filename CF_IGNORE_MISSING_FILES Comma/newline-delimited list or glob of files to ignore when detecting missing files (avoids reinstall) CF_PARALLEL_DOWNLOADS Parallel mod downloads (default 4) CF_OVERRIDES_SKIP_EXISTING Skip overrides files that already exist in /data (default false; world data is always skipped) CF_FORCE_REINSTALL_MODLOADER Force reinstall of the modpack's mod loader (default false) REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS Clear old configs before modpack install (see Mods and Plugins) CF_PAGE_URL Modpack page URL CF_SLUG Modpack slug CF_FILE_ID Specific file ID CF_EXCLUDE_MODS Mods to exclude CF_FORCE_INCLUDE_MODS Force include mods 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "AUTO_CURSEFORGE"
  CF_API_KEY: "${CF_API_KEY}"  # optional on Java 17+ images (built-in key); required on java8
  CF_SLUG: "all-the-mods-9"

Note: Since 2026.7.1 the image includes a CurseForge API key on Java 17 and newer. The java8 image (and other pre-Java 17 tags) does not; set CF_API_KEY yourself or install the pack on a Java 17+ image first.

docs.title: Modrinth Modpacks
docs.text:
Variable Description TYPE / MODPACK_PLATFORM MODRINTH MODRINTH_MODPACK Modpack slug/ID/URL MODRINTH_VERSION Specific version MODRINTH_LOADER Mod loader (forge, fabric, quilt) 
environment:
  EULA: "TRUE"
  TYPE: "MODRINTH"

docs.title: Java Versions
docs.text: A guide to Java requirements by Minecraft version and image tag selection.

docs.title: Supported Java Versions
docs.text:
Image Tag Java Version Base OS Architecture Notes latest, stable Java 25 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, riscv64 Default; stable points to most recent release java25 Java 25 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, riscv64 java25-alpine Java 25 Alpine amd64, arm64 java25-jdk Java 25 Ubuntu+JDK amd64, arm64 Full JDK included java21 Java 21 Ubuntu amd64, arm64 java21-jdk Java 21 Ubuntu+JDK amd64, arm64 Full JDK included java21-alpine Java 21 Alpine amd64, arm64 java25-graalvm Java 25 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 Oracle GraalVM (see notes) java21-graalvm Java 21 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 Oracle GraalVM (see notes) java17-graalvm Java 17 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 Oracle GraalVM (see notes) java17 Java 17 Ubuntu amd64, arm64 java16 Java 16 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7 java11 Java 11 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7 Legacy java8 Java 8 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7 Forge 1.17 and below

The stable tag

The stable tag always points to the most recent release version of the image. Unlike latest which may include pre-release builds, stable provides a consistent, production-ready image.

docs.title: Deprecated Tags
docs.text:
Deprecated Tags

The following tags are deprecated and should not be used for new deployments:

  • java23, java23-alpine, java23-jdk -- Use java25 instead
  • java24, java24-graalvm -- Use java25 instead
  • java20, java20-graalvm, java20-alpine, java17-graalvm-ce, java17-openj9 -- no longer updated
  • java17-alpine -- Use java17 or java21-alpine instead

docs.title: Programmatic Access
docs.text:
The full list of supported image tags and their metadata is available as JSON:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itzg/docker-minecraft-server/refs/heads/master/images.json

docs.title: Java Requirements by Version
docs.text: Minecraft Version Minimum Java Recommended Java 1.21+ Java 21 Java 21 or 25 1.20.5 - 1.20.6 Java 21 Java 21 1.18 - 1.20.4 Java 17 Java 17/21 1.17 Java 16 Java 17 1.12 - 1.16.5 Java 8 Java 8/11 1.11 and below Java 8 Java 8

docs.text:
Forge requires specific Java versions:

Forge/Minecraft Version Required Java Forge 1.20.5+ Java 21 Forge 1.18 - 1.20.4 Java 17 Forge 1.17.x Java 16/17 Forge 1.16.5 and below Java 8 required

docs.title: Mod Compatibility Issues
docs.text: Some mods require specific Java versions. Check the mod documentation.

docs.title: Architecture-Specific Tags
docs.text:
Support for various CPU architectures:

Tag Java Linux Architecture latest, stable 25 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, riscv64 java25 25 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, riscv64 java25-alpine 25 Alpine amd64, arm64 java25-jdk 25 Ubuntu+JDK amd64, arm64 java21 21 Ubuntu amd64, arm64 java21-jdk 21 Ubuntu+JDK amd64, arm64 java21-alpine 21 Alpine amd64, arm64 java25-graalvm 25 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 java21-graalvm 21 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 java17-graalvm 17 Oracle Linux amd64, arm64 java17 17 Ubuntu amd64, arm64 java16 16 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7 java11 11 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7 java8 8 Ubuntu amd64, arm64, armv7

docs.title: ARM Devices (Raspberry Pi, etc.)
docs.text:
image: itzg/minecraft-server:java17
# armv7 (32-bit Raspberry Pi) is supported only by java16, java11 and java8
# java17+ support amd64/arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4/5 64-bit)

docs.title: GraalVM Variants
docs.text:
The Oracle GraalVM variants (java25-graalvm, java21-graalvm, java17-graalvm) are listed as supported tags in the official docs (the variants were restored in release 2026.8.0).

GraalVM notes (from official docs)

  • Based on the Oracle GraalVM container images, which as of JDK 17 are under the GraalVM Free License.
  • These images use Oracle Linux, so the Forge installer will not work (zlib-ng). Use another image for the initial installation and Forge version upgrades.

docs.title: Java 8 and CurseForge
docs.text:
Java 8 is in maintenance mode

java8, java8-jdk, and other pre-Java 17 tags (java11, java16) pin an older mc-image-helper that predates the built-in CurseForge API key. AUTO_CURSEFORGE and CURSEFORGE_FILES on those images require you to set CF_API_KEY yourself. Java 17+ images include a key.

docs.title: Version Selection Guide
docs.text:
Minecraft 1.21+ --> java21 or latest (Java 25)
Minecraft 1.18-1.20.4 --> java17 or java21
Forge 1.16.5 and below --> java8 (required)
Modpacks --> Check modpack requirements

When in doubt

Use java21 for Minecraft 1.20.5+. The latest/stable tags now use Java 25, which works with all modern Minecraft versions.

services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server:java21
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "PAPER"
      VERSION: "LATEST"

docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server:java17
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "FABRIC"
      VERSION: "1.20.4"

docs.title: Mods and Plugins
docs.text: How to install and manage mods and plugins.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• Mods: Used with Forge/Fabric/Quilt servers, client installation also required
  • Plugins: Used with Paper/Spigot/Bukkit servers, server-side only

docs.title: Volume Mounts
docs.text:
volumes:
  - ./data:/data
  - ./mods:/mods:ro      # Mods (read-only)
  - ./plugins:/plugins:ro # Plugins (read-only)
  - ./config:/config      # Configuration files

docs.title: Download via Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Description MODS List of mod URLs (comma/space separated) PLUGINS List of plugin URLs MODS_FILE File containing mod URL list PLUGINS_FILE File containing plugin URL list

docs.title: Auto-removal
docs.text:
When items are removed from MODS, PLUGINS, or MODRINTH_PROJECTS lists, the corresponding files are automatically deleted from the server. This ensures clean mod/plugin management without manual cleanup.

No manual cleanup needed

Simply remove an entry from the environment variable list, and on the next server start the previously downloaded file will be removed automatically.

docs.title: MODRINTH_PROJECTS
docs.text:
Automatically download mods/plugins from Modrinth:

environment:
  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: |
    fabric-api
    lithium
    sodium
    iris

docs.title: Specify Version and Prefix
docs.text:
Each project entry supports multiple formats:

Format Description Example project Latest release fabric-api project:version_id Specific version fabric-api:abcd1234 project:release_type Release type lithium:beta prefix:project Loader/type prefix datapack:my-datapack

Available Prefixes:

Prefix Description datapack Install as a datapack instead of mod fabric Force Fabric loader type forge Force Forge loader type paper Force Paper plugin type 
environment:
  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: |
    fabric-api:version_id
    lithium:beta
    sodium:release
    datapack:terralith
    forge:jei

docs.title: Additional Options
docs.text:
Variable Default Description MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES none required, optional MODRINTH_PROJECTS_DEFAULT_VERSION_TYPE release beta, alpha VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS false Automatically determines the latest Minecraft version that all listed mods support MODRINTH_LOADER (auto) Override loader type for Modrinth downloads (e.g., fabric, forge)

VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS

When set to true, the server will automatically determine the latest Minecraft version that all listed Modrinth projects support. This is useful for keeping mod compatibility without manually tracking version support across mods.

MODRINTH_LOADER

Override the loader type sent to Modrinth API. Useful for custom server setups, for example when using Sinytra Connector with Forge to load Fabric mods: 

environment:
  TYPE: "FORGE"
  MODRINTH_LOADER: "fabric"  # Download Fabric versions for use with Sinytra Connector


environment:
  TYPE: "FABRIC"
  VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS: "true"
  MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES: "required"
  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: |
    fabric-api
    lithium

docs.title: Modrinth Modpacks
docs.text:
Install modpacks from Modrinth using MODRINTH_MODPACK:

environment:
  MODRINTH_MODPACK: "adrenaline"

docs.title: Modpack Options
docs.text: Variable Default Description MODRINTH_MODPACK Modpack project slug, ID, or URL MODRINTH_FORCE_INCLUDE_FILES Force include specific files that would otherwise be excluded MODRINTH_DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_INCLUDES false Disable the default exclude/include behavior MODRINTH_OVERRIDES_EXCLUSIONS Exclude files from overrides using ant-style patterns (e.g., *.txt,config/unwanted/**) MODRINTH_FORCE_SYNCHRONIZE false Force re-synchronization of modpack files on every start

docs.title: API Key
docs.text:
A CurseForge API key is included by the image on Java 17 and newer (since 2026.7.1); you can always supply your own. The java8 image (and other pre-Java 17 tags) does not include a key, so CF_API_KEY must be set there:

environment:
  CF_API_KEY: "${CF_API_KEY}"

docs.title: CURSEFORGE_FILES
docs.text:
environment:
  CF_API_KEY: "${CF_API_KEY}"
  CURSEFORGE_FILES: |
    jei
    journeymap
    jade

docs.title: Additional CurseForge Options
docs.text:
Variable Default Description CF_API_KEY (built-in on Java 17+) CurseForge API key. Required only on java8 / pre-Java 17 tags CF_API_KEY_FILE Path to a file containing the API key CF_MOD_LOADER_VERSION (auto) Override the mod loader version for CurseForge modpacks

CF_MOD_LOADER_VERSION

Use this to pin a specific mod loader version when installing CurseForge modpacks. By default, the version specified in the modpack manifest is used.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text:
• Project page URL: https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/jei
  • Slug: jei
  • Project ID: 238222
  • Slug:FileID: jei:4593548
  • List file: @/extras/cf-mods.txt

docs.title: Download from Spiget (SpigotMC)
docs.text:
Download Paper/Spigot plugins:

environment:
  SPIGET_RESOURCES: "9089,34315"  # Resource IDs

Find the resource ID from the SpigotMC page URL: https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/example-plugin.12345/ → ID: 12345

docs.title: Extra Files
docs.text:
Download additional configuration or resource files using APPLY_EXTRA_FILES:

Variable Description APPLY_EXTRA_FILES Download extra files. Format: destination<source_url

The format uses < to separate the destination path from the source URL:

environment:
  APPLY_EXTRA_FILES: |
    config/extra.yml<https://example.com/extra.yml
    plugins/MyPlugin/config.yml<https://example.com/plugin-config.yml

Note

Destination paths are relative to the server's /data directory. Files are downloaded on each server start, so they will be updated if the source changes.

docs.title: Packwiz Modpacks
docs.text:
Modpacks managed with Packwiz:

environment:
  PACKWIZ_URL: "https://example.com/pack.toml"

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
/data/mods.txt or URL:

# Comment
https://example.com/mod1.jar
https://example.com/mod2.jar

# Empty lines are ignored
modrinth:fabric-api
curseforge:jei

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
environment:
  MODS_FILE: "/data/mods.txt"
  # or
  PLUGINS_FILE: "https://example.com/plugins.txt"

docs.title: ZIP File Modpacks
docs.text:
environment:
  MODPACK: "https://example.com/modpack.zip"

docs.title: Generic Pack
docs.text:
Support for multiple packs:

environment:
  GENERIC_PACKS: |
    https://example.com/pack1.zip
    https://example.com/pack2.zip

docs.title: Remove Old Mods
docs.text:
environment:
  REMOVE_OLD_MODS: "TRUE"

docs.title: Exclude Specific Mods
docs.text:
environment:
  REMOVE_OLD_MODS: "TRUE"
  REMOVE_OLD_MODS_INCLUDE: "*.jar"
  REMOVE_OLD_MODS_EXCLUDE: "keep-this-mod.jar"

    image: itzg/minecraft-server:java21

docs.title: Mixed Sources
docs.text:

  MODRINTH_PROJECTS: "fabric-api,lithium"
  MODS: |
    https://example.com/custom-mod.jar
  MODS_FILE: "/data/extra-mods.txt"

docs.title: Removing Old Configs on Modpack Update
docs.text:
Set REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS=TRUE to remove all files in /data/config before a modpack is downloaded and unpacked (added 2026.9.2). Useful when a modpack update would otherwise override locally customized configs.

Variable Default Description REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS false Enable removal before modpack install REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS_INCLUDE * Comma-separated file glob patterns to remove REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS_EXCLUDE Comma-separated file glob patterns to keep REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS_DEPTH 16 Directory depth CONFIG_OUT_DIR /data/config Target directory 
environment:
  REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS: "TRUE"
  REMOVE_OLD_CONFIGS_EXCLUDE: "*.toml"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration
docs.text: Variable interpolation, automatic RCON commands, and other advanced configuration options.

docs.title: Variable Interpolation
docs.text: Dynamically substitute environment variables in configuration files.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
Use ${CFG_VARIABLE_NAME} format in configuration files:

# config.yml
server-name: ${CFG_SERVER_NAME}
max-players: ${CFG_MAX_PLAYERS}

# docker-compose.yml
environment:
  CFG_SERVER_NAME: "My Server"
  CFG_MAX_PLAYERS: "50"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description REPLACE_ENV_IN_PLACE true Interpolate variables in files within /data REPLACE_ENV_DURING_SYNC false Interpolate variables during sync REPLACE_ENV_VARIABLE_PREFIX CFG_ Prefix for interpolation variables

docs.title: Supported File Extensions
docs.text: .yml, .yaml, .txt, .cfg, .conf, .properties

docs.title: Exclusion Settings
docs.text:
environment:
  REPLACE_ENV_SUFFIXES_EXCLUSIONS: ".json"
  REPLACE_ENV_VARIABLES_EXCLUDES: "CFG_SECRET"

docs.title: Automatic RCON Commands

environment:
  RCON_CMDS_STARTUP: |
    gamerule keepInventory true
    gamerule doDaylightCycle false
    difficulty hard

docs.title: On Player Connect
docs.text:
environment:
  RCON_CMDS_ON_CONNECT: |
    say Welcome to the server!
    give @a minecraft:bread 16

docs.title: On Player Disconnect

  RCON_CMDS_ON_DISCONNECT: |

docs.title: On First Player Connect
docs.text:

  RCON_CMDS_FIRST_CONNECT: |
    say Server is now active!

docs.title: On Last Player Disconnect

  RCON_CMDS_LAST_DISCONNECT: |

docs.title: Using YAML Blocks in Docker Compose

environment:
  RCON_CMDS_STARTUP: |-
    gamerule keepInventory true
    gamerule doDaylightCycle false

  TYPE: "CUSTOM"
  CUSTOM_SERVER: "https://example.com/server.jar"

docs.title: Additional Server Arguments

  EXTRA_ARGS: "--world-dir ./worlds/"

docs.title: Force Server Redownload

  FORCE_REDOWNLOAD: "true"
