  ROLLING_LOG_MAX_FILES: "7"

docs.title: Proxy Settings
docs.text:
Using HTTP/HTTPS proxy:

environment:
  PROXY: "http://proxy.example.com:8080"
  # or
  PROXY_HOST: "proxy.example.com"
  PROXY_PORT: "8080"
  PROXY_NON_PROXY_HOSTS: "localhost|*.internal.com"

docs.title: APPLY_EXTRA_FILES
docs.text:
Automatically copy/download configuration files:

environment:
  APPLY_EXTRA_FILES: |
    /config/spigot.yml=/data/spigot.yml
    https://example.com/bukkit.yml=/data/bukkit.yml

docs.title: Sync Directory
docs.text:
volumes:
  - ./sync:/data/sync
environment:
  SYNC_SKIP_NEWER_IN_DESTINATION: "false"

docs.title: Example: Complete Advanced Configuration
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "PAPER"
      VERSION: "1.20.4"

      # Variable interpolation
      REPLACE_ENV_IN_PLACE: "true"
      CFG_SERVER_NAME: "Production Server"
      CFG_DISCORD_WEBHOOK: "${DISCORD_WEBHOOK}"

      # Automatic RCON commands
      RCON_CMDS_STARTUP: |-
        gamerule keepInventory true
        whitelist on

      RCON_CMDS_FIRST_CONNECT: |-
        say Server is waking up!

      # Logging
      LOG_LEVEL: "info"
      LOG_TIMESTAMP: "true"
      ROLLING_LOG_MAX_FILES: "14"

      # Shutdown settings
      STOP_SERVER_ANNOUNCE_DELAY: "60"
      STOP_DURATION: "120"

    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
      - ./config:/config:ro

docs.title: Sending Commands
docs.text: Various methods to send commands to the server.

docs.title: RCON (Default Method)
docs.text: RCON is enabled by default.

docs.title: Using rcon-cli
docs.text:
# Interactive mode
docker exec -i mc rcon-cli

# Execute single command
docker exec mc rcon-cli say Hello World
docker exec mc rcon-cli op player_name
docker exec mc rcon-cli stop

docs.title: RCON Configuration
docs.text:
environment:
  ENABLE_RCON: "true"        # Default
  RCON_PASSWORD: "secure_password"
  RCON_PORT: "25575"         # Default

docs.title: Using Docker Secrets
docs.text:
environment:
  RCON_PASSWORD_FILE: "/run/secrets/rcon_password"

secrets:
  rcon_password:
    file: ./rcon_password.txt

docs.title: Console Pipe
docs.text:
When not using RCON:

environment:
  ENABLE_RCON: "false"
  CREATE_CONSOLE_IN_PIPE: "true"

docker exec --user 1000 mc mc-send-to-console op player_name

docs.title: Docker CLI
docs.text:
docker attach mc
# Detach: Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Q

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
docker compose attach mc
# Detach: Ctrl+P, Ctrl+Q

docs.title: Configuration Requirements
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true

Note: Full interactive console (auto-completion, color output) requires RCON.

docs.title: SSH Console
docs.text:
Access server console via SSH connection.

Variable Default Description ENABLE_SSH false Enable SSH console
  • Port: 2222 (inside container)
  • Password: Same as RCON password
  • Password-based authentication only

docs.title: Docker Compose Example
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
      - "2222:2222"   # SSH console
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      ENABLE_SSH: "true"
      RCON_PASSWORD: "your_password"

docs.title: WebSocket Console
docs.text: Stream server logs and send commands via WebSocket connection.

docs.title: Enable
docs.text: Variable Default Description WEBSOCKET_CONSOLE false Enable WebSocket console WEBSOCKET_ADDRESS 0.0.0.0:80 Bind address WEBSOCKET_DISABLE_ORIGIN_CHECK false Disable origin check WEBSOCKET_ALLOWED_ORIGINS - Allowed origins (comma-separated) WEBSOCKET_PASSWORD - WebSocket password (uses RCON_PASSWORD if unset) WEBSOCKET_DISABLE_AUTHENTICATION false Disable authentication WEBSOCKET_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE 50 Number of log history lines

      WEBSOCKET_PASSWORD: "your_password"

docs.title: Message Types
docs.text: Type Direction Description StdinMessage Client → Server Send command StdoutMessage Server → Client Standard output StderrMessage Server → Client Error output LogHistoryMessage Server → Client Log history on connect AuthFailureMessage Server → Client Authentication failed

Automatic commands based on server events:

environment:

  RCON_CMDS_STARTUP: |

  # On player connect

docs.text:
services:
  mc:

    tty: true
    stdin_open: true

      EULA: "TRUE"

docs.title: SSH + WebSocket
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      RCON_PASSWORD: "my_secure_password"

docs.title: Command Summary
docs.text: Method Command/Configuration Usage RCON CLI docker exec mc rcon-cli <cmd> Default method Console Pipe mc-send-to-console <cmd> When RCON is disabled Interactive docker attach mc Real-time interaction SSH ssh user@host -p 2222 Remote access WebSocket Web client Web-based management

docs.title: Autopause / Autostop
docs.text: Features to save server resources when no players are online.

docs.title: Native Auto-Pause (Minecraft 1.21.2+)
docs.text:
Recommended for Minecraft 1.21.2+

Starting from Minecraft 1.21.2, the server natively supports auto-pause functionality. This is simpler and more reliable than the container-level AutoPause feature below.

Minecraft 1.21.2 introduced the pause-when-empty-seconds server property, which pauses the game tick loop when no players are connected. The itzg/minecraft-server image exposes this as the PAUSE_WHEN_EMPTY_SECONDS environment variable.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Variable Default Description PAUSE_WHEN_EMPTY_SECONDS - Seconds to wait before pausing when no players are connected

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      PAUSE_WHEN_EMPTY_SECONDS: "300"  # Pause after 5 minutes
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

docs.title: Native vs Container-Level Comparison
docs.text: Feature Native Auto-Pause Container AutoPause Minecraft Version 1.21.2+ only Any version Configuration Single env var Multiple env vars Mechanism Game tick pause Process suspension Network Handling Built-in Requires knock detection Rootless Support No extra config Requires CAP_NET_RAW Complexity Low Medium

docs.title: Autopause (Container-Level)
docs.text:
Legacy Feature for Minecraft < 1.21.2

For Minecraft 1.21.2+, use the native PAUSE_WHEN_EMPTY_SECONDS above. The container-level AutoPause below is recommended only for older Minecraft versions.

Pauses the server process when no players are online.

docs.title: Enable
docs.text:
environment:
  ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE: "true"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE false Enable Autopause AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_EST 3600 Wait time (seconds) after last player leaves before pausing AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_INIT 600 Wait time (seconds) after server start without any connections before pausing AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_KN 120 Wait time (seconds) after port connection attempt before pausing AUTOPAUSE_PERIOD 10 Status check interval (seconds) AUTOPAUSE_KNOCK_INTERFACE eth0 Network interface AUTOPAUSE_STATUS_RETRY_LIMIT 10 Number of retries for server status check AUTOPAUSE_STATUS_RETRY_INTERVAL 2 Interval (seconds) between status check retries

docs.title: Additional Options
docs.text: Variable Description MAX_TICK_TIME Set to -1 to disable watchdog (recommended) DEBUG_AUTOPAUSE true - Enable debugging output

docs.title: State Files
docs.text:
The autopause feature uses files in /data to manage state:

File Description .paused Created when the server is paused, deleted when resumed. Can be used to check pause status. .skip-pause Create this file to temporarily skip auto-pause. Remove to re-enable. 
# Check if server is currently paused
docker exec mc test -f /data/.paused && echo "Paused" || echo "Running"

# Temporarily disable auto-pause
docker exec mc touch /data/.skip-pause

# Re-enable auto-pause
docker exec mc rm /data/.skip-pause

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE: "true"
      AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_EST: "300"    # Pause after 5 minutes
      AUTOPAUSE_TIMEOUT_INIT: "120"   # 2 minutes after server start
      MAX_TICK_TIME: "-1"             # Disable watchdog
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

docs.title: Rootless Environment (Podman)
docs.text:
Additional configuration required for rootless containers:

Requirements for Rootless

  • CAP_NET_RAW capability is required for knock detection
  • Set SKIP_SUDO=true to avoid sudo-related issues
  • Consider using slirp4netns port forwarder for better compatibility
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    cap_add:
      - CAP_NET_RAW
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE: "true"
      SKIP_SUDO: "true"

Docker CLI:

docker run -d \
  --cap-add=CAP_NET_RAW \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  -e ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE=true \
  -e SKIP_SUDO=true \
  itzg/minecraft-server

Podman with slirp4netns:

podman run -d \
  --cap-add=CAP_NET_RAW \
  --network slirp4netns:port_handler=slirp4netns \
  -e EULA=TRUE \
  -e ENABLE_AUTOPAUSE=true \
  -e SKIP_SUDO=true \
  -p 25565:25565 \
  itzg/minecraft-server

docs.title: Autostop
docs.text: Completely stops the server when no players are online.

docs.title: Enable
docs.text:
environment:
  ENABLE_AUTOSTOP: "TRUE"

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description ENABLE_AUTOSTOP false Enable Autostop AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_EST 3600 Wait time (seconds) after last player leaves before stopping AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_INIT 1800 Wait time (seconds) after server start without any connections before stopping AUTOSTOP_PERIOD 10 Status check interval (seconds)

docs.title: Additional Options
docs.text: Variable Description DEBUG_AUTOSTOP true - Enable debugging output USES_PROXY_PROTOCOL true - Enable PROXY Protocol support (for HAProxy, Fly.io, etc.)

docs.title: Basic Example
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      ENABLE_AUTOSTOP: "TRUE"
      AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_EST: "600"    # Stop after 10 minutes
      AUTOSTOP_TIMEOUT_INIT: "300"   # 5 minutes after server start
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

docs.title: Temporarily Disable Autostop
docs.text:
Create /data/.skip-stop file to prevent autostop:

docker exec mc touch /data/.skip-stop

Remove:

docker exec mc rm /data/.skip-stop

docs.title: Autopause vs Autostop Comparison
docs.text: Feature Native Auto-Pause Autopause (Container) Autostop Minecraft Version 1.21.2+ Any Any Behavior Game tick pause Process suspension Stop container Recovery Speed Instant Instant Requires server restart Resource Savings Low-Medium Medium High Configuration Simple (1 var) Complex (multiple vars) Moderate Use Case Modern servers Older servers, quick recovery Maximum resource savings

docs.title: HAProxy / Fly.io
docs.text:
environment:
  ENABLE_AUTOSTOP: "TRUE"
  USES_PROXY_PROTOCOL: "true"

docs.title: Enable Debugging
docs.text:
environment:
  DEBUG_AUTOPAUSE: "true"
  # or

docs.title: Default Healthcheck

docs.title: Manual Deployment (Manifests)
docs.text:
# deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: minecraft
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: minecraft
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: minecraft
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: minecraft
          image: itzg/minecraft-server
          env:
            - name: EULA
              value: "TRUE"
            - name: TYPE
              value: "PAPER"
            - name: MEMORY
              value: "4G"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 25565
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
          resources:
            requests:
              memory: "4Gi"
              cpu: "1000m"
            limits:
              memory: "6Gi"
              cpu: "2000m"
      volumes:
        - name: data
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: minecraft-data
---
# pvc.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: minecraft-data
spec:
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 10Gi
---
# service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: minecraft
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - port: 25565
      targetPort: 25565
  selector:
    app: minecraft

#!/bin/bash
CONTAINER="mc"
BACKUP_DIR="./backups"
DATE=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)

mkdir -p "$BACKUP_DIR"

# Save world
docker exec $CONTAINER rcon-cli save-all
sleep 5
docker exec $CONTAINER rcon-cli save-off

# Backup
tar -czf "$BACKUP_DIR/world_$DATE.tar.gz" ./data/world

# Re-enable saving
docker exec $CONTAINER rcon-cli save-on

# Delete old backups (7 days)
find "$BACKUP_DIR" -name "*.tar.gz" -mtime +7 -delete

docs.title: Complete Production Configuration
docs.text:
services:
  mc:
    image: itzg/minecraft-server:java21
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      EULA: "TRUE"
      TYPE: "PAPER"
      VERSION: "1.20.4"

      # Memory and Performance
      MEMORY: "8G"
      USE_AIKAR_FLAGS: "true"
      VIEW_DISTANCE: "10"
      SIMULATION_DISTANCE: "8"

      # Server Settings
      MOTD: "Welcome to Production Server"
      MAX_PLAYERS: "100"
      DIFFICULTY: "normal"
      PVP: "true"
      TZ: "Asia/Seoul"

      # Security
      ENABLE_WHITELIST: "true"
      WHITELIST_FILE: "/config/whitelist.txt"
      OPS_FILE: "/config/ops.txt"
      RCON_PASSWORD_FILE: "/run/secrets/rcon_password"

      # Logging
      LOG_TIMESTAMP: "true"
      ROLLING_LOG_MAX_FILES: "14"

      # Monitoring
      ENABLE_JMX: "true"
      JMX_HOST: "0.0.0.0"
    ports:
      - "25565:25565"
      - "7091:7091"
    volumes:
      - mc-data:/data
      - ./config:/config:ro
    secrets:
      - rcon_password
    healthcheck:
      test: mc-health
      start_period: 2m
      interval: 10s
      retries: 24
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 10G
        reservations:
          memory: 8G

secrets:
  rcon_password:
    file: ./secrets/rcon_password.txt

volumes:
  mc-data:

docs.title: Mods and Plugins
docs.text: This guide covers installing mods and plugins for your Minecraft server using mcctl CLI.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Type Description Server Types Mods Modify game mechanics, require client installation Forge, NeoForge, Fabric, Quilt Plugins Server-side only, no client changes needed Paper, Purpur, Spigot, Bukkit, Leaf, Folia, Pufferfish

docs.title: Create Server with Mod Support
docs.text:
First, create a server with the appropriate type for mods or plugins:

# For mods (Forge/Fabric)
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# For plugins (Paper)
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

docs.title: Configure Mods/Plugins
docs.text:
Use mcctl config to set mod and plugin sources:

# Modrinth mods (Fabric example)
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# CurseForge mods (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+ images)
mcctl config modded CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap"

# SpigotMC plugins
mcctl config survival SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315"

# Apply changes
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

Restart Required

After changing mod/plugin configuration, restart the server to apply changes.

docs.title: With mcctl mod
docs.text:
mcctl mod writes the same keys for you:

# Search Modrinth
mcctl mod search sodium

# Add Modrinth projects (mcctl checks the slugs on Modrinth)
mcctl mod add modded fabric-api lithium

# Other sources
mcctl mod add modded --curseforge jei journeymap
mcctl mod add survival --spiget 28140
mcctl mod add modded --url https://example.com/custom-mod.jar

# List and remove
mcctl mod list modded
mcctl mod remove modded lithium

--curseforge writes CURSEFORGE_FILES, --spiget writes SPIGET_RESOURCES, and --url writes PLUGINS on the plugin servers and MODS on the others. For server types not in the Overview table, including modpack types, mcctl mod add asks for --force. Restart the server afterwards.

docs.title: Installation Sources
docs.text: Source Best For API Key Required mcctl Config Key Modrinth Modern mods/plugins No MODRINTH_PROJECTS CurseForge Large mod library No (built in for Java 17+ images) CURSEFORGE_FILES Spiget SpigotMC plugins No SPIGET_RESOURCES Direct Download Custom/private files No MODS / PLUGINS Modpacks Pre-configured collections Varies Server TYPE

docs.title: Modrinth vs CurseForge
docs.text: Feature Modrinth CurseForge API Key Not required Optional (built in for Java 17+ images) Dependency Resolution Automatic Manual Version Auto-detect Yes No Mod Library Size Growing Largest Plugin Support Yes Limited

docs.title: Spiget vs Modrinth for Plugins
docs.text: Feature Spiget Modrinth Platform SpigotMC resources Modrinth projects ID Format Numeric resource ID Slug or project ID Dependency Support No Yes Download Restrictions Some plugins restricted None

docs.title: Setting Mod Sources
docs.text:
# View current configuration
mcctl config myserver

# Add Modrinth mods
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# Enable dependency download
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES "required"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: Setting Plugin Sources
docs.text:
# Modrinth plugins (Paper server)
mcctl config survival MODRINTH_PROJECTS "luckperms,chunky,spark"

# SpigotMC plugins (numeric IDs)
mcctl config survival SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315,6245"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival

docs.title: Using Shared Directories
docs.text:
mcctl init creates shared/plugins/, which every server mounts read-only at /plugins. The image copies those jars into the server's plugins/ folder when it starts.

~/minecraft-servers/
  shared/
    plugins/                 # Plugin JARs for all servers (read-only mount)
  servers/<name>/data/
    mods/                    # Mod JARs for one server

Put manually downloaded plugins in shared/plugins/. Put mod JARs in the server's own servers/<name>/data/mods/, or list their download URLs in MODS (see Direct Download).

docs.title: Remove Old Mods
docs.text:
Configure automatic cleanup of old mods before applying new content:

mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS "TRUE"

docs.title: Exclude Specific Files
docs.text:
mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS_INCLUDE "*.jar"
mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS_EXCLUDE "keep-this-mod.jar"

docs.title: Hybrid Servers
docs.text:
For hybrid servers like Cardboard (Fabric with Bukkit plugins):

mcctl config myserver TYPE "FABRIC"
mcctl config myserver USES_PLUGINS "true"

docs.title: Environment Variable Processing
docs.text:
By default, environment variables are not processed in files copied by the sync. To enable it:

mcctl config myserver REPLACE_ENV_DURING_SYNC "true"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration (Manual)
docs.text:
For complex configurations not supported by mcctl config, edit config.env directly:

# Edit server configuration file
nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

Example config.env:

# Modrinth mods (one line, comma-separated)
MODRINTH_PROJECTS=fabric-api,lithium,sodium,iris

# Dependency settings
MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=required

Each value must stay on one line; for long lists use a listing file (see Using Listing Files). mcctl takes a hand edit into server.yaml the next time it changes the server.

docs.title: CurseForge
docs.text: Download mods and plugins from CurseForge - the largest mod hosting platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Feature Value Official Website https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft API Key Required No (built in for Java 17+ images; set CF_API_KEY only for java8/pre-17 tags or your own key) API Console https://console.curseforge.com/ Dependency Resolution Manual (metadata only) Mod Library Size Largest

docs.title: Step 1: Get API Key
docs.text:
Skip this step on Java 17+ images, which include a key. mcctl gives a new server the tag its VERSION needs, so a modpack server created with -v 1.16.5 or older runs on java8 and needs a key. You need your own key only for java8 and other pre-Java 17 tags, or to use your own.

  1. Go to CurseForge API Console
  2. Sign in and create an API key
  3. Set the key on the server in Step 2, or for every server as in Step 4: Configure API Key

docs.title: Step 2: Create Server and Add Mods
docs.text:
# Create a Forge server
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.4

# Only with your own key (java8 and other pre-Java 17 tags, or your own key)
mcctl config modded CF_API_KEY '<your-api-key>'

# Add CurseForge mods
mcctl config modded CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap,jade"

# Restart to apply changes
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

API Key Optional

Java 17+ images include a built-in CF_API_KEY; set it only for java8/pre-17 tags or to use your own key. Set it per server with mcctl config; a key only in the platform .env does not reach servers.

docs.title: Step 1: Create CurseForge Account
docs.text:
1. Go to CurseForge
  2. Click "Sign In" or "Register"
  3. Complete the registration process

docs.title: Step 2: Access API Console
docs.text:
1. Go to https://console.curseforge.com/
  2. Sign in with your CurseForge account
  3. Accept the API Terms of Service

docs.title: Step 3: Generate API Key
docs.text:
1. Click "Create API Key" or navigate to API Keys section
  2. Give your key a descriptive name (e.g., "Minecraft Docker Server")
  3. Copy the generated API key immediately

Security

  • Store your API key securely
  • Never commit API keys to version control
  • Add .env to your .gitignore file

docs.title: Step 4: Configure API Key
docs.text:
Set the key for one server:

mcctl config myserver CF_API_KEY '<your-api-key>'

Or for every server: add a CF_API_KEY line to ~/minecraft-servers/servers/global.env, put the value in ~/minecraft-servers/.env in single quotes, then stop and start the servers:

# servers/global.env
CF_API_KEY

# .env
CF_API_KEY='your_api_key_here'

A key only in .env does not reach servers: they receive only the .env keys named in servers/global.env.

Keys that contain $

mcctl config writes the value in single quotes for you, and single quotes in .env keep it literal too. Do not escape $ as $$: inside single quotes it stays $$.

docs.title: Supported Reference Formats
docs.text:
Format Description Example Project URL Full URL to mod page https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/jei File URL URL with specific file https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/jei/files/4593548 Slug Short identifier from URL jei Project ID Numeric project identifier 238222 Slug:FileID Slug with specific file jei:4593548 ID:FileID Project ID with file ID 238222:4593548 Slug@Version Slug with version string jei@10.2.1.1005

Finding Project IDs

  1. Go to the mod page on CurseForge
  2. Scroll down to the "About Project" section
  3. Find "Project ID" (e.g., 238222 for JEI)

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
# Add mods (comma-separated)
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap,jade"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: Specific Versions
docs.text:
# Pin to specific file ID
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei:4593548,journeymap:4596105"

# Pin by version string
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei@10.2.1.1005"

docs.title: Mixed References
docs.text:
# Different reference formats together
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap:4596105,238222"

docs.title: With mcctl mod
docs.text:
# Add references to CURSEFORGE_FILES (mcctl does not check them)
mcctl mod add myserver --curseforge jei journeymap jade

# Remove one again
mcctl mod remove myserver jade

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Config Key Description CURSEFORGE_FILES Comma- or space-separated list of mod references

API Key Location

Set CF_API_KEY per server with mcctl config, or add its name to servers/global.env to pass the .env value to every server. A key only in .env does not reach servers.

docs.title: Forge Mod Server
docs.text:
# Create server without starting it
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.4 --no-start

# Configure mods
mcctl config modded CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap,jade,mouse-tweaks,appleskin"
mcctl config modded MEMORY "6G"

# Start server
mcctl start modded

docs.title: Mixed Sources (CurseForge + Modrinth)
docs.text:
# Create Fabric server
mcctl create mixed -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# CurseForge mods (CF_API_KEY optional on Java 17+ images)
mcctl config mixed CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,journeymap"

# Modrinth mods (no API key needed)
mcctl config mixed MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,sodium,lithium"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop mixed && mcctl start mixed

docs.title: Pinned Versions for Reproducibility
docs.text:
# Pin specific file versions for consistent builds
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei:4593548,journeymap:4596105,jade:4587399"

docs.title: Auto-Removal and Upgrades
docs.text:
• Files are automatically upgraded when newer versions are available
  • Removed references are automatically cleaned up
  • To remove CurseForge mods, remove their references:
# Remove references as they are written in CURSEFORGE_FILES
mcctl mod remove myserver jei journeymap
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

To drop the whole list, delete CURSEFORGE_FILES under env: in servers/myserver/server.yaml, run mcctl migrate spec myserver, then stop and start the server.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Manual Dependency Management

CurseForge can detect missing dependencies but cannot automatically resolve them.

You must manually add required dependencies to CURSEFORGE_FILES.

Example: If JEI requires Forge API, you need to add both:

mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES "jei,forge-api"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration (Manual)
docs.text:
For complex configurations, edit config.env directly. Each value stays on one line; for long lists, use a listing file (below).

nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

Example config.env:

# CurseForge mods (one line, comma-separated)
CURSEFORGE_FILES=jei,journeymap,jade,mouse-tweaks,appleskin,storage-drawers

docs.title: Using Listing Files
docs.text:
For very large mod lists:

# Create mod list file
nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/data/cf-mods.txt

Content of cf-mods.txt:

# Core mods
jei
journeymap

# Utility mods
jade
mouse-tweaks

# Specific versions
create:5678901

Then reference it in config.env:

CURSEFORGE_FILES=@/data/cf-mods.txt

/data in the container is the server's servers/myserver/data/ folder.

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text: Issue Cause Solution 401 Unauthorized Invalid or missing API key Check CF_API_KEY for the server (mcctl config <server> CF_API_KEY, or servers/global.env and .env) 403 Forbidden API key lacks permissions Regenerate API key from console Mod not found Wrong slug or ID Verify from CurseForge URL Version mismatch Mod doesn't support server version Use specific file ID for compatible version Missing dependencies Dependencies not resolved Manually add required mods

docs.title: Check API Key Configuration
docs.text:
# Key set for one server (don't share the output!)
mcctl config myserver CF_API_KEY

# Key passed to every server
grep CF_API_KEY ~/minecraft-servers/servers/global.env ~/minecraft-servers/.env

docs.title: Check Current Configuration
docs.text:
# View all configuration
mcctl config myserver

# View specific setting
mcctl config myserver CURSEFORGE_FILES

docs.title: View Server Logs
docs.text:
# Check for mod loading errors
mcctl logs myserver

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl logs myserver -f

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable debug output to troubleshoot issues:

mcctl config myserver DEBUG "true"
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver
mcctl logs myserver

docs.title: Verify API Key
docs.text:
Test your API key with curl:

curl -H "x-api-key: YOUR_API_KEY" \
  "https://api.curseforge.com/v1/mods/238222"

docs.title: Direct Download
docs.text: Download mods and plugins directly from URLs or use local files.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Feature Value API Key Required No Supports Any accessible URL or local file Use Cases Custom mods, private files, direct URLs

docs.title: Methods
docs.text: Method Description Use Case MODS / PLUGINS Direct URL list Simple URL-based downloads Shared plugins directory shared/plugins/, mounted in every server Manually downloaded plugins Server data folder servers/<name>/data/mods/ Local mod files for one server

docs.title: Using Direct URLs
docs.text:
# Create a Fabric server
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# Add mods from direct URLs
mcctl config modded MODS "https://example.com/custom-mod.jar,https://github.com/user/repo/releases/download/v1.0/mod.jar"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

docs.title: Using Local Files
docs.text:
• Plugins: put JARs in ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/. Every server mounts it read-only at /plugins, and the image copies the JARs into the server's plugins/ folder when the server starts.
  • Mods: put JARs in the server's own ~/minecraft-servers/servers/<name>/data/mods/. There is no shared mods folder.

docs.title: MODS Variable
docs.text:
For Forge/Fabric servers, download mods from URLs:

# Single mod
mcctl config myserver MODS "https://example.com/custom-mod.jar"

# Multiple mods (comma-separated)
mcctl config myserver MODS "https://example.com/mod1.jar,https://example.com/mod2.jar"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: PLUGINS Variable
docs.text:
For Paper/Spigot servers, download plugins from URLs:

# Single plugin
mcctl config myserver PLUGINS "https://example.com/custom-plugin.jar"

# Multiple plugins
mcctl config myserver PLUGINS "https://example.com/plugin1.jar,https://example.com/plugin2.jar"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: With mcctl mod
docs.text:
# Append a URL: to PLUGINS on plugin servers (Paper and its forks, Spigot, Bukkit), to MODS on the others
mcctl mod add myserver --url https://example.com/custom-mod.jar

docs.title: Supported Delimiters
docs.text:
URLs can be separated by:

  • Commas: url1,url2,url3
  • Spaces: url1 url2 url3
  • Newlines: only in a file named by MODS_FILE or PLUGINS_FILE (see Using File Lists)

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description MODS Comma- or space-separated mod URLs or container paths PLUGINS Comma- or space-separated plugin URLs or container paths

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
mcctl init creates shared/. A server's data/ folder is its /data in the container:

~/minecraft-servers/
  shared/
    plugins/    # Mounted read-only at /plugins in every server
    mods/       # Not mounted by servers
  servers/<name>/data/
    mods/       # This server's mods (/data/mods)
    plugins/    # This server's plugins (/data/plugins)

docs.title: Using Shared Directories
docs.text:
1. Place plugin JAR files in shared/plugins/
  2. Restart the servers; the image copies the JARs into each server's plugins/ folder
  3. No configuration needed
# Example: Add a custom plugin
cp ~/downloads/custom-plugin.jar ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/

# Available to all Paper/Spigot servers after their next start

# A mod for one server goes into that server's data folder
cp ~/downloads/custom-mod.jar ~/minecraft-servers/servers/modded/data/mods/

docs.title: Benefits
docs.text:
Benefits of shared/plugins/:

  • Shared across servers: One file serves all servers
  • No configuration needed: Just drop files in the directory
  • Read-only mount: Server cannot modify source files
  • Easy updates: Replace file, restart servers

docs.title: GitHub Releases Download
docs.text:
# Create server
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# Add mods from GitHub releases
mcctl config modded MODS "https://github.com/CaffeineMC/sodium-fabric/releases/download/mc1.21-0.6.0/sodium-fabric-0.6.0+mc1.21.jar"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

docs.title: Mixed Sources
docs.text:
# Create server
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# Direct URLs for custom mods
mcctl config modded MODS "https://example.com/custom-mod.jar"

# Modrinth for popular mods
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

docs.title: Local Development Setup
docs.text:
For mod development with local builds:

  1. Build your mod
  2. Copy it to the server's data/mods/ folder
  3. Restart server
# Copy built mod to the server's mods folder
cp ~/my-mod/build/libs/my-mod-1.0.jar ~/minecraft-servers/servers/modded/data/mods/

# Restart server to load the mod
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

docs.title: Server Network with Shared Plugins
docs.text:
All servers share the same plugins from shared/plugins/:

# Create multiple servers without starting them
mcctl create lobby -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start
mcctl create creative -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Place shared plugins
cp luckperms.jar ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/
cp vault.jar ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/

# The servers start with these plugins
mcctl start --all

docs.title: Advanced Configuration (Manual)
docs.text:
For advanced configurations, edit config.env directly. Each value stays on one line; for long lists, use a file list (below).

nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

Example config.env:

# Direct mod URLs (one line, comma-separated)
MODS=https://example.com/mod1.jar,https://example.com/mod2.jar,https://github.com/user/repo/releases/download/v1.0/mod3.jar

# Auto-cleanup settings
REMOVE_OLD_MODS=TRUE

docs.title: Using File Lists
docs.text:
For very large mod lists:

# Create mod list file
nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/data/mods.txt

Content of mods.txt:

# Performance mods
https://example.com/lithium.jar
https://example.com/phosphor.jar

# Utility mods
https://example.com/mod-menu.jar

# Comments starting with # are ignored
# Blank lines are also ignored

# You can also use special prefixes
modrinth:fabric-api
curseforge:jei

Then set MODS_FILE in config.env:

MODS_FILE=/data/mods.txt

docs.title: Sync Path Customization
docs.text:
Customize where mods/plugins are synced:

# In config.env
COPY_MODS_SRC=/custom-mods
COPY_MODS_DEST=/data/mods
COPY_PLUGINS_SRC=/custom-plugins
COPY_PLUGINS_DEST=/data/plugins

docs.title: Remove Old Mods
docs.text:
Configure automatic cleanup before applying new content:

mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS "TRUE"

docs.title: Exclude Specific Files
docs.text:
mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS_INCLUDE "*.jar"
mcctl config myserver REMOVE_OLD_MODS_EXCLUDE "keep-this-mod.jar"

docs.text: Issue Cause Solution Download failed Invalid URL or network issue Verify URL is accessible File not found Wrong path Check the file is in shared/plugins/ or the server's data/mods/ Permission denied File permissions Ensure files are readable Mods not loading Wrong server type Verify TYPE matches mod loader

# Follow logs in real-time

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable debug output to troubleshoot:

mcctl config myserver DEBUG "true"
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver
mcctl logs myserver

docs.text:
Test URL accessibility:

curl -I "https://example.com/mod.jar"

ls -la ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/data/mods/

docs.title: Modpacks
docs.text: Install pre-configured modpack collections from various sources.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Platform Config Key API Key Required Best For Packwiz PACKWIZ_URL No Custom/self-hosted modpacks CurseForge CF_PAGE_URL, CF_SLUG No (built in for Java 17+ images) Popular modpacks Modrinth MODRINTH_MODPACK No Open-source modpacks FTB FTB_MODPACK_ID No Feed the Beast modpacks ZIP Archive MODPACK, GENERIC_PACKS No Manual/custom archives

Modpacks and Server Types

mcctl create <name> -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack <slug> and mcctl create <name> -t MODRINTH --modpack <slug> set TYPE and the modpack for you. For the other platforms, create the server with --no-start, set TYPE and the platform's keys with mcctl config, then start it. Without --no-start, mcctl create starts the server right away and generates its world before the modpack is set.

docs.title: Packwiz
docs.text: Packwiz is a command-line tool for creating and managing modpacks with support for both CurseForge and Modrinth sources.

docs.title: Quick Start with mcctl
docs.text:
# Create a Fabric server for the Packwiz modpack, without starting it
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Set Packwiz modpack URL
mcctl config modded PACKWIZ_URL "https://example.com/modpack/pack.toml"

# Start the server
mcctl start modded

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description PACKWIZ_URL URL to the pack.toml modpack definition file

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Processing Order: Packwiz definitions are processed before other mod definitions (MODPACK, MODS, etc.), allowing for additional customization
  • Server-Side Only: Pre-configured to download only server-compatible mods
  • Multiple Sources: Supports both CurseForge and Modrinth mod sources

docs.title: Client-Side Mods
docs.text: If client-side mods cause issues, ensure they are marked as "client" rather than "both" in the pack.toml side setting.

docs.title: Learn More
docs.text: • Packwiz Official Documentation

docs.title: CurseForge Modpacks
docs.text: Install modpacks from CurseForge with automatic upgrade support.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
API Key Optional

Java 17+ images include a built-in CF_API_KEY; set it only for java8/pre-17 tags or to use your own key. See CurseForge Guide for setup instructions.

docs.title: Quick Start with mcctl
docs.text:
# Create the server (writes TYPE=AUTO_CURSEFORGE and CF_SLUG), without starting it
mcctl create modded -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack all-the-mods-8 --no-start

# Set memory (modpack servers start with 6G; large packs need more)
mcctl config modded MEMORY "8G"

# Start the server
mcctl start modded

--modpack-version writes CF_FILENAME_MATCHER, which picks the modpack file whose name contains it, and --exclude-files writes CF_EXCLUDE_MODS. --mod-loader is ignored with a warning: the modpack's manifest decides the loader. To pick the modpack by page URL instead of the slug, set CF_PAGE_URL with mcctl config.

docs.title: Modpack Specification Methods
docs.text: Method Description Example CF_PAGE_URL Full modpack page URL https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/modpacks/all-the-mods-8 CF_SLUG Short identifier from URL all-the-mods-8 CF_FILE_ID Specific file ID for version pinning 4567890 CF_FILENAME_MATCHER Substring to match filename server

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description CF_API_KEY CurseForge API key (optional: built in for Java 17+ images; set only for java8/pre-17 tags or your own key) CF_PAGE_URL Full URL to modpack or specific file CF_SLUG Short identifier from URL path CF_FILE_ID Specific file ID for version pinning CF_FILENAME_MATCHER Substring for desired filename matching

docs.title: Mod Filtering
docs.text:
# Exclude specific mods
mcctl config modded CF_EXCLUDE_MODS "optifine,journeymap"

# Force include mods incorrectly tagged as client-only
mcctl config modded CF_FORCE_INCLUDE_MODS "some-mod"

# Parallel download count
mcctl config modded CF_PARALLEL_DOWNLOADS "6"
Config Key Description CF_EXCLUDE_MODS Comma/space-delimited project slugs or IDs to exclude CF_FORCE_INCLUDE_MODS Force inclusion of mods incorrectly tagged as client-only CF_EXCLUDE_ALL_MODS Exclude all mods (for server-only setup) CF_PARALLEL_DOWNLOADS Number of concurrent mod downloads (default: 4)

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# Create the CurseForge modpack server without starting it
mcctl create atm8 -t AUTO_CURSEFORGE --modpack all-the-mods-8 --no-start

# Configure modpack
mcctl config atm8 MEMORY "8G"
mcctl config atm8 CF_EXCLUDE_MODS "optifine,journeymap"
mcctl config atm8 CF_PARALLEL_DOWNLOADS "6"

# Start server
mcctl start atm8

docs.title: Modrinth Modpacks
docs.text: Install modpacks from Modrinth.

docs.title: Quick Start with mcctl
docs.text:
# Create the server (writes TYPE=MODRINTH and MODRINTH_MODPACK), without starting it
mcctl create modded -t MODRINTH --modpack cobblemon-modpack --no-start

# Set memory (modpack servers start with 6G)
mcctl config modded MEMORY "8G"

# Start the server
mcctl start modded

--mod-loader, --modpack-version and --exclude-files write MODRINTH_LOADER, MODRINTH_VERSION and MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES. Run mcctl create without a name to be asked for these instead.

docs.title: Modpack Specification Methods
docs.text: Method Description Example Project slug URL identifier cobblemon-modpack Project ID Numeric ID 1234567 Page URL Full modpack URL https://modrinth.com/modpack/cobblemon-modpack mrpack URL Direct mrpack file URL https://example.com/pack.mrpack Local path Container path /packs/custom.mrpack

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Default Description MODRINTH_MODPACK - Project slug, ID, URL, or path VERSION - Set to LATEST or SNAPSHOT for auto-selection MODRINTH_MODPACK_VERSION_TYPE - Narrow to release, beta, or alpha MODRINTH_VERSION - Exact modpack version ID MODRINTH_LOADER auto Specific loader: forge, neoforge, fabric, quilt

docs.title: File Management
docs.text:
# Exclude specific files
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES "optifine,shaders"

# Force include specific mods
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_FORCE_INCLUDE_FILES "some-server-mod"

# Force synchronize (when iterating on mod compatibility)
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_FORCE_SYNCHRONIZE "true"

docs.title: Excluding Client-Only Mods
docs.text:
Some modpacks bundle client-only mods (HUD/UI mods such as Status Effect Bars) that crash a dedicated server with an error like:

java.lang.BootstrapMethodError: Attempted to load class
net/minecraft/client/gui/screens/Screen for invalid dist DEDICATED_SERVER
→ Failed to start the minecraft server

This happens when the modpack incorrectly marks a client mod as server-compatible, so the image's automatic client-mod filtering does not catch it. Exclude such mods by (partial) file name when creating the server:

# Exclude one or more client-only mods (comma-separated)
mcctl create myserver -t MODRINTH --modpack create-plus \
  --mod-loader neoforge --exclude-files statuseffectbars

In the Web Console, use the Exclude mods field in the Create Server dialog's modpack section. The values are written to MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES (or CF_EXCLUDE_MODS for CurseForge) in the server's config.env.

For a Modrinth modpack, the dialog looks up each bundled mod on Modrinth and adds the ones marked as unsupported on servers to Exclude mods; check the list before you create the server. The dialog also offers only the loader and Minecraft version pairs the modpack has, and the API refuses other pairs.

After the server has started once, its Mods tab lists the jars the modpack installed. Switching a jar to Excluded adds it to the same exclude list; restart the server to apply.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# Create the Modrinth modpack server without starting it
mcctl create cobblemon -t MODRINTH --modpack cobblemon-modpack --no-start

# Configure modpack
mcctl config cobblemon MODRINTH_MODPACK_VERSION_TYPE "release"
mcctl config cobblemon MEMORY "6G"
mcctl config cobblemon MODRINTH_EXCLUDE_FILES "optifine,shaders"

# Start server
mcctl start cobblemon

docs.title: FTB Modpacks
docs.text: Install modpacks from Feed the Beast.

docs.title: Quick Start with mcctl
docs.text:
# Create the server without starting it (mcctl create -t does not accept FTBA)
mcctl create ftb --no-start

# Set server type (use FTBA, not FTB)
mcctl config ftb TYPE "FTBA"

# Set modpack ID (from URL)
mcctl config ftb FTB_MODPACK_ID "23"

# Set memory (FTB packs are large)
mcctl config ftb MEMORY "8G"

# Start the server
mcctl start ftb

FTBA vs FTB

Use TYPE: "FTBA" (with the "A" suffix). The "FTB" alias is deprecated and refers to CurseForge.

docs.title: Finding Modpack ID
docs.text:
The modpack ID is in the URL:

https://www.feed-the-beast.com/modpacks/23-ftb-infinity-evolved-17 -> ID is 23

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description FTB_MODPACK_ID Numeric modpack ID (required) FTB_MODPACK_VERSION_ID Specific version ID (optional) FTB_FORCE_REINSTALL Set to true to force reinstallation

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text:
• Auto-upgrade: Without version pinning, restart container to get latest
  • Manual upgrade: Update FTB_MODPACK_VERSION_ID and recreate container

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
# Create the FTB modpack server without starting it
mcctl create infinity --no-start

# Configure modpack
mcctl config infinity TYPE "FTBA"
mcctl config infinity FTB_MODPACK_ID "23"
mcctl config infinity MEMORY "8G"

# Start server
mcctl start infinity

docs.title: ZIP Modpacks
docs.text: Install modpacks from ZIP archives.

docs.title: Quick Start with mcctl
docs.text:
# Create the server with the type and version the pack was built for, without starting it
mcctl create modded -t FORGE -v 1.20.1 --no-start

# Set modpack URL
mcctl config modded MODPACK "https://example.com/modpack.zip"

# Start the server
mcctl start modded

docs.title: Multiple Packs
docs.text:
For multiple packs or additional content:

# Set multiple packs (comma-separated)
mcctl config modded GENERIC_PACKS "https://example.com/base-pack.zip,https://example.com/addon-pack.zip"

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description MODPACK URL or container path to modpack ZIP GENERIC_PACKS Multiple pack URLs/paths (comma/newline separated)

docs.title: Comparison Table
docs.text: Feature Packwiz CurseForge Modrinth FTB ZIP API Key No Optional (built in for Java 17+) No No No Auto-upgrade Yes Yes Yes Yes No Version Control pack.toml CF_FILE_ID MODRINTH_VERSION FTB_MODPACK_VERSION_ID Manual Custom Mods Yes Limited Limited No Yes Dependency Resolution Yes Partial Yes Yes No Multi-source Support Yes No No No N/A

docs.title: Common Issues
docs.text: Issue Cause Solution Modpack not loading Wrong TYPE Set appropriate TYPE (AUTO_CURSEFORGE, MODRINTH, FTBA) Missing mods Client-only exclusion Use CF_FORCE_INCLUDE_MODS or MODRINTH_FORCE_INCLUDE_FILES Out of memory Insufficient allocation Increase MEMORY value (8G+ recommended for large packs) Version mismatch Incompatible versions Pin specific version with version ID variables

docs.title: Check Current Configuration
docs.text:
# View all configuration
mcctl config myserver

# View specific settings
mcctl config myserver TYPE
mcctl config myserver CF_PAGE_URL
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_MODPACK

docs.title: View Server Logs
docs.text:
# Check for modpack loading errors
mcctl logs myserver

# Follow logs in real-time
mcctl logs myserver -f

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
Enable debug output to troubleshoot issues:

mcctl config myserver DEBUG "true"
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver
mcctl logs myserver

docs.title: Advanced Configuration (Manual)
docs.text:
For complex configurations, edit config.env directly:

nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

Example config.env for CurseForge modpack:

TYPE=AUTO_CURSEFORGE
CF_PAGE_URL=https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/modpacks/all-the-mods-8
MEMORY=8G
CF_EXCLUDE_MODS=optifine,journeymap
CF_PARALLEL_DOWNLOADS=6

Example config.env for Modrinth modpack:

TYPE=MODRINTH
MODRINTH_MODPACK=cobblemon-modpack
MODRINTH_MODPACK_VERSION_TYPE=release
MEMORY=6G

docs.title: Modrinth
docs.text: Download mods and plugins from Modrinth - an open-source mod hosting platform.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Feature Value Official Website https://modrinth.com/ API Key Required No Dependency Resolution Automatic (optional) Version Auto-detect Yes Supported Types Mods, Plugins, Datapacks

docs.title: Create Server and Add Mods
docs.text:
# Create a Fabric server
mcctl create modded -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1

# Add Modrinth mods
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# Enable automatic dependency download
mcctl config modded MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES "required"

docs.title: Add Plugins to Paper Server
docs.text:
# Create a Paper server
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Add Modrinth plugins
mcctl config survival MODRINTH_PROJECTS "luckperms,chunky,spark"

# Restart to apply changes
mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival

docs.title: With mcctl mod
docs.text:
# Search Modrinth
mcctl mod search lithium

# Add projects by slug or project ID; mcctl checks them on Modrinth first
mcctl mod add modded fabric-api lithium

# Restart to apply changes
mcctl stop modded && mcctl start modded

mcctl mod add adds each project's slug to MODRINTH_PROJECTS. Set version specifiers and loader prefixes (below) with mcctl config.

docs.title: Finding Project Slug
docs.text:
The slug is the URL portion after /mod/ or /plugin/.

Example: https://modrinth.com/mod/fabric-api -> slug is fabric-api

Project Slug

You can use either the project slug or the project ID from Modrinth.

docs.title: Project Entry Formats
docs.text:
Use different formats in the MODRINTH_PROJECTS value:

Format Description Example project Latest release fabric-api project:version Specific version ID or number fabric-api:0.92.0 project:release Latest release type fabric-api:release project:beta Latest beta lithium:beta project:alpha Latest alpha sodium:alpha prefix:project Loader override fabric:sodium

docs.title: Version Specifiers
docs.text:
# Latest release
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api"

# Specific version
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api:0.92.0"

# Beta version
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "lithium:beta"

# Multiple mods with mixed versions
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,sodium:release,iris:beta"

docs.title: Loader Prefix
docs.text:
Override the auto-detected loader for specific projects:

# Force Fabric loader
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric:fabric-api"

# Force Paper loader for plugins
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "paper:luckperms"

# Datapack
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "datapack:better-villages"

docs.title: Core Settings
docs.text:
# Add mods (comma-separated)
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,sodium"

# Download dependencies automatically
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES "required"

# Default version type for all mods
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS_DEFAULT_VERSION_TYPE "release"

docs.title: Dependency Options
docs.text:
Value Description none No dependencies (image default) required Download required dependencies only optional Download required and optional dependencies

New servers created by mcctl start with required.

docs.title: Version Control
docs.text:
# Auto-detect Minecraft version from mods
mcctl config myserver VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS "true"

# Override loader type
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_LOADER "fabric"

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Default Description MODRINTH_PROJECTS - Comma-separated list of projects (one per line in a listing file) MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES none (new mcctl servers: required) none, required, or optional MODRINTH_PROJECTS_DEFAULT_VERSION_TYPE release Default: release, beta, alpha VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS false Auto-set Minecraft version MODRINTH_LOADER auto Override loader type

docs.title: Fabric Performance Server
docs.text:
# Create server without starting it
mcctl create performance -t FABRIC -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Configure mods
mcctl config performance MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium,phosphor,ferritecore,krypton,c2me-fabric"
mcctl config performance MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES "required"
mcctl config performance MEMORY "4G"

# Start server
mcctl start performance

docs.title: Paper Plugin Server
docs.text:
# Create server without starting it
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Configure plugins
mcctl config survival MODRINTH_PROJECTS "luckperms,vault,chunky,spark"
mcctl config survival MEMORY "4G"

# Start server
mcctl start survival

docs.title: Mixed Version Types
docs.text:
# Set default to beta
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS_DEFAULT_VERSION_TYPE "beta"

# Override individual mods
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,sodium:release,iris:alpha"

docs.title: Advanced Configuration (Manual)
docs.text:
For settings mcctl config does not cover, edit config.env directly. Each value stays on one line; for long lists, use a listing file (below).

nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/config.env

Example config.env:

# Modrinth mods (one line, comma-separated)
MODRINTH_PROJECTS=fabric-api,lithium,phosphor,ferritecore,krypton,c2me-fabric

# Dependency settings
MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES=required

# Custom loader (for custom server types)
MODRINTH_LOADER=fabric

docs.title: Using Listing Files
docs.text:
For very large mod lists, use a listing file:

# Create mod list file
nano ~/minecraft-servers/servers/myserver/data/mods.txt

Content of mods.txt:

# Performance mods
fabric-api
lithium
sodium

# Utility mods
iris:beta
modmenu

# Specific versions
fabric-api:0.92.0

Then reference it in config.env:

MODRINTH_PROJECTS=@/data/mods.txt

docs.title: Auto-Removal
docs.text:
When you remove a project from MODRINTH_PROJECTS, the corresponding file is automatically removed from the server.

# Remove sodium from the list
mcctl config myserver MODRINTH_PROJECTS "fabric-api,lithium"

# Restart to apply (sodium will be removed)
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.text: Issue Cause Solution Mod not found Wrong slug or ID Verify slug from Modrinth URL Version mismatch Mod doesn't support server version Use VERSION_FROM_MODRINTH_PROJECTS or check compatibility Missing dependencies Dependencies not downloaded Set MODRINTH_DOWNLOAD_DEPENDENCIES: "required" Wrong loader Auto-detection failed Use loader prefix or MODRINTH_LOADER

docs.title: Spiget (SpigotMC)
docs.text: Download plugins from SpigotMC using the Spiget API.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Feature Value Official Website https://www.spigotmc.org/ Spiget API https://spiget.org/ API Key Required No Supported Types Plugins only Server Types Paper, Spigot, Bukkit

Spiget vs Spigot

The config key uses SPIGET (with an "E"), not "SPIGOT". Spiget is a third-party API that provides programmatic access to SpigotMC resources.

docs.title: Create Server and Add Plugins
docs.text:
# Create a Paper server
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

# Add SpigotMC plugins (using numeric resource IDs)
mcctl config survival SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315,6245"

# Restart to apply changes
mcctl stop survival && mcctl start survival

docs.title: Finding Resource IDs
docs.text: The resource ID is the numeric portion at the end of the SpigotMC resource URL.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Plugin URL Resource ID LuckPerms https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/luckperms.28140/ 28140 Vault https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/vault.34315/ 34315 PlaceholderAPI https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/placeholderapi.6245/ 6245 WorldEdit https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/worldedit.13932/ 13932 CoreProtect https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/coreprotect.8631/ 8631

docs.title: How to Find Resource ID
docs.text:
1. Go to SpigotMC Resources
  2. Search for the plugin you want
  3. Click on the plugin to open its page
  4. Look at the URL: https://www.spigotmc.org/resources/plugin-name.XXXXX/
  5. The number at the end (XXXXX) is the resource ID

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
# Add plugins (comma-separated numeric IDs)
mcctl config myserver SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315,6245"

# Or append IDs with mcctl mod (mcctl does not check them)
mcctl mod add myserver --spiget 28140 34315

# Restart to apply
mcctl stop myserver && mcctl start myserver

docs.title: View Current Configuration
docs.text:
# View all configuration
mcctl config myserver

# View Spiget resources
mcctl config myserver SPIGET_RESOURCES

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text: Config Key Description SPIGET_RESOURCES Comma-separated list of SpigotMC resource IDs

docs.title: File Handling
docs.text:
The Spiget API handles different file types automatically:

File Type Action .jar file Moved directly to plugins directory .zip file Extracted into plugins directory

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Download Restrictions

Some plugins on SpigotMC restrict automated downloads through Spiget. These plugins require external download authentication that Spiget cannot provide.

Example restricted plugins:

  • EssentialsX (ID: 9089)
  • Some premium plugins

For these plugins, manually download and use the shared plugins directory.

docs.title: Manual Download Alternative
docs.text:
For restricted plugins, use the shared plugins directory:

# Download plugin manually and place in shared directory
# Location: ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/

# Every server copies the file into its plugins/ folder at its next start

docs.title: Paper Server with Multiple Plugins

mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Configure plugins
mcctl config survival SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315,6245"
mcctl config survival MEMORY "4G"

# Start server
mcctl start survival

mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1

mcctl config survival MODRINTH_PROJECTS "chunky,spark"

docs.title: Combined with Manual Plugins
docs.text:
For plugins that restrict Spiget downloads:

  1. Download the plugin manually from SpigotMC
  2. Place the JAR file in ~/minecraft-servers/shared/plugins/
  3. The plugin is copied into each server when the server starts
# Create server without starting it (shared/plugins/ is mounted automatically)
mcctl create survival -t PAPER -v 1.21.1 --no-start

# Add Spiget plugins for ones that work
mcctl config survival SPIGET_RESOURCES "28140,34315"

# Manual plugins in shared/plugins/ are automatically available
mcctl start survival

docs.title: Console Bento UI Implementation Plan
docs.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Extend the approved dashboard Bento UI hierarchy across every mcctl console screen while preserving existing operational behavior and information density.

Architecture: Add four presentational primitives under src/components/bento/, refactor the dashboard pilot onto them, and migrate one route at a time. Pages continue to own hooks, derived state, permissions, and mutations; Bento components receive display-ready props and never fetch or cache data.

Tech Stack: Next.js 14 App Router, React 18, TypeScript, MUI 5, TanStack Query, Vitest, Testing Library, Playwright, pnpm, Node 22.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-28-console-bento-design.md

docs.title: Global Constraints
docs.text:
• Preserve existing API calls, hooks, permissions, navigation, actions, and domain behavior.
  • Add no backend, database, API contract, component-library, CSS-framework, or runtime-dependency changes.
  • Use one column below sm, six columns from sm, and twelve columns from md; gaps are 16px on mobile and 20px from sm upward.
  • Standard Bento surfaces use a 16px radius and divider-colored border; only heroes use strong gradients or shadows.
  • Color never communicates status without text or an icon, and mobile DOM order is the reading order.
  • Dense tables, forms, tabs, file browsers, and terminals stay dense inside Bento surfaces.
  • Use only metrics available from existing page data; do not invent trends or add duplicate data requests for decoration.
  • Initial skeletons match loaded grid spans, and no screen may create document-level horizontal scrolling at 375px.
  • Run all console commands with PATH=/home/smallmiro/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin:$PATH.

docs.title: Review Focus
docs.text:
• Stale SSE data: dashboard and operational status must say Reconnecting or Disconnected, never Live; Tasks 1, 2, 4, and 9 pin this behavior.
  • Long server, world, hostname, and user text: content must wrap or truncate inside minmax(0, 1fr) tracks without page overflow; Tasks 1, 2, 3, 5, and 11 cover style invariants and representative long values.
  • Destructive actions after layout moves: server/world delete confirmations and disabled states must remain intact; Tasks 3 and 5 retain interaction tests.
  • Permission-sensitive controls: page shells must not bypass or replace existing guarded feature components; Tasks 2, 3, and 11 exercise existing child components and admin boundaries.
  • Loading, empty, API-error, and partial-data states: every migrated page must retain a useful landmark and action without a geometry collapse; each page task adds or updates these tests.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
Extend the approved dashboard Bento UI pilot across the mcctl console without reducing the information density needed for day-to-day Minecraft server operations. The result should feel like one coherent control surface: important state and actions are visually prominent, dense operational data remains easy to scan, and every page works from a 375px mobile viewport through a wide desktop.

The primary users are server administrators and delegated operators. Success means they can identify system state, find the primary action, and reach detailed data at least as quickly as before while the console gains a consistent visual hierarchy.

docs.title: Chosen Approach
docs.text:
Use a small set of shared Bento layout primitives, proven by the dashboard pilot, and migrate screens incrementally. The alternatives were a theme-only restyle, which cannot express page-level hierarchy, and page-local restyles, which would duplicate layout rules and drift over time. Shared primitives give the console a common grammar while leaving each operational page free to choose the layout its content needs.

This is not a tile-everything redesign. Bento composition is used for page hierarchy, summaries, status, filters, and primary actions. Tables, forms, tab panels, file browsers, and terminal output retain their dense task-oriented presentation inside a suitable surface.

docs.title: Included
docs.text:
• Extract the dashboard's responsive grid, elevated surface, page hero, and metric presentation into reusable console components.
  • Refactor the dashboard to consume those components without changing its behavior.
  • Apply the system to the server list, server detail, server console, worlds, players, backups, routing, audit logs, settings, and admin users pages.
  • Align loading, empty, error, and disconnected states with the final page geometry.
  • Preserve existing API calls, hooks, permissions, navigation, actions, and domain behavior.
  • Validate desktop, tablet, and 375px mobile layouts.

docs.title: Excluded
docs.text:
• Backend, database, or API contract changes.
  • Navigation information-architecture changes.
  • New charts, fabricated trends, or metrics not already available from existing data.
  • A new component library, CSS framework, or runtime dependency.
  • A light theme.
  • Redesigning login and signup flows beyond applying the shared surface and spacing language.

docs.title: Visual System
docs.text:
The current dark Modrinth-inspired palette remains the foundation. Bento UI adds hierarchy through scale, span, spacing, subtle accent gradients, and restrained elevation rather than introducing a second visual identity.

  • Breakpoints follow the existing MUI theme: one column below sm, six columns from sm, and twelve columns from md.
  • Grid gaps are 16px on mobile and 20px from sm upward.
  • Standard Bento surfaces use a 16px corner radius, a divider-colored border, and no background image.
  • Hero surfaces may use a semantic accent gradient and stronger shadow. Ordinary content panels stay neutral.
  • Accent colors come only from the existing MUI semantic palette. Color never carries status without text or an icon.
  • Hover lift is limited to interactive or summary cards. Static data panels do not move.
  • Motion is removed when prefers-reduced-motion is enabled.
  • Mobile DOM order is the reading order; CSS placement must not create a different visual sequence.

docs.title: Shared Components
docs.text: Create a focused src/components/bento/ module rather than expanding global MUI overrides.

docs.title: BentoGrid
docs.text: A semantic Box wrapper that supplies the one/six/twelve-column responsive grid, standard gaps, stretched items, and minmax(0, 1fr) tracks. Pages choose their own spans through sx; the component does not encode page-specific templates.

docs.title: BentoPanel
docs.text: A Paper-based surface for bounded sections. It owns the standard radius, border, overflow behavior, and optional semantic accent. It accepts normal MUI Paper properties and sx so dense existing components can be placed inside without wrappers fighting their layout.

docs.title: PageHero
docs.text: A responsive page introduction with one h1, optional eyebrow/icon, description, status, metrics, and action slot. On mobile, actions wrap below the title. Destructive actions remain visually separated from the primary action. Pages with no useful summary use the compact variant rather than filling space.

docs.title: BentoMetricCard
docs.text:
The reusable form of the dashboard StatCard. It supports a label, value, optional unit, icon, description, semantic accent, and an optional computed progress value clamped to 0–100. It does not calculate business metrics. Dashboard keeps a compatibility export while migrating to the shared implementation.

Page-specific skeletons use these primitives and match the loaded geometry. A generic skeleton abstraction is intentionally excluded because each screen's information hierarchy differs.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text: Keep the approved pilot composition: status hero, four metrics, server overview, routing summary, recent activity, and changelog. Refactor only the visual primitives. SSE-overlay status, unhealthy-server attention counts, and Live/Reconnecting behavior must remain unchanged.

docs.title: Servers
docs.text:
The list page uses a compact operational hero with total/running/attention counts and the create-server action. Search and filters sit in a full-width control panel directly above the server collection. Server cards retain all current controls and permissions.

The server detail page uses a status hero for identity, health, address, and lifecycle actions. Resource summaries form a metric row. Existing tabs remain the primary detail navigation and occupy one full-width panel so configuration, files, backups, access, mods, and world controls remain dense and predictable.

The server console is a focus screen, not a decorative mosaic. A compact hero shows server and connection state; the terminal receives the dominant remaining viewport area; command and connection controls form one adjacent or stacked panel depending on width. Log lines and terminal keyboard behavior are unchanged.

docs.title: Worlds and Players
docs.text:
Worlds uses a summary hero, availability metrics, then filter/actions and the world collection. Map, analysis, upload, lock, and assignment behavior stay unchanged.

Players uses a summary hero and server selector, followed by online/known/whitelist/operator summaries. Existing rosters and management controls stay in dense panels. Loading one server or roster must not reflow unrelated sections.

docs.title: Backups, Routing, and Audit Logs
docs.text:
Backups places backup health, last run, schedules, and primary backup action near the top; schedules and history remain full-width operational panels.

Routing emphasizes router state and exposed destinations. Status and summary cards use Bento hierarchy, while hostname and tunnel records remain dense lists.

Audit logs keeps filters and export action prominent, uses summary metrics only where the existing endpoint supplies them, and keeps the log table full width. Live-stream disconnection is shown as explicit status text.

docs.title: Settings and Admin Users
docs.text:
Settings uses a compact hero and groups platform, network, and other existing settings into stable panels. Forms keep their current validation and submission behavior.

Admin users uses a compact hero with user counts and the existing management list in a full-width panel. Permission and destructive account actions remain explicit and require the same confirmations as today.

Login and signup remain centered task pages; only surface radius, border, spacing, and accents are aligned with the shared visual language.

docs.title: Data and State Flow
docs.text:
Pages continue to own data fetching and business-derived values through the current hooks. Shared Bento components are presentational and receive already-derived values through props. They do not call APIs, subscribe to SSE, inspect permissions, or cache state.

Existing behavior remains authoritative:

  1. Page hooks fetch data and expose loading/error state.
  2. Existing SSE hooks overlay live status where currently supported.
  3. The page derives display metrics and passes them to heroes or metric cards.
  4. Existing feature components render actions and dense details inside Bento surfaces.

This boundary keeps visual migration independent from backend behavior and makes each page reversible without changing data contracts.

docs.title: Loading, Empty, and Error States
docs.text:
• Initial loading renders a skeleton with the same grid spans and approximate heights as the loaded content.
  • Section-level refresh keeps established content visible when the existing query behavior supports it.
  • Empty states explain what is absent and preserve the existing creation or recovery action.
  • Page-level fetch errors use one prominent panel with retry behavior when already available.
  • SSE disconnection changes live-status text and icon; it does not imply that cached server state is live.
  • Long labels, hostnames, server names, and translated browser-generated text must wrap or truncate without horizontal page overflow.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
• Each page has exactly one h1 in its hero or compact header.
  • Major groups use named section landmarks where this improves navigation.
  • Icon-only actions retain accessible labels and visible tooltips.
  • Status is always communicated by text in addition to color.
  • Focus order follows DOM and mobile reading order.
  • Existing keyboard interactions for dialogs, tabs, tables, file tools, and the terminal remain intact.
  • Progress indicators expose accessible labels and determinate values only when a real ratio exists.

docs.title: Migration Order
docs.text:
1. Foundation: add shared Bento primitives and refactor the dashboard onto them.
  2. Primary operations: migrate servers list, server detail, and server console.
  3. Resource operations: migrate worlds and players.
  4. Supporting operations: migrate backups, routing, and audit logs.
  5. Administration: migrate settings, admin users, login, and signup surface styling.
  6. Consistency pass: remove superseded page-local layout styles and verify the whole console together.

Each phase must leave the console usable and testable. A phase is committed only after its focused tests and repository checks pass.

docs.title: Testing and Acceptance
docs.text:
Implementation follows test-driven development for shared behavior and page structure.

  • Shared component tests cover semantic elements, variants, progress clamping, action rendering, and reduced-motion styling where practical.
  • Page tests verify the hero title/status, primary actions, critical metrics, loading geometry, and existing permission-sensitive behavior.
  • Existing feature tests remain unchanged unless markup movement requires queries to target accessible roles instead of implementation details.
  • Focused tests run after each red/green cycle.
  • Each phase runs the console test suite, type check, lint, and production build under the repository-supported Node 22 environment.
  • Browser QA covers 375px mobile, a tablet width, and desktop. No page may create document-level horizontal scrolling.
  • Visual QA checks light-on-dark contrast, focus visibility, long content, empty data, loading data, API failure, and disconnected SSE state.

The migration is accepted when every included page uses the shared hierarchy, all existing actions remain reachable, the verification suite passes, and manual responsive checks reveal no clipped controls or document-level overflow.

docs.title: Rollback and Risk Control
docs.text:
The migration changes presentation in page-sized commits and introduces no data migration. If a page regresses, its composition can be reverted independently while retaining the shared primitives for completed pages. The highest-risk screens are server detail and server console because of their dense interactions; they are migrated early enough to validate the system before repetitive support pages are changed.

No global MuiCard or MuiPaper change will be used to force Bento styling onto untouched areas. This avoids accidental changes to dialogs, menus, and specialized feature components.
